descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the Alapin Sicilian! This is the perfect way to shut down ANYONE who plays the sicilian against you. We begin with pawn to e4
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/2p5/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Black played the sicilian defense - which means we can stop them in their tracks with the alapin. To play the alapin, we play pawn to c3. The idea is pretty clear: prepare to take the center with pawn to d4 on the next move.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1ppppp/2n5/2p5/4P3/2P5/PP1P1P: This move did nothing to stop us from playing pawn to d4, which is the whole idea of the alapin.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1ppppp/2n5/8/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/: Let's take back on d4 with our pawn and keep our strong center
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2np4/8/3PP3/8/PP3PPP/RN: The beauty of having the whole center is we can kick black's pieces around. Pawn to d5, kicking their knight!
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/3p4/3Pn3/4P3/8/PP3PPP/R: Let's keep kicking that knight around - pawn to f4!
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1npppp/3p4/3P4/4PP2/8/PP4PP/R: Now that we own the literal entire center, it's time to develop. Knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1npppp/3p4/3P4/4PP2/5N2/PP4PP: Well done! Black is completely paralyzed here
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3p4/3PP3/8/PP3PPP/R: Let's spice things up: pawn takes pawn on d5. The idea is to draw out black's queen and hit her with a bunch of attacks
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/8/PP3PPP/RN: We ideally want to play knight to c3 and hit the queen, but we need to defend our pawn first. Knight to f3.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3q4/3P2b1/5N2/PP3PPP/: NOW we can go knight to c3, hitting the queen.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/8/3P2b1/2N2N2/PP3PPP: Black ran away - big mistake! Pawn to d5, hitting their knight.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/8/3Pn3/6b1/2N2N2/PP3PPP/: Game over!!! And we'll do it in style too - with queen sacrifice. Knight takes knight on e5
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/8/3PN3/8/2N5/PP3PPP/R1Bb: Our queen is gone. How do we win her back? Hint: bishop to b5
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp1qpppp/8/1B1PN3/8/2N5/PP3PPP/R1: Black was forced to block the check with the queen, and now we get her. Bishop takes queen!
descriptions.r2k1bnr/pp1Bpppp/8/3PN3/8/2N5/PP3PPP/R1B: We're already a piece up, and now we win a second. King takes bishop on d1.
What a gorgeous line. Your opponent will probably report you for cheating.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/3p2n1/3P4/4PP2/8/PP4PP/: Now it's time for US to develop. Knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p1nn1/3P4/4PP2/5N2/PP4: This is actually a big mistake for black - they're trying to develop their pieces without having any pawns in the center. We can hit their knights AGAIN with pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/5nn1/3Pp3/5P2/5N2/PP4PP: Pawn takes back on e5, hitting the knight once more.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/6n1/3nP3/8/5N2/PP4PP/RN: Wait so... did we just lose a pawn? Nope - we actually just won a knight! First: bishop to b5 check, forcing black to block with their bishop
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp1bpppp/6n1/1B1nP3/8/5N2/PP4PP/: Now that black's queen is disconnected from defending their knight, we can just... take it! Queen takes knight on d5.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp1bpppp/6n1/qB1QP3/8/5N2/PP4PP/R: One last move that makes this tactic work: knight to c3 both block's the queen's check AND defends our bishop.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp1bpppp/6n1/qB1QP3/8/2N2N2/PP4PP: Better development, better center, and did I mention we're a piece up?
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/3p4/2p5/4P3/2P5/PP1P1PP: We played c3 with the simple idea of pushing d4 next. Since Black hasn't done anything to challenge that plan, we can go ahead and play pawn to d4 now.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/3p4/8/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/R: Black just gave up the fight for the center - amazing. Pawn takes pawn on d4 and the center is ours.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p1n2/8/3PP3/8/PP3PPP/R: Black is attacking our e4 pawn with a horse - let's defend it with a horse. Knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2np1n2/8/3PP3/2N5/PP3PP: Here's a great example of why owning the center is so important: black just developed a knight and we can push our d-pawn to d5 to kick it away.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p1n2/3Pn3/4P3/2N5/PP3P: Let's keep kicking that knight around with pawn to f4
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p1nn1/3P4/4PP2/2N5/PP4: Let's keep developing with knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p1nn1/3P4/4PP2/2N2N2/P: The computer gives us a +2 eval advantage just because our center is soooo good.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp3ppp/3pb1n1/8/4PP2/5N2/PP4PP/R: Aaaaand that's a fork. Pawn to f5 forks the bishop and knight.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp3ppp/3pb1n1/5P2/4P3/5N2/PP4PP/: The piece is ours and the game is OVER!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/8/2pp4/4P3/2P5/PP1P1PPP: A center pawn for a center pawn is a good trade. Pawn takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/pp2pppp/8/2pq4/8/2P5/PP1P1PPP/R: Now we continue with our main point for the alapin: pawn to d4, striking in the center.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/pp2pppp/8/3q4/3p4/2P5/PP3PPP/RN: Let's take back with our pawn to keep a pawn in the center (remember, that's the entire point of playing pawn to c3 on our second move). Pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/8/PP3PPP/RN: Simple chess: knight to f3 to defend our pawn.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3q4/3P2b1/5N2/PP3PPP/: NOW we can go knight to c3, hitting the queen.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/q7/3P2b1/2N2N2/PP3PPP: Black ran their queen away - a big mistake! We can capitalize by pushing our pawn to d5.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp2pppp/8/q2Pn3/6b1/2N2N2/PP3PPP/: Black's king is incredibly exposed - let's hit him with bishop to b5 check
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp1npppp/8/qB1P4/6b1/2N2N2/PP3PPP: Before we continue our big attack, let's castle our king to safety.

Well done! Although the material is equal, black is in huge trouble here. Their pieces are uncoordinated, undeveloped, and unsafe. The computer loves our position so much that it gives us a +3 point advantage and 70% winrate from here!
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/2pq4/3P2b1/2P2N2/PP3: A lot of other courses recommend simply unpinning with our bishop here. I don't know about you but when I see a check, I play it: queen to a4 check. This is going to set up a ton of fun traps against our opponent.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/2pq4/Q2P2b1/2P2N2/P: Let's play bishop to c4. Although the eval bar says the position is equal, most of your opponents are about to make a mistake
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/2p5/Q1BPq1b1/2P2N2/: And that right there is a mistake! First things first, we need to block the check: bishop to e3.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/2p5/Q1BPq3/2P1Bb2/P: Most of our opponents see this position and think they're winning a free pawn after we take the bishop back. Not so fast! We can play knight to d2 and hit the queen AND bishop.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/2p5/Q1BP2q1/2P1Bb2/: We have to take the bishop back - knight takes bishop on f3.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/2p5/Q1BP4/2P1BN2/PP: There's only one way to save both the our rook and our knight here: king to e2
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp3ppp/2n1pn2/2p5/Q1BP4/2P1BN2/PP: I know what you're thinking: we're a pawn down and we can't castle - what the hell did we get ourselves into? Well, the computer actually thinks we're completely winning now. The main idea? Exploiting the pin on the c6 knight. Black has no good way of defending it. We can get rid of the knight's last defender, the b7 pawn, by sacrificing our bishop onto a6.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/pp3ppp/B1n1pn2/2p5/Q2P4/2P1BN2/P: Aaaaand now it's checkmate in 2. Black totally forgot that castling pins their pawn to their king, and know we can take the knight completely for free. Queen takes knight on c6 check.
descriptions.1k1r1b1r/pp3ppp/B1Q1pn2/2p5/3P4/2P1BN2/P: Checkmate in 1 - can you find it? Hint: queen to b7.
descriptions.1k1r1b1r/pQ3ppp/B3pn2/2p5/3P4/2P1BN2/PP2: Crazy how quick we went from defending black's attack to checkmating black ourselves.
descriptions.1r2kb1r/pp3ppp/B1n1pn2/2p5/Q2P4/2P1BN2/P: Fine, if black won't take our bishop with their pawn, we'll take black's pawn with our bishop. Bishop takes pawn on b7.
descriptions.4kb1r/pr3ppp/2n1pn2/2p5/Q2P4/2P1BN2/PP2K: Now queen takes knight on c6 check, forking the king and rook.
descriptions.4kb1r/p2r1ppp/2Q1pn2/2p5/3P4/2P1BN2/PP2K: Ideally we can add pressure to the d7 rook by hopping our knight to e5, but if we did that right now, black's queen could take our queen. So our plan? Move black's queen off that light-square diagonal. We can do that with a simple h-rook to g1.
descriptions.4kb1r/p2r1ppp/2Q1pn2/2p5/3P4/2P1BN1q/PP2: Awesome - NOW we can play knight to e5, adding pressure to the d7 rook.
descriptions.4kb1r/p2r1ppp/2Q1pn2/2p1N3/3P4/2P1B2q/PP: We are completely and utterly crushing black here. In a second we are about to win their rook and then probably the game.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1npppp/6n1/3PP3/8/5N2/PP4PP/R: Let's just... keep pushing! Pawn to e6
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1np1pp/4p1n1/3P4/8/5N2/PP4PP/: Pawn takes pawn back on e6
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2p1pp/4Pnn1/8/8/5N2/PP4PP/RNB: Now a knockout blow: Queen to a4 check. Whatever black blocks with will get taken by our pawn.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1np1pp/4P1n1/8/Q7/5N2/PP4PP/R: Aaaaand that's a free knight. Pawn takes knight on d7.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/4p3/2p5/4P3/2P5/PP1P1P: Black's kinda copying us - we played c3 to build up to pawn to d4. Black played e6 to build up to d5. Well, we're a bit quicker: pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2pp4/3PP3/2P5/PP3PPP: Two good moves here: taking or pushing. I recommend taking. Pawn takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/8/2pp4/3P4/2P5/PP3PPP/RN: Simple chess - let's develop our bishop to b5
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n5/1Bpp4/3P4/2P5/PP3PPP: Now we can develop our knight to f3 and castle.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp1b1ppp/2n5/1Bpp4/3P4/2P2N2/PP3: Black is completely ignoring their kingside development. Let's castle our king to safety before opening up the center and taking advantage of black's uncastled king.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp1b1ppp/2n2n2/1Bpp4/3P4/2P2N2/P: One last move before we open up the center: bishop to g5
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp1bbppp/2n2n2/1Bpp2B1/3P4/2P2N2/: It looks like black will have enough time to castle, but they won't. Pawn takes pawn on c5, opening up the center.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp1b1ppp/2n2n2/1Bbp2B1/8/2P2N2/PP: Let's take advantage of black's uncastled king: rook to e1 check.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp1bbppp/2n2n2/1B1p2B1/8/2P2N2/PP: With black's bishop pinned, now is a GREAT time to take black's knight. They'll have to take back with their pawn. Bishop takes knight on f6
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp1bbp1p/2n2p2/1B1p4/8/2P2N2/PP3P: Finally, queen takes the free pawn on d5!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1ppp1p/6p1/2p5/4P3/2P5/PP1P1P: Whenever we get a chance, we play the d4 pawn push
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1ppp1p/6p1/8/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/: Pawn takes pawn back on d4
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pp1pppbp/6p1/8/3PP3/8/PP3PPP/RN: Black is continuing to develop but we have the entire center - which is great for us! Let's play knight to c3.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pp2ppbp/3p2p1/8/3PP3/2N2N2/PP3P: We got everything we wanted out of this opening - the center and development. You can play bishop to b5 next
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/3ppn2/8/3PP3/2N5/PP3PPP/: We'll keep it simple and keep developing: knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2bppp/3ppn2/8/3PP3/2N2N2/PP3PP: More simple development: bishop to d3.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bppp/3ppn2/8/3PP3/2NB1N2/PP3: We're looking great! Pawns in the center, pieces developed, and king castled. The eval bar gives us +1 point advantage.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/4p3/8/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/: We'll take back with pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/3p4/3PP3/8/PP3PPP/RN: Let's push our pawn to e5 and really squeeze black's position
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/3P4/8/PP3PPP/: We'll keep developing: knight to f3
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/1b1P4/5N2/PP3: We can block the check with knight to c3
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/1b1P4/2N2N2/P: Well done! We're a bit better than black here
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/2n1p3/8/3PP3/8/PP3PPP/: Let's go pawn to d5 and hit the knight.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/2n5/3p4/4P3/8/PP3PPP/R: We'll recapture with pawn to d5 and re-hit the knight
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/8/3Pn3/8/8/PP3PPP/RNBQ: Let's develop with knight to c3
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/8/3Pn3/8/2N5/PP3PPP/R1: Well done! We're slightly better than black here
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/8/2p1p3/4P3/2P5/PP1P1P: Knight to f3, hitting black's undefended pawn.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/2n5/2p1p3/4P3/2P2N2/PP: Bishop to c4 now, hitting black's weak f2 pawn and also preventing black from playing d5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/2n5/2p1p3/2B1P3/2P2N2/: Well done! I like our position here
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2nppp/2n1p3/3pP3/3P4/2N2N2/PP: OK, pretty even game from here, though I'll definitely take our position over Black's
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/2N2b2/PP3PPP/: Let's recapture our piece - pawn takes bishop on f3
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/8/3q4/2N2P2/PP3P1P/R1: Now for a queen trade - queen takes queen
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp2pppp/8/8/3n4/2N2P2/PP3P1P/R1B1: Black is 1 move away from forking us on c2 - let's play knight to b5 and threaten the same thing on their side of the board
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp2pppp/8/1N6/8/5P2/PP3P1P/n1BK1B: Let's give black a taste of their own medicine - knight to c7
descriptions.N4bnr/pp1kpppp/8/8/8/5P2/PP3P1P/n1BK1B1R: Well done! Both sides played perfectly here
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp1qpppp/2n2n2/2p5/Q1BP2b1/2P2N2/: This was black's only good response - and it means we probably don't have any more traps for them. We can at least win a pawn with pawn takes pawn on c5.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp1qpppp/2n2n2/2P5/Q1B5/2P2b2/PP3: Take back with pawn takes bishop on f3, of course.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp1q1ppp/2n1pn2/2P5/Q1B5/2P2P2/PP: Black is attacking our pawn - let's defend it with bishop to e3.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp1q1ppp/2n1pn2/2P5/Q1B5/2P1BP2/P: Both sides played perfectly, but at least we have an interesting game ahead of us a free pawn in our pocket.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp1bpppp/5n2/2pq4/Q2P4/2P2N2/PP3: We made black retreat their bishop from our side of the board - that's great. Now it's our turn to retreat: queen back to b3.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp1bpppp/5n2/2p5/3P4/1qP2N2/PP3P: Most of the time our opponents will trade our queen here, which is great for us. Now after pawn takes queen on b3, our rook is opened up.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp1bpppp/5n2/2p5/3P4/1PP2N2/1P3P: Well done! Both sides played perfectly here so the evaluation is equal
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp1ppppp/5n2/2p5/4P3/2P5/PP1P1P: Let's push our pawn up to e5 and hit black's knight, forcing it to move somewhere.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp1ppppp/8/2pnP3/8/2P5/PP1P1PPP: Let's develop our own knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1ppppp/2n5/2pnP3/8/2P2N2/PP1P: I like playing bishop to c4 here, hitting the undefended knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1ppppp/1nn5/2p1P3/2B5/2P2N2/P: Now black is hitting OUR undefended bishop. Let's tuck it back onto b3
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp1p1ppp/4p3/2pnP3/8/2P2N2/PP1P: Let's grab the center with pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp1p1ppp/4p3/3nP3/3p4/2P2N2/PP3: Pawn captures back on d4, making sure we still have  pawns in the center
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/3pp3/3nP3/3P4/5N2/PP3PPP: We can develop our bishop to c4 next

shortDescriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/2p5/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Let's continue with the Alapin Sicilian

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/RNB: Look, I like the Queen's Gambit. It was a good TV show. But I HATE playing against the opening. Let's crush the Queen's Gambit with the Albin Countergambit. When they try to give us a pawn, we flip the script and gambit our OWN pawn. First step: play into the Queen's Gambit with pawn to d5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3p4/2PP4/8/PP2PPPP/R: And we have arrived at the Queen's Gambit, where white is giving away their c4 pawn. Usually we either take or defend. In the Albin Countergambit, we actually gambit a pawn of our own with pawn to e5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3pp3/2PP4/2N5/PP2PPPP: OK if white doesn't take us, we take white. Pawn takes on d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/2PQ4/2N5/PP2PPPP/: There are 3 attackers on the d5 pawn - we really have no way to defend it. So instead, lets focus on development. Knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3Q4/2P5/2N5/PP2PPPP: DON'T trade queens here. Instead, keep on developing. Bishop to e6, hitting the queen and giving us a tempo.
descriptions.r2Qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/8/2P5/2N5/PP2PPPP/: Rook takes back on d8, of course. For the price of 1 pawn, we have developed our knight, bishop, and rook - not a bad deal.
descriptions.3rkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/8/2P5/2N1P3/PP3PPP/: This is white's most common move and it just LOST them the game. They were trying to defend their c4 pawn, but they missed our even bigger threat: knight to b4, threatening a fork on c2.
descriptions.3rkbnr/ppp2ppp/4b3/8/1nP5/2N1P3/PP3PPP/1: It just gets worse and worse... White moved their rook out of the way, but its the king we care about. Knight to c2 check.
descriptions.3rkbnr/ppp2ppp/4b3/8/2P5/2N1P3/PPn1KPPP/: Aaaand with the king blocking his own bishop, now we can play bishop to c4 check.
descriptions.3rkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/8/2b5/2N1PK2/PPn2PPP/1R: Why not take a free bishop? Bishop captures on f1.
descriptions.3rkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/8/8/2N1PK2/PPn2PPP/1RB2: Well done! We literally just have a free bishop. I don't need to tell you why that's winning.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3pP3/2P5/8/PP2PPPP/RN: White accepted our countergambit. Great. Now we push our pawn to d4 to stop them from developing their knight to c3.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/2Pp4/4P3/PP3PPP/R: White is trying to trade off our central pawn so they can continue developing. Before we trade pawns, though, let's play a check: bishop to b4.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1bPp4/4P3/PP1B1PP: Our bishop is hanging. So what do we do? Defend it? NO! We play pawn takes e3, inviting White to take our free bishop. If they do, its game over.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1BP5/4p3/PP3PPP/R: We're a bishop down. We have no pieces developed. We have a weak pawn. How are we going to win this? Well, we're going to steal the queen. Right now, we can't take the queen because the king defends her. Let's force the king out of the way with pawn takes f2 with check.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1BP5/8/PP2KpPP/RN: OMG we get to do the coolest move ever now. OK, so the king decided to stay with his queen, so we can't just capture the queen. We could play pawn captures knight on g1 and make a new queen, but then White takes our old queen with check, then takes our new queen on the next move. So, heres what to do: We play pawn takes knight on g1 and promote to a KNIGHT. Now White is in check and cannot take our queen. It's just so beautiful...
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1BP5/8/PP2K1PP/RN: One move here wins us the queen. Can you find it? Hint: Bishop to g4, skewering the king against his own queen.
descriptions.rn1qk1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1BP3b1/8/PP3KPP/R: Aaaand queen takes queen on d1.
descriptions.rn2k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1BP3b1/8/PP3KPP/RN: One of my favorite lines on this website. I mean, we literally PROMOTED TO A KNIGHT TO WIN A QUEEN.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/2Pp4/5N2/PP2PPPP/: White added an attacker on our d4 pawn. We can add a defender with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/2Pp4/4PN2/PP3PP: Black didn't stop our main threat bishop to b4 check, so now we play bishop to b4 check.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/1bPp4/4PN2/PP1B: DON'T trade bishops here. Instead, play pawn captures pawn on e3. White will be forced to take back with the f-pawn which weakens their king.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/1BP5/4pN2/PP3PP: Don't capture back the bishop here. Instead, play pawn takes pawn on f2 with check. White cannot capture our pawn because then we will win their queen.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/1BP5/5N2/PP2KpP: One more thing before taking our bishop back: let's trade queens. Queen takes queen on d1.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/1BP5/5N2/PP3pPP: NOW we can win our bishop back. Knight takes bishop on b4.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1nP5/5N2/PP3pPP/R: Well done! We are a pawn up, we have a pawn 1 square from becoming a queen, we have stopped white from castling, and we have damaged white's pawn structure. Life is good.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3Pp3/3P4/8/PP2PPPP/RN: White took our pawn - we should take it back with queen to d5.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3qp3/3P4/5N2/PP2PPPP/: White's knight just came out - let's attack it with pawn to e4.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3q4/3Pp3/2N2N2/PP2PPP: White attacks our queen instead of moving their knight. Now, instead of moving our queen, we'll PIN their knight. Bishop to b4.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/3qN3/1b1Pp3/2N5/PP2PP: White moved their knight into our territory - but now it's trapped! Seriously - take a look - it has no escape squares. Now how do we capture this trapped knight? First, we need to trade off our bishop so there's no Queen to a4 ideas. Bishop takes knight on c3.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/3qN3/3Pp3/2P5/P3PPPP/: Now we can attack the trapped knight with pawn to f6.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp3pp/5p2/3qN3/Q2Pp3/2P5/P3PPP: This... doesn't matter. It's just delaying the inevitable. Simply pawn to b5 here to block check.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/p1p3pp/5p2/1p1qN3/Q2Pp3/2P5/P3P: Well done! We're winning this knight no-matter what white does.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1BP5/8/PP3KPP/RN1: The king took his eyes off the queen. Now she's ours. Queen takes queen on d1.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3p4/2P5/2N5/PP2PPPP: This was so weak from White. They had 3 attackers on our pawn but ran away like they were scared. Now we turn our weakest pawn into an asset: Pawn to d4, kicking the knight away.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/8/2Pp4/2N5/PP2PPPP/: Well done! We now own the center and the computer gives us a HUGE edge over our opponent. We'll likely win from here.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1BP5/8/PP4PP/RN1Q: White knew that if he took the knight, we'd just skewer him against his queen. It's too bad for him that the game is already lost. Queen to h4 check.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1BP4q/6P1/PP5P/RN: Now queen to e4, check, forking the king and rook.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1BP1q3/6P1/PP2B2P: Aaaand finally, queen takes rook on h1. No surprise there.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1bP5/4P3/PP1B2PP/: White took with the pawn instead of the bishop, which means we won't quite win the queen in this variation. That said, taking with the pawn opened up the king to an attack. Queen to h4 check.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1bP4q/4P1P1/PP1B3: Now queen to e4, forking the rook, the e3 pawn, and the e5 pawn.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1bP1q3/4PQP1/PP1B: That queen move blocked the attack on the rook and the e3 pawn, but did nothing to protect the e5 pawn. We'll want to take that pawn, but first, lets trade off our hanging bishop. Bishop takes bishop on d2.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/2P1q3/4PQP1/PP1N3: Now we get our gambited pawn back. Queen takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4q3/2P5/4PQP1/PP1N3P/: Well done! We got our pawn back and are ready to continue playing chess! We win 60% of the time from here.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/1bP5/4PN2/PP1B2: Now that the kingside is weakened, we can finally trade bishops. Bishop takes bishop on d2.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/2P5/4PN2/PP1N2P: Let's target that weak e5-pawn with queen to e7. White has no way to defend.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp1qppp/2n5/4P3/2P5/4PN2/PP1NB: Aaaand knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp1qppp/8/4n3/2P5/4PN2/PP1NB1P: Well done! We've equalized our material and have a better pawn structure. Odds are, we win this game.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3qp3/3P4/2N5/PP2PPPP/: White didn't defend their d-pawn, so let's just take. Queen takes on d4.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4p3/3Q4/2N5/PP2PPPP/R: And pawn takes back on d4, of course.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/1N6/3p4/8/PP2PPPP/R1B: White is threatening to fork us on c7. We'll stop that threat, but first, let's throw in a check. Bishop to b4.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/1N6/1b1p4/8/PP1BPPPP/: And bishop takes bishop on d2, forcing white to lose their right to castle.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/1N6/3p4/8/PP1KPPPP/R4: Now we can finally defend against the c7 fork threat. Knight to a6.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2ppp/n7/1N6/3p4/8/PP1KPPPP/R: Well done! We're about equal in this position and have a good game ahead of us.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1bP1q3/4PNP1/PP1B: That knight move blocked the attack on the rook and the e5 pawn, but did nothing to protect the e3 pawn. Queen takes e3.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1bP5/4qNP1/PP1BB2: OK, we gambited a pawn and won it back. Our queen and bishop are in a bit of trouble now. The best way to continue is to trade down all our pieces and head into an endgame. Bishop takes bishop on d2.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/2P5/4qNP1/PP1NB2P: Our queen is.. actually pretty safe here. Let's just develop. Knight to c6.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/2P5/4qNP1/PP1NB: Well done! We are stopping White from castling and we have pressure on the e5 pawn. We win 60% of games from here!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3pp3/2PP4/4P3/PP3PPP/: White declined our countergambit. Whatever. Pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/2PP4/8/PP3PPP/RNB: Let's continue developing with knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/2PP4/2N5/PP3PPP: Let's continue developing with bishop to b4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/1bPP4/2N2N2/PP3: Well done! We're ready to play a game of chess!
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/2P5/4PN2/PP1Q2P: Look at what what we've done to white's position: they have weak pawns on e3 and e5. Our goal from here? Take them. Start with bishop to g4, which develops a piece and also opens our rook to defend our own queen.
descriptions.r2Qk1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/2P3b1/4PN2/PP4PP: Rook takes queen back on d8, of course.
descriptions.3rk1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/2P3b1/4PN2/PP1N2P: Well... I guess we should develop another piece. Let's play knight to e7.
descriptions.3rk2r/ppp1nppp/2n5/4P3/2P3b1/4PN2/PP1N2P: Well done! We'll be hunting down those weak e-file pawns.
descriptions.3rkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/8/2P5/2N5/PP1BPPPP/: OK, let's take our pawn back. Bishop takes on c4.
descriptions.3rkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/8/2b5/2N5/PP1BPPPP/2K: The king committed to the queenside. Let's attack! Knight to b4, threatening the pawn on a2.
descriptions.3rkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/8/1nb5/P1N5/1P1BPPPP/2K: We were going to move our knight to a2 no-matter what. That pawn push didn't change much. Knight to a2.
descriptions.3rkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/8/2b5/P7/NP1BPPPP/2KR1B: Bishop takes back on a2, of course.
descriptions.3rkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/8/8/P7/bP1BPPPP/2KR1BNR: Well done! Thanks to our very strong bishop and rook, we'll win most of the games from here.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3qp3/3P4/4P3/PP3PPP/R: We should play pawn takes on d4, with the goal of isolating White's pawns.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3q4/3P4/8/PP3PPP/RNBQ: Let's add another attacker to the d4 pawn with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/5N2/PP3PPP/: Let's remove the knight as a defender of the d4 pawn with bishop to g4, pinning the knight to the queen.
descriptions.r3kbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/3P2b1/5N2/PP2BPPP: White really wants to castle here - our goal is to stop them. First, play bishop to b4 check.
descriptions.r3k1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/1b1P2b1/2N2N2/PP2: Next, we're going to trade down all the pieces into an endgame. First up: bishop takes knight on f3.
descriptions.r3k1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/1b1P4/2N2B2/PP3PP: Our queen is under attack. Let's move it out of the way with queen to c4. This stops white from being able to castle.
descriptions.r3k1nr/ppp2ppp/2B5/8/1bqP4/2N5/PP3PPP/R1: Recapturing with our queen is actually a mistake. We really don't want white to castle, so let's keep our queen on c4 and instead capture back with pawn to c6. Yup, it's weird doubling our pawns, but this is actually the best move here.
descriptions.r3k1nr/p1p2ppp/2p5/8/1bqP4/2N5/PP2QPPP/R: Now we trade down our queens. Queen takes queen on e2.
descriptions.r3k1nr/p1p2ppp/2p5/8/1b1P4/2N5/PP2KPPP/R: Finally, let's castle queenside, attacking that isolated d4 pawn.
descriptions.2kr2nr/p1p2ppp/2p5/8/1b1P4/2N1B3/PP2KPPP: Now develop our knight to e7. Why? We want to eventually get it to f5 so it can attack the weak d4 pawn.
descriptions.2kr3r/p1p1nppp/2p5/8/1b1P4/2N1B3/PP2KPPP: Well done! 13 moves in, and there have still been thousands of games that have reached this exact position.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/2Pp4/P4N2/1P2PP: White played a3 to stop our bishop from coming to b4. They are playing really well, TBH. The main line from here is simply developing our bishop to g4.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/2Pp2b1/P4N2/1P1N: So this is intresting. White defended their knight, but blocked their queen. This frees up our queen to cause some trouble: queen to e7, putting another attacker on that annoying e5 pawn.
descriptions.r3kbnr/ppp1qppp/2n5/4P3/2Pp2b1/P4N1P/1P1: There's a couple moves we can do here. They're all... fine. I recommend bishop takes knight on f3, with the plan to castle on the next move
descriptions.r3kbnr/ppp1qppp/2n5/4P3/2Pp4/P4N1P/1P2PP: OK now we can long castle. This puts our king in safety and also defends our weak d4 pawn.
descriptions.2kr1bnr/ppp1qppp/2n5/4P3/2Pp4/P4N1P/1P2P: Honestly, white played that pretty perfectly. We have our work cut out for us to win this game.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/2Pp4/5NP1/PP2PP: White played pawn to g3 so they can put their light-squared bishop on g2. We can prepare to fight back against this by playing bishop to e6. The plan is to create a battery with our queen and bishop on the next move.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/4P3/2Pp4/5NP1/PP2P: There is a hanging pawn but we should not take it. Remember the plan: create a battery with queen to d7.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pppq1ppp/2n1b3/4P3/2Pp4/5NP1/PP2P: With our queen and bishop developed, now we can follow white and castle too.
descriptions.2kr1bnr/pppq1ppp/2n1b3/4P3/2Pp4/5NP1/PP1: With our king safe and our battery made, there's nothing else to do but attack. Pawn to h5.
descriptions.2kr1bnr/pppq1pp1/2n1b3/4P2p/2Pp4/5NP1/PP: Well done! We'll march our pawn all the way to white's king. This opens up a file for our rook, and it'll be very uncomfortable for white.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the Bishop's Opening! It's one of the trappiest openings I've ever seen, and you'll pretty much always be winning in the first few moves. First step: pawn to e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: I'm gonna let you take a wiiiiild guess at why it's called the bishop's opening. No, it's not because we play our knight on the second move. Bishop to c4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/4p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1P: Black is attacking our e4 pawn. The boring way to play would be knight to c3, defending our pawn. But are we boring? NO! Pawn to d4, counterattacking black.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/2BPn3/8/PPP2PPP/: Black took our pawn - but now we can take theirs and put black in a lot of trouble: pawn takes e5.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/2b1P3/2B1n3/8/PPP2PPP: It looks like black is going for some weird reverse-fried-liver-attack on us with a fork on f7, but this doesn't work because we have a fork of our own: queen to d5. Now we're hitting the knight on e4 AND threatening checkmate on f7.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/3QP3/2B1n3/8/PPP2bPP/: Black is worried about a pawn on our side of the board, meanwhile we are 1 move away from CHECKMATING him on his side of the board. Simply sidestep our king to f1.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pppp1ppp/8/3QP3/2B1n3/8/PPP2bPP: OK, black finally dealt with the checkmate threat, but now we can win a piece: queen takes knight on e4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pppp1ppp/8/4P3/2B1Q3/8/PPP2bPP/: A pawn for a knight? That's a good trade
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/2BpP3/8/PPP2PPP/: This was black's best response to the bishop's opening. Don't worry though, we still have a couple more tricks up our sleeve: first, knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/8/2Bpn3/5N2/PPP2PPP/: Well, now we're TWO pawns down... let's win one back AND win a tempo with queen takes pawn on d4. Black has to either retreat or defend their knight now.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/3n4/8/2BQ4/5N2/PPP2PPP: Black chose to retreat their knight, but they did it the wrong way! That means we win the game now. All we have to do is castle. You'll see why in a second.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/8/2nQ4/5N2/PPP2PPP/R: So why did we castle? We don't even CARE about taking the knight back. Now we have the killer rook to e1 check.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppppbppp/8/8/2nQ4/5N2/PPP2PPP/RN: Black had to block the check on the king, but now the g7 pawn has no defender! Queen takes pawn on g7
descriptions.rnbqkr2/ppppbpQp/8/8/2n5/5N2/PPP2PPP/RNB: The rook is safe... for now. Bishop to h6 and black has no way to defend it.
descriptions.rnbqkr2/ppppbpQp/7B/8/2n5/5N2/PPP2PPP/RN: With black's bishop pinned to the king, black's rook is lost. There is no good way to save it. The best black can do is try and get their king to escape before checkmate but honestly, they have no chance at winning this game.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/2b5/2BpP3/5N2/PPP2P: Black had a chance to take our e4 pawn, but now that offer is expired. Pawn push to e5.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/2b1P3/2Bp2n1/5N2/PPP2: Hey knight! Wrong way! Pawn to h3 kicks it out.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/2b1P3/2Bp4/5N1P/PPP2n: Black's knight just sacrificed himself for... literally no reason. Don't be scared. King takes knight. Black has no follow-up.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/2b1P3/2B5/3p1N1P/PPP2: Our king will be safe back down on f1
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/2b1P3/2B5/5N1P/PPp3P1: That was black's plan the whole time? They sacrificed their knight to win a pawn?? Hey, I'm not complaining. Queen takes pawn on c2.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/2b1P3/2B5/5N1P/PPQ3P1: Points to black for the cool (but meaningless) sacrifice
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/4p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1PP: Dang... black played slow and safe, and now they've basically shut down all our opening tricks. From this position, I recommend knight to f3. This transposes to a sideline in the Philidor Defense (course coming soon!)
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2pp1/3p3p/4p3/2B1P3/5N2/PPPP: Black shut down a potential knight-to-g5, but that move was a little TOO slow. With 2 pieces developed to black's 0, let's crash open the center with pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2pp1/3p3p/8/2BpP3/5N2/PPP2PP: Alright, should I show you a crazy line? This is the Bishop's Opening after all. Three sacrifices in a row. Ready? First sacrifice: pawn to c3.
descriptions.rnbq1bnr/ppp2kp1/3p3p/8/4P3/2p2N2/PP3PPP: Third sacrifice: Knight to e5. If black takes, we win their queen.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp3p1/3p3p/4N3/4P3/2p5/PP3PPP/: Black didn't take, so we don't win the queen. But do you know what we DO win? THE KING! Forced mate now. First: Queen to h5 check.
descriptions.rnbq1bnr/ppp1k1p1/3p3p/4N2Q/4P3/2p5/PP3P: Then we finish black off with queen to f7 CHECKMATE
descriptions.rnbq1bnr/ppp1kQp1/3p3p/4N3/4P3/2p5/PP3PP: But hey! At least black didn't lose their queen right :D
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pP3/2B1n3/8/PPP2PPP/: Black just gave us a pawn for literally no reason, but I won't complain! Bishop takes pawn on d5 and now we have a free pawn AND we're attacking the undefended knight.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/2nBP3/8/8/PPP2PPP/RNB: Ya know what I could really go for right now? A queen. Notice that the black queen is only defended by the black king. We can deflect the king away from his queen by sacrificing our bishop on f7. After that - free queen!
descriptions.rnbq1b1r/ppp1kBpp/8/2n1P3/8/8/PPP2PPP/RN: Black reaaaallly doesn't want to lose their queen. Good thing we can force them to! Dark-square bishop check on g5.
descriptions.rnbq1b1r/ppp2kpp/8/2n1P1B1/8/8/PPP2PPP/R: Two ways to win the queen. It really doesn't matter which you choose but the computer slightly prefers taking with the bishop so.... bishop takes queen on d8.
descriptions.rnbB1b1r/ppp2kpp/8/2n1P3/8/8/PPP2PPP/RN1: Don't you just love free queens?
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/2BPP3/8/PPP2: Black walked right into a bullet. Pawn to d5 wins us the center and a tempo on that knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/3Pp3/2BnP3/8/PPP2P: Instead of retreating from the bullet, black walked right into the gun. Now pawn to c3 TRAPS the knight! Seriously, look! The knight has nowhere to go now.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p1pp1ppp/5n2/1p1Pp3/2BnP3/2P5/P: Let's calmly retreat our bishop to d3. The knight is still trapped.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1pp1ppp/5n2/1pbPp3/3nP3/2PB4/PP: Now we win our knight! Pawn takes knight on d4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1pp1ppp/5n2/1p1Pp3/3bP3/3B4/PP3: OK, we're a piece up, but black could potentially have a strong attack on our f2 pawn. The #1 priority is king safety now, so ignore taking that b5 pawn and instead play knight to f3 so we can castle on the next move.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1pp1ppp/5n2/1p1Pp3/3bP3/3B1N2/P: Nice! After we castle on the next move, we'll be a clean piece up
descriptions.rnbq1bnr/ppp2kp1/7p/4p3/4P3/2p5/PP3PPP/R: 3 sacrifices. Black accepted all of them, and now we win a queen. Queen takes queen on d8.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/4p3/2BPP3/8/PPP2P: Big mistake from black! Now we can force their king to lose his right to castle! Pawn takes pawn on e5
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/4p3/2B1P3/8/PPP2PPP: Queen takes queen! Black must recapture with the king
descriptions.rnbk1b1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/4p3/2B1P3/8/PPP2PPP: Let's keep our foot on the pedal! Knight to f3 attacks the e5 pawn, and also threatens some f7-forks down the road
descriptions.r1bk1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/4p3/2B1P3/5N2/PPP: Let's have some fun! Knight to g5, threatening a fork on f7
descriptions.r2k1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n1bn2/4p1N1/2B1P3/8/PPP: Black thinks they defended the fork on f7, but they actually didn't. Bishop takes bishop on e6.
descriptions.r2k1b1r/ppp3pp/2n1pn2/4p1N1/4P3/8/PPP2PP: And NOW we fork with knight to f7, winning a rook
descriptions.r4b1N/ppp1k1pp/2n1pn2/4p3/4P3/8/PPP2PPP/: Our knight is trapped but who cares - we won a rook!
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1P: When black plays knight to c6 here, we'll copy them with knight to c3. We'll wait on doing anything on the kingside for now, because we're unsure if we want to play knight to f3 or pawn break on f4.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1P3/2N5/PP: For those who have taken the Vienna Game course, this position will look VERY familiar. That's because we've just transposed into one of my favorite lines from it! From here, we play queen to g4 and attack the now-undefended g7 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n2q2/2b1p3/2B1P1Q1/2N: Black has a double attack on our weak f2 pawn. If we don't defend it, we lose on the spot. That's why we play... knight to d5. Yes that's right we completely ignore the attack and just play knight to d5. Trust me and do it.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2bNp3/2B1P1Q1/8/PP: King to d1 only move. The amazing thing? Black's attack actually stop here. The attack looks scary but there's no real follow-up
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2ppp/2np4/2bNp3/2B1P1Q1/8/PP: Now it's OUR turn to attack. Queen to g7.
descriptions.r3k1nr/ppp2pQp/2npb3/2bNp3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1: Instead of taking the rook, we should actually play knight takes c7, forking the king and the OTHER rook.
descriptions.r5nr/ppNk1pQp/2npb3/2b1p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1q: Instead of taking the other rook, we instead take the bishop! Knight takes bishop on e6. Black cannot capture back because their pawn is pinned.
descriptions.r6r/pp1knpQp/2npN3/2b1p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1qP: Now is a good time to attack the black queen and give her the boot. Knight to h3.
descriptions.r6r/pp1knpQp/2npN3/2b1p3/2B1P3/7N/PPPP1q: This line was one of my favorites from the Vienna Game course. There are a lot of variations, so if you want to dive deeper, definitely check out that courseâafter finishing this one, of course.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/2b1p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1P: Black just copied us - zero points for creativity. Let's punish them with pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/2BbP3/8/PPP2PPP/: We'll play knight to f3 to attack that d4 bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/2BbP3/5N2/PPP2: Let's grab that bishop! Knight takes bishop on d4.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/2BnP3/8/PPP2PPP/: We'll develop our bishop to e3 next, to hit the knight and force it to run away.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/2B1P3/4B3/PPP2: With the dark-squared bishop gone we can play queen to g4 and pose a real threat on g7.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n2q2/4p3/2B1P1Q1/4B3/: Might as well develop our last piece: knight to c3.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2ppp/2n2q2/3pp3/2B1P1Q1/2N1B: Uh oh! Black just forked us - they're attacking our bishop on c4 and our queen on g4. We HAVE to lose one, and honestly, I'd rather lose our bishop. Queen drops down to safety on g3.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2ppp/2n2q2/4p3/2p1P3/2N1B1Q1: OK we're a full bishop down... now what? One move here wins us the game: knight to d5. Now WE'RE the ones forking: we're attacking the queen on f6 and the pawn on c7.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2ppp/2n3q1/3Np3/2p1P3/4B1Q1/: Since the queen moved out of the way, let's take the pawn. Knight takes pawn on c7, leading us to ANOTHER fork of the king and rook.
descriptions.r1bk2nr/ppN2ppp/2n3q1/4p3/2p1P3/4B1Q1/PP: Finally, knight takes rook on a8
descriptions.N1bk2nr/pp3ppp/2n5/4p3/2p1P3/4B1q1/PPP2P: One last thing: before we recapture the queen, we can activate our rook with a queenside castle, checking the black king.
descriptions.N2k2nr/pp1b1ppp/2n5/4p3/2p1P3/4B1q1/PPP2: Nice! Now a simple f-pawn takes queen on g3
descriptions.N2k2nr/pp1b1ppp/2n5/4p3/2p1P3/4B1P1/PPP3: Well done! From here we'll win the game with our 2 point material advantage
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/2B1n3/8/PPP2PP: Sacrifice? Sacrifice!!! Bishop takes pawn on f7. Don't worry, we'll win our piece back on the next move :)
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pppp1kpp/2n5/4P3/4n3/8/PPP2PPP/: Can you spot the tactic to win our piece back? Hint: Queen to d5 check, forking the king and knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp2pp/2n5/3QP3/4n3/8/PPP2PPP/: And now we simply take the knight e4 :)
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp2pp/2n5/4P3/4Q3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Who doesn't love being a pawn up?
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/2BQ4/5N2/PPP2PPP: Black is playing correctly so far. Let's just continue our development with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/2BQ4/2N2N2/PPP: Black attacked our queen, let's move it to h4 to add a bit of pressure on the f6 knight.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppppbppp/2n2n2/8/2B4Q/2N2N2/PPP2: Let's add even MORE pressure to that f6 knight. Bishop to g5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppppbppp/2n2n2/6B1/2B4Q/2N2N2/P: Finally,  let's castle queenside. Our rook will be super powerful along the open d-file.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/6B1/2B4Q/2N2N2/: You can feel how fragile black's position is here. One move and we'll shatter them: bishop to d3, adding a TON of pressure to the h7 pawn.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/6B1/7Q/2NB1N2/P: Black is almost paralyzed. Meanwhile all our pieces are super active and pointed towards his king. That's why from here, we win over 75% of the time!
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3pp3/2BPP3/8/PPP2PP: If we play our cards right, we can force black to lose his right to castle AND mess up his pawn structure. Pawn takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/4P3/2p1P3/8/PPP2PPP: Let's trade queens, forcing black to lose his right to castle.
descriptions.rnbk1b1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/4P3/2p1P3/8/PPP2PPP: Now we win our piece back with pawn takes knight on f6.
descriptions.rnbk1b1r/ppp2p1p/5p2/8/2p1P3/8/PPP2PPP/R: There's a million good moves here. Let's just go for knight to c3.
descriptions.rnbk1b1r/ppp2p1p/5p2/8/2p1P3/2N5/PPP2PPP: Nice! Black can't castle and they have doubled isolated pawns on the f-file. The computer gives us almost a +1 point advantage for that.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/2B1P3/2N5/PP: Now we'll push pawn to d3. Again, we're just waiting for more information before we decide if we want to play knight to f3 or push our pawn to f4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b1p3/2B1P3/2NP4/: Now that black committed their dark-squared bishop to c5, we can put our own dark-squared bishop on g5 and pin black's knight to the queen. Black's dark-squared bishop would have to retreat if black wants to unpin.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/2b1p1B1/2B1P3/2NP: Not only did black do NOTHING to address the pin the knight , how they've locked their dark-squared bishop out so it will NEVER be able to unpin the knight. Well - let's put pressure on the pinned piece: knight to d5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2pp1/2np1n1p/2bNp1B1/2B1P3/3P: We'll take the knight on f6 with our bishop, messing up black's pawn structure.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2p2/2np1p1p/2bNp3/2B1P3/3P4/P: Finally let's develop our knight to e2. You might be asking why e2 and not f3? Well, our knight really has nowhere to go if we put it on f3, and if we put it on e2, we can still play f4 in the future if we want.
Perfectly played! Black's kingside pawn structure is so messed up that we have +0.5 point advantage on the eval bar
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1pp1/2n2n1p/2b1p1B1/2B1P3/2N: We'll want to keep this nasty pin we have on black. Bishop comes back to h4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1p2/2n2n1p/2b1p1p1/2B1P2B/2N: Bishop drops back to g3, of course.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2p2/2np1n1p/2b1p1p1/2B1P3/2NP: It would be great to break up this h6-g5 pawn structure on the right side of the board. Let's play pawn to h4. Ideally black takes our pawn and and we can recapture with the bishop and re-instate our pin.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2p2/2np1n1p/2b1p3/2B1P1pP/2NP: Ah, black didn't take the bait. Let's just push pawn to h5 to make sure black can never push pawn to h5 themselves.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2p2/2np1n1p/2b1p2P/2B1P1p1/2N: Nice! Black's kingside is extremely weak and we have a +1 point eval advantage over our opponent.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/1bB1P3/2NP4/P: Black might be trying to take our knight and damage our pawn structure. Let's develop our g-knight to e2 to make sure that doesn't happen.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/1bB1P3/2NP4/: Nice! Not the craziest line in the bishop's opening, but we made it out with a slight advantage over black.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b1p1B1/2B1P3/2N: Black didn't do anything to address our pin on the knight, which means we put pressure on the pinned piece! Knight to d5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppppbppp/2n2n2/3Np1B1/2B1P3/3P4: Let's snag that bishop! Knight takes bishop on e7.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppppqppp/2n2n2/4p1B1/2B1P3/3P4/P: Finally let's develop our knight to e2. You might be asking why e2 and not f3? Well, our knight really has nowhere to go if we put it on f3, and if we put it on e2, we can still play f4 in the future if we want.
Perfectly played! We have an advantage over black in this game.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/2BpP3/5N2/PPP2: We've transposed to the Scotch Gambit (course coming soon!). The f6 knight is attacking our pawn - let's flip the script with pawn to e5. Now our pawn is attacking the f6 knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/3pP3/2Bp4/5N2/PPP: Black said "you attack my knight? i attack your bishop.". Let's just move our bishop to b5, pinning their c6 knight. Now black has to ACTUALLY address our attack on their f6 knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B1pP3/3pn3/5N2/PPP: Black's center is looking way too strong. Let's play knight takes pawn on d4 to fight back. Our e5 pawn is safe because black's c6 knight is still pinned.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pppb1ppp/2n5/1B1pP3/3Nn3/8/PPP2P: Black's c6 knight is unpinned, and now it's free to take our e5 pawn. Let's just get rid of it before it does any damage. Bishop takes knight on c6
descriptions.r2qkb1r/p1pb1ppp/2p5/3pP3/3Nn3/8/PPP2PPP: Let's castle our king to safety
A perfectly played game from both sides! From here you'll have to play a real game of chess
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/2b5/2BpP3/8/PPP2PPP/: Did someone say sacrifice? Bishop takes pawn on f7. Don't worry - we'll win a bishop back :)
descriptions.rnbq2nr/pppp1kpp/8/2b5/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/RN: OK so how do we win the bishop back? Easy. Queen to h5 check, forking the king and bishop.
descriptions.rnbq2nr/pppp1k1p/6p1/2b4Q/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP: Now we just take the bishop! Queen to c5.
descriptions.r1bq2nr/pppp1k1p/2n3p1/2Q5/3pP3/8/PPP2PP: We reaaaalllyyy want that d4 pawn. Let's add an attacker with knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bq2nr/ppp2k1p/2np2p1/2Q5/3pP3/5N2/PPP2: We'll toss in a check to move our queen to safety before we take that d4 pawn. Queen to d5.
descriptions.r2q2nr/ppp2k1p/2npb1p1/3Q4/3pP3/5N2/PPP2: Game over. Game over. Knight to g5 forking the king and bishop.
descriptions.r2q2nr/ppp1k2p/2npb1p1/3Q2N1/3pP3/8/PPP2: Queen takes e6 and there's literally a mate in 1.
descriptions.r2q2nr/ppp1k2p/2npQ1p1/6N1/3pP3/8/PPP2PP: Mate in 1 after this. You got it :)

shortDescriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Let's continue with the Bishop's Opening

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Let's learn the Caro-Kann! This opening was invented in 1886 by GM Levy Rozman and remains one of the best counter attacks to white playing pawn e4. OK, not all of that is true, but let's start with playing with pawn to c6.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/2p5/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R: White is greedy taking the whole center, now we fight back with pawn to d5. White has a choice here - do they take? Do they push? Or do they ignore?
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3pP3/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/: White chose to push their pawn, bringing us to the caro-kann advanced variation. This is the most popular move by White, probably because they are too scared to take. The truth is they should be scared to play us in general, because we've studied every possible response. Let's play pawn to c5 immediately, trying to destabilize the center.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/8/2PpP3/8/8/PPP2PPP/RNB: White is greedy and took our pawn. Let's immediately attack their weak pawns with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/2PpP3/8/P7/1PP2PPP/: Taking the pawn back on e5 is actually a bit poisonous. Let's continue with our regular play: Pawn to e6, opening up our bishop and giving our knight a way to develop.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/2PpP3/1P6/P7/2P2PP: We still shouldn't take the pawn. Instead, pawn to a5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1p3ppp/2n1p3/pPPpP3/8/P7/2P2PPP: Finally!!! Black made a mistake. NOW we can take the pawn. Knight to e5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1p3ppp/4p3/pPPpn3/8/P7/1BP2PPP/: White's bishop is powerful right now. The best move to fight back is pawn to f6.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1p4pp/4pp2/pPPpB3/8/P7/2P2PPP/R: And we take back of course! Pawn takes on e5
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1p4pp/4p3/pPPpp2Q/8/P7/2P2PPP/R: Oh no a check!!!! Actually white is playing awful here and we have a huge advantage. Let's play pawn to g6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/1p5p/4pnp1/pPPpQ3/8/P7/2P2PPP/R: Well done!! Even though we are down a pawn, We are definitely winning one back soon and our strong center means the computer gives us a 2 or 3 point advantage!!
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/2PpP3/5P2/8/PPP3PP/: This was a very strong response from white, actually. I wouldn't have guessed the next move in a million years. It's knight h6. I'm not going to even try and explain that one to you.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n4n/2PpP3/5P2/2P5/PP4P: White is playing well here. Let's play the classic pawn to e6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1p2n/2PpP3/1P3P2/2P5/P: Now we can fight back against White's strong pawns with pawn to a5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/1p3ppp/2n1p2n/pBPpP3/1P3P2/2P5/: Let's unpin with bishop to d7.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p1b1ppp/2B1p2n/p1PpP3/1P3P2/2P5: Take back of course. Bishop to c6.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p3ppp/2b1p2n/p1PpP3/1P3P2/2P5/P: Because White's king is so weak, the computer gives us a 1 or 2 point advantage from this position.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/8/2ppP3/3P4/2P5/PP3PPP/: White once again rejects taking our pawn, and from here we will win lots of games. Knight to c6 immediately, adding more pressure to the d4 pawn.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/2ppP3/3P4/2P2N2/PP3: We're going to get this position a LOT. Let's slightly clarify the situation with pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3pP3/3P4/5N2/PP3PPP: The d4 pawn is now White's biggest weakness. Our game plan: attack this pawn with everything we have. Let's develop our bishop to g4, pinning the knight to remove a defender of the d4 pawn.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3pP3/3P2b1/5N1P/PP3P: This mindless move from white gives us a huge edge. Bishop takes knight on f3.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3pP3/3P4/5Q1P/PP3PP1: Now we just have knight takes d4, attacking the queen.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/8/3pP3/3n4/3Q3P/PP3PP1/R: Let's bring our knight back to c6.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3pP3/8/3Q3P/PP3PP1/R: Beautiful! We are simply up a pawn.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3pP3/3P4/5P1P/PP3P2/: Let's bring our queen out to b6, adding yet another attacker to the d4 pawn.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp2pppp/1qn5/3pP3/3P4/5P1P/PP3P2/: Well done! White has a really hard time defending their position here.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/2ppP3/3P1P2/2P5/PP4: Has white moved like... a single piece this game? I don't think so. Anyways, pawn takes on d4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3pP3/3P1P2/8/PP4PP/: OK let's play a move you've never played before: pawn to h5. The point is... well the point is pretty complicated. Something about strengthening our light squares yada yada yada. All I know is black wins most of their games when they play pawn to h5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2ppp1/2n5/3pP2p/3P1P2/5N2/PP4: OK let's pin the knight. Bishop to g4.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2ppp1/2n5/3pP2p/3P1Pb1/5N2/PP2: Now that our bishop is developed, we can play pawn to e6.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp3pp1/2n1p3/3pP2p/3P1Pb1/5N2/PP: The last step is to develop our queen to b6.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp3pp1/1qn1p3/3pP2p/3P1Pb1/5N2/PP: Well done! Even though the material is equal, the computer thinks we are better in this position.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1p3ppp/2n1p3/p1PpP3/1P6/P7/1BP2: If they don't take us, we'll take them. Pawn takes on b4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1p3ppp/2n1p3/2PpP3/1P6/8/1BP2PP: And now rook takes rook on a1.
descriptions.2bqkbnr/1p3ppp/2n1p3/2PpP3/1P6/8/2P2PPP/: YES! Now we get our pawn back. Knight takes pawn on b4.
descriptions.2bqkbnr/1p3ppp/4p3/2PpP3/1n6/8/2P2PPP/BN: Well done!! The computer loves our position here, and white bishop is stuck staring at his pawn.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3P4/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/R: This time white decides to take our pawn, taking us into the exchanged variation. Let's take back with pawn to d5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/8/3p4/2PP4/8/PP3PPP/RNB: This is the start of the Panov-Botvinnik Attack. The name doesn't matter, what matters is developing and strengthening the center. Knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/3p4/2PP4/2N5/PP3PPP: Honestly, that d4 pawn looks a bit weak. Let's play pawn to g6, with the idea to place our bishop on g7 on our next move to stare down at that d-pawn.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pp1p/5np1/3p4/2PP4/2N2N2/PP3: We continue with out plan: bishop to g7.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/5np1/3P4/3P4/2N2N2/PP3PP: White wanted to trade pawns? OK. Knight takes back on d5.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/6p1/3n4/2BP4/2N2N2/PP3PP: Our knight is under attack. We can either retreat or trade, and I don't believe in retreating. Knight takes on c3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/6p1/8/2BP4/2P2N2/P4PPP/R: The bishop on c4 is unprotected, and the pawn on c3 is unprotected. We can attack both with queen to c7. White will lose one of them.
descriptions.rnb1k2r/ppq1ppbp/6p1/8/2BP4/2P2N2/P4PPP/: Well done! We are putting serious pressure on White with our queen. The computer thinks we have a better position here.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3pP3/3P2b1/5N2/PP2BP: Let's play pawn to e6. This move opens up our bishop, and also opens up the e7 square for our knight on the next move. Right now our knight is kind of trapped at home.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/3P2b1/5N1P/PP2: This is just a bad move from white, plain and simply. When White plays h3, we take the knight on f3, removing a defender of the d4 pawn.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/3P4/5B1P/PP3PP: Now we get queen to b6, adding another attacker to the d4 pawn. Also kind of cool: queen to b6 is only possible because we moved our c pawn at the start of the game! If we didn't, she would be blocked in. Funny how that works.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/3pP3/3P4/4BB1P/PP3P: White saved one pawn but now loses another. Queen takes b2.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/3P4/4BB1P/Pq1N1: Let's develop our bishop to b4, pinning the knight to the king.
descriptions.r3k1nr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/1b1P4/4BB1P/Pq1: Well done! We are up a pawn and have a very playable position.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/1BppP3/3P4/2P5/PP3P: White pins our knight? Let's pin White's pawn. Queen to a5. Now White has to decide what to do with their bishop.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pp2pppp/2B5/q1ppP3/3P4/2P5/PP3P: Of course we take back. Pawn takes on c6.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/p3pppp/2p5/q1ppP3/3P4/2P5/PP1B1: White is threatening a discovered attack on our queen. We need to retreat, while still keeping the defense of our c5 pawn. Let's do so with queen to b6.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/p3pppp/1qp5/2ppP3/3P4/2P5/PP1B1: Well done! We are better in this position. And we have ideas of bishop to a6 in the future.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p4/3PP3/2N5/PPP2PP: If White doesn't move their pawn, then fine, we'll take them instead. Pawn takes on e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/8/3PN3/8/PPP2PPP/R1: Let's develop the knight with knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/2p2n2/8/3P4/6N1/PPP2PPP: White declined taking our knight. Let's send a pawn up to ask him why. Pawn to h5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2ppp1/2p2n2/7p/3P3P/6N1/PPP2P: With White's h-pawn out of the way, we can target White's queen with bishop to g4.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp2ppp1/2p2n2/7p/3P2bP/6N1/PPP1: Now our tried & true pawn to e6 to open up our bishop.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp3pp1/2p1pn2/7p/3P2bP/5NN1/PPP: Let's develop our bishop to d6, attacking White's the very unstable kingside.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pp3pp1/2pbpn2/7p/3P2bP/5NN1/PPP1: Well done! We are threatening to take White's knight and double his pawns. The computer is giving us the edge in this position.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/3P2b1/5N2/PP2B: Let's starting routing our knight to his new home. First, knight to e7.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp2nppp/2n1p3/3pP3/3P2b1/2N2N2/P: Then, knight to f5. Now we are putting even more pressure on that weak d4 pawn.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pPn2/3P2b1/2N1BN2/: Dang, White really wants to defend that pawn. Their bishop has turned into a glorified pawn now. Let's continue developing, putting our bishop on his home on e7.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2bppp/2n1p3/3pPn2/3P2b1/P1N1BN: Well done! We have a good position here.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2ppp1/2p2n2/7p/3P4/5NN1/PPP2P: Our pawn continues! Pawn to h4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2ppp1/2p2n2/8/3P3p/5N2/PPP1NP: Finally let's put our bishop on g4.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp2ppp1/2p2n2/8/3P2bp/5N2/PPP1N: Well done! Black wins most games from this position.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/2ppP3/3P4/2P1B3/PP3:
Our mission: attack that bishop. 
Our method: use our king's knight.
Our first step: knight to h6 to eventually go to f5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n4B/2ppP3/3P4/2P5/PP3P: White took our knight to double up our pawns. We really have no choice. Pawn takes bishop on h6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pp1p/2n4p/2ppP3/3P4/2P2N2/PP: Now the always fun queen to b6.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp2pp1p/1qn4p/2ppP3/3P4/2P2N2/P: Well done! We have a ton of threats on white and it'll be hard for our opponent to deal with them. Black wins over 60% of the time from this position.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/8/3p4/3P4/3B4/PPP2PPP/R: This is a sharp line from white. Let's exploit the fact that his pawn is unprotected with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/3p4/3P4/2PB4/PP3PPP: Let's continue with the other knight. Knight to f6. This will also allow us to develop our bishop to g4 in the future.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/3p4/3P4/2PB3P/PP3: White wasted some time there trying to thwart our bishop. Let's go aggressive with pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/2n2n2/3pP3/8/2PB3P/PP3PP: And now we take with the knight. Knight to e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/5n2/3pn3/8/2PB3P/PP3PP1/: Well done! We have a good position and are ready to continue our game.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/3P4/3P4/8/PP3PPP/RN: If White wants to trade, we trade. Knight takes back on d5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/8/3n4/3P4/2N5/PP3PPP/R1: Let's continue developing and apply a bit of pressure on the center with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n5/3n4/3P4/2N2N2/PP3PP: Let's continue with bishop to f5, piercing through White's queenside.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp2pppp/2n5/3n1b2/2BP4/2N2N2/PP3: We have two attackers on our knight. Let's defend with pawn to e6.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3n1b2/2BP4/2N2N2/PP: Well done! We have a solid position here.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/3p4/3P1B2/2PB4/PP: Remember we developed the knight so we can put the bishop on g4. Well let's do that! Bishop to g4.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/3p4/3P1Bb1/1QPB4/P: White escaped, and is now threatening our b7 pawn. Let's defend with queen to d7.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp1qpppp/2n2n2/3p4/3P1Bb1/1QPB4/P: The last piece we need to develop is the bishop. Let's play pawn to e6 to open it up.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp1q1ppp/2n1pn2/3p4/3P1Bb1/1QPB1N: White's dark-square bishop is better than ours. Let's go for a trade with bishop to d6.
descriptions.r3k2r/pp1q1ppp/2nBpn2/3p4/3P2b1/1QPB1N2/: Now queen takes back on d6.
descriptions.r4rk1/pp3ppp/2nqpn2/3p4/3P2b1/1QPB1N2/PP: Well done navigating the caro kann main line!! Proud of you.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/1BPpP3/8/8/PPP2PPP/: Let's switch our focus to attacking the other pawn with pawn to e6. This opens up our bishop to attack the c5 pawn, and gives our knight a path for developing.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/1BPpP3/1P6/8/P1P2P: White is trying to stabilize their pawn, so let's destabilize. Pawn to a5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1p3ppp/2n1p3/pBPpP3/1P6/2P5/P4P: And now pawn takes b4, opening up our rook.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1p3ppp/2n1p3/1BPpP3/1P6/8/P4PPP: Last thing: let's unpin our selves with bishop to d7. Now that the knight is unpinned, the pawn on b4 is technically under attack.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/1p1b1ppp/2B1p3/2PpP3/1P6/8/P4PPP: And we take back. Bishop takes c6.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/1p3ppp/2b1p3/2PpP3/1P6/8/P4PPP/R: Well done! We'll continue with our regular development from here.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/2p2N2/8/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/R: If White takes our knight we enter a very fun line. First step, we take back with our e-pawn! e-pawn takes on f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/2p2p2/8/3P4/2P5/PP3PPP/R: Let's develop our bishop with a plan to castle kingside. Bishop to d6.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/2pb1p2/8/3P4/2PB4/PPQ2PP: White is threatening some annoying stuff with their queen and bishop pointed at h7. Let's throw in a check before we do anything else. Rook to e8.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3ppp/2pb1p2/8/3P4/2PB4/PPQ1NP: OK let's stop our pawn from getting captured with pawn to h5.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pp1/2pb1p2/7p/3P4/2PBB3/PPQ1: White developed their bishop because they are going to castle queenside. When players castle on opposite sides, that means a war is brewing. Let's play knight to d7.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp1n1pp1/2pb1p2/7p/3P4/2PBB3/PP: One last thing before the war breaks out: knight to f8. This protects the crucial h7 square. As they say: "Knight on f8, never mate"
descriptions.r1bqrnk1/pp3pp1/2pb1p2/7p/3P4/2PBB3/PPQ1: Well done! The positions are equal and we are ready to play a fantastic game of chess. Everything we did was theory by the way: this exact position has been reached a hundred thousand times!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/8/3p4/3P4/5N2/PPP2PPP/R: Let's copy white with knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/3p4/3P4/3B1N2/PPP2P: With white developing their bishop so early, we have the opportunity to pin the knight. Bishop pins the knight on g4.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/3p4/3P2b1/3B1N2/PPP: Let's get our other knight into the game and attack the now-undefended pawn on d4. Knight to c6.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/3p4/3P2b1/2PB1N2/P: Now we want our other bishop in the game. Let's open it up with pawn to e6.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1pn2/3p4/3P2b1/2PB1N1P/: We should keep the pin and drop our bishop back to h5.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1pn2/3p2Bb/3P4/2PB1N1P/: The best move here is bishop to d6.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp3ppp/2nbpn2/3p2Bb/3P4/2PB1N1P/P: Let's force White's bishop back with pawn to h6.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp3pp1/2nbpn1p/3p3b/3P3B/2PB1N1P/: And now the key: Queen to c7, setting up a battery.
descriptions.r3k2r/ppq2pp1/2nbpn1p/3p3b/3P3B/2PB1N1P/: Well done! The computer likes our position here, and  black wins something like 60% of the time from this position.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n4n/2PpP3/5P2/5N2/PPP3: As usual, when the knight comes out we want to pin him. Bishop to g4
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp2pppp/2n4n/2PpP3/5Pb1/4BN2/PPP: Ah now we see the point of our knight on h6. We can hop into f5 to attack the bishop. OK that wasn't so hard.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp2pppp/2n5/2PpPn2/5Pb1/5N2/PPP2: White's pawns are looking a little too stable. Let's cause some chaos with pawn to g5.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp2pp1p/2n5/2PpPnP1/6b1/5N2/PPP2: Now look at this cool move. With 1 pawn push we will attack 2 undefended pawns. Pawn to e6.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp3p1p/2n1p3/2PpPnP1/6b1/5N2/PPP: That was cool! Now our queen looks at the pawn on g5 and the bishop looks at the pawn on c5. We are going to get our material back!
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/2PpP3/8/5N2/PPP2PPP: White wants to defend their pawns, but we won't make it so easy for them. Bishop to g4.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/1BPpP3/6b1/5N2/PPP2P: Let's toss in a check with queen to a5.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/qBPpP3/6b1/2N2N2/PPP2: Now we can play pawn to e6. This stabilizes our center, opens up our bishop to attack the pawn on c5, and gives our knight a path to develop.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/qBPpP3/6b1/2N2N2/PPP: Well done! We have a chess game ahead of us.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1pn2/3p2B1/3P2b1/2PB1N2: Let's unpin ourselves with bishop to e7.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2bppp/2n1pn2/3p2B1/3P2b1/2PB1N: White set up a battery on our h7 pawn. Let's push it to h6 so it doesn't get taken.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2bpp1/2n1pn1p/3p4/3P2bB/2PB1N2: Now let's go rook to c8 - it may not be attacking the queen just yet but give it a few moves and you'll be glad you did it.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp2bpp1/2n1pn1p/3p4/3P2bB/2PB1N2: Well done! The position is equal and we are ready to play!
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp2bppp/2n1p3/3pPn2/3P2b1/2N1BN1P: Now we take the knight! The knight is one of the last defenders of that weak d4 pawn, so we are very happy to remove it. Bishop takes f3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp2bppp/2n1p3/3pPn2/3P4/2N1BB1P/P: Let's take a moment to castle here.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2bppp/2n1p3/3pPn2/3P4/2N1BB1P/: We have one pawn-break in our pocket, and now is a good time to use it. Pawn to f6.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2b1pp/2n1pP2/3p1n2/3P4/2N1BB1P: White took! Which means we can play bishop to f6, adding yet ANOTHER attacker to the weak d4 pawn.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp4pp/2n1pb2/3p1n2/3P4/2N1BB1P/P: Well done! This is a great position to play as black. All our pieces are aligned towards White's biggest weakness.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2B1p3/2PpP3/8/8/PPP2PPP/: Let's take back of course. Pawn takes on c6.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/p4ppp/2p1p3/2PpP3/1P6/8/P1P2PPP: Very common move in this type of position: pawn to a5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/5ppp/2p1p3/p1PpP3/1P6/2P5/P4PPP: And then we take with pawn to b4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/5ppp/2p1p3/2PpP3/1P6/8/P4PPP/RN: Now the very fun queen to h4. The point is we are attacking the b4 pawn, but also have some tricky checks up our sleeve.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/5ppp/2p1p3/2PpP3/1P5q/8/P2B1PPP: Now for our tricky check: queen to e4 forking the king, the g2 pawn, AND the e5 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/5ppp/2p1p3/2PpP3/1P2q3/8/P2BQPP: Do NOT trade queens here. Queen to g2.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/5ppp/2p1p3/2PpP3/1P6/5Q2/P2B1Pq: And now our queen retreats to g6.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/5ppp/2p1p1q1/2PpP3/1P6/5Q2/P2B1: Well done! We are doing great here! Look how weak and exposed White's king is. There is nowhere for him to hide. As long as we keep our queen on the board, White has problems. Meanwhile, all our pawns are connected and coordinated
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp2pppp/2n4n/2PpP3/5Pb1/5N2/PPP1: Now our favorite move; pawn to e6, opening up an attack on the undefended c5 pawn.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1p2n/2PpP3/5Pb1/4BN2/PP: Now knight to f5, hitting the bishop.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1p3/2PpPn2/5Pb1/4BN2/PP: Well done! Black wins most of their games from this position.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/2p2p2/8/3P4/5N2/PPP2PPP/: Knight to f3 is a slow move. Let's develop our bishop and prepare to castle. Bishop to d6.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/2pb1p2/8/3P4/3B1N2/PPP2P: Now we should take the open file with our rook. Rook to e8.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3ppp/2pb1p2/8/3P4/3B1N1P/PPP2: Our next plan is to route our knight all the way to the king. Every marathon starts with a step. Knight to d7.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp1n1ppp/2pb1p2/8/3P4/2PB1N1P/P: Second step of our marathon: Knight to f8.
descriptions.r1bqrnk1/pp3ppp/2pb1p2/8/3P4/2PB1N1P/PP3: OK turns out the marathon was only two steps. Black wins something like 60% of the time from this position. Good luck!
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pp1/2pb1p2/7p/3P4/2PB4/PPQ1N: White castled directly into our pawn. Interesting. Let's push our pawn forward to h4.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pp1/2pb1p2/8/3P3p/2PB3P/PPQ1: Now let's develop our knight and bring him over to help defend our king. Knight to d7.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp1n1pp1/2pb1p2/8/3P3p/2PBB2P/P: And the knight completes his journey with knight to f8
descriptions.r1bqrnk1/pp3pp1/2pb1p2/8/3P3p/2PBB2P/PPQ: Well done! The stage is set and the game can begin!
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/1BPpP3/8/4B3/PPP2P: OK now let's develop and route our knight as planned. Knight to e7.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2nppp/2n1p3/1BPpP3/8/2P1B3/PP: And now the knight ends up on his home on f5, attacking the bishop.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1p3/1BPpPn2/3B4/2P5/PP: White plays that move 90% of the time. If we take, we help their pawn structure, so we wont take. Instead, let's unpin our king with bishop to d7.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp1b1ppp/2n1p3/1BPpPn2/3B4/2P5/P: Well done! We have a solid position position and are ready to finish developing and castle.
