descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the Danish Gambit! You will sacrifice a pawn, and then another one, and then ANOTHER one. Yes, a 3 pawn sacrifice in your first 4 moves. In return you'll get a huge attack on your opponent. Let's begin with moving the King's pawn to e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Now for pawn sacrifice #1. Pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB: Remember, these are sacrifices! So we don't take back. Now for pawn sacrifice #2, pawn to c3.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/4P3/2p5/PP3PPP/RNB: Now for pawn sacrifice #3: bishop to c4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/2B1P3/8/Pp3PPP/RNB: OK, we lost 3 pawns in 4 moves. This is like shooting yourself in the foot 3 times at the start of a marathon. But it turns out that when played right, our foot with holes in it is faster than our opponent's. Bishop takes b2, setting up 2 extremely powerful bishops along the diagonals, piercing our opponent's position..
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/8/1bB1P3/8/PB3PPP/RN: Black is giving us a check right away. Let's use it as an excuse to develop another piece with knight to c3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/1bB1P3/2N5/PB3PPP: Now we get to set up a powerful attack. Queen to b3 both attacks Black's bishop and sets up a battery on the f7 pawn.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/1bB1P3/1QN5/PB3P: Um, hello? Black just hung their bishop. Queen takes on b4.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppppqppp/8/8/1bB1P3/2N5/PB3PPP/: OK this is going to sound crazy but let's play yet another gambit. Let's develop our knight from g1 to e2 losing our e4 pawn.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/pppp1ppp/8/8/1bB1q3/2N5/PB2NPPP: Now we can play queen b3, attacking Black's bishop and setting up our strong battery.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/pppp1ppp/8/8/2B1q3/1Qb5/PB2NPPP: In this case, let's take with our bishop to keep the threat on both the f7 and g7 pawns.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/pppp1ppp/6q1/8/2B5/1QB5/P3NPPP/: This is just a brutal position for Black. Take a moment and look at the board. All our pieces are out, and pointed directly at Black's weakest pawns. From here, we can simply castle kingside.

How does Black even play this position? It is impossible. The computer thinks that despite being a few pawns down, our position is so good we actually have a +3 point advantage. White wins over 80% of the time from here.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/2B1P3/8/PB3PPP/R: Black is trying to catch up in development. Let's not let them. Pawn to e5 kicking away the knight.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3pP3/2B5/8/PB3PPP/R: This was Black's only move. Let's take their knight with pawn to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5P2/8/2p5/8/PB3PPP/RN1Q: OK now we trade queens! Queen takes d8. This makes black lose the right to castle.
descriptions.rnbk1b1r/ppp2ppp/5P2/8/2p5/8/PB3PPP/RN2K: Let's continue with our pawn attack. Pawn takes g7.
descriptions.rnbk3r/ppp2pbp/8/8/2p5/8/PB3PPP/RN2K1NR: Black totally forgot about our bishop on b2! Bishop takes g7 and the game is essentially over.
descriptions.rnbk2r1/ppp2pBp/8/8/2p5/8/P4PPP/RN2K1NR: Let's toss in a check because why not. Bishop to f6 check.
descriptions.rnbk2r1/ppp2p1p/5B2/8/2p5/8/P4PPP/RN2K1N: Black's position is just destroyed. No two-ways around it. Good job.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4P2n/2B5/8/PB3PPP/RN: A blunder from black! Can you find the best move? Hint: Queen takes h5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4P2Q/2B5/8/PB3PPP/RN: Well done! Black really did not want to move their knight back, and for that they just lost the piece altogether.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/2B1P3/1Qb5/PB3PPP: Black took our knight, so it's best to take back with our queen here, setting up a strong attack on the dark squares. Queen takes c3.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/2B1P3/2Q5/PB3PPP: Let's continue developing with knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/2B1P3/2Q2N2/PB: Now is a good time to castle kingside ourselves.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/2B1n3/2Q2N2/PB3P: Checkmate in 1: can you find it? Yup, it's queen to g7.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppppqppp/5n2/4P3/2B5/8/PB3PPP/R: Black tried to be sneaky by pinning our pawn to our king, but this is actually a big mistake. Our queen can copy our opponent's queen, moving to e2 and breaking the pin.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppppqppp/8/4P3/2B5/8/PB2QPPP/RN: Take a breath and look at Black's position here. They have no pawns out, no pieces out, and they're completely boxed in. Our position is absolutely suffocating them. From here, let's get even more development with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppppqppp/2n5/4P3/2B5/2N5/PB2QPP: Poor Black... they do not deserve what is happening to them. Knight to d5, attacking the queen.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/3NP3/2B5/8/PB2QPPP: And now yet ANOTHER brilliant sacrifice: knight to f6. This game is crazy.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1p1p/2n2p2/4P3/2B5/8/PB2QPP: Now we take back with pawn to f6 with discovered check! Unreal.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppppnp1p/2n2P2/8/2B5/8/PB2QPPP/: No hesitation - we just take the knight here with our pawn. Pawn to e7.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppppqp1p/2n5/8/2B5/8/PB2QPPP/R3: That rook is ours! Bishop takes h8.
descriptions.r1b1kb1B/ppppqp1p/2n5/8/2B5/8/P3QPPP/R3K: Black is not having fun right now.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/5P2/3p4/1bB5/8/PB3PPP/RN: Here we should actually defend with our bishop, not our knight, forcing black to capture us. Bishop to c3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/5P2/3p4/2B5/2b5/P4PPP/RN: And we take back with our knight to c3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/5P2/8/2p5/2N5/P4PPP/R2QK: We don't even need to trade queens here. Let's play pawn takes g7 first.
descriptions.rnb1k2r/ppp2pPp/8/8/2p5/2N5/P4PPP/R2qK1N: Aaaaand now we will win. This was a huge mistake from black. By trading queens, we get our rook to the open file with rook takes d1. What's coming next is a brutal fork.
descriptions.rnb1k1r1/ppp2pPp/8/8/2p5/2N5/P4PPP/3RK1N: Now knight to d5, threatening a fork on c7 AND a fork on f6.
descriptions.r1b1k1r1/ppp2pPp/n7/3N4/2p5/8/P4PPP/3RK1: Finally, we get knight to f6, forking the opponent's king and rook.
descriptions.r1b3N1/ppp1kpPp/n7/8/2p5/8/P4PPP/3RK1NR: Not much else to say here except black is completely destroyed.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppppbp1p/2n2P2/8/2B5/8/PB2QPPP/: And we take again! Pawn takes e7, attacking the queen.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppppqp1p/2n5/8/2B5/8/PB2QPPP/R3: Did you forget about our bishop? Our opponent did. Now we have the killer bishop takes h8, winning us a rook for absolutely free.
descriptions.r1b1k1nB/ppppqp1p/2n5/8/2B5/8/P3QPPP/R3K: Wow wow wow. We sacrificed 3 pawns and a knight and won all of it back and MORE. Good job.
descriptions.rnb1k3/ppp2prp/8/3N4/2p5/8/P4PPP/3RK1NR: Black can take our pawn, that is totally fine. We are much more interested in knight to c7, forking the opponent's king and rook.
descriptions.rnb1k3/ppN2prp/8/8/2p5/8/P4PPP/3RK1NR b: Well done. We are winning the opponent's rook and also the game.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP: Black has declined our gambit, but they did so poorly. Let's play pawn to d5, attacking their knight.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppppnppp/8/3Pp3/4P3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Now let's continue following basic opening principles with developing our knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppppnppp/8/3Pp3/4P3/5N2/PPP2PPP: Well done! We will continue developing, castling, and have ourselves a good game!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/4P3/2Pp4/PP3PPP/RN: Black is too scared, and they are giving back the pawn. Fine, let's take it. Bishop takes d3.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/4P3/2PB4/PP3PPP/RN: Well done! We'll continue developing and castle kingside.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/R: Black is just ignoring taking us, and they are counter offering a center pawn. Let's take with pawn takes d5.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/8/PP3PPP/RN: Let's defend our pawn with knight to f3.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/5N2/PP3PPP/: Well done! Black declined our gambit in this line. Our plan here is to just continue developing and castle king-side. You got this!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/2B1P3/8/PB3PPP/RN: Black played the top computer move. Here, we should recapture with the bishop with bishop takes d5. We don't want to take with the pawn, because it blocks our bishop, and we don't want to take with the queen because that would result in a queen trade which is not what we want in a gambit. So, bishop takes d5 is the move.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3B4/4P3/8/PB3PPP/RN: Black is putting us in a tough position to be honest. Here, I recommend sacrificing your bishop on f7 with check.
descriptions.rnbq1b1r/ppp2kpp/5n2/8/4P3/8/PB3PPP/RN1Q: Now we play queen takes d8. Unfortunately, we have not ACTUALLY won a queen because black has a way to win ours back.
descriptions.rnbQ3r/ppp2kpp/5n2/8/1b2P3/8/PB3PPP/RN2K: Yup, because black checked us and discovered an attack on our queen, Black is winning our queen back. From here, we can actually be a little clever. Let's play queen d2. We are still losing our queen, but this trick will let us keep the right to castle.
descriptions.rnb4r/ppp2kpp/5n2/8/4P3/8/PB1b1PPP/RN2K1: And now we play knight takes d2. We have kept our right to castle and even gotten some development out of this.
descriptions.rnb4r/ppp2kpp/5n2/8/4P3/8/PB1N1PPP/R3K1N: Well done! Black played perfectly against our opening and we managed to make it all the way to an endgame where we have a slight advantage. Good luck!
descriptions.rnbk3r/ppp2pPp/8/8/1bp5/8/PB3PPP/RN2K1NR: Let's block check with knight to c3.
descriptions.rnbk2r1/ppp2pPp/8/8/1bp5/2N5/PB3PPP/R3K1: OK our pawn is under attack. Remember that our pawn is our biggest asset right now - it is 1 square away from becoming a queen. To save it we have a beautiful move: castle queenside, checking our opponent.
descriptions.rn1k2r1/pppb1pPp/8/8/1bp5/2N5/PB3PPP/2KR: Now that our king is unpinned, we can play knight to d5 attacking Black's bishop and re-defending our g7 pawn with our own bishop.
descriptions.rn1k2r1/pppb1pPp/8/3N4/1bp5/8/PB3PPP/2KR: Well done! This is an absolutely beautiful position for us. We have a safe king, more development, and a pawn that is a huge asset 1 square from becoming a queen.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/8/2B1P3/2Q2N2/PB: Let's move our f-rook over to e1. Our plan is to move both rooks to the center of the board.

Black played against us perfectly, but we aren't doing too bad. We have more development. We have a pawn in the center. We have a killer battery. This position looks really really good for us and White wins something like 60% of the time from here.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the English! Instead of pushing our central pawns, we umm... we push our non-central pawns. It's the greatest breakthrough in chess since en passant! To start, we push our c-pawn to c4
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppppppp/5n2/8/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP/R: As always, we are going to put our knight on c3 behind our c4 pawn, making sure black can never go to d5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/4pn2/8/2P5/2N5/PP1PPPP: Black is walking into some very dangerous territory. We can play pawn to e4 and enter something called the "Mikenas-Carls" variation. If they don't play PERFECTLY from here on out, we'll win the game. You'll see what I mean in a second. Pawn to e4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/4pn2/8/1bP1P3/2N5/PP1P1: BOOM! Black just made a HUGE MISTAKE. Notice how the black bishop just left the defense of the g7 pawn? We'll punish them for that. First things first: we need to get the f6 knight out of the way. Let's play pawn to to e5
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/4pn2/4P3/2P5/2b5/PP1P1P: That's fine. B-pawn takes bishop on c3 and we're still threatening the knight on f6.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/4p3/4P3/2P1n3/2P5/P2P1P: Beautiful. Can you find the fork? Yup, queen to g4 forking the e4 knight and the g7 pawn. Black can't save them both...
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/4p3/4P1n1/2P3Q1/2P5/P2P: ...well looks like black can TRY to save them both. But a simple pawn to h4 and black is 100% losing a knight.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/4p3/4P1n1/2P3QP/2P5/P2P: Well done! We're winning that knight :D
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP/R: The name of the game is to attack the d5 square. Let's do it again with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/2P5/2N5/PP1PPP: We'll continue with developing our knight to f3, adding a bit of pressure to the e5 pawn.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b1p3/2P5/2N2N2/PP: Ooooooh. Now we can play one of my favorite moves in chess: Knight takes pawn on e5, SACRIFICING our knight. Don't worry, we'll win him back.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/2b1n3/2P5/2N5/PP1PPP: Can you spot how we'll win the knight back? With a pawn fork! Pawn to d4 forks blacks bishop and knight. This is a super common tactic that shows up in a bunch of openings, so keep your eye out :D
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/2b5/2nP4/2N5/PP2PPPP: And of course, pawn takes bishop on c5. We have to win back our material.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/2P5/2n5/2N5/PP2PPPP/: Nice! Even though material is equal, black's knight is so misplaced that the computer gives us a +2 point advantage.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/4p3/2P5/2N5/PP1PPP: Now that the d5 square is covered, we can attack the e5 pawn. Knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/2P5/2N2N2/PP: We've entered the Four Knights English. It's called the four knights english because the first time it was played was in England over the course of four nights. From here, we play pawn to e3 with hopes of playing pawn to d4 next.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/1bP5/2N1PN2/P: Black is threatening to take our knight and mess up our pawn structure. Honestly, its a valid threat. We should move our queen to c2 so that if black ever takes our knight, we can just recapture with the queen.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/4p3/1bP5/2N1PN2/P: I like the idea of planting our knight in the center, just to be a little annoying... Knight to d5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2np4/3np3/1bP5/4PN2/PPQP: HUGE mistake! Black just lost the game. First, we capture back with pawn takes knight on d5. Black HAS to move their knight on c6 out of the way.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp1nppp/3p4/3Pp3/1b6/4PN2/PPQP1: Now we can win a bishop. Do you spot the tactic? That's right, queen to a4 forking the king and bishop
descriptions.r2qk2r/pppbnppp/3p4/3Pp3/Qb6/4PN2/PP1P1P: Then queen takes bishop on b4 :)
descriptions.r2qk2r/pppbnppp/3p4/3Pp3/1Q6/4PN2/PP1P1P: You just won yourself a free bishop :D
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3p4/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP/R: Woahhh. The whole POINT of the english opening is to stop black from playing pawn to d5 and black just... did it anyway? Well, obviously we are going to capture it. No d5 allowed! Pawn takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3q4/8/8/PP1PPPPP/RNB: This is kinda like playing against the Scandinavian Defense (i have a course on that too) but its actually WAY better for white since we have both our central pawns. Let's play knight to c3 next, gaining a tempo on that queen.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/8/8/2N5/PP1PPPPP/R1B: This position looks like the beginning of a chess game, except way better for us because we've already developed a knight and black is missing a central pawn. Let's stop black from developing their last central pawn with knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/8/8/2N2N2/PP1PPPPP: Now we can start developing OUR central pawns. Pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/3P4/2N2N2/PP2PPP: And let's develop the other one too. Pawn to e4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/1b1PP3/2N2N2/PP3P: Black has pinned our knight, which means our e4 pawn is no longer defended. The best move here is to develop our bishop and re-defend our pawn, with bishop to d3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/1b1PP3/2NB1N2/PP3: Our development and our center are soooo much better than black's. Even with equal material, the computer is giving us a +1.3 point advantage. Awesome job!
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pppp1ppp/4p3/4P3/1bP5/2N5/PP1P1: OK so how do we punish black's huge mistake of abandoning the g7 pawn? Simple! By attacking the g7 pawn with queen to g4.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pppp1ppp/4p3/4P3/1bP3Q1/2N5/PP1: Beautiful! Black has a few ways to save the g7 pawn, but they all come at a cost of pawn structure or development. The computer loves our position so much that we get a +1.3 point advantage.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/2P1P3/2N5/PP1P: Black was a little too slow to take the center. Now we can push our pawn to e5 and attack the knight.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppn1ppp/4p3/3pP3/2P5/2N5/PP1P1: NOW we take the pawn on d5. It's important that we do this after we chase away the knight. Pawn takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4p3/3Pn3/8/2N5/PP1P1PPP: Once again, we take the center and attack the knight with our pawn - pawn to d4!
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4p1n1/3P4/3P4/2N5/PP3PP: Now that the knight is gone, its a good time to undouble our pawns. Pawn takes pawn on e6.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/4b1n1/8/3P4/2N5/PP3PPP/: Can you follow the pattern? Attack a piece. Take a pawn. Attack a piece. Take a pawn. We just took a pawn, so now we attack a piece. Pawn to d5.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/4b1n1/3P4/8/2N5/PP3PPP/: Nice!! We have a solid space advantage over black. The eval bar says +0.8 for us.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp2pp/8/4pp2/2P5/2N5/PP1PPPPP: Black is charging right at us with no fear!! The best defense is offense. Let's charge right back with pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp2pp/8/5p2/2PPp3/2N5/PP2PPPP: Black declined trading pawns, and is taking up even MORE space. The good news for us? They left a perfect hole on f4 for our dark-squared bishop. Now we're way ahead in development.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp2pp/5n2/5p2/2PPpB2/2N5/PP2P: Now that our dark-square bishop is developed, we can play pawn to e3 and turn our focus to king-side development.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp2pp/5n2/5p2/2PPpB2/2N1P3/PP: Nice! Our center is stronger and we have more development than black. The computer gives us a +1 point advantage.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/1bP5/2N5/PP1PPPP: It's probably a little early for black to bring out their bishop. We can attack it with knight to d5.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/2bNp3/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP: Black is insisting on putting the bishop in the center - which means we can punish him again! Pawn to e3 with the idea to push pawn to d4 next.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pp1p1ppp/2p5/2bNp3/2P5/4P3/PP1P: Honestly, trading our knight for black's bishop is totally worth it. Who doesn't love the bishop pair? Pawn to d4, sacrificing our knight to win the bishop.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pp1p1ppp/8/2bpp3/2PP4/4P3/PP3PP: Pawn takes bishop, of course - evening out the material.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pp1p1ppp/8/2Ppp3/2P5/4P3/PP3PPP: Well done! Our bishop pair gives us a +1 eval advantage
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/2b1p3/2P5/2N5/PP1PPP: Black got greedy with their bishop by putting it in the center - time to chase it around! We can play pawn to e3 now, then pawn to d4 on next move to send it running.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/2b1p3/2P5/2N1P3/PP1: That move didn't change anything! We still play pawn to d4 to knock around the bishop.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/2b5/2Pp4/2N1P3/PP3P: Recapture with our pawn, of course. Pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/2b5/2PP4/2N5/PP3PPP: Well done! Now we have 2 pawns in the center while black has 0 - and they also have to spend a turn moving their bishop.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppppp1p/5np1/8/2P5/2N5/PP1PPPP: Black is trying to make space for their bishop on g7. That's... honestly a pretty good idea. Let's copy them with pawn to g3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppppppbp/5np1/8/2P5/2N3P1/PP1PPP: And we continue copying! Bishop to g2.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppppppbp/5np1/8/2P5/2N3P1/PP1PP: Theres a million good moves for us here... let's just go for pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PP4/2N3P1/PP: Black is setting up an attack on the d4 pawn we just pushed. Let's add a defender to it with knight to f3. This also lets us castle on the next move :)
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppnppbp/3p1np1/8/2PP4/2N2NP1/P: Well done!! We are slightly ahead in evaluation and winrate
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppp1p/6p1/8/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP/R: Black wants to fianchetto their bishop on g7. As always, we put our knight behind our pawn. Knight to c3.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppppppbp/6p1/8/2P5/2N5/PP1PPPPP: We've entered the English Opening: Great Snake Variation. No reason you need to know that, I just thought the name was cool. From here, we'll actually copy black and fianchetto our OWN bishop. Pawn to g3, to prepare bishop to g2.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp1ppbp/3p2p1/8/2P5/2N3P1/PP1P: We continue our plan to fianchetto: bishop to g2.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2P5/2N3P1/PP1P: Let's keep developing with knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2P5/2N2NP1/PP: Well done! That's what I like to see :) It's a symmetrical game, and you'll play on from here.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/2p5/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP/R: Black copied us, taking us into the symmetrical english variation. Let's continue with our regular stuff: knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1ppppp/2n5/2p5/2P5/2N5/PP1PPP: Huh... black is still copying us... Whatever, let's keep going with pawn to g3 to put our bishop on g2.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1ppp1p/2n3p1/2p5/2P5/2N3P1/PP: What the... HEY BLACK STOP COPYING US. Bishop to g2.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pp1pppbp/2n3p1/2p5/2P5/2N3P1/PP:
BLACK!!!!! STOP STEALING OUR MOVES!!!!! ASDGADSGefadsvad
Just develop our knight to f3
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1pppbp/2n2np1/2p5/2P5/2N2NP1/P: im done. i quit. black isn't even playing the game. they just COPY US BLINDLY. No. You know what? Let's play a move they CANT copy. Pawn to d4. GOOD LUCK TRYING TO DO THAT BLACK
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1pppbp/2n2np1/8/2Pp4/2N2NP1/PP: Phew. Hey, sorry, I think I lost my cool there for a second. Let's take the pawn back with knight to d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp1pppbp/2n2np1/8/2PN4/2N3P1/PP: OK not to be a hypocrite but let's copy black and castle.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/2p5/8/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP/R: OK we usually play knight to c3, but in this case and ONLY this case, we actually play knight to f3. It's annoying to remember, I know.  Someone should make a website to help you practice....
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p4/2P5/5N2/PP1PPPP: Our pawn is under attack! Let's defend it by uncovering our bishop with pawn to e3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/2p2n2/3p4/2P5/4PN2/PP1P: Ok NOW we can finally put our knight on c3. This whole opening felt wrong with our knight still on b2. I'm glad we could finally put him on his rightful place.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp2pppp/2p2n2/3p4/2P3b1/2N1PN2/: The black bishop used to defend the b7 pawn, but now it's pinning our knight to our queen. We can turn the tables: by moving the queen to b3, now it's no longer in a pin AND its attacking the b7 pawn.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp2pppp/1qp2n2/3p4/2P3b1/1QN1PN2: Now that our knight isn't pinned, we can play knight to e5 to attack the g4 bishop
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp2pppp/1qp2n2/3pN3/2P3b1/1QN1P3: Nice!! We got out of that sticky pin. And if black ever trades our queens, we're happy to open up the a-file for our rook.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/2bNp3/2P5/4PN2/PP: Black saved their bishop from being traded off, but let's chase it. The plan is to play pawn to a3, followed by pawn to b4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pp2ppp/2np1n2/p1bNp3/2P5/P3PN2/: Dang! OK we can't play pawn to b4 anymore so... new plan. Pawn to b3 in order to put our bishop on b2.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pp2ppp/2np1n2/p1bNp3/2P5/PP2PN2: Well done! We'll plant our bishop on b2 next, and then play the game from there.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/4p3/2P5/2N5/PP1PPPP: Black chose to really strengthen their center, at the cost of blocking their dark-square bishop in. We'll develop our knight to f3 - standard stuff.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp3pp/3p4/4pp2/2P5/2N2N2/PP1PP: Don't be scared here! Black is pretending that pawn to e4 attacking our knight is a threat. In reality, it's an empty threat. We can continue with our regular development of fianchetto-ing our bishop. Pawn to g3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp3pp/3p1n2/4pp2/2P5/2N2NP1/PP: Now let's finish our fianchetto! Bishop to g2.
Well done! After a castle, we'll enjoy the rest of the game with an extremely strong bishop on g2.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/4P3/2Pp4/2N5/PP1P1: In this case, black's knight is just a little better than ours. To keep our advantage, we need to get both knights off the board. Pawn takes knight on f6....
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pP2/8/2P5/2p5/PP1P1PPP: ...and then recapture with the b-pawn. B-pawn takes c3. Almost always, you want to capture with your pawns TOWARDS the center.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pq2/8/2P5/2P5/P2P1PPP/: Pretty much any move here is good. For this course, let's just keep basic development with knight to f3.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pq2/8/2P5/2P2N2/P2P1PP: Nice! Next, we'll develop our bishop to d3 and then castle. The position is about equal.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP/R: As always, we put our knight behind our pawn, adding tons of pressure on that d5 square. Knight to c3.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/2P5/2N5/PP1PPPP: We have 2 options here. We COULD play d4 and head into the Queenâs Gambit Declinedâbut I already wrote a whole course on that. In the spirit of fresh, exciting material, letâs mix it up: pawn to e3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/2P5/2N1P3/PP1P: Black developed their knight, let's develop ours. Knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bppp/4pn2/3p4/2P5/2N1PN2/PP1: Black is saying "hey, I'm going to castle kingside". Well then, let's start pointing our pieces at the kingside. We'll push our pawn to b3, to make space for our bishop on b2. From there, we'll have a laser bishop pointing directly at the kingside.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/4pn2/3p4/2P5/1PN1PN2/P: Perfect, now time for our laser bishop. Bishop to b2.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bppp/4pn2/2pp4/2P5/1PN1PN2/P: Black put a pawn on c5 so they can push their d pawn to d4. They're trying to storm our center! We cannot allow this. Let's chop down that d-pawn with pawn takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bppp/5n2/2pp4/8/1PN1PN2/PB1P: Black is trying the same thing! They really want to push a pawn to d4. We can stop that by putting our OWN pawn on d4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bppp/5n2/2pp4/3P4/1PN1PN2/PB: Nice! We put an end to blacks central pawn storm.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/RNB: Let's learn the Englund Gambit. A nasty weapon you can use against your opponent when they start with the Queen's pawn. The Gambit actually begins on our first move, completely giving away our pawn with pawn to e5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/3P1B2/8/PPP1PPPP: LOL. Looks like our opponent premoved their opening! Pawn takes bishop on f4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4P3/8/8/PPP1PPPP/RNB: When they take, we try and win the pawn back immediately with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/8/5N2/PPP1PPPP: Now we add one more attacker with queen to e7.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppppqppp/2n5/4P3/5B2/5N2/PPP1PP: Jackpot. If White puts their bishop out, we strike. Queen to b4 check.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/1q3B2/5N2/PPPN: White protected their king but not their bishop. Now we take that sucker. Queen takes f4.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/5q2/4PN2/PPPN1: Now we make out like a bandit. Queen back to b4.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/1q6/4PN2/PPPN1: Well done! We are simply up a bishop.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/1q3B2/2N2N2/PP: White defended their king but forgot about their bishop. It's ours now. Queen takes f4.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/5q2/2N1PN2/PPP: And now the getaway! Queen to b4.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/1q6/2N1PN2/PPP: We are simply up a bishop - and thats a good thing ;).
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/1q6/5N2/PPPBPP: Black saved the king but left the pawn unprotected. Queen takes b2.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/8/2B2N2/PqP1PP: A great move from White, defending the rook and attacking our queen. Except this isn't actually a great move at all and it just lost White the game. Now we have the absolutely beautiful bishop to b4.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/1b6/2B2N2/PqPQ: And now we take with bishop to c3.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/8/2Q2N2/PqP1PP: Can you find the best move? Hint: our queen sneaks in for checkmate on c1.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/8/2Q2N2/P1P1PP: Congratulations!! We just checkmated White in 8 moves. It doesn't get better than that.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/1q3B2/5N2/PPPQ: Silly white didn't defend their b2 pawn! Now we take with queen to b2.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/5B2/2Q2N2/PqP1: And now we unleash our bishop-pin-trick again. Bishop to b4.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/1b6/2Q2N2/PqPB: Yay! A queen! Bishop takes c3.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/8/2B2N2/PqP1PP: Aaaaaand now we have checkmate Can you find it? Hint: Queen to c1.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/8/2N2N2/PqPBPP: Our queen is outnumbered, let's bring a bishop to help her. Bishop to b4.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/3NP3/1b6/5N2/PqPBP: A very tense position. Let's simplify with bishop takes d2.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/3NP3/8/8/PqPNPPPP/: Black is threatening a fork on c7. Let's threaten the same thing but in on the other side of the board with knight to b4.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppNp1ppp/8/4P3/1n6/8/PqPNPPPP/R: OK white went for the check. We have to move our king to d8.
descriptions.N1bk2nr/pp1p1ppp/8/4P3/1n6/8/PqPNPPPP/R2: Black went for the rook, now we get the queen. Knight jumps into c2.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/8/2N2N2/PqPQPP: OK they didn't hang checkmate but we still get a rook out of this whole thing. Queen takes a1.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/8/2N2N2/P1P1PP: Oh! And we get a knight out of this thing too. Queen takes knight on c3.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/8/2q2N2/P1P1PP: It's... it's lookin real bad for White here. Good job.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/3NP3/5q2/5N2/PPP1P: White is forking our queen and the c7 pawn. Do not panic! We can simply slide our queen over one square to e4.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppNp1ppp/2n5/4P3/4q3/5N2/PPP1PP: Again, still fine. Don't panic. King slides one square to d8.
descriptions.N1bk1bnr/pp1p1ppp/2n5/4P3/4q3/5N2/PPP1PP: Yes white won a rook, but now their knight is stuck. It will never escape our prison on a8. Now we can take in the middle with knight to e5.
descriptions.N1bk1bnr/pp1p1ppp/8/4N3/4q3/8/PPP1PPPP/R: And take back! Queen takes e5
descriptions.N1bk1bnr/pp1p1ppp/8/4q3/8/8/PPP1PPPP/R2Q: With White's knight stuck in jail, and our queen strong in the center, our position is good. Well done!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/3Pp3/8/8/PPP1PPPP/RN: OK they pushed. Now we just play chess. Knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/3Pp3/2P5/8/PP2PPPP: Now let's develop our bishop to b4 with check.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/3Pp3/1bP5/8/PP2PPPP: Well done! We have a slight edge on our opponent.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/8/4P3/1N6/8/PqPNPPPP/R: Finally, let's take back with our queen. Queen to b4.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/8/4P3/1q6/8/P1PNPPPP/R: Well done untangling yourself from that tricky situation!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/3P4/4P3/PPP2PPP/: OK they didn't take, so that means we will. Pawn takes d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/RNBQ: Now we push our queen's pawn up to d5, fighting back for the center.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/RNB: Well done! Now to play chess...
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppppqppp/2n5/4P3/8/2N2N2/PPP1PP: White has given up defending their pawn. Great! Let's take it back with knight to e5.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppppqppp/8/4N3/8/2N5/PPP1PPPP/R: Now queen takes back on e5
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4q3/4P3/2N5/PPP2PPP/: Let's pin the knight, the only current defender of the pawn on e4. Bishop to b4.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/8/4q3/1b2P3/2N5/PPP2PP: We gambited a pawn and won it back! Time to continue the rest of the game.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppppqppp/8/4n3/5B2/2N2N2/PPP1PP: OK our knight is a liability at this point. Let's trade it for White's. Knight takes f3 with check.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppppqppp/8/8/5B2/2N2P2/PPP1PP1P: Now we stop the bishop's threat with pawn to d6.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp1qppp/3p4/8/5B2/2N2P2/PPP1PP: White is ahead here because they have a slight developmental advantage. It's a gambit and this happens sometimes.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/1b6/2N2N2/PqPB: Not gonna lie, we are in a bad spot right now. Sometimes gambits work, sometimes they dont. This is one of the donts. The best move here is queen to a3.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/1b6/qRN2N2/P1P: Our queen needs to run, and the only safe square is a5.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/q3P3/1b6/1RN2N2/P1: That's a wrap. We are in a bad position but not completely lost. The material is still equal.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/3NP3/1b6/q4N2/P1PB: White is threatening a fork on c7. Let's drop our bishop back to a5 to defend.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/b2NP3/8/q4N2/P1PBP: Not a great ending for us, but that's how it goes sometimes.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Let's learn the french defense! I've had ENOUGH of these pawn-e4 players. It's time we stopped them once and for all. So how do we do it? We start off the french with pawn to e6.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R: After white takes the center with pawn to d4, we can enter the french defense. We IMMEDIATELY strike back in the center with pawn to d5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/3PP3/8/PPPN1PPP: Instead of trading pawns, white has left tension in the center. Let's BLOW UP the center with pawn to c5. This is going to be fun...
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2pp4/3PP3/2P5/PP1N1P: Like I said, our mission is to blow up the center. We'll do this by trading off the pawns. Pawn takes pawn on d4 first.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/3p4/3PP3/8/PP1N1PPP/: And now pawn takes pawn on e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/8/3PN3/8/PP3PPP/R1BQ: Developing a piece with check is usually a good idea. Bishop to b4.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pp3ppp/4p3/8/1b1PN3/8/PP1B1PPP/: Aaaaaand finally white blundered. They forgot that their queen was the only defender of the d4 pawn. Queen takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/pp3ppp/4p3/8/Qb1qN3/8/PP1B1PPP/: We need to block check and defend the b4 bishop at the same time. Knight to c6 seems to do the job :)
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/8/Qb1qN3/8/PP1B1PP: Well done! We have a pawn up and white's knight is in trouble.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3pP3/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/: We've entered the french defense advanced variation. Basically, white wants to hang onto their central pawns. Well... we won't let them. Pawn to c5!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2ppP3/3P4/2P5/PP3PPP: Dang, white REALLY doesn't want to lose their central pawns. Let's add another attacker to the d4 pawn with queen to b6.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/pp3ppp/1q2p3/2ppP3/3P4/2P2N2/PP: Why not add yet ANOTHER attacker to the d4 pawn? Knight to c6!
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2P2N2/P: Two steps: One, clean up a bit of tension in the center. Two, add an attacker to the d4 square. First, we clean up the tension with pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/3pP3/3P4/5N2/PP2B: OK, now as I promised, we'll add another attacker to the d4 pawn. We'll do this by rotating our g-knight all the way to f5. To get the g-knight to f5, first we play g-knight to e7.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp2nppp/1qn1p3/3pP3/3P4/5N2/PP2: White castled, and now we are literally just winning a pawn. Knight to f5 will win us the d4 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/3pPn2/3P4/4BN2/PP: I guess white technically saved the d4 pawn, but they gave up the b2 pawn instead. Queen takes pawn on b2.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pPn2/3P4/4BN2/Pq1: Time to get our king to safety too. Let's develop our bishop to e7 and prepare to castle.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pp2bppp/2n1p3/3pPn2/3P4/4BN2/Pq1: French defense just won us a pawn! Woohoo!
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/3pPn2/3P4/2N2N2/P: After working all day for that d4 pawn, we finally win it. Knight on f5 takes pawn on d4 :)
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/3pP3/3N4/2N5/PP2B: We're a pawn up, BUT our king is in the center and our pieces are less developed. In times like this, if we CAN trade queens, it's best to trade queens. Queen takes knight on d4.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/3q4/2N5/PP2BP: Very nice! Can't complain about a free pawn.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PB1N2/: OK finally, it's time. It's time to grab that freaking d4 pawn. Pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/3pP3/3P4/3B1N2/PP: It might look like that pawn on d4 is free, but if we take it with our knight, white has a sneaky trick where he can check our king with bishop to b5. The only way to ACTUALLY threaten the pawn on d4 now is to block any checks to our king, which we can do with bishop to d7.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp1b1ppp/1qn1p3/3pP3/3P4/3B1N2/PP: Sweet! Now we finally get our free pawn. Knight takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp1b1ppp/1q2p3/3pP3/3N4/3B4/PP3PP: We have to capture back. Queen avenges our knight on d4.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp1b1ppp/4p3/3pP3/3q4/2NB4/PP3PPP: We have a 1 point advantage, and the only way to keep it is to stop white's knight from getting to c7 and forking us. We can do that with pawn to a6.
descriptions.r3kbnr/1p1b1ppp/p3p3/3pP3/3q4/2NB4/PP3PP: Woohoo! We are up a free pawn :)
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2ppP3/3P4/5N2/PPP2PP: White is letting us give away a c-pawn for a central pawn - sounds like a good trade to me! Pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/3pP3/3N4/8/PPP2PPP/R: Let's keep developing! Knight to e7 to prepare knight to f5 or g6 in the future. You'll notice in the french defense that we have to be creative with developing our kingside knight, because white's e5 pawn typically blocks the regular f6 square.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2nppp/4p3/3pP3/3N4/2N5/PPP2PP: Let's develop our other knight while we're at it. Knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2nppp/2n1p3/1B1pP3/3N4/2N5/PP: Let's unpin our king. Bishop to d7!
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp1bnppp/2n1p3/1B1pP3/3N4/2N5/PP: Well done! We are almost done developing and have 2 central pawns to white's 1.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2nppp/2N1p3/3pP3/8/2N5/PPP2PP: We can recapture with the pawn or the knight here. The computer says capturing with the knight is slightly better, so knight takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/8/2N5/PPP2PPP: Well done! We have 2 central pawns to white's 1, leaving us with a bit of an advantage.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/3PP3/2N5/PPP2PP: And we have entered the french defense main line! Here I recommend playing knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p2B1/3PP3/2N5/PPP: White pins us? We pin white! Bishop to b4 pinning the knight to the king
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3pP1B1/1b1P4/2N5/PP: Oh no!!! White is attacking our pinned knight!!! This is fine, actually. We counter attack with pawn to h6.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2pp1/4pP1p/3p2B1/1b1P4/2N5/PP: White takes our knight? We take white's bishop. Pawn takes bishop on g5.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2pP1/4p3/3p2p1/1b1P4/2N5/PPP2: Really only 1 move here that doesn't let white promote: rook to g8.
descriptions.rnbqk1r1/ppp2pP1/4p3/3p2pQ/1b1P4/2N5/PPP: White is being sneakyyyyy. It looks like we can take the free pawn with our rook, but white's queen will infiltrate our backline if we do. Let's add one more attacker to the free pawn with queen to f6.
descriptions.rnb1k1r1/ppp2pP1/4pq2/3p2pQ/1b1P4/2N5/PP: Well done! We have a 60% winrate from here.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/3pP3/3Q4/5N2/PPP2PPP: Sometimes white takes with the queen. When the do this, they're basically begging us to play knight c6 to hit the queen.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/1B1pP3/3Q4/5N2/PPP: White's trying to pin and take our knight on c6, but our knight is very happy on c6. If we play g-knight to e7, we can always replace our knight if it gets captured.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2nppp/2n1p3/1B1pP3/3Q4/5N2/PP: Well done! With white's queen slightly mispositioned, we have a small advantage coming into the middlegame
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2PpP3/8/8/PPP2PPP/RN: White won't always play this move, but when they do, its GREAT for us. Bishop to c5 both develops our bishop and recaptures our pawn - not to mention now white only has 1 central pawn while we have 2!
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pp3ppp/4p3/2bpP3/8/8/PPP2PPP/RN: Well done! White is going to have a hard time holding onto that weak e5 pawn.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3pP3/3P4/2N5/PPP2P: Our knight has 3 possible moves: retreating like a coward, jumping to e4 and dying, and staying middle-ground with knight to d7. Let's go for the middle-ground: knight to d7.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppn1ppp/4p3/3pP3/3P4/2N2N2/PPP: It's time to crash open the center. Pawn to c5
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/4p3/2ppP1B1/3P4/2N2N2/: This move actually helps us! Now we can move our queen to b6 and add another attacker to the d4 pawn, which is something we wanted to do anyway.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/pp1n1ppp/1q2p3/2ppP1B1/3P4/2N2N: Well done! We're going to get rid of the d4 pawn, which destabilizes the e5 pawn and white's whole center.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3P4/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/R: White took our pawn, taking us to the french defense exchange variation. Let's return the favor with pawn takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/3P4/2N5/PPP2PPP/R: White is attacking our pawn. Can you guess what we're going to do? That's right, defend it. Knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/3P4/2N2N2/PPP2P: We need to develop our bishop and castle kingside. It almost doesn't matter where we develop it, but for this course, we'll go bishop to b4 and pin the white knight.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/1b1P4/2N2N2/PPP: The exchange french is super boring. White did not want us to have any fun this game.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/3P4/3B4/PPP2PPP/R: Now that white's bishop blocked the queen from protecting her pawn on d4, we can attack the pawn with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3p4/3P4/3B1N2/PPP2P: White's light-squared bishop is usually really good in the french defense. Let's attack it with knight to b4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/1n1P4/3B1N2/PPP2P: Sweet! White let us take their light-square bishop, so lets do it :) Knight takes bishop on d3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/3P4/3n1N2/PPP2PPP: Well done! We have a slight eval advantage and we win over half our games from here! Next, we'll continue developing and castle kingside
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/3PP3/3B4/PPP2PP: Here, we can actually take the e4 pawn. It'll win us a tempo on white. Pawn takes pawn on e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/8/3PB3/8/PPP2PPP/RN: Now knight to f6 and white is forced to move their bishop for the 3rd time in a row.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/3P4/5B2/PPP2PPP/: Let's continue with the very common french defense theme to crash the center: Pawn to c5. If white ever takes our pawn, we can trade queens and make white lose their right to castle.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/4pn2/2p5/3P4/5B2/PPP1NPP: Finally, let's get ready to kingside castle with bishop to e7.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2bppp/4pn2/2p5/3P4/5B2/PPP1NPP: Perfectly played! We'll castle and finish up our development next.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pp3ppp/4p3/8/1b1P4/2N5/PP3PPP/R: We'll keep developing with knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3ppp/4pn2/8/1b1P4/2N2N2/PP3PPP: It's probably a good time to castle, especially since white's king is still stuck in the middle of the board.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/4pn2/8/1b1P4/2NB1N2/PP3P: If we can get our bishop to b7, it'll get an amazing diagonal that will pressure black for the rest of the game. Let's prep bishop to b7 with pawn to b6.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p4ppp/1p2pn2/8/1b1P4/2NB1N2/PP3: Now we put the bishop on the amazing diagonal :) Bishop to b7.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/pb3ppp/1p2pn2/8/1b1P4/2NB1N2/PP: We are looking fantastic here. Well done.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2pp1/4pn1p/3pP3/1b1P4/2N5/PPP: We want to plant our knight on e4, but white's c3 knight is defending that square... let's just capture it! Bishop takes knight on c3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2pp1/4pn1p/3pP3/3P4/2P5/P1PB1: NOW we can plant our knight on e4
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2pp1/4p2p/3pP3/3Pn3/2PB4/P1PB: The best move here is to get rid of white's bishop pair. Knight takes bishop on d2.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2pp1/4p2p/3pP3/3P4/2PB4/P1PQ1: The last thing we should do is undermine black's strong center. Pawn to c5!
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3pp1/4p2p/2ppP3/3P4/2PB4/P1PQ1: Well done! Both sides played at literally 100% accuracy.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/2PP4/8/PP3PPP/RNB: Now we're in the Monte Carlo Variation. There's honestly a lot of choices here - why don't we play bishop b4 with check?
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/1bPP4/2N5/PP3PPP/: Let's play knight to f6 next, adding a defender to our d5 pawn.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/1bPP4/2N2N2/PP3P: Let's castle next, seems fine to me
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/1bPP4/2N2N2/PP2: White moved their bishop - which is our queue to finally capture the pawn on c4. This is clever because it means white basically wasted a turn on the bishop, just to move it again on the next turn. Pawn takes pawn on c4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/5n2/8/1bpP4/2N2N2/PP2BP: Nice! Because we wasted one of whites moves, we are slightly ahead in the eval bar.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3p4/3P4/2PB4/PP3PPP: In the French Defense Exchange Variation, we're likely going g-knight to e7. If we do that right now, accidentally block in our dark-square bishop. So first, let's first go bishop to d6.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2nb4/3p4/3P4/2PB4/PP3PP: Nice! In the future we'll go g-knight to e7 and short-castle.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2pP4/3P4/8/PPPN1PPP/: Here's a twist! We don't want to take back with pawn to d5. Instead, we develop our queen with queen takes d5. Now the queen is attacking the d4 pawn and defending the c5 pawn.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2Pq4/8/8/PPPN1PPP/R1: Let's take back with the bishop to get some more development. Bishop takes pawn on c5.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/pp3ppp/4p3/2bq4/8/8/PPPN1PPP/R1: Nice, we have a bit more development and will be first to castle.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/3P4/5N2/PPP2PPP/R: Let's just... keep copying white. Knight develops to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/3P4/3B1N2/PPP2P: Like I said, we just keep copying white! Bishop develops to d6.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/3b1n2/3p4/3P4/3B1N2/PPP2: I'm serious, we just KEEP copying white!!! King castles.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/3b1n2/3p4/3P4/2PB1N2/PP: Let's add a pin to the knight with bishop to g4.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/ppp2ppp/3b1n2/3p4/3P2b1/2PB1N2/: Nice! It's a symmetrical and dead even position
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2pq4/3P4/5N2/PPPN1PP: Oooooh a free pawn! Pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/3q4/2Bp4/5N2/PPPN1PP: Alright, maybe we were a little too aggressive with our early queen push. Let's drop her back to d6.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/pp3ppp/3qp3/8/2Bp4/5N2/PPPN1PPP: Let's keep developing with knight to f6.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/pp3ppp/3qpn2/8/2Bp4/1N3N2/PPP2P: We'll keep developing with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/2nqpn2/8/2BN4/5N2/PPP2PP: If I'm being honest, there was no way to hang onto that pawn. We won a pawn, then they won it back. Sometimes that's life. Let's trade knights next: knight takes knight on d4.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/3qpn2/8/2BN4/8/PPP2PPP/R: Let's keep developing - bishop to e7.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pp2bppp/3qpn2/8/2BN4/8/PPP2PPP/R: Nice - both sides played absolutely perfectly.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2pp4/3PP3/5N2/PPPN1P: White is letting us remove one of their central pawns. I say lets do it! Pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/3p4/3NP3/8/PPPN1PPP/: White has a strong knight in the center. Let's get rid of it with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/1B1p4/3NP3/8/PPPN1: With two attackers on our c6 knight, we need to add a defender. G-knight to e7.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2nppp/2n1p3/1B1p4/3NP3/8/PPPN: Nice, the game is dead even so far. Good luck with the rest of it.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2pp1/4pn1p/3pP3/1b1P3B/2N5/PP: We need to break this annoying pin. Pawn to g5!
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2p2/4pn1p/3pP1p1/1b1P3B/2N5/P: Well done! Once black removes their bishop, we can finally bring our knight to safety.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/3b1n2/3p2B1/3P4/3B1N2/P: What if I told you we.... KEEP COPYING WHITE. Bishop to g4.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/ppp2ppp/3b1n2/3p2B1/3P2b1/3B1N2: It's a completely even and symmetrical position - good luck with the rest of your game :)
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/P1P2N2/: White really weakened the b3 square with that move. Our plan? Get our knight on b3 and have it be anchored by a pawn on c4. First, let's lock in the queenside and get our pawn to c4. This makes it really hard for white to do anything on the queenside.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/3pP3/2pP4/P1P2N2/: Let's keep going with our plan: getting a knight on b3. We can get there by going knight to a5.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pp3ppp/1q2p3/n2pP3/2pP4/P1P2N2/: OK now do NOT put your knight on b3. If we do, white will just trade off the knights and open up the queenside. Instead, we will keep our knight on a5 for the rest of the game and THREATEN to put our knight on b3. White has to keep their knight on d2 just to defend the b3 square. In the meantime, we can keep developing with bishop to d7.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pp1b1ppp/1q2p3/n2pP3/2pP4/P1P2N2/: Nice!! Look how white's e2 bishop, d2 knight, and c1 bishop all can't move. It's wild how paralyzed they are.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2pp1/4p2p/3pP3/3Pn1Q1/2P5/P1P: White came with a pretty serious threat: capturing our pawn on g7. And if we castle, we're probably going to get checkmated. The only real way to defend our pawn is to play pawn to g6!
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2p2/4p1pp/3pP3/3Pn1Q1/2PB4/P1: Now we can get rid of white's bishop pair - and white's right to castle! Knight takes bishop on d2.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2p2/4p1pp/3pP3/3P2Q1/2PB4/P1P: Finally, let's crash the center, as we love to do in the french! Pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3p2/4p1pp/2ppP3/3P2Q1/2PB4/P1P: This was a perfectly played opening from both sides - now onto the rest of the game!
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppn1ppp/4p3/3pP3/3P1P2/2N5/PPP: White's center is wayyyy to strong right now. We need to break it down. Pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/4p3/2ppP3/3P1P2/2N2N2/: We definitely want to play pawn takes d4 at some point, but first lets develop one last piece. Knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/2n1p3/2ppP3/3P1P2/2N1B: NOW we can take that central d4 pawn. Pawn takes pawn on d4. We've traded one of our side pawns for one of white's center ones, which is always good.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/2n1p3/3pP3/3N1P2/2N1B3: So far, both sides are playing absolutely perfectly... Let's stick with our principles and develop our bishop to c5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1n1ppp/2n1p3/2bpP3/3N1P2/2N1B3: White is looking to castle queenside. Let's castle kingside and have ourselves a battle

shortDescriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R: How do we continue the french defense?

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the Fried Liver Attack, one of the most dangerous openings in chess. An opening where you can potentially checkmate your opponent in 8 moves. It starts with pawn to e4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1P: Now develop our bishop to c4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/2B1P3/5N2/PP: Black played knight f6, which means we can play the Fried Liver Attack. To start the attack, let's play knight g5, threatening the pawn on f7 with the bishop and knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/3pp1N1/2B1P3/8/PP: This was Black's only way to stop capture on f7. Now let's capture on d5 with our e-pawn.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/3np1N1/2B5/8/PPPP1P: Black played the very natural recapture with the knight, but now they are in trouble. Here we detonate an explosive. Knight to f7. Kaboom.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp2kpp/2n5/3np3/2B5/8/PPPP1PPP: Let's bring out the queen with check on f3. We are checking the king and have a double attack on the knight on d5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp3pp/2n5/3np3/2B5/5Q2/PPPP1PP: Black moved their king, so now we can take their knight with bishop d5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp3pp/2n5/3Bp3/8/5Q2/PPPP1PPP/: Well done! We have a dominant position against Black's exposed king. The computer puts our position at a +2 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bq1bkr/ppp3pp/2n5/3np3/2B5/5Q2/PPPP1PP: Black ran their king to g8, and now we have mate on the board. Bishop takes knight on d5.
descriptions.r1b2bkr/ppp3pp/2n5/3qp3/8/5Q2/PPPP1PPP/R: Black is giving up their queen to delay the inevitable. Queen takes queen on d5.
descriptions.r4bkr/ppp3pp/2n1b3/3Qp3/8/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Final capture, queen takes bishop on e6 checkmate.
descriptions.r4bkr/ppp3pp/2n1Q3/4p3/8/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB1: That was best case for the Fried Liver Attack. But let's be real, most of our opponents won't play those awful moves LOL - so how do we win if black has other ideas?
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp3pp/2n1k3/3np3/2B5/5Q2/PPPP1: Black has brought the king to defend the knight on d5. Let's put even more pressure on the d5 knight by developing our knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp3pp/4k3/3np3/1nB5/2N2Q2/PPPP: Black added yet another defender to their knight, and is also threatening a fork on c2. Weirdly enough, we shouldn't get so worried about defending the pawn, and we should just castle.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pp4pp/2p1k3/3np3/1nB5/2N2Q2/PPP: This was literally Black's only move, adding another defender to the knight. Now pawn to d4, shattering the defenses in the center.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pp4pp/2p1k3/3np3/2BP4/2N2Q2/PPn: Black is attacking our rook in the corner, forgetting that all the action is happening in the center of the board. D-pawn takes e5.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pp4pp/2p1k3/3nP3/2B5/2N2Q2/PP3P: Forget about our rook, let's add even more pressure to the center with other rook to d1, pinning the queen.
This is a crazy position. We are down 7 points of material, but our position is so crushing that the computer puts us at +9 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p1N1/2B1n3/8/PPPP: Black is trying to bait us into playing knight takes f7. If we do, we're actually losing. Let's avoid this by taking f7 with our bishop.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppppkBpp/2n5/4p1N1/4n3/8/PPPP1P: Now we play pawn to d4, taking the center and baiting Black to take our knight. If they do, they lose their queen.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppppkBpp/8/4p1N1/3nn3/8/PPP2PPP: Black thinks they won a free pawn, in reality they are giving us time to escape our pieces. Let's play pawn to c3 attacking their knight.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppppkBpp/8/4p1N1/3nn3/2P5/PP3PP: Well done! Wherever black moves their knight, we will be able to escape or trade our pieces out of danger, leaving us with a +3 point positional advantage. White wins this position over 80% of the time.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppppkBpp/2n5/4p1n1/3P4/8/PPP2PP: Black took the bait, now we capture the knight back with bishop to g5, skewering the king against his own queen.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pppp1kpp/2n5/4p1B1/3P4/8/PPP2PP: Now bishop to d8, winning the queen.
descriptions.r1bB1b1r/pppp1kpp/2n5/4p3/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/: Well done! We are up a queen and have an easy win ahead of us.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppppkBp1/2n4p/4p1N1/3Pn3/8/PPP2: Let's recapture with knight to e4.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pppp1kp1/2n4p/4p3/3PN3/8/PPP2PP: The best move here is to move our pawn to d5, destabilizing their knight.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pppp1kp1/2n4p/3Pp3/4N3/8/PPP2PP: Well done! Despite being equal in material, the computer puts us at a +2 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp3pp/4k3/3np3/2Bn4/2N2Q2/PPPP: Black is threatening our queen, but we can gain tempo by playing bishop captures knight on d5 with our bishop with check.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp3pp/3k4/3Bp3/3n4/2N2Q2/PPPP1: Black is attacking our queen and threatening a fork on c2. Let's move our queen to d3 to cover that square.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp3pp/3k4/3Bp3/3n4/2NQ4/PPPP1P: Well done! Black's king is in the middle of the board and we are up in material. This is a completely winning position for us.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp3pp/4k3/3np3/2B5/2N2Q2/PPnP1: Black forgot their knight was a defender of their other knight. Now we can play bishop takes d5 with check.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp3pp/4k3/3Bp3/8/2N2Q2/PPnP1PP: Well done! Black is in an awful position down material, with their king checked in the middle of the board, and our pieces about to swarm.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pp4pp/2p1k3/3n4/1nBp4/2N2Q2/PPP: With blacks middle pawn out of the way, we can add our rook to the mix. Rook to e1.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pp4pp/2pk4/3n4/1nBp4/2N2Q2/PPP2: Now we add our bishop to the mix. Bishop to f4. Our pieces are swarming.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pp4pp/2pk4/3n4/1nBp1B2/2N2Q2/PP: Well done! Even though we are a knight down, all pieces are aiming right for Blacks king in the middle of the board and the computer puts us at a +4 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp1n1pp/4k3/3np3/2B5/2N2Q2/PPP: Black retreated their knight to e6, but this is too passive. Now, pawn to d4 immediately is extremely strong.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pp2n1pp/2p1k3/3np3/2BP4/2N2Q2/P: If Black won't open up the center, we'll do it for them. D-pawn takes e5.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pp1kn1pp/2p5/3nP3/2B5/2N2Q2/PPP: Let's bring our bishop in. Bishop to g5.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppk1n1pp/2p5/3nP1B1/2B5/2N2Q2/P: Black is continuing to run their king. Let's cut down the pieces in the middle to expose him. Bishop takes d5. It's important to do this with the bishop to save the knight for a future check.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppk1n1pp/8/3pP1B1/8/2N2Q2/PPP2P: Now leap in with our knight. Knight to b5 check.
descriptions.rkbq1b1r/pp2n1pp/8/1N1pP1B1/8/5Q2/PPP2PP: Let's open up a line of possible line of sight to the king. Pawn to e6. We are now threatening checkmate.
descriptions.rkb2b1r/pp2n1pp/4P3/qN1p2B1/8/5Q2/PPP2PP: Black is delaying the inevitable. The second we get a free move, we will win the game. Let's block the check with bishop to d2.
descriptions.rkb2b1r/pp2n1pp/4P3/1q1p4/8/5Q2/PPPB1PPP: Checkmate in 1. Can you find it? Hint: It's bishop to f4.
descriptions.rkb2b1r/pp2n1pp/4P3/1q1p4/5B2/5Q2/PPP2PP: You stuck with it! You are mastering how to convert your positional advantage into a win.
descriptions.rkbq1b1r/p3n1pp/1p2P3/1N1p2B1/8/5Q2/PPP2: Black is gasping for air, giving their king a space to breath. Let's slide our queen to g3 check.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pk2n1pp/1p2P3/1N1p2B1/8/6Q1/PPP: And now another check, forcing the king out of his hiding hole. Knight to d6.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/p3n1pp/1pkNP3/3p2B1/8/6Q1/PPP2P: Finally, let's fork the queen and rook. Knight to f7.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/p3nNpp/1pk1P3/3p2B1/8/6Q1/PPP2P: Well done! We are completely winning from here.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp1n1pp/4k3/3n4/2Bp4/2N2Q2/PPP: Black is too focused on gaining material. Let's add even more pressure in the center with bishop to f4, preparing us to castle queenside next move.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp1n1pp/4k3/3n4/2B2B2/2p2Q2/PP: With the center cleared up, we can add even more pressure to the middle with castle queenside.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp1n1pp/4k3/3n4/2B2B2/5Q2/PpP2: Instead of taking back our pawn, it's better to slide our king to b1 and use the black pawn as cover.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pp2n1pp/2p1k3/3n4/2B2B2/5Q2/PpP: Black added yet another defender to their knight. Let's remove the king as a defender with by moving our h-rook to e1 with check.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/pp2nkpp/2p5/3n4/2B2B2/5Q2/PpP2P: Now we unleash our trick. Bishop to c7 attacking the queen and discovering a check on the king. We win the queen this way.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppB1n1pp/2p5/3n4/2B5/5Q2/PpP2PP: Cute - the king made a trip around the board and has returned to his home square beside his queen. Now we take her. Bishop takes d8.
descriptions.r1bk1b1r/pp2n1pp/2p5/3n4/2B5/5Q2/PpP2PPP: Our material is equal again! Let's remove all cover from the king. Bishop takes d5.
descriptions.r1bk1b1r/pp2n1pp/2p5/3B4/8/5Q2/PpP2PPP/1: Well done! This game is over for Black. His queen is gone and all our pieces are pointed at him. It's only a matter of time.
descriptions.rk1q1b1r/pp2n1pp/4b3/1N1p2B1/8/5Q2/PPP2P: By moving the bishop, the king has gained another escape square. Let's cut him off with our queen. Queen to c3.
descriptions.rk1q1b1r/p3n1pp/1p2b3/1N1p2B1/8/2Q5/PPP2: Black is delaying the inevitable. Let's play bishop to f4 check.
descriptions.r2q1b1r/pk2n1pp/1p2b3/1N1p4/5B2/2Q5/PPP2: Now throw in another check. Knight to d6.
descriptions.r2q1b1r/p3n1pp/kp1Nb3/3p4/5B2/2Q5/PPP2PP: Checkmate in 1. Can you find it? Hint: It's Queen to a3.
descriptions.r2q1b1r/p3n1pp/kp1Nb3/3p4/5B2/Q7/PPP2PPP: Way to stick with it! Enjoy the win.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b1p1N1/2B1P3/8/P: Black is trying to play a nasty trick on us called The Traxler. Although it's tempting to take Knight takes f7, The Traxler is a tricky line that we can't guess our way through. In this course, I recommend simply taking the pawn on f7 with our Bishop.
descriptions.r1bq3r/ppppkBpp/2n2n2/2b1p1N1/4P3/8/PPPP: Now let's retreat our bishop back to b3.
descriptions.r1bq3r/ppppk1pp/2n2n2/2b1p1N1/4P3/1B6/PP: Well done! We are a pawn up, the Black king is exposed, and we are ready to castle.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/n2Pp1N1/2B5/8/PPPP1: Black has played the main line. Here let's give a check with bishop to b5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p4ppp/2p2n2/nB2p1N1/8/8/PPPP1PP: Black has thwarted our Fried Liver Attack. Let's retreat our bishop back to d3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p4ppp/2p2n2/n3p1N1/8/3B4/PPPP1P: OK! The position is equal and we are ready to continue the game.
