descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the Italian game! This is by far the most played opening at the non-professional level. It's traditional, it's old school, it's chess the way your grandpa taught you. Let's just get into it with pawn to e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: When Black responds pawn to e5, now we can go knight to f3, attacking Black's pawn. You've probably done this a million times before.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1P: Most of the time black puts their knight out to defend their pawn - which brings us to the italian game. We'll have our opponent saying mama mia in no time. First, let's bring our bishop to c4. This targets the f7 pawn: the weakest pawn in black's position.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1P3/5N2/PP: Here, the key move that makes this game an italian one is pawn to c3. We're setting up pawn to d4 in the future to attack the bishop Black just put out.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b1p3/2B1P3/2P2N2: Now we continue our plan: pawn to d4 to take the center and attack this bishop. This leads to some very fun, aggressive, forcing lines.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b5/2BpP3/2P2N2/P: Take back with pawn to d4. We take back with the pawn to keep the bishop under attack.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/1bBPP3/5N2/PP3P: We have to protect our king. Let's do it with knight to c3, developing a piece.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/1bBPn3/2N2N2/PP3P: We just lost a pawn, and now we have two attackers on our knight. Do you know the crazy part? We actually will ignore all of that entirely and just castle our king to safety.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/1bBP4/2n2N2/PP3PP: If black capture with the knight, we recapture with pawn to c3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/2BP4/2b2N2/P4PPP/: Black is hitting our rook, and they're hoping that we move our rook out of the way so they have enough time to castle their king to safety. If Black castles, our entire attack is over before it even got started. That's why in this position, we sacrifice the rook! Bishop to a3 blocking Black's castle.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/2BP4/B4N2/P4PPP/b: Black took the bait and lost the game! Rook to e1, checking the king. The king can't move so instead the check must be blocked.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppppnppp/8/8/2BP4/B4N2/P4PPP/b2Q: We can grab the knight with bishop to e7. Now do you see just how much trouble Black is in if they take our rook?
descriptions.r1b4r/ppppkppp/8/8/2BP4/5N2/P4PPP/b2Q2K1: Finally, we end up a knight up after queen to a1.
descriptions.r1b4r/ppppkppp/8/8/2BP4/5N2/P4PPP/Q5K1 b: Wow! That's what black gets for trying to take our rook. Maybe next time they'll learn their lesson.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/2B1P3/5N2/PP: Let's be aggressive and dynamic. Pawn to d4 to take the center and open up the position.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/2BPn3/5N2/PPP2: This was inaccurate from Black. Lets capture on e5 to regain our pawn and open up the d-file for our queen.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b1P3/2B1n3/5N2/PPP: Black is threatening a fork (or a check) on f2. But what's better than a fork or a check threat? A checkmate threat. Queen to d5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/3QP3/2B1n3/5N2/PPP2: That's fine. King to f1. All part of the plan.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/3QP3/2B1n3/5N2/PPP: Black stopped the checkmate threat but they forgot about our other key point: we are attacking the undefended knight on e4. Queen takes e4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/2B1Q3/5N2/PPP2: Well done! We are simply up a piece.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/1bn2n2/8/2BPP3/5N2/PP3P: Retreating was a huge mistake for Black. We are ready to march our pawns forward, driving Black's knights away. Pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/1bn5/4P3/2BP2n1/5N2/PP3: The knight jumped forward. We can force him back with pawn to h3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/1bn4n/4P3/2BP4/5N1P/PP3: Now let's switch our focus to Black's other knight. Pawn to d5. This, folks, is what happens when you have pieces in the middle without pawns to defend them: you get harassed.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/1b5n/n2PP3/2B5/5N1P/PP3: With black's knights on the edges of the board (gross) we can continue our master plan. Bishop to g5 attacking the queen.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp2pp/1b3p1n/n2PP1B1/2B5/5N1P/: Here, we can sacrifice our bishop on c4 by playing the calculated pawn takes f6. We are threatening pawn takes g7 on the next move, discovering an attack on both black's queen and rook.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp2pp/1b3P1n/n2P2B1/2B5/5N1P/P: Well done! We have absolutely humiliated black's position and we will be winning this game. The computer gives a +4 point advantage here.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/2BP4/B1b2N2/P4PPP: Ah, Black blocked our bishop so now they can castle again. In this case, lets slide our rook over to c1 and hit the bishop. Now we've gained a tempo: Black must move their bishop before castling.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2np4/b7/2BP4/B4N2/P4PPP/: Now an awesome move: Queen to a4. It both hits the bishop and pins the knight to the king. As you'll see in a second, Black has no way to get out of this.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np4/b7/Q1BP4/B4N2/P4PP: Black thinks that after castling, their problems are over. But now pawn to d5 hitting the knight. The knight is the only defender of the bishop, and after it moves, we get the bishop for free.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/3p4/b2Pn3/Q1B5/B4N2/P4P: We can't take the bishop yet! Because then black will take our knight and open up our king. Instead, let's first play knight takes knight on e5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/8/b2Pp3/Q1B5/B7/P4PPP/2: Now we can finally take the bishop. Queen to a5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/8/Q2Pp3/2B5/B7/P4PPP/2R: Well done! We are up a piece and up in development. Black really has nothing here.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/3p4/8/1nBP4/5N2/P4PPP/2R: There's a fork: can you spot it? Queen to e1. Hitting the king and knight
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp1qppp/3p4/8/1nBP4/5N2/P4PPP/2: Of course, we take the free knight. Queen captures on b4.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp1qppp/3p4/8/1QBP4/5N2/P4PPP/2: Well done! We are up a piece, our king is castled, and our pieces are more developed.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/2BPn3/2b2N2/PP3PP: Do NOT recapture here! The secret of the Italian game is we want to play d5 to control the center, hit the knight, and gain a tempo. So, play pawn to d5. Now both the knight and the bishop are under attack.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/3Pn3/2B1n3/2b2N2/PP3P: Now we can finally capture back with pawn takes c3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/3P4/2n1n3/2P2N2/P4PPP: Black took our bishop but we'll avenge him. Queen to d4 forking the two knights.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/3n4/3P4/3Qn3/2P2N2/P4PP: Black thought they were clever saving their two knights, but they're not. Now we get queen takes g7.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1pQp/3n1q2/3P4/4n3/2P2N2/P4P: Let's trade queens. Queen takes on f6.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1p1p/3n1n2/3P4/8/2P2N2/P4PPP: Remember: we're still down a piece. Only one move here keeps our advantage and gives us a chance to win us the game: Rook to e1.
descriptions.r1b2k1r/pppp1p1p/3n1n2/3P4/8/2P2N2/P4PPP: Aaaand Black blundered. Bishop checks on h6.
descriptions.r1b3kr/pppp1p1p/3n1n1B/3P4/8/2P2N2/P4PPP: Once again, only one move wins us the game. The idea is to move our rook up to e5, then slide it over to deliver checkmate. Rook to e5.
descriptions.r1b3kr/pppp1p1p/5n1B/3PR3/4n3/2P2N2/P4PP: BLUNDER!! Now we have forced checkmate in 3 no-matter what. Black's knight is stopping us from checkmating with rook to g5. So, let's attract it away with knight to d2. Sacrificing the knight but if they take, we get checkmate.
descriptions.r1b3kr/ppp2p1p/3p1n1B/3PR3/4n3/2P5/P2N1P: Black didn't take the bait, but its still a forced checkmate. If Black doesn't take our knight, we take theirs, now sacrificing the rook. Knight takes on e4.
descriptions.r1b3kr/ppp2p1p/3p3B/3PR3/4n3/2P5/P4PPP/R: Black was so worried about defending the g5 square they forgot we have checkmate in 1 with rook to e8!
descriptions.r1b1R1kr/ppp2p1p/3p3B/3P4/4n3/2P5/P4PPP/: Well done! Would you believe me if I said thousands of games went exactly this way?
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1pp1/2n4p/2b1p3/2B1P3/2P2N2: Black played h6 to stop our knight from galloping in, but this move is too slow, and we're able to continue our real plan: pawn to d4 to attack the bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1pp1/2n4p/8/1bBPP3/5N2/PP3P: Black checked us. Let's use this as an opportunity to develop a piece with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2pp1/2np3p/8/1bBPP3/2N2N2/PP: Let's castle to get out of this pin.

Well done! Our position is the definition of good chess: pieces developed, pawns in the center, king castled to safety. The computer actually gives us a +2 point advantage just because we played so solid.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/2BpP3/5N2/PPP2: Instead of capturing back, let's castle our king. Once our king is safe, we'll win the pawn back and start a large attack.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/2Bpn3/5N2/PPP2PP: Black took another pawn! But this one was a trap. Now we have rook to e1, pinning the knight to the king.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/3p4/2Bpn3/5N2/PPP2P: Black hit our bishop, so now we need to retreat right? Wrong. Bishop takes on d5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/3pn3/5N2/PPP2PP: We lost our bishop, lets win a piece back. Knight to c3. It looks like our knight could be captured by the pawn, but then we would win the queen. It also looks like the knight can be captured by Black's knight, but Black's knight is actually pinned.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/8/3pn3/2N2N2/PPP2PP: OK, time to win our piece back. When the queen retreats, its most accurate to do it with rook to e4 with check.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp1bppp/2n5/8/3pR3/2N2N2/PPP2PP: And now we win our pawn back. Knight takes on d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2n5/8/3NR3/2N5/PPP2PPP: Castling is a mistake from Black. Now we have knight takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp1bppp/2N5/8/4R3/2N5/PPP2PPP/R: OMG that's a huge mistake. Black miscalculated and now we will win a piece. First, Knight takes back on d1.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1p1Rppp/2p5/8/8/8/PPP2PPP/R1BN2: Well done! Black blundered and now we are winning the game.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2b2/3P4/2B1n3/5N2/PP3: Black played the best move, getting their bishop out of danger. Instead of just taking the knight on c6, let's once again add another threat. Rook to e1, pinning the knight to the king. The whole point of these in-between moves is that we'll capture a piece at the end of the day no-matter what, but we can make improving moves in the meantime. Rook to e1.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppppnppp/5b2/3P4/2B1n3/5N2/PP3PP: No more inbetween-moves. Let's capture with rook to e4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp1nppp/3p1b2/3P4/2B1R3/5N2/PP3: Let's continue development with bishop to g5. We're essentially forcing a bishop trade but you'll see why in a second.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp1npp1/3p3p/3P2N1/2B1R3/8/PP3P: The whole point of the Italian Game is to attack, attack, attack. We never back down or defend. That's why in this position, we don't retreat our knight but instead play bishop to b5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp2npp1/2pp3p/1B1P2N1/4R3/8/PP3P: We CANNOT let Black's king castle. Once they do, our attack is completely over. Lets throw our knight into f7, forcing the king to capture us.
descriptions.r1bq3r/pp2nkp1/2pp3p/1B1P4/4R3/8/PP3PPP/: Now we begin the attack. Queen to f3 check.
descriptions.r1bq2kr/pp2n1p1/2pp3p/1B1P4/4R3/5Q2/PP3P: Let's bring our other rook to the party. Rook to e1. We are now threatening to capture the knight.
descriptions.r1bq2kr/pp2n1p1/3p3p/1p1P4/4R3/5Q2/PP3PP: Yet another mistake from black. Now we go rook takes knight to e7, threatening to fork the queen and king with our rook on the next move.
descriptions.r1bq2kr/pp2R1p1/3p3p/1p1P4/8/5Q2/PP3PPP/: Well done! It is pretty much impossible to lose in this position. We are simply threatening too much. A fork with rook e8, a checkmate in 2 with queen to f7. It's all but over.
descriptions.r1b3kr/pppp1p1p/3n3B/3PR3/4n3/2P2N2/P4PP: Black's knight is stopping us from checkmating with rook to g5. Let's move our rook over to e1 to attack it.
descriptions.r1b3kr/pppp3p/3n1p1B/3PR3/4n3/2P2N2/P4PP: Black just made breathing room for their king. Let's plug it back up with rook to e7 (only winning move).
descriptions.r1b3kr/ppppR2p/5p1B/3P1n2/4n3/2P2N2/P4PP: Black is attacking our bishop, but we have an even better attack. Rook to e8 check - winning us the rook.
descriptions.r1b1R2r/pppp1k1p/5p1B/3P1n2/4n3/2P2N2/P4: Now rook takes rook on h8.
descriptions.r1b4R/pppp1k1p/5p1n/3P4/4n3/2P2N2/P4PPP/: And rook takes knight on e4.
descriptions.r1b4R/pppp1k1p/5p1n/3P4/4R3/2P2N2/P4PPP/: When the dust settles, we have a rook for a bishop, more active pieces, and a safer king.
descriptions.r1bq1k1r/ppp1npp1/3p3p/1B1P2N1/4R3/8/PP3: Remember: attack, attack, attack. Queen to h5. Now Black cannot take our knight or they lose their rook. We also threaten checkmate on f7.
descriptions.r1bq1k1r/ppp1np2/3p2pp/1B1P2NQ/4R3/8/PP3: With both our queen and knight under attack, we need to do SOMETHING. Queen to f3. This loses our knight but wins us the game.
descriptions.r1bq1k1r/ppp1np2/3p2p1/1B1P2p1/4R3/5Q2/P: Now we can infiltrate with queen to f6. We are hitting the rook once and hitting the knight in the middle twice.
descriptions.r1bq1k2/ppp1np2/3p1Qp1/1B1P2p1/4R2r/8/PP: If black wants to trade rooks, that's fine. It doesn't change anything. Rook takes h4.
descriptions.r1bq1k2/ppp1np2/3p1Qp1/1B1P4/7p/8/PP3PPP: Now we bring our other rook as a replacement. Rook to e1.
descriptions.r2q1k2/pppbnp2/3p1Qp1/1B1P4/7p/8/PP3PPP/: Now for the nail in the coffin. Forget about our bishop and play rook takes on e7.
descriptions.r4k2/pppbqp2/3p1Qp1/1B1P4/7p/8/PP3PPP/6K: Mate in 1: can you find it? Queen to h8.
descriptions.r4k1Q/pppbqp2/3p2p1/1B1P4/7p/8/PP3PPP/6K: Wow. That was pretty long for an "openings" course huh? I like this checkmate because the Black queen cut off the Black king's escape square. She is suffocating her husband.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1PP: Black is playing Philidor defense, which is frankly way too passive. Look how Black is even blocking in their own dark-square bishop! When Black goes passive, we go aggressive: we can get an advantage here with pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/4p3/3PP3/5N2/PPP2P: Ordinarily we want our bishop to go on c4, so it can attack the weak f7 pawn. But, given black brought their knight out so early, it's best to pin it against the king with bishop to b5
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/2np4/1B2p3/3PP3/5N2/PPP: We have a few good options here: castling, taking the knight, taking the pawn. In this course I recommend developing our other knight with knight to c3. The chess engine loves this move, and white in that position wins more than 60% of their games!
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/2np4/1B6/3pP3/2N2N2/PPP: We really should take back our pawn, so let's play knight to d4.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/3p4/1B6/3nP3/2N5/PPP2PP: Remember! Capture the bishop first with check, then capture the knight. Bishop takes d7.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pppq1ppp/3p4/8/3nP3/2N5/PPP2PPP/R: Now queen takes the knight. Queen to d4. Because Black's knight is off the board, our queen is now pretty safe in the center and she does more good than harm.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pppq1ppp/3p1n2/8/3QP3/2N5/PPP2PPP: Let's play bishop to g5, this puts some pressure on Black's knight and if it moves, we'll be preventing black from castling.
descriptions.r3k2r/pppqbppp/3p1n2/6B1/3QP3/2N5/PPP2PP: Finally, let's castle queenside. Our rook will be on the same file as Black's queen so once the position opens up, Black will be in trouble.

Well done! Hundreds of thousands of games end up in this exact position believe it or not. We have a stronger center, our king is safe, more pieces are developed and active, and the computer is giving us a +1 point advantage.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/8/3pP3/5N2/PPP2PPP/: We recapture of course, and in this case it is best to do it with our knight. Recapturing with our queen would make her a target immediately, so we'll keep her safe for now. Knight to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/8/3NP3/8/PPP2PPP/: Black is attacking our pawn. Let's defend it while developing with knight to c3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bppp/3p1n2/8/3NP3/2N5/PPP2PP: Black is clearly looking to castle kingside. Our plan? Castle queenside and launch a huge attack on this bozo. Step 1? Developing our bishop to f4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/3p1n2/8/3NPB2/2N5/PPP2: Last step before castling is developing our queen. Let's slide her to d2, nice and easy.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/1pp1bppp/p2p1n2/8/3NPB2/2N5/PPP: Now we complete our plan: castle queenside. This also lines up our queen and rook creating a powerful battery.
Well done! We just have a very comfortable position against black here. White has a 60% winrate from here.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/4p3/2BPP3/5N2/PP: Now we can lock in the center and seal away Black's dark square bishop with pawn to d5. This also hits Black's knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/3Pp3/2B1P3/5N2/P: Well done! The computer gives us a slight edge because of our space advantage.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/q7/3pn3/2N2N2/PPP2P: Let's win our piece back now. Knight takes e4. This also sets up a discovered check for the next move.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/q7/3pN3/5N2/PPP2PPP: Black stopped our discovered check threat. Let's create a double attack on that bishop by moving our e4 knight to g5.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/q5N1/3p4/5N2/PPP2P: Remember how we lost a pawn at the start? Now we win it back. Knight takes e6.
descriptions.2kr3r/ppp3pp/2nbR3/q7/3p4/5N2/PPP2PPP/R1: We can develop a piece and gain a tempo with bishop to g5, hitting the rook.
descriptions.2k1r2r/ppp3pp/2nbR3/q5B1/3p4/5N2/PPP2PPP: Let's get our queen and rook on the same file with queen to e2. If black trades rooks, it only helps us activate our queen.
descriptions.2k1r2r/ppp3pp/2nbR3/q5B1/3p4/5N2/PPP1QPP: Well done! We navigated through the opening and have a better position than our opponent.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p1p1bppp/2p5/8/4R3/2N5/PPP2PPP/: Great, we doubled Black's pawns. Now let's trade queens with queen to d8.
descriptions.r1bb1rk1/p1p2ppp/2p5/8/4R3/2N5/PPP2PPP/R: Let's target the weak c6 pawn with rook to c4.
descriptions.r1bb1rk1/p1p2ppp/2p5/8/2R5/2N5/PPP2PPP/R: Well done! We have more development and better pawn structure than our opponent.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/1B6/3pP3/5N2/PPP2P: We could take with the knight or the queen here. The chess engine prefers taking with the knight but I actually recommend taking with the queen. At most levels of play, developing the queen at this point will just be crushing for our opponent. Our win rate is 57% when we take with the queen vs just 52% when we take with the knight. Queen takes on d4.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/2np4/1B6/3QP3/5N2/PPP2P: Now that the knight is no longer pinned, we need to take it or move our queen. I recommend taking it with bishop to c6.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2bp4/8/3QP3/5N2/PPP2PPP/: Now let's continue developing with knight to c3.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2bp1n2/8/3QP3/2N2N2/PPP2: We can set up a pin on the knight while developing our bishop with bishop to g5.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp1bppp/2bp1n2/6B1/3QP3/2N2N2/PP: Finally, let's castle queenside, bringing our rook and queen on the same file.

Well done! The computer gives us a slight edge here but honestly, White wins more than 60% of their games from here because of how threatening our position is. As long as your opponent doesn't play perfectly, you have a great chance at a win here.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pppbnpp1/3p3p/1B1P2N1/4R3/8/PP3PP: This was the only good move black could play. Remember: in the Italian, we attack. Instead of retreating our knight, we play the calm queen to e2. This protects our bishop and also lines up our rook and queen on the same file.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pppbnpp1/3p4/1B1P2p1/4R3/8/PP2QPP: Now we see the other brilliancy of queen to e2. We slide our other rook over to e1 creating a BAZOOKA aimed right at the Black king.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pppbnpp1/3p4/1B1P2p1/4R3/8/PP2QP: Rook takes knight on e7, winning our material back
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1Rpp1/3p4/1Q1P2p1/8/8/PP3PPP/: Well done! Black pretty much played perfectly here, not falling for any of our traps, and we still came out slightly ahead.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/7q/3pn3/2N2N2/PPP2P: Knight takes e4, winning our piece back and threatening some nasty discovered checks in the future.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/7q/3pN3/5N2/PPP2PPP: Black stopped our discovered check. Let's stop black from castling queenside with bishop to g5.
descriptions.r3k2r/ppp2ppp/2nbb3/6Bq/3pN3/5N2/PPP2PPP: We can trade a knight for a bishop AND double Black's pawns with knight to d6.
descriptions.r3k2r/pp3ppp/2npb3/6Bq/3p4/5N2/PPP2PPP/R: Let's drop our bishop back to safety with bishop to f4. This does two things: first, it hits the d6 pawn. Second, it frees up our knight to hit the d4 pawn.
descriptions.r3k2r/pp3ppp/2npb3/3q4/3p1B2/5N2/PPP2PPP: Let's add one final attacker to the d4 pawn with pawn to c3.
descriptions.r3k2r/pp3ppp/2npb3/3q4/3p1B2/2P2N2/PP3PP: Black can't capture our pawn because then we win the Queen (the bishop on e6 is pinned). This is a very comfortable position for white, and Black is completely tangled up.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1nppp/3p4/3P2N1/2B1R3/8/PP3P: Black castled right into the danger zone. Now we get the beautiful sacrifice: knight takes on h7.
descriptions.r1bq1r2/ppp1nppk/3p4/3P4/2B1R3/8/PP3PPP/: Now bring our queen into the game. Queen to h5 check.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1npp1/3p4/3P3Q/2B1R3/8/PP3PP: Let's slide our rook to h4, threatening checkmate in 1.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1npp1/3p4/3P3Q/2B4R/8/PP3PPP: Black played perfectly this time - we have an interesting attack but its by no means a guaranteed win. Good luck!
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/8/3P4/2nQn3/2P2N2/P4PP: Taking either knight is fine here. The computer slightly prefers queen takes c4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/3n4/3P4/2Q5/2P2N2/P4PP: Now let's drop our queen to safety on b3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/3n4/3P4/8/1QP2N2/P4PPP: Well done! We navigated through the opening and are left with an equal position.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1pp1/2n2n1p/8/1bBPP3/2N2N2/P: If black tries knight to f6, we simply push our e pawn up to e5 and chase him away.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1pp1/2n4p/4P3/1bBPn3/2N2N2/P: Black is thinking they're clever with bringing the knight forward and placing a double attack on our knight on c3. But, our position is so strong we don't have to worry. We'll actually sacrifice a pawn here by castling our king.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1pp1/2n4p/4P3/1bBP4/2n2N2/PP: We take back with pawn to c3, now sacrificing our pawn to the bishop. Don't worry, this is all part of the plan.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1pp1/2n4p/4P3/2BP4/2b2N2/P4P: Our rook is under attack, but we actually don't care, we have a trick up our sleeve. Queen to b3 sets up a double attack on black's weak f7 pawn AND hits black's bishop on c3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1pp1/2n4p/4P3/2BP4/1Q3N2/P4P: Black took the bait and forgot about their poor f7 pawn. As punishment for their forgetfulness, they will lose the game. Bishop to f7 with check.
descriptions.r1bq1k1r/pppp1Bp1/2n4p/4P3/3P4/1Q3N2/P4P: Black's king thinks he's safe on the dark square, but he forgot one thing. Bishop to a3 check.
descriptions.r1bq1k1r/ppp2Bp1/2np3p/4P3/3P4/BQ3N2/P4P: Let's trade with pawn to d6, opening up the center to expose black's king.
descriptions.r1bq1k1r/pp3Bp1/2np3p/8/3P4/BQ3N2/P4PPP/: Now let's bring our light-square bishop to g6, threatening queen to checkmate on the  next move.
descriptions.r1b2k1r/pp4p1/2np1qBp/8/3P4/BQ3N2/P4PPP/: It doesn't really matter where black moved the queen to protect the checkmate. She is just overloaded right now, both protecting the f7 square and the d6 pawn. Bishop takes d6 with check and black cannot take back.
descriptions.r1b2k1r/pp2n1p1/3B1qBp/8/3P4/1Q3N2/P4PPP: From here, we just play the cold blooded rook to e1, adding another attacker on the e7 knight.
It doesn't take a chess engine to see that black is losing this game LOL.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the Jobava London! If you want a solid opening, this right here is a solid opening. If you want a coin flip, idk go learn the Englund Gambit or something.  This course right here is for WINNERS! Now let's begin with pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3p4/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/R: Let's develop our knight to c3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3p4/3P4/2N5/PPP1PP: Now let's go bishop to f4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/3p4/3P1B2/2N5/PP: There's no way Black messed up already omg. Here we can go knight to b5, threatening to fork on c7.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/1N1pp3/3P1B2/8/PP: And that's a free pawn. Yum. Bishop takes pawn on e5. You COULD also take with the pawn but in this course I'll stick with the bishop.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/1N1pn3/3P4/8/PPP1PP: We need to avenge our bishop - pawn takes knight on e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/1N1pP3/4n3/8/PPP1PPPP: Did someone say queen sacrifice? I sure did. Queen to d5. Don't worry, we'll win her back.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/1N1qP3/4n3/8/PPP1PPPP: Knight to c7 forking the king, rook, and QUEEN. I promised you we'd win her back :D
descriptions.r1b2b1r/pp1k1ppp/8/3NP3/4n3/8/PPP1PPPP/R: We sacrificed our queen and we won 3 pawns. That's pretty cool.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/1N1p4/3P1B2/8/PP: Black has no idea what they're doing. Knight hops onto c7, forking the king and rook.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppNk1ppp/2n1pn2/3p4/3P1B2/8/PPP: And now knight to a8 winning a rook.
descriptions.N1bq1b1r/pp1k1ppp/2n1pn2/3p4/3P1B2/8/PPP: That may seem silly but 100,000+ games have gone exactly like this LOL
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppn1ppp/8/1N1pP3/8/8/PPP1PPPP/: Well, the black knight ran away, but now it's blocking the black queen! That means we win ANOTHER free pawn :D. Queen takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/2p5/1N1QP3/8/8/PPP1PPP: Shoot!! We are forked... or are we? There's only one move here that saved both our pieces: knight to d6 check.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1n1ppp/2pb4/3QP3/8/8/PPP1PPPP/: And now we recapture while moving our queen to safety with queen to d6
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1n1ppp/2pQ4/4P3/8/8/PPP1PPPP/R: Two pawns up and ready to castle, woohoo!
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/2pp4/3P1B2/2N5/PPP1: Let's reinforce our center with pawn to e3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/2pp4/3P1B2/2N1P3/: Black just lost the game. Knight to b5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/2n2n2/1Nppp3/3P1B2/4P3/P: Taking with the bishop or the pawn are both great options. In this course, let's take with the bishop :) Bishop takes on e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/5n2/1Nppn3/3P4/4P3/PPP2P: Now pawn captures knight on e5
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/8/1NppP3/8/4P3/PPP2PPP: OK great, another free pawn. Queen to d5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/8/1NpQP3/8/4P3/PPP2PPP: We are about to castle queenside and be unstoppable.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/8/1NppP3/4n3/4P3/PPP2PPP: Screw it. Queen sacrifice on d5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/8/1NpqP3/4n3/4P3/PPP2PPP: I think you know what comes next - knight triple fork on c7.
descriptions.r1bk1b1r/ppN2ppp/8/2pqP3/4n3/4P3/PPP2PPP: Aaaand let's take the queen with knight to d5.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3p1b2/3P1B2/2N5/PP:
Black is putting out their bishop just BEGGING for 
us to attack. Let's set it up with pawn to f3.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p1b2/3P1B2/2N2P2/: Now we hit em with the pawn to g4. Bam.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2pp1/4pnbp/3p4/3P1BPP/2N2P2/: Let's solidify our center with pawn to e3, also opening up our bishop.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/ppp2pp1/3bpnbp/3p4/3P1BPP/2N1PP2: Here, we can play the very-unique move knight to h3 to defend our bishop. If we played knight to e2, we'd block in our own bishop.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/ppp2pp1/4pnbp/3p4/3P1bPP/2N1PP1N: And take back with knight to f4! Black just helped us develop. Also now we hit the bishop
descriptions.rn1qk2r/ppp2ppb/4pn1p/3p4/3P1NPP/2N1PP2/: Now we have a killer blow here... PAWN TO G5!! So sick.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/ppp2ppb/4pn2/3p2p1/3P1N1P/2N1PP2: They took the bait and the game is now over. Pawn takes on g5.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pppn1ppb/4p3/3p2P1/3P1N2/2N1PP2/: Now we march. Pawn to g6 hitting the bishop.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pppn2pb/4p1p1/3p4/3P1N2/2N1PP2/P: Now the knight gets to eat. Knight takes on e6, hitting the queen and threatening a fork on c7.
descriptions.rnq1k2r/pppn2pb/4N1p1/3p4/3P4/2N1PP2/PPP: Let's add our other knight to the mix. Knight takes on d5.
descriptions.rnq1k2r/pppn2pb/4N1p1/3N4/3P4/4PP2/PPP5/: This is one of the most humiliating positions I have ever seen for Black.
descriptions.r1bk1b1r/ppN2ppp/8/2pqP3/6n1/4P3/PPP2PPP: Lets get that queen! Knight to d5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/8/qNpQP3/6n1/4P3/PPP2PPP: Important! The best move is to drop the knight back. Knight to c3.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/8/qNpQP3/4n3/4P3/PPP2PPP: Important! We need to block with pawn to c3 here.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp3ppp/8/qNpQPb2/4n3/2P1P3/PP3PPP: Black defended their knight but honestly, I don't care about their knight. Bishop to c4 threatening the f7 pawn.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pp3ppp/6b1/qNpQP3/2B1n3/2P1P3/PP3: Black stops one threat, but we have another. Queen takes b7.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pQ3ppp/6b1/qNp1P3/2B1n3/2P1P3/PP3: OK I don't care what your ELO is. You're winning this game lol.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pQ3ppp/8/qNp1Pbn1/2B5/2P1P3/PP3PP: What else is there to say.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/3P1B2/2N5/PPP1: Once again we jump knight to b5 here to attack c7.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/n3pn2/1N1p4/3P1B2/8/PPP: Black defended our fork, so let's continue with solid chess. Pawn to e3, defending our center and opening up our bishop.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/n1p1pn2/1N1p4/3P1B2/4P3/: Black gave us the boot. Let's drop the knight back to c3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppn2ppp/2p1pn2/3p4/3P1B2/2N1P3/: Dropping the knight so we can't double Black's pawns was Black's best move here. Let's keep developing with knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppn2ppp/2pbpn2/3p4/3P1B2/2N1PN2/: Now here we should not trade! Instead, let's launch our knight into the center with knight to e5. Our knight is going to be strong for the rest of the game.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppn2ppp/2pbpn2/3pN3/3P1B2/2N1P3: Let's continue developing with bishop to d3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppn2ppp/3bpn2/2ppN3/3P1B2/2NBP3: Trying to break into our center is Black's best try. From here we should capture with pawn to c5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppn2ppp/4pn2/2bpN3/5B2/2NBP3/PP: Best move is queen to f3, preparing to castle queenside and maybe even attack on Black's weak kingside.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppn2ppp/4pn2/2b1N3/3p1B2/2NBPQ2: Let's capture with pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppn2ppp/4pn2/4N3/3b1B2/2NB1Q2/P: Now let's set up a pin with king castles queenside.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppn2ppp/4pn2/4N3/5B2/2bB1Q2/PPP: Now we win a queen. Can you find the move? Yes, bishop to h7 check, discovering an attack on the queen.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppn2ppn/4p3/4N3/5B2/2b2Q2/PPP2P: Now rook takes queen on d8
descriptions.r1bR1rk1/ppn2ppn/4p3/4N3/5B2/2b2Q2/PPP2P: Well done! We have an incredible position here. And with our queen still on the board, I think we win this every single time
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp3ppp/4pn2/3nN3/3b1B2/2NB1Q2/P: An awful move from black. Now we have the killer bishop takes pawn on h7 with check.
descriptions.r1bq1r2/pp3ppk/4pn2/3nN3/3b1B2/2N2Q2/PPP: And the follow up: rook takes bishop on d4.
descriptions.r1bq1r2/pp3ppk/4pn2/3nN3/3R1B2/2N2Q2/PPP: I would just resign here if I were black...
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/3p4/3p1B2/2N1P3/PPP: Let's take back with our e-pawn
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/1p2pppp/p4n2/3p4/3P1B2/2N5/PPP2: They played a6 to stop our knight from coming in. Fine, let's focus on the other knight with knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/1p2pppp/p1n2n2/3p4/3P1B2/2N2N2/: Our knight's journey continues. Let's put our knight on the outpost with knight to e5.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2pppp/p1n2n2/3pNb2/3P1B2/2N5/P: Are you ready? Now we have the insanely fun pawn to g4!
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2pppp/p1n2nb1/3pN3/3P1BP1/2N5/: You can run but you can't hide. Pawn to h4 now.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2ppp1/p1n2nb1/3pN2p/3P1BPP/2N5: Yummy bishop. Knight takes on g6.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2p1p1/p1n2np1/3p3p/3P1BPP/2N5/: Black has a gross pawn structure. Let's solidify it for them so it stays gross. Pawn to g5.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2p1p1/p1n2np1/3p2Pp/3P1B1P/2N5: The position is delicious. The computer puts us at a +2 point advantage.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2pppp/p4nb1/3pn3/3P1BPP/2N5/PP: Let's take back with our pawn. Pawn to e5.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2pppp/p5b1/3pP3/4nBPP/2N5/PPP2: And now we take their knight. Knight captures on e4
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2pppp/p7/3pP3/4bBPP/8/PPP2P2/R: Now for a beautiful move, pawn to f3. Now the bishop is trapped LOL.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2pppp/p7/3pP3/4bBPP/5P2/PPP5/R: We just trapped their bishop. Black should resign here.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppn2ppp/2p1pn2/3pb3/3P1B2/2NBP3: Black taking our knight for the bishop is just a mistake. We should take back with pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppnn1ppp/2p1p3/3pP3/5B2/2NBP3/P: We forced the knight to retreat, now for Queen to h5 threatening checkmate on the next move. Black's king has no friends to help him.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppnn1p1p/2p1p1p1/3pP2Q/5B2/2NBP: Let's tuck our queen into h6.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppnn1p1p/2p1p1pQ/3pP3/5B2/2NBP3: Well done! We are strangling our opponent with this strong attack. It's not going to end well for Black.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2pp1/4pnb1/3p3p/3P1BPP/2N2P2: That just seems like an overcommitment. We play pawn to g5 here, locking in Black's weird position and kicking away the knight.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pppn1pp1/4p1b1/3p2Pp/3P1B1P/2N2: Let's strengthen our center with pawn to e3.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp1n1pp1/4p1b1/2pp2Pp/3P1B1P/2N: With the c pawn blocking out Black's dark square bishop, we get to do our favorite idea again: knight to b5, hitting the c7 square twice.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp1n1pp1/4p1b1/qNpp2Pp/3P1B1P/4P: Easy, just block with pawn to c3. Our knight is defended by our bishop
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp1n1pp1/4p1b1/qNpp2Pp/3P1B1P/2P: Well done! The computer hates Black's position. Every piece is just so passive. Despite material being equal, the computer gives us a 1.5 point advantage.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/2p2n2/3p4/3P1B2/2N5/PPP: Black is preventing our knight from ever getting to b5, sadly. Onto our next plan: pawn to e3.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp2pppp/2p2n2/3p1b2/3P1B2/2N1P3: Now we play pawn to f3, setting up pawn to e4 to attack the bishop in the future.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp3ppp/2p1pn2/3p1b2/3P1B2/2N1PP: You know what? Screw it. Pawn to g4.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp3ppp/2p1pnb1/3p4/3P1BP1/2N1PP: Black is on their heels. Let's go once more. Pawn to h4.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp3pp1/2p1pnbp/3p4/3P1BPP/2N1PP: Let's play bishop to d3 here, simply attacking their bishop.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pp3pp1/2pbpn1p/3p4/3P1BPP/2NQPP2: Let's keep our development going with knight to e2, defending our bishop
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/pp3pp1/2pbpn1p/3p4/3P1BPP/2NQPP: Castling was a mistake from black. Their kingside is so weak! Let's castle queenside.
Well done! The chess engine loves our position here. We have pieces and pawns and rooks that are about to swarm blacks king. And frankly black doesn't have the resources to defend.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp1n1pp1/n3p1b1/1Npp2Pp/3P1B1P/4: Now is a good time to make our pyramid of pawns. Pawn to c3.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pp1n1pp1/n3p1b1/1Npp2Pp/3P1B1P/2: Well done! The computer really likes our position here. Look how weak Black's pieces are.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp3ppp/n1pbpn2/3p4/3P1B2/2N1P3/P: OK Black wants to trade bishops here. Let's do it. Bishop to d6.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pp3ppp/n1pqpn2/3p4/3P4/2N1P3/PPP: And now bishop takes knight on a6 to double Black's pawns on the weak a file.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pp3ppp/B1pqpn2/3p4/3P4/2N1P3/PPP: Well done! Our position looks great.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pppn1pp1/3bp1b1/3p2Pp/3P1B1P/2N1: If Black wants to trade, they get no arguments from us. Bishop takes on d6.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pp1n1pp1/3pp1b1/3p2Pp/3P3P/2N1PP: Now we are going to develop our knight - but in a weird way. Let's go knight to h3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp1n1pp1/2npp1b1/3p2Pp/3P3P/2N1PP: And the knight completes his journey with knight to f4, hitting the bishop.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp1n1pp1/2npp1b1/3p2Pp/3P1N1P/2N1: Well done! The computer gives us the edge in this position.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp3ppp/n1p1pn2/3p4/1b1P1B2/2N1P3: Let's play bishop takes a6 to double Black's pawns on the weak a file.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp3ppp/B1p1pn2/3p4/1b1P1B2/2N1P3: Well done! Our position looks nice.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2pppp/p4n2/3pnb2/3P1BP1/2N5/PP: We want the bishop more than we want the knight. Pawn takes f5.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2pppp/p1n2n2/3p1P2/3P1B2/2N5/P: Finally, queen to d3 to defend our pawn and prepare a queenside castle.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1p2pppp/p1n2n2/3p1P2/3P1B2/2NQ4/: Although our pawn structure is kind of messed up, the computer thinks we have a great position and, after castling, life will be good.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pp3pp1/2p1pn1p/3p4/3P1bPP/2NQPP2: Of course we recapture with our knight to f4.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp1n1pp1/2p1pn1p/3p4/3P1NPP/2NQPP: Well done! We are waiting to see what side black castles and we'll start a strong attack from there.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp3pp1/2p1pnb1/3p3p/3P1BPP/2N1P: This is Black's best try. Here, we must go pawn to g5.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp3pp1/2p1pnb1/3p2Pp/3P1B1P/2N1: Well done! Both white and black played perfectly and we ended up in this fun position. Enjoy!
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/3bpn2/1N1p4/3P1B2/8/PPP1: We can trade a knight for a bishop? Sounds good to me. Knight captures on d6.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3ppp/3ppn2/3p4/3P1B2/8/PPP1PPP: Let's continue with the solid pawn to e3, stabilizing our center and preparing to develop our bishop
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp3ppp/2nppn2/3p4/3P1B2/4P3/PPP2: Let's develop our knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp3ppp/2nppn2/3p4/3P1B2/4PN2/PP: Time to make a pyramid with pawn to c3. This solidifies our center which is always a good thing.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp3ppp/2nppn2/3p4/3P1B2/2P1PN2/: Last piece to develop: bishop to e2.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp3ppp/2np1n2/3pp3/3P1B2/2P1PN2: We like our pyramid. We don't want to ruin our pyramid. So don't capture! Instead just play bishop to g5.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp3ppp/2np1n2/3pp1B1/3P4/2P1PN2: Well done! The computer likes our position against black here.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2pp1/2nbpnbp/3p4/3P1BPP/2N1PP1: As is very common in the london, let's trade off our bishops. Bishop to d3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2pp1/2nbpn1p/3p4/3P1BPP/2NbPP1: And queen takes back on d3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2pp1/2n1pn1p/3p4/3P1bPP/2NQPP1: Of course, knight takes back on f4. Thanks for the free development, Black!
descriptions.r3k2r/ppp2pp1/2nqpn1p/3p4/3P1NPP/2NQPP2/: Well done! Our king is safe.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the King's Gambit! On move 2 we'll shoot ourselves in the foot by giving away a pawn and weakening our king - but if Black doesn't know all the tricks and traps it will be us who is victorious (and suffering from an injured foot). We begin with pawn to e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Now here comes the gambit. We're going to give away our f-pawn. Pawn to f4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/4Pp2/8/PPPP2PP/RNB: They took our gambit! Now, before we can do anything else, we need to protect against Black's very annoying threat of queen to h4. We can defend against it with knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1p1p/8/6p1/4Pp2/5N2/PPPP2PP: That's a nice move by Black, defending the f4 pawn and also threatening to move their pawn to g5 and kick out our knight. I don't like them having such a good pawn. Let's attack it right away and say "hey, make a decision". Pawn to h4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp3p/5p2/6p1/4Pp1P/5N2/PPPP2P: Black chose to defend their pawn - and they made the wrong choice! Now we have the beautiful sacrifice: knight to g5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp3p/8/6p1/4Pp1P/8/PPPP2P1/RN: There is a beautiful diagonal just calling our queen's name! Queen to h5 check.
descriptions.rnbq1bnr/ppppk2p/8/6pQ/4Pp1P/8/PPPP2P1/R: Black is in for a rough time. Queen takes g5 check.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp3p/8/6Q1/4Pp1P/8/PPPP2P1/RN: King goes back to e8? Queen should go back to h5.
descriptions.rnbq1bnr/ppppk2p/8/7Q/4Pp1P/8/PPPP2P1/RN: And now we have the always nice queen to e5 check, forking the king and rook.
descriptions.rnbq1bnr/pppp1k1p/8/4Q3/4Pp1P/8/PPPP2P1/: We could just straight up win the rook, but even better is bishop to c4, checking the king once again.
descriptions.rnbq1bnr/pppp1k1p/8/4Q3/2B1Pp1P/8/PPPP2P: You probably have a forced checkmate here. At minimum you end up gobbling a few pieces and leaving their king stranded in the center of the board. Game is as good as over.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/8/4Pp2/5N2/PPPP2PP/: Instead of immediately defending their f-pawn, Black is taking their time and protecting the e5 square so our knight can't hop to it in the future. In this position we should take the center with pawn to d4.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/8/3PPpb1/5N2/PPP3PP: Mistake from black! They totally forgot about their hanging pawn. Let's take with bishop f4.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/8/3PPB2/5b2/PPP3PP/: Now Black is sending their only developed piece out to die! Obviously we take back, and it's best to take back with the queen. Queen to f3.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/8/3PPB2/5Q2/PPP3PP/: Beautiful! We are ahead in development and have the entire center.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1p1p/8/8/4PppP/5N2/PPPP2P1/: OK well we should probably move the knight. Knight to e5. This puts a double attack on the g4 pawn.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1p2/8/4N2p/4PppP/8/PPPP2P1/: This is a weak defense from Black. Sure, they saved their g4 pawn, but now we have bishop to c4 - and who will defend their f7 pawn?
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1p2/7n/4N2p/2B1PppP/8/PPPP2: Lets play pawn to d4, owning the center and threatening the f4 pawn with our bishop.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2p2/3p3n/4N2p/2BPPppP/8/PPP3: Very common response from Black, trying to kick out our knight. We'll oblige. Knight to d3 attacking the f4 pawn.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2pb1/3p3n/7p/2BPPppP/3N4/PPP3: Black is threatening our pawn on d4. We can defend it while winning back a pawn in one move. Can you find it? Hint: knight takes f4, opening up our queen.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2pb1/3p3n/7p/2BPPNpP/8/PPP3P1: We're doing great here! The material is equal but the computer loves our position.
descriptions.rnbq1b1r/ppppk2p/5n2/6Q1/4Pp1P/8/PPPP2P1: This is a nice try by Black but its not enough. Pawn to e5 and they are still miserable.
descriptions.rnbq3r/ppppk1bp/5n2/4P1Q1/5p1P/8/PPPP2P1: Um, ok? Queen takes bishop on g7.
descriptions.rnbq3r/ppppk1Qp/5n2/4P3/5p1P/8/PPPP2P1/R: You definitely got it from here.
descriptions.rnbq1bnr/pppp1k1p/8/6Q1/4Pp1P/8/PPPP2P1/: That's a free queen! Queen takes d8.
descriptions.rnbq1br1/ppppk2p/5n2/4P1Q1/5p1P/8/PPPP2P: Nice try black but no. Pawn takes knight on f6 with check. Our queen lives on for another day.
descriptions.rnbq1br1/pppp1k1p/5P2/6Q1/5p1P/8/PPPP2P1: Now we have bishop to c4 check, winning us the rook and also the game.
descriptions.rnbq1br1/ppp2k1p/5P2/3p2Q1/2B2p1P/8/PPPP: Don't let that stop us! Bishop takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.rn1q1br1/ppp2k1p/4bP2/3B2Q1/5p1P/8/PPPP2: Once more! Bishop takes bishop on e6.
descriptions.rn1q1br1/ppp4p/4kP2/6Q1/5p1P/8/PPPP2P1/R: Aaaaand now we take the rook... Queen to g8.
descriptions.rn1q1bQ1/ppp4p/4kP2/8/5p1P/8/PPPP2P1/RNB: I just don't think it can get better than that.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/4Pp2/5N2/PPPP2PP/: This time Black has decided to immediately attack our center. In this case, we should recapture with pawn takes d5.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3q4/5p2/5N2/PPPP2PP/R: Black moving their queen out so early is a big mistake! Now we can develop a piece and force the queen to move. Knight to c3.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/4q3/8/5p2/2N2N2/PPPP2PP: OK, they gave one sad check. This is a good excuse to develop yet another piece. Bishop to e2.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/3bq3/8/5p2/2N2N2/PPPPB1: That's fine. We can just castle here.
descriptions.rnb1k2r/ppp2ppp/3bqn2/8/5p2/2N2N2/PPPPB1: Ah! A blunder! Can you find the tactic? Hint: It's bishop to b5, checking the king. After they block with bishop or pawn, we win the queen.
descriptions.rn2k2r/pppb1ppp/3bqn2/1B6/5p2/2N2N2/PPPP: And they took the bait! Now rook to e4 pins the queen, and she is ours.
GG! This is a win for us.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/4q3/2b5/5p2/2N2N2/PPPPB: And yet another mistake by Black! Now we are borderline winning. Pawn to d4, hitting the enemy bishop and opening up our own bishop to recapture the pawn on f4.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2ppp/3bq3/8/3P1p2/2N2N2/PPP1: They defended the f4 pawn, but we still have plans to win it soon. For now, let's unpin ourselves by castling kingside.
descriptions.rnb1k2r/ppp2ppp/3bqn2/8/3P1p2/2N2N2/PPP1: And yet another mistake by Black! Now we have a killer tactic. Can you find it? It's tricky. Hint: bishop to b5 checking the king. Afterwards, we will skewer the enemy queen against her own king.
descriptions.rnb1k2r/pp3ppp/2pbqn2/1B6/3P1p2/2N2N2/PP: And they fell for it! Now the skewer. Rook to e1. The queen is ours.
Black is not surviving this. Good job with this tricky trap!
descriptions.rnbq1b1r/pppp1k1p/5n2/4P1Q1/5p1P/8/PPPP2: Black is delaying the inevitable. Queen to f4, repinning the knight to the king.
descriptions.rnb2b1r/ppppqk1p/5n2/4P3/5Q1P/8/PPPP2P1/: Almost there! Before we can take the knight, we need to unpin ourselves. Bishop to e2.
descriptions.rnb4r/ppppqkbp/5n2/4P3/5Q1P/8/PPPPB1P1/R: Look at this point the game is over. Yes we can take the knight and probably win. But let's let it marinate even longer by castling, pointing a battery right at the king.
Black can do nothing. Multiple pieces will be lost. Multiple tears will be shed. Multiple ELO points will be gained by you.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2p1p/3p4/4N3/4PppP/8/PPPP2P1: Time to get out of danger! Let's take our pawn back with knight g4.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2p1p/3p4/8/4PpbP/8/PPPP2P1/R: Easy choice, let's take back. Queen to g4.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2p1p/3p1n2/8/4PpQP/8/PPPP2P1: Black is trying to attack us but we have queen takes f4. Now we're the ones up a pawn!
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2p1p/2np1n2/8/4PQ1P/8/PPPP2P1: Let's develop a piece with bishop to b5, pinning their knight to their king. They have no light squared bishop to unpin!
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2p1p/2np1n2/1B6/4PQ1P/8/PPPP2: Well done! Our pawn gambit turned into a pawn gain. The computer says we have a 1 or 2 point advantage here!
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bp2/3p3n/7p/2BPPppP/3N4/PPP3: Black is attacking our h4 pawn - but don't get scared! Bishop takes f4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2p2/3p3n/7p/2BPPBpb/3N4/PPP3P: This is fine. Pawn to g3 blocking check.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2p2/3p1b1n/7p/2BPPBp1/3N2P1/P: Now we defend our center pawn with pawn to c3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2p2/3p1b1n/7p/2BPPBp1/2PN2P1/: Well done navigating through all that! For the price of one pawn, we have the complete center, tons of development, and a safe king. Sure, some play is needed to win the game, but I like our odds.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2p2/3p3n/7p/2BPP1pP/3N1p2/PP: This was Black's best move here - we're forced to capture. Pawn takes f3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2p2/3p3n/7p/2BPP2P/3N1p2/PPP: A blunder from black! After Queen takes f3, our queen is let loose on the black position and will start causing serious problems.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2p2/3p3n/7p/2BPP1bP/3N1Q2/PP: Nice try but we have the easy queen f2.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2p2/3p3n/7p/2BPP1bP/3N4/PPP2: Everything is defended in our position & we have a strong attack coming. Good job!
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/8/3PPp2/5N2/PPP3P: Simple chess. Knight to c3 to defend our e4 pawn.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/8/3PPp2/2N2N2/PPP: We have a slightly favorable position and are ready to continue the game!
descriptions.rnbqkbn1/pppp1p1r/8/4N2p/2B1PppP/8/PPPP2: Now we can play pawn to d4. We get a huge center & tons of development, all for the price of one pawn at the start.
descriptions.rnbqkbn1/ppp2p1r/3p4/4N2p/2BPPppP/8/PPP3: And now we simplify. Knight takes f7.
descriptions.rnbq1bn1/ppp2k2/3p4/7p/3PPppP/8/PPP3P1/R: Now we finally win back the pawn we lost at the start. Bishop takes f4.
descriptions.rnbq1bn1/ppp2k2/3p4/7p/3PPBpP/8/PPP3P1/R: Well done. With a better position, we are ready to continue our game.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1p1p/5n2/4N3/4PppP/8/PPPP2P: This is Black's best move, and it's actually quite challenging. We don't want to just take on g4 right away. Instead, let's play pawn up to d4 taking the center.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1p1p/8/4N3/3PnppP/8/PPP3P1/: This is too greedy from black. We have bishop to f4 here.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1p1p/8/4N3/3PnBpP/8/PPP3P1/: This is a great position for us, we are farther ahead in development and own the center. And what is Black's knight even doing?
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bp2/3p3n/7p/2BPP1pP/3N1P2/PP: Yes, Black can check us on the next move. No, we do not care (you'll see why). Let's continue our development with bishop to f4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2p2/3p3n/7p/2BPPBpb/3N1P2/PPP: Let's put on our running shoes and get our king to safety. King to d2.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2p2/2np3n/7p/2BPPBpb/3N1P2/PP: Lets defend our d pawn and make space for our king with pawn to c3.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2p2/2np1q1n/7p/2BPPBpb/2PN1P2: Finally, let's complete our king's journey with king to c2.

Look - it's a weird position. Frankly, Black played all the right moves and you don't always get a dominant position at the end of an opening. That said, our pieces are strong, developed, and in the center. Everything is defending everything else. Our king is safe. Life could be worse.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2p2/3p4/7p/4PpNP/8/PPPP2P1/R: Retreat once more! Knight to f2.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp1bp2/3p4/7p/4Pp1P/8/PPPP1NP1: Losing our pawn next is both unavoidable and fine. In the meantime, let's take the center with pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2p2/3p4/7p/3PPp1b/8/PPP2NP1/: They take our pawn? We take their pawn. Bishop to f4.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2p2/3p4/7p/3PPB2/8/PPP2bP1/R: Take back with king to f2.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2p2/3p4/7p/3PPB2/8/PPP2KP1/R: Well done! Our king loves running around in the King's Gambit, and that's totally fine! Go, little king, go.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3P4/5p2/5N2/PPPP2PP: Let's defend our central pawn with pawn to c4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/2p2n2/3P4/2P2p2/5N2/PP1P: Do not - I repeat - do not capture here! Instead of being a greedy boy/greedy girl, we should sacrifice our pawn back. Pawn to D4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/5n2/3p4/2PP1p2/5N2/PP4PP: Now we can push our c-pawn forward to c5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/5n2/2Pp4/3P1p2/5N2/PP4PP: The position is about equal and it's in your hands to win the game.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp1bp1p/3p4/8/4PpNP/8/PPPP2P1/: They want to take h4 with check. Frankly we have no good way to stop it so.... let's take the center? Pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2p1p/3p4/8/3PPpNb/8/PPP3P1/R: Come to papa little knight. Knight to f2, blocking check.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2p1p/3p4/8/3PPp2/8/PPP2bP1/R: Easy choice, take back. King to f2.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2p1p/3p4/8/3PPp2/8/PPP2KP1/R: Black played well; we played well. Black has a safe king; we have the whole center. It's going to be a good rest of the game.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2p1p/3p1n2/8/4PpNP/8/PPPP2P1: A good move from black. We should stay out of trouble and just trade here. Knight to f6.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2p1p/3p1q2/8/4Pp1P/8/PPPP2P1: Now is a good time to develop our knight. Knight to c3.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2p1p/3p1q2/8/4Pp1P/2N5/PPPP2: Another good playing from both sides. Good luck!
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2p1p/3p1n2/4N3/3PPppP/8/PPP3: Definitely Black's best responses. And honestly, we have a hole to climb out of. Knight to d3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2p1p/3p4/8/3PnppP/3N4/PPP3P1: Let's take on f4 with our bishop.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2p1p/3p4/8/3PnBpP/3N4/PPP3P1: Look it's not a great end of the opening for us... We played a risky gambit at the start of the game and the opponent played all the right moves with 100% accuracy. Very very few games end up like this. Now it's time to earn your keep and play your heart out.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2p1p/3p4/6p1/3PPp2/5N2/PPP3P: Remember - we don't like that pawn on g5. Let's hit it with pawn to h4. This should feel familiar.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2p1p/3p4/8/3PPppP/5N2/PPP3P1: We can't go forward like we're used to because of the pawn on d6. Let's instead drop our knight back home to g1. Welcome back home Mr. knight.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2p1p/3p4/8/3PPppP/8/PPP3P1/R: It's a funky position, but at the end of the day the burden is on Black to justify why they have two weak pawns on f4 and g4, and why they allowed us to take the center.

shortDescriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Let's continue with the King's Gambit.
