descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/RNB: Letâs learn the Kingâs Indian Defense! My chess coach always told me: control the center, develop your pieces, castle early. But letâs be realâthatâs soooo basic. In this opening, we flip the script. First, we rush to castle, willingly give up the center, and only then do we strike back with our pawns. This leads to extremely fun games when White plays d4. Step 1: knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppppppp/5n2/8/2PP4/8/PP2PPPP/R: There's about a million different moves White could have played here. For us, it doesn't really matter. We're going to play the same 5-or-so starting moves no matter what: First, pawn to g6 to make space for our bishop.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppppp1p/5np1/8/2PP4/2N5/PP2PPP: One last piece to develop before we can castle! Bishop to g7.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppppppbp/5np1/8/2PPP3/2N5/PP3PPP: Alright, when White plays e4, theyâre threatening to push e5 next move and go after our knightâwhich is kinda scary.  So before we castle, thereâs one last step: we play pawn to d6 to stop white from advancing any further with their e-pawn. WHENEVER White plays pawn to e4, we MUST play pawn to d6.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PPP3/2N2N2/PP: OK, we can finally castle. Woohoo. Step one of the King's Indian Defense is complete.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PPP3/2NB1N2/: A key idea in the KID is to attack the d4 pawn. White made a mistake here by bringing the bishop to d3 - they now block the queen from defending that pawn. We'll use this to our advantage. First: bishop to g4 pinning the knight to the queen, removing a defender of that d4 pawn.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PPP1b1/2NB1N: Let's trade with the knight. Bishop takes on f3.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PPP3/2NB1Q1P: Now we execute our trap: Knight to c6, targeting the now undefended d4 pawn.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1ppbp/2np1np1/8/2PPP3/2NBBQ1P: White added a defender to the d4 pawn, let's add an attacker. Knight to d7 opens up our bishop to the square.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pppnppbp/2np2p1/8/2PPP3/3BBQ1P/P: That move just lost White the game. No, seriously, the position went from equal to a +4 point advantage for us. The winning move: Moving our d7 knight to e5, forking the queen and bishop.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1ppbp/2np2p1/4P3/2P1P3/3BBQ1P: Oh no! They captured our knight, ending our fork! Nope. We can go knight to e5 AGAIN, renewing the very same fork. And this time, there is no pawn capture.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p2p1/4n3/2P1P3/3BB1QP/: Now to win our material back: Knight takes the undefended bishop on d3 with check.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p2p1/8/2P1P3/3nB1QP/PP: We are FEASTING. Knight takes the b2 pawn next.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p2p1/8/2P1P3/4B1QP/Pn1: Well done! The game is essentially over.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PPP3/2N2N2/P: The point of the KID is to give white the center, then fight back after we castle our king. We can fight back with two possible pawn-breaks: pawn to c5 or pawn to e5. In THIS position, it's best to go pawn to e5. Yes, you'll have to memorize a couple of these things but, hey, what are you on this website for anyways?
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2pbp/3p1np1/4p3/2PPP3/2N2N2/: White ignored our pawn break and just castled. Well, let's do something they can't ignore: pawn takes on d4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2pbp/3p1np1/8/2PNP3/2N5/PP2B: Let's put our rook on e8, so it can stare down at the e4 pawn. We have two attackers on the e4 pawn, so White will have to defend. See how we're taking control of the game now?
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/ppp2pbp/3p1np1/8/2PNP3/2N2P2/PP: White defended their pawn, but in doing so they just opening up a diagonal line of sight to their king. Yikes. Let's take advantage of this and play pawn to c6, hoping to play queen to b6 on the next move to pin the knight to the king. The other idea with our pawn to c6 move is we are setting up pawn to d5 in the future to smash open the center.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pbp/2pp1np1/8/2PNP3/2N1BP2/P: And THIS was the wrong response from white. They defended that diagonal to the king, sure, but their bishop is undefended and remember: our rook is staring down the e-file. If we smash open the center now, odds are we can take that undefended bishop after some pawn captures. Pawn to d5.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pbp/2p2np1/3P4/3NP3/2N1BP2/P: Remember how blacks's dark-squared bishop is undefended behind that e-pawn? Well now we have the awesome sacrifice Knight takes d5. We're taking advantage that White cannot capture back because otherwise our rook takes their bishop.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pbp/2p3p1/3n4/3NP3/2N2P2/PP2: White backed up, telling us: Hey, let's slow things down a little. Our response: No. Let's go knight to f4, attacking the OTHER bishop.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pbp/2p3p1/8/2BNPn2/2N2P2/PP3: White keeps running their bishops away, but they're missing the bigger picture. Queen to g5, threatening checkmate in 1! White has to be careful or they'll lose their king very very quickly.
descriptions.rnb1r1k1/pp3pbp/2p3p1/6q1/2BNPn2/2N2PB1/: Remember how a long time ago, White opening up a diagonal to their king, and we wanted to pin the knight to the king with our queen? Well - with the bishop no longer controlling that diagonal, we finally can. Queen to c5!
descriptions.rnb1r1k1/pp3pbp/2p3p1/2q5/2BNPn2/2N2PB1/: Well done! We left our knight to die, but we are completely winning here because we'll actually get TWO pieces back. In our next moves, we'll take the knight on d4 with our bishop with check, then proceed to take the c4 bishop. Because we end a piece up, the computer gives us a +3 point advantage.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PPPP2/2N5/PP4: White is playing the "Four Pawns Attack". The name is a bit on the nose, but the threat is very real. White has taken the entire center and has full control over the middle of the board... for now. If we play this right, White will lose because they overextended and have too many weak squares. First things first, lets castle.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PPPP2/2N2N2/: Time to take back the center. Pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/2pP4/2P1PP2/2N2N: White wants a stable center, we don't. Remember, its WHITE's king thats still in the middle of the board. Let's try another pawn break pawn to e6.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3ppnp1/2pP4/2P1PP2/2NB1N: Let's open up the center. Pawn to d5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/4PP2/2NB1N2/: Here, let's play pawn to b5, completely taking all the queenside space. Yes - if you're paying attention - we are sacrificing the b-pawn with that move.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p4pbp/3p1np1/1NpP4/4PP2/3B1N2/P: With the knight no longer defending the e4 pawn, lets add an attacker to it. Rook to e8. This also creates a pin on the king that will come in handy very soon.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/p4pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/4PP2/2NB1N2/P: White returned the knight to defend the e4 pawn, but let's capture the pawn anyways. Knight to e4.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/p4pbp/3p2p1/2pP4/4NP2/3B1N2/PP4: It looks like we just lost a piece, but we have one move here that wins it back. Pawn to f5, attacking the pinned knight.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/p5bp/3p2p1/2pP1p2/4NP2/3B1N2/PP: Not only will we win our material back, this position is very hard to hold on to as White. In fact, we're winning from here like 75% of the time, and the computer gives us a big advantage.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2pbp/3p1np1/4P3/2P1P3/2N2N2/: White captured our pawn - now we capture back. Pawn takes e5.
descriptions.rnbQ1rk1/ppp2pbp/5np1/4p3/2P1P3/2N2N2/PP: Rook takes back, of course. Rook to d8.
descriptions.rnbr2k1/ppp2pbp/5np1/4N3/2P1P3/2N5/PP2BP: It looks like we just lost a pawn, but we have an easy way to win one back. Knight takes on e4 "sacrificing" our knight but now our bishop stares at their knight.
descriptions.rnbr2k1/ppp2Nbp/6p1/8/2P1n3/2N5/PP2BPPP/: White tried a "Desperado" (in chess it means they know they're losing material, so they're desperate). With our rook under attack we only have one choice... Bishop takes knight on c3 with check.
descriptions.rnbr2k1/ppp2N1p/6p1/8/2P1n3/2P5/P3BPPP/R: Now we get the knight for free. King takes on f7.
descriptions.rnbr4/ppp2k1p/6p1/8/2P1n3/2P5/P3BPPP/R1B: Well done!! We are simply up a piece and will win this game.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/4P3/2PP1P2/2N5/: White marches on! Here, capture with pawn to e5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/5np1/4P3/2PP4/2N5/PP4P: Now we drop our knight back to d7 to add a ton of pressure to the e5 pawn. On the next move, we'll try to destabilize white's position even further.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pppnppbp/6p1/4P3/2PP4/2N2N2/PP4: Now to destabilize the center: pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp1nppbp/6p1/2p1P3/2PP4/2N1BN2/: With our king safe and White's king in the middle of the board, clearing out the center can only help us. Pawn takes on d4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp1nppbp/6p1/4P3/2PB4/2N2N2/PP4: Oh no - White's position is a disaster. Now we have the simple but deadly knight to c6 hitting the e5 pawn and the bishop.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp1nppbp/2n3p1/4P3/2PB4/2N2N2/P: Let's chop, chop, chop. Knight takes bishop on d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp1nppbp/6p1/4P3/2PQ4/2N2N2/PP2: Now knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1bQ1rk1/pp2ppbp/6p1/4n3/2P5/2N2N2/PP2B1: Rook takes back on d8, of course.
descriptions.r1br2k1/pp2pp1p/6p1/4b3/2P5/2N5/PP2B1PP/: Well done! We're in an endgame up a pawn, with a safer king, and more developed pieces. The computer gives us a +4 point advantage and we win here over 70% of the time.
descriptions.rnb1r1k1/pp3pbp/2p3p1/6q1/2BNP3/2N2PPn/P: Well done! In a second we'll grab the bishop and move our rook to d8 to pin the knight to the queen. The computer gives us a +2 point advantage.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p4pbp/3p1np1/1ppP4/4PP2/2NB1N2/: They ignored us? Let's keep storming down. Pawn to c4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p4pbp/3p1np1/1p1P4/2p1PP2/2N2N2: We don't stop now. Pawn to b4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p4pbp/3p1np1/3P4/1pp1PP2/5N2/PP: Let's attack that weak e4 pawn with rook to e8.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/p4pbp/3p1np1/3P4/1pp1PP2/5N2/PP: Well done! The computer gives us a +1 point advantage and we win over 60% of our games from here.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PPP3/2N2P2/PP: This is called the SÃ¤misch Variation. Don't ask me how to pronounce that. Let's castle.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PPP3/2N1BP2/: Before white has a chance to castle queenside, we're going to strike back in the center. Pawn to c5. This is the SÃ¤misch gambit.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/2pP4/2P1P3/2N1BP: White tried to shut down the center, but we have another pawn break up our sleeve. Pawn to e6. We want to open up the center while White's king is still there.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3ppnp1/2pP4/2P1P3/2N1BP2: Let's crack that center open. Pawn takes on d5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/4P3/2N1BP2/P: We know White wants to castle queenside here. Let's just set up a pawn storm now. Pawn to a6.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/1p3pbp/p2p1npB/2pP4/4P3/2N2P2/P: We have a move we've seen a couple times already in the KID: sacrificing our knight on e4. We want to open up our queen - you'll see why in a second.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/1p3pbp/p2p2pB/2pP4/4N3/5P2/PP1Q: Now with our queen opened up, we get queen to h4 check, forking the king and bishop. Now do you see the point?
descriptions.rnb2rk1/1p3pbp/p2p2pB/2pP4/4N2q/5PP1/PP1: Queen drops down and wins the bishop. Queen to h6.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/1p3pbp/p2p2pQ/2pP4/4N3/5PP1/PP5P: Of course, bishop takes back on h6.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/1p3p1p/p2N2pb/2pP4/8/5PP1/PP5P/R: Lastly, let's develop our knight to d7.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1p1n1p1p/p2N2pb/2pP4/8/5PP1/PP5P: Well done! The computer gives us a +1 point advantage even though material is equal, and black wins SEVENTY percent of games here. Our safe king  and better pawn structure will give us the edge.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p4pbp/3p1np1/1BpP4/4PP2/2N2N2/P: We sacrificed our pawn, now we sacrifice our knight with knight to e4. Don't worry, we have a tactic to win back our material.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p4pbp/3p2p1/1BpP4/4NP2/5N2/PP4P: Now for our tactic: Queen to a5 check, forking the king and bishop.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/p4pbp/3p2p1/qBpP4/5P2/2N2N2/PP4P: That won't stop us LOL. Bishop takes knight on c3.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/p4p1p/3p2p1/qBpP4/5P2/2P2N2/P5PP: Now we finally get our material back. Queen takes bishop on b5.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/p4p1p/3p2p1/1qpP4/5P2/2P2N2/P5PP: Well done! We have a safe king, a crushing queen, and are preventing white from castling. All of this means that we win 70% of the time from here, and the computer loves our position.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/1p3pbp/p2p1np1/2pP4/4P3/2N1BP2/: This was a bad move from white. Now we have pawn to b5, storming down.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/5pbp/p2p1npB/1ppP4/4P3/2N2P2/PP: We continue our pawn storm. Pawn to b4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/5pbp/p2p1npB/2pP4/1p2P3/2N2P2/P: Well done!! Our attacking marching down the board - and the computer gives us an advantage for it.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/2P5/2N1BP2/P: White took back with the wrong pawn. Now we have rook to e8, pinning the bishop to the king.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/2P5/2N1BP2/P: Well done! White will probably castle out of the pin, but we own a very powerful file now.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp1nppbp/6p1/2pPP3/2P5/2N2N2/PP: Huh, white just gave us a pawn. I don't have any problems with that. Knight takes on e5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2pp1p/6p1/2pPb3/2P5/2N5/PP4PP: Well done! We're up a pawn, the computer gives us a +1 point advantage, and Black wins most of the time from here.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/8/2PPP3/2N1B3/P: Once again, we want to crash the center. Pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/2P5/2P1P3/2N1B3/: Instead of capturing back right away, let's play queen to a5 to attack c5 and pin the knight to the king. With the knight pinned to the king, e4 is no longer protected.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/pp2ppbp/3P1np1/q7/2P1P3/2N1B3/PP: Forget about that pawn, let's play knight takes e4. Remember, the e4 pawn is unprotected due to the pin on the knight.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/pp2Ppbp/6p1/q7/2P1n3/2N1B3/PP2BP: Rook to e8 - I'm bold but not bold enough to let white make a queen.
descriptions.rnb1r1k1/pp2Ppbp/6p1/q7/2P1n3/2N1B3/PP2B: Well done! Even though we're down a pawn or two, our position is so active and developed that we will win our material back and still be compensated with a good position. Black wins over 2/3 games from here.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/2P5/2P1P3/2N1BP2: White accepted our gambit - we take back with pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnbr2k1/pp2ppbp/5np1/2B5/2P1P3/2N2P2/PP4: White won a pawn - hence the "gambit". That's fine. First things first, knight to c6 to defend our e7 pawn.
descriptions.r1br2k1/pp2ppbp/2n2np1/2B5/2P1P3/2N2P2/P: Let's trade rooks here - rook takes on d1.
descriptions.r1b3k1/pp2ppbp/2n2np1/2B5/2P1P3/2N2P2/PP: Our goal: capture that pawn on c4. The method: swing our f6 knight over to get there. The first step: Knight to d7, hitting the bishop.
descriptions.r1b3k1/pp1nppbp/2n3p1/8/2P1P3/B1N2P2/PP4: Let's damage White's pawn structure here with bishop takes knight on c3. Usually we don't want to trade bishops for knights, but in this case it's worth it because we make White have double isolated pawns on the c-file.
descriptions.r1b3k1/pp1npp1p/2n3p1/8/2P1P3/B1P2P2/P5P: Back to our plan: Let's move our d7 knight to e5 to attack that weak c4 pawn.
descriptions.r1b3k1/pp2pp1p/2n3p1/4n3/2P1PP2/B1P5/P5P: White attacked our knight but I'm not one to retreat my pieces. Onwards! Knight to g4, threatening a fork.
descriptions.r1b3k1/pp2pp1p/2n3p1/8/2P1PPn1/B1P5/P3K1: With the White king blocking the light-squared bishop from defending the c4 pawn, now is the perfect time to try and capture that c4 pawn again. Bishop to e6.
descriptions.r5k1/pp2pp1p/2n1b1p1/8/2P1PPn1/B1P5/P3K1: Well done! Our pieces are developed, active, and coordinated, and we will likely win our pawn back.
descriptions.r1b3k1/pp1nppbp/2n3p1/8/2P1P3/2N1BP2/PP4: Let's damage White's pawn structure here with bishop takes knight on c3. Usually we don't want to trade bishops for knights, but in this case it's worth it because we make White have double isolated pawns on the c-file.
descriptions.r1b3k1/pp1npp1p/2n3p1/8/2P1P3/2P1BP2/P5P: Let's continue our plan: d7 knight to e5 threatening capture of the c4 pawn.
descriptions.r1b3k1/pp2pp1p/2n3p1/4n3/2P1P3/2P1BP2/P5: Well done! Black wins over 60% of the time here, and we will likely win the c4 pawn soon after adding another attacker or two.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3ppnp1/2pP4/2P1PP2/2N2N2: Let's break open the center with pawn to d5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/2P2P2/2N2N2/: This is a mistake from white - they completely weakened their kingside. Here' lets develop quickly with bishop to f5.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP1b2/2P2P2/2N2N: Now we launch our knight to e4.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/pp3pbp/3p2p1/2pP4/2P1bP2/3B1N2/: Here, it's best to capture the knight on f3 instead of the bishop on d3. We want to leave white with their bad light-square bishop. It's bad because all their pawns are already on light squares so the bishop doesn't do much. Bishop takes knight on f3.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/pp3pbp/3p2p1/2pP4/2P2P2/3B1Q2/P: Let's develop our knight to d7.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp1n1pbp/3p2p1/2pP4/2P2P2/3B1Q2/: Well done! We are in a great spot here, and Black wins most of the time from this position. Look how powerful our dark-squared diagonal is!
descriptions.r1br2k1/pp2ppbp/2n2np1/2B5/2P1P3/2N2P2/P: Our target is the pawn on c4. Let's play pawn to b6 to gain a tempo and open up our light squared bishop.
descriptions.r1br2k1/p3ppbp/1pn2np1/8/2P1P3/B1N2P2/PP: Now we continue: Bishop to a6, hitting the pawn.
descriptions.r2r2k1/p3ppbp/bpn2np1/8/2P1P3/B1N2P2/PP2: Well done! The computer puts this position as equal despite us being a pawn down because of our strong bishops and ownership of the d-file.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/2p5/2PPP3/2N1BP2: White completely ignored our pawn break. Here, the best way to play is to develop your queen to a5, getting a nice pin on the c3 knight.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/q1p5/2PPP3/2N1BP2: White is essentially telling us they plan to castle queenside. With that in mind, let's continue developing with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pp2ppbp/2np1np1/q1p5/2PPP3/2N1BP: It would be nice to attack that weak c4 pawn. Ideally we can do that by putting our bishop on a6. So, let's make a pathway for our bishop to get there: pawn to b6.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p3ppbp/1pnp1np1/q1p5/2PPP3/2N1BP: Continue with our plan: bishop to a6, attacking the very weak c4 pawn.
descriptions.r4rk1/p3ppbp/bpnp1np1/q1p5/2PPP3/2N1BP2/: Well done! Black wins over 66% of the time from here.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2pbp/3p1np1/3Pp3/2P1P3/2N2N2: White pushing to d5 shut down the center, but created a nice spot for our knight on c5. Our goal is to rotate our b-knight to c5 where he can't be bothered. The only way White can prevent our knight on c5 is with pawn to b4, so let's prevent that pawn move with pawn to a5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/1pp2pbp/3p1np1/p2Pp3/2P1P3/2N2N: White castled without putting up a fight, so now we can continue with our plan of getting our knight to c5. Step 1: Knight to a6
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp2pbp/n2p1np1/p2Pp3/2P1P3/P1N: Let's continue with our plan: Knight to c5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp2pbp/3p1np1/p1nPp3/2P1P3/P1N: You know what's better than our knight on c5? Our knight on b3. But before we can plant it there, we need to defend the b3 square so the queen doesn't capture. Pawn to a4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp2pbp/3p1np1/2nPp3/p1P1P3/P1N: And now our knight marches forward! Knight to b3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp2pbp/3p1np1/3Pp3/p1P1P3/PnN1: Well done! Our knight is a monster on that square.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/3p1np1/6B1/2PPP3/2N5/P: With our king safe and White's king in the middle, let's crash open the center. Pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/2pP2B1/2P1P3/2N5: Don't let White stabilize the center. Pawn to e6, trying to pawn break once again.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3ppnp1/2pP2B1/2P1P3/2N5/: Let's capture with pawn to d5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP2B1/2P5/2N5/PP: Let's play queen to b6, getting out of the pin and putting pressure on White's b2 pawn.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/pp3pbp/1q1p1np1/2pP2B1/2P5/2N2N2: Let's continue developing. Bishop to f5.
descriptions.rn3rk1/pp3pbp/1q1p1np1/2pP1bB1/2P5/2N2N2: Now that the bishop is on f5, we can launch our knight to the center of the board with knight to e4, hitting the queen.
descriptions.rn3rk1/pp3pbp/1q1p2p1/2pP1bB1/2P1N3/5N2/: Capture back with bishop to e4 of course.
descriptions.rn3rk1/pp3pbp/1q1p2p1/2pP2B1/2P1b3/5N2/P: Well done! The position is equal and we are ready to play a game of chess!
descriptions.rnbr2k1/ppp2pbp/5np1/4p1B1/2P1P3/2N2N2/P: Let's continue developing. Bishop to e6.
descriptions.rn1r2k1/ppp2pbp/4bnp1/4N1B1/2P1P3/2N5/PP: We lost a pawn but our position is still fine, as long as we chase away the bishop - and we need to do it NOW. Otherwise, pawns will rain down from white's kingside. Pawn to h6.
descriptions.rn1r2k1/ppp2pb1/4bnpp/4N3/2P1P2B/2N5/PP2: Now pawn to g5. Go away, bishop.
descriptions.rn1r2k1/ppp2pb1/4bn1p/4N1p1/2P1P3/2N3B1/: Now we play knight to a6. This one I... I don't really know why? But the computer says its the only move to keep our advantage so let's just play it.
descriptions.r2r2k1/ppp2pb1/n3bn1p/4N1p1/2P1P3/2N3B1/: Well done! Black wins over 70% of their games from here!!
descriptions.rnbr2k1/ppp2pbp/6p1/4N3/2P1N3/8/PP2BPPP/: Bishop takes back on e5. The material stays equal.
descriptions.rnbr2k1/ppp2p1p/6p1/4b3/2P1N3/8/PP2BPPP/: Well done! We're doing very well here.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pbp/6p1/3p4/3NP3/4BP2/PP2B1P: Well done! Black wins 60% of the time here because of how misplaced their pieces are and the pressure coming down the diagonal from our bishop and down files from our rook and queen.
descriptions.r1br2k1/pp2ppbp/2n2np1/2BN4/2P1P3/5P2/PP: With white's knight out of the way, we can active our bishop with knight to d7. This opens up our bishop to stare at the undefended b2 pawn. We are technically gambiting our own e7 pawn here but we will win it back very shortly.
descriptions.r1br2k1/pp1nBpbp/6p1/8/2P1P3/5P2/PP4PP/R: White won a pawn and attacks our rook? We win a pawn and attack White's rook. Bishop takes on b2.
descriptions.r1br2k1/pp1nBp1p/6p1/8/2P1P3/5P2/Pb4PP/R: Well done! The position is equal and we are ready to continue our game.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/1p3pbp/p2p1np1/2pP4/P3P3/2N1BP2: White played a4 to stop our pawn from going to b5, so I guess our pawn storm idea is over right? WRONG. Queen to a5, basically saying "I'm going to go b5 on the next move anyways".
descriptions.rnb2rk1/1p3pbp/p2p1np1/q1pP4/P3P3/2NBBP2: Now we continue our plan of the pawns. Pawn to b5.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/5pbp/p2p1np1/qppP4/P3P3/2NBBP2/1: Don't stop now! Pawn to b4.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/5pbp/p2p1np1/q1pP4/Pp2P3/3BBP2/1: Finally, we want to develop our knight. Knight to d7.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/3n1pbp/p2p1np1/q1pP4/Pp2P3/3BBP2: Well done! Look how cramped White's position is here.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3pPnp1/2p5/2P1PP2/2N2N2/: We could take back with bishop or the pawn, but in this case, taking back with pawn to e6 is best. It opens up our rook and we'll have ideas to target that f4 pawn in the near future.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp4bp/3ppnp1/2p5/2P1PP2/2NB1N2/: Let's continue developing with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp4bp/2nppnp1/2p5/2P1PP2/2NB1N2: The power move here is planting our knight on d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp4bp/3ppnp1/2p5/2PNPP2/2NB4/PP: We need to take back with pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp4bp/3ppnp1/1N6/2PpPP2/3B4/PP4: It looks like our pawn structure is broken but all we need to do to fix it is play pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp4bp/3p1np1/1N2P3/2PpP3/3B4/PP: Now pawn captures back on e5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp4bp/5np1/1NP1p3/3pP3/3B4/PP4P: White's pawn push opened up a diagonal line of sight to our king. If we're not careful, White could have some nasty checking ideas with their light-squared bishop or queen. Let's develop our last minor piece and defend that diagonal with bishop to e6.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp4bp/4bnp1/1NP1p3/3pP3/3B4/PP4P: Well done! the position is equal and now we get to play chess.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/q1P5/2P1P3/2N1BP2: Now that the e4 pawn is defended again, let's just capture back with pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/pp2ppbp/5np1/q1p5/2P1P3/2N1BP2/P: Well done! The position is equal.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/1pp2pbp/3p1np1/p2Pp1B1/2P1P3/2N: White is pinning our knight to our queen, which is annoying. Let's play pawn to h6 to kick it out.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/1pp2pb1/3p1npp/p2Pp3/2P1P2B/2N2: If we played pawn to g5 to attack the bishop further, we would be overextending. Here, I recommend continuing with our plan of getting our knight to c5 and going knight to a6.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp2pb1/n2p1npp/p2Pp3/2P1P2B/2N: White has no way to stop knight to c5, so there's no need to rush. Let's move our queen out of the pin first with Queen to e8.
descriptions.r1b1qrk1/1pp2pb1/n2p1npp/p2Pp3/2P1P2B/2N: Getting the f5 pawn push is crucial in this position. That's why here, we drop our knight back to h7 to make space for the f-pawn to go forward.
descriptions.r1b1qrk1/1pp2pbn/n2p2pp/p2Pp3/2P1P2B/2N5: Well done! We are ready to continue our game.
descriptions.r1br2k1/pp1nNpbp/6p1/8/2P1P3/5P2/PP4PP/R: King to f8, threatening the knight and gaining a tempo
descriptions.r1br1k2/pp1n1pbp/6p1/3N4/2P1P3/5P2/PP4PP: Bishop wins our pawn back with bishop to b2.
descriptions.r1br1k2/pp1n1p1p/6p1/3N4/2P1P3/5P2/Pb4PP: Well done! We have an equal position here.
descriptions.rnb2rk1/1p3pbp/p2p1np1/q1pP4/P3P3/R1N1BP: With the rook now defended on a3, the pawn on a4 is no longer pinned and we can't play pawn to b5. So, let's just develop. Knight from b8 to d7.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1p1n1pbp/p2p1np1/q1pP4/P3P3/R1N1: Well done! In the future we will set up the f5 pawn break.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/4PP2/2N2N2/P: We need to keep developing. Next up is our bishop: bishop to g4. We do bishop first because if we moved the knight out to d7, it would block in our bishop. Bishop to g4.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/4PPb1/2N2N2/: Now we develop our last minor piece. Knight to d7.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp1n1pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/4PPb1/2N2N1: Bishop takes knight on f3. If we try retreating instead, our bishop would get trapped on the next move.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp1n1pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/4PP2/2N2B1P: Let's slide our rook over to e8 and put pressure on the weak e4 pawn.
descriptions.r2qr1k1/pp1n1pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/4PP2/2N2B1P: Well done! The position is equal and we are ready to play a game of chess!
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pbp/2pp1np1/8/2PNP3/2N2P2/PP: After the king moves off the diagonal, it's best to play b-knight to d7. At some point we'll play pawn to d5, but not quite yet.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp1n1pbp/2pp1np1/8/2PNPB2/2N2P2: White is attacking our pawn, and here we have the very fun move knight to h5, baiting them into taking that pawn.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp1n1pbp/2pB2p1/7n/2PNP3/2N2P2/: Yes we sacrificed a pawn, but in return we'll get a great position. Queen to f6, hitting both the bishop and knight.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp1n1pbp/2pB1qp1/7n/2P1P3/1NN2P: White just defended their bishop by moving their knight, clearing the way for their queen. For us, thereâs only one move hereâknight to f4. In the KID, we love launching our knights straight at the White king.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp1n1pbp/2pB1qp1/8/2P1Pn2/1NN2P: Well done! We have a solid position and will take white's light-square bishop on the next move.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/2pP4/2P1P3/2N1B3: We don't want to let White stabilize the center. Pawn to e6.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3ppnp1/2pP4/2P1P3/2N1BN2: If White doesn't take us, we'll take white. Pawn takes on d5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/4P3/2N1BN2/P: Rook to e8, targeting that weak e4 pawn.
descriptions.rnbqr1k1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2pP4/4P3/2N1BN2/P: Well done! The position is equal and we are ready to start playing chess!
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp1n1pbp/2pp1np1/6B1/2PNP3/2N2P: The plan is simple: pawn to h6 to attack their bishop.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp1n1pb1/2pp1npp/6B1/2PNP3/2N2P: Well done! The position is equal and its time to play chess.
descriptions.rnbr2k1/ppp2pbp/5np1/3Np3/2P1P3/5N2/PP2B: Here's a fun one: the knight is attacking our c7 pawn. We are going to defend it with... rook to d7. It looks weird but it leads into a really fun line.
descriptions.rnb3k1/pppr1pbp/5np1/3NN3/2P1P3/8/PP2BPP: Oh no! Our rook is attacked. Why the heck did we move our rook to d7 in the first place??? Well, now we have the awesome rook sacrifice with knight takes on d5.
descriptions.rnb3k1/pppN1pbp/6p1/3n4/2P1P3/8/PP2BPPP/: Our knight is hanging and we're down material. What do we do? The killer knight to b4 threatening a fork on c2.
descriptions.rNb3k1/ppp2pbp/6p1/8/1nP1P3/8/PP2BPPP/R1: Knight to c2, forking the king and rook.
descriptions.rNb3k1/ppp2pbp/6p1/8/2P1PB2/8/PP2BPPP/n2: Our rook takes that poor trapped knight now. Rook to b8.
descriptions.1rb3k1/ppp2pbp/6p1/8/2P1PB2/8/PP2BPPP/n2: Well done! Black wins most of the games from here!

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the London system! Before we get started, I have to warn you: this opening is basically the same 5 boring moves over and over and nobody will be your friend. If you're ok with that, then let's get started with pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3p4/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/R: By the way - it's not too late to turn back! You can return to the home page and learn literally any other opening!! Still here? OK... second move of the london is bishop to f4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/3P1B2/8/PPP1PPP: We'll continue with our regular london system: pawn to e3.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/3bp3/3p4/3P1B2/4P3/PPP2: Black has abandoned the guard of the g7 pawn - let's play queen to g4 to attack it.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/3P1bQ1/4P3/PPP2: Black has BLUNDERED! And this was their most common move too!! Before we recapture the bishop, we can takes a free pawn with queen to g7
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp2pQp/4pq2/3p4/3P1b2/4P3/PPP2: Before we take back the bishop, let's trade queens. Queen takes queen on f6.
descriptions.rnb1k2r/ppp2p1p/4pn2/3p4/3P1b2/4P3/PPP2P: NOW we can finally take back the bishop -  pawn to f4.
descriptions.rnb1k2r/ppp2p1p/4pn2/3p4/3P1P2/8/PPP2PPP: A free pawn is a free pawn!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp1p1pp/5p2/3p4/3P1B2/8/PPP1PP: Regular london stuff: pawn to e3.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp3pp/5p2/3pp3/3P1B2/4P3/PPP2P: Black just... gave us a free pawn? It looks weird but this has happened in over a million games. Pawn takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp3pp/8/3pp3/5B2/4P3/PPP2PPP/R: Instead of bishop taking back - we have an even better move! Queen to h5 check
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp4p/6p1/3pp2Q/5B2/4P3/PPP2PPP: now QUEEN takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp4p/6p1/3pQ3/5B2/4P3/PPP2PPP/: Black just lost the game in like 5 moves hahaha
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3p1b2/3P1B2/8/PPP1PP: When black breaks out the symmetrical bishop variation, I recommend breaking OUT of the traditional london setup and instead going for something they probably haven't seen before: pawn to c4.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/5b2/2pP1B2/8/PP2PPPP: It looks like we just gave black a free pawn - but they're going to have a hard time holding onto it. Pawn to e3 opens up our light-squared bishop to attack their c4 pawn.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/p1p1pppp/8/1p3b2/2pP1B2/4P3/PP3: Black tried to hold onto their pawn but it's actually a huge BLUNDER. We have the very-cool queen to f3 here, hitting black's rook.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/p3pppp/2p5/1p3b2/2pP1B2/4PQ2/PP: Black blocked our attack on their rook but now we have an even BETTER idea: bishop takes knight on b8, discovering an attack on the undefended f5 bishop.
descriptions.1r1qkbnr/p3pppp/2p5/1p3b2/2pP4/4PQ2/PP3P: Free bishop? Free bishop! Queen takes bishop on f5.
descriptions.1r1qkbnr/p3pppp/2p5/1p3Q2/2pP4/4P3/PP3PP: A pawn for a bishop - that's a good trade
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3p4/3P1B2/8/PPP1PP: The next normal london move is pawn to e3
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/5n2/2pp4/3P1B2/4P3/PPP2: When black goes for the c5 pawn-break here, I actually like breaking AWAY from our normal london setup and instead playing knight to c3. This is setting up a deadly trap that most of our opponents will fall for...
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/2pp4/3P1B2/2N1P3/: Black's most common move here is actually a BLUNDER. Now we can hop our knight into b5 and set up a knight fork on c7.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/2n2n2/1Nppp3/3P1B2/4P3/P: Taking with the bishop or the pawn are both great options. In this course, let's take with the bishop :) Bishop takes on e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/5n2/1Nppn3/3P4/4P3/PPP2P: Pawn takes knight on e5, of course.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/8/1NppP3/4n3/4P3/PPP2PPP: Now we have an incredible sequence that will win us another pawn and a crushing position. First step: queen SACRIFICE on d5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/8/1NpqP3/4n3/4P3/PPP2PPP: Do you see how we can win our queen back? Hint: Knight to c7 forking the king and queen.
descriptions.r1bk1b1r/ppN2ppp/8/2pqP3/4n3/4P3/PPP2PPP: We need to win our queen back, so knight takes queen on d5 of course.
descriptions.r2k1b1r/pp3ppp/4b3/2pNP3/4n3/4P3/PPP2PPP: There's a few different ways we can protect/save our knight here. I recommend the simple pawn to c4 to lock in black's position.
descriptions.r2k1b1r/pp3ppp/4b3/2pNP3/2P1n3/4P3/PP3PP: Well done! We are +4 on the eval-bar and the only thing to keep in mind is to NOT castle queenside because black's knight is eyeing our f2 pawn.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/8/2pp4/3P1B2/8/PPP1PPPP: Black is offering us a free pawn - but we shouldn't actually take it. If we do, we'll lose the center and black will pretty easily regain the pawn again. Instead, let's continue with our normal london setup: pawn to e3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2n5/2pp4/3P1B2/4P3/PPP2: Normally we play pawn to c3 here (and thatâs perfectly fine), but thereâs another option â a trap that HALF your opponents will fall for: knight to c3. Our goal is to get our knight onto c7 and fork black.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/2pp4/3P1B2/2N1P3/: OUR OPPONENT FELL FOR OUR TRAP!! Knight to b5 immediately, threatening knight fork to c7. Black is going to lose material here. By the way, this position actually transposes into a line from the Jobava London course â one of my personal favorites on the site. If youâre enjoying this position, youâll definitely love the Jobava London course.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp2pppp/2n2n2/qNpp4/3P1B2/4P3/P: Pawn to c3, blocking the check. Our threat on c7 remains.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/2n2n2/qNppp3/3P1B2/2P1P3: We can win a pawn (and a good position) by playing bishop takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/5n2/qNppn3/3P4/2P1P3/PP3: Pawn takes knight on e5, of course.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp1n1ppp/8/qNppP3/8/2P1P3/PP3PP: Our e5 pawn is under attack! We can defend it AND win a pawn of our own with queen to d5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp1n1ppp/8/qNpQP3/8/2P1P3/PP3PP: We have the center. We have more development. We have a safer king. We have 2 of our opponent's pawns. We have a 3 point eval advantage.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp1pppp/2n5/3p4/3P1B2/8/PPP1PP: We'll continue with our normal london setup: pawn to e3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp1p1pp/2n2p2/3p4/3P1B2/4P3/PP: Black went pawn to f6 to prepare pawn to e5 on the next move. Let's go knight to f3 to fight back for that e5 square.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp3pp/2n2p2/3pp3/3P1B2/4PN2/PP: Black miscounted: they have 2 defenders on the e5 pawn, but we have 3 attackers. That means we're going to win material. Pawn takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/3pp3/5B2/4PN2/PPP2PP: Next: knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp3pp/8/3pn3/5B2/4P3/PPP2PPP/R: Finally: bishop takes knight on e5.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3p1b2/3P1B2/4P3/PP: When black goes for the symmetrical bishop variation, we should always look for that deadly c4 pawn break. Pawn to c4.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p1b2/2PP1B2/4P3/P: So what's our main idea with our c4 pawn break? Taking advantage that black's bishop is no longer defending the b7 pawn. Queen to b3 to attack that b7 pawn.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/p1p2ppp/1p2pn2/3p1b2/2PP1B2/1Q2: We'll continue with more development: knight to c3.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/p1p1bppp/1p2pn2/3p1b2/2PP1B2/1QN: Black wasted a move by moving their bishop to e7 - we can take advantage and likely just win the game right here. First: pawn takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/p1p1bppp/1p3n2/3p1b2/3P1B2/1QN1P: Now the killer knight to b5, eyeing that c7 square.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/p1p2ppp/1p1b1n2/1N1p1b2/3P1B2/1Q: Black added a defender - let's get rid of that defender with bishop takes bishop on d6...
descriptions.rn1qk2r/p4ppp/1p1p1n2/1N1p1b2/3P4/1Q2P3/: ...and then add an attacker with rook to c1
At the end of the day, we're going to play knight to c7. Black has a couple ways they can try to get out of it, but none of them work. We will win material and then win the game.
descriptions.rB1qkbnr/p3pppp/2p5/1p6/2pP4/4PQ2/PP3PPP: Black is trying to fight fire with fire - but our fire is bigger: queen takes pawn on c6 FORKING black's king and rook.
descriptions.rB2kbnr/p2qpppp/2Q5/1p6/2pP4/4P3/PP3PPP/: And queen takes the free rook on a8, of course.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/3P1B2/4P3/PPP2: Regular london stuff: knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/3bpn2/3p4/3P1B2/4PN2/PPP: Taking black's bishop here will only help them bring out their queen. We could retreat our bishop but my mother didn't raise a coward. My favorite move? Let's take the center of the board with knight to e5.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3ppp/3bpn2/2ppN3/3P1B2/4P3/PPP: Black is opening up the center before they've castled their king - that's a big mistake we can take advantage of. Bishop to b5 check.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pp1b1ppp/3bpn2/1BppN3/3P1B2/4P3/: Black blocked with their bishop, and now it's game over. We will win material here 100% of the time after playing knight to d7.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp1n1ppp/3bpn2/1Bpp4/3P1B2/4P3/PP: It look's like black was able to just recapture and survive our attack - but look again! Their bishop is hanging on d6. Simply bishop takes bishop on d6 and we're up a piece.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pp1n1ppp/3Bpn2/1Bpp4/3P4/4P3/PPP2: We're up a bishop - I don't need to tell you why that's winning.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pp1N1ppp/4pn2/1Bpp4/3P1b2/4P3/PP: So how do we win material? Before recapturing our bishop, we play knight to c5 discovered check.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pp3ppp/4pn2/1BNp4/3P1b2/4P3/PPP2: Awesome. No-matter where black goes next, we'll recapture the bishop on f4, ending up up-a-pawn and also up-4-points-on-the-eval-bar.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2pp4/3P1B2/4P3/PPP2P: We can't really develop our bishop to d3 anymore because black could push pawn to c4 and make us move it again. With that in mind, let's develop knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/2pp4/3P1B2/4PN2/PP: We can set up a trap that half our opponents will fall for: knight to c3. Our threat: hopping our knight to b5 and targeting the c7 square forking the king and rook. If Black doesn't address this immedietly, they will lose the game.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1pn2/2pp4/3P1B2/2N1PN2: OUR OPPONENT FELL FOR OUR TRAP!! They didn't protect against knight to b5 and we 100% win material now. Knight to b5!!
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/2n1pn2/qNpp4/3P1B2/4PN2/: Block check with pawn to c3. We still threaten knight to c7 on the next move.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/2n2n2/qNppp3/3P1B2/2P1PN: We have 3 ways to take the e5 pawn. All are good, but according to the computer, taking it with our knight is best. Knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/2n2n2/qN1pN3/2pP1B2/2P1P: Black cut off our bishop from defending our knight! Now our knight is hanging!!! Defending our knight with pawn to a4 is a great move, but a BRILLIANT move is sacrificing our other knight onto c4!!!!
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/2n2n2/qN6/2pP1B2/2P1P3/P: Now that our other knight is dead and out of the way, we are free to play knight to c7, forking black's king and rook!
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppN2ppp/2n2n2/q7/2pP1B2/2P1P3/P: That knight sacrifice was a chess.com certified brilliant move!!! Awesome job
descriptions.r2qk2r/p1p1bppp/np3n2/1N1p1b2/3P1B2/1Q2P: That knight is defending the c7 square, so what do we do? Attack the knight! Queen to a4.
descriptions.r2qk2r/p1p1bppp/np3n2/1N1p1b2/Q2P1B2/4P3: Our attack is absolutely crushing black. All our pieces are pointing to c7, we are attacking the undefended a6 knight, and our queen has a discovered check up her sleeve whenever we move our knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/3p4/3P1B2/4P3/PP: We'll continue with the standard move: knight to f3.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/3p4/3P1Bb1/4PN2/P: Black pins our knight? We pin black's knight. Bishop to b5.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/1B1p4/3P1Bb1/4PN2: Next we'll try and kick black's bishop out. Pawn to h3.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/1B1p3b/3P1B2/4PN1: And then pawn to g4, chasing the bishop down.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pnb1/1B1p4/3P1BP1/4PN: Now that our knight on f3 is unpinned, let's hop it to e5 and do a double attack on black's c6 knight.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/2nbpnb1/1B1pN3/3P1BP1/4P2: We have 2 attackers on the c6 knight, and white only has 1 defender - that means we can take it! Knight takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r2qk2r/p1p2ppp/2pbpnb1/1B1p4/3P1BP1/4P2P: Now bishop takes pawn on c6 - winning a pawn and FORKING the king and rook.
descriptions.r2q3r/p1p1kppp/2Bbpnb1/3p4/3P1BP1/4P2P/P: Of course, we take the rook! Bishop to a8.
descriptions.B2q3r/p1p1kppp/3bpnb1/3p4/3P1BP1/4P2P/PP: This exact game has been played by 2200+ ELO players over and over and over again.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/3bpn2/3pN3/3P1B2/4P3/PP: Black castled - let's continue with our normal london setup: knight to d2.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/3bpn2/2ppN3/3P1B2/4P3/PP: More normal london stuff: pawn to c3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp3ppp/2nbpn2/2ppN3/3P1B2/2P1P3: More usual london stuff: bishop to d3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp3ppp/2n1pn2/2ppb3/3P1B2/2PBP3: Black was so annoyed by our knight that they took it - and that was their first mistake. Pawn recaptures on e5 to boot the knight away.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp1n1ppp/2n1p3/2ppP3/5B2/2PBP3/: Black has two attackers on our e5 pawn - so let's bring in our second defender: knight to f3.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppqn1ppp/2n1p3/2ppP3/5B2/2PBPN2/: Black is wayyyyy too focused on taking our pawn. They forgot the point of chess is to take the KING. We can get started on taking black's king with a greek gift sacrifice: bishop takes pawn on h7.
descriptions.r1b2r2/ppqn1ppk/2n1p3/2ppP3/5B2/2P1PN2/P: Like every greek gift, we follow it up with the knight: knight to g5
descriptions.r1b2r2/ppqn1pp1/2n1p1k1/2ppP1N1/5B2/2P1P: Wow! That's bold of black - walking INTO the attack instead of running away. All it takes to win the game now is a simple queen to c2 check.
descriptions.r1b2r2/ppqn2p1/2n1p1k1/2ppPpN1/5B2/2P1P3: We can en passant! We can en passant and discover attack on the queen!!! E5 pawn en passants to f6
descriptions.r1b2r2/ppqn2p1/2n1pk2/2pp2N1/5B2/2P1P3/P: At this point we are spoiled for options. We could just straight up win a queen right now if we wanted to. Even better is to throw in a check with knight to h7 first.
descriptions.r1b2r2/ppqn1kpN/2n1p3/2pp4/5B2/2P1P3/PPQ: Ok NOW take the queen. Bishop to c7.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppq2ppp/2nbpn2/2ppN3/3P1B2/2PBP3: Black adds an attacker to our knight? We add a defender to our knight. Knight from d2 to f3.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppqn1ppp/2nbp3/2ppN3/3P1B2/2PBPN: As soon as you see black's knight leave f6, it means black's king has no more defenders and we can start an attack. Knight from f3 to g5 threatening to take the h7 pawn.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppqn1p1p/2nbp1p1/2ppN1N1/3P1B2/2: Ah dang... looks like our attack was blocked... NOT!! Knight sacrifice on h7!!!!
descriptions.r1b2r2/ppqn1p1k/2nbp1p1/2ppN3/3P1B2/2PBP: And we follow it up with queen check to h5. Black can't capture because their g6 pawn is pinned to their king.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppqn1p2/2nbp1p1/2ppN2Q/3P1B2/2PB: The only move to keep our advantage and beat black here? ANOTHER knight sacrifice on g6!!
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppqn1p2/2nbp1N1/2pp3Q/3P1B2/2PBP: We literally have a 100% winrate from here.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp1pppp/2n5/3p1b2/3P1B2/4P3/PPP: Remember! Whenever black plays the symmetrical bishop to f5, we pawn break with c4 and start a huge attack on the queenside.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp1pppp/2n5/5b2/2pP1B2/4P3/PP3P: Black took our pawn - let's take back with bishop to c4.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp1pppp/2n5/5b2/2BP1B2/4P3/PP3P: Great! Black just gave us the center and a slight advantage
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n1p3/3p1b2/2PP1B2/4P3/P: We'll continue developing queenside with knight to c3.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n1p3/3p1b2/2PP1B2/2N1P3: Well done! We have an even position and will have to play chess to win from here.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p4/3P1B2/8/PPP1PPP: Let's continue with our normal london setup: pawn to e3.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p1b2/3P1B2/4P3/PPP: When black breaks out the symmetrical bishop variation, we should always look for the pawn to c4 pawn break - it lets our queen develop to b3 in the future to target the weak b7 pawn. Pawn to c4!
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/3p1b2/2PP1B2/4P3/P: Queen to b3! Let's target that weak b7 pawn
descriptions.rn2kbnr/pp3ppp/1qp1p3/3p1b2/2PP1B2/1Q2P3: Let's play pawn to c5 here. It locks in black's dark-squared bishop in and also pressures black to take our queen. If they do, we get to open up our rook for free!
descriptions.rn2kbnr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/2Pp1b2/3P1B2/1P2P3/: Well done! We have a 60% winrate from here :)
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p1b2/2PP1B2/8/PP2P: Black isn't taking our "free" pawn - fine. Let's target their undefended pawn with queen to b3.
descriptions.rn2kbnr/pp2pppp/1qp5/3p1b2/2PP1B2/1Q6/PP: If black takes our queen, we can take back with our a-pawn and open up our rook. Let's pressure black to take our queen (and lock in the center) with pawn to c5.
descriptions.rn2kbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/2Pp1b2/3P1B2/1P6/1P2: Both sides played that pretty perfectly - it's an even game.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/3P1B2/4P3/PPP2: Let's continue with our normal london setup: knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/3bpn2/3p4/3P1B2/4PN2/PPP: Taking black's bishop here will only help them bring out their queen. We could retreat our bishop but my mother didn't raise a coward. My favorite move? Let's take the center of the board with knight to e5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppn1ppp/3bpn2/3pN3/3P1B2/4P3/PP: Let's develop our other knight to d2.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppn1ppp/3bpn2/3pN3/3P1B2/4P3/P: Let's develop our bishop to d3 next.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppn1ppp/3bpn2/3pN3/3P1B2/3BP3/: Well done! This was a pretty normal london setup game, now it's up to you to get the win!
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/2p2n2/3p4/3P1B2/4P3/PPP: Instead of our boring normal london setup, let's go for an exciting pawn break: pawn to c4.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp2pppp/2p2n2/3p1b2/2PP1B2/4P3/: Black abandoned the guard of the b7 pawn! Let's attack it with queen to b3.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp2pppp/1qp2n2/3p1b2/2PP1B2/1Q2P: If black takes our queen, we can take back with our a-pawn and open up our rook. Let's pressure black to take our queen (and lock in the center) with pawn to c5.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp2pppp/2p2n2/2Pp1b2/3P1B2/1P2P3: Well done! We have an edge over our opponent going into the middlegame.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/5b2/2pP1B2/4P3/PP3P: Let's collect our pawn back: bishop takes pawn on c4.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/5b2/2BP1B2/4P3/PP3P: Well done! We have the center and a slight advantage over black
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/3p4/3P1B2/4PN2/P: We'll continue with our usual setup: knight to d2.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2nbpn2/3p4/3P1B2/4PN2/PP: We don't want to take black's bishop, but we also don't necessarily want our own bishop to be taken. Let's put our knight in the middle instead. Knight to e5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2nbpn2/3pN3/3P1B2/4P3/P: Let's continue with our normal london setup: pawn to c3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2nbp3/3pN3/3PnB2/2P1P3/: I don't like that black's knight is on our side of the board - let's get rid of him. Knight takes knight on e4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2nbp3/4N3/3PpB2/2P1P3/P: Now we can target that isolated pawn with queen to c2 - this also prepares us to castle queenside.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp3pp/2nbp3/4Np2/3PpB2/2P1P3/P: Black defended their pawn - let's castle queenside and call it a day.
Well done! We're slightly ahead on the eval bar.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2p1p/3bp1p1/3p4/3P1BQ1/4P3/P: Black is threatening pawn to e5, which would open an attack our bishop and our queen at the same time. Let's... avoid that. Queen retreats to f3.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2p1p/4p1p1/3p4/3P1Q2/4P3/PPP: Well done! We have an equal position and are ready for the middlegame
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/4pn2/2pp4/3P1B2/4PN2/PPP: We can't really develop our bishop to d3 anymore because black could push pawn to c4 and make us move it again. With that in mind, let's develop our b-knight to d2.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1pn2/2pp4/3P1B2/4PN2/P: Finally: pawn to c3, another normal london move.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp3ppp/2n1pn2/2pp4/3P1B2/2P1PN2: Well done! You successfully played the most boring opening in chess
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1pp1pppp/p1n5/3p4/3P1B2/4P3/PPP: Continue with our normal london setup: knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/1pp1pppp/p1n2n2/3p4/3P1B2/4PN2/: More normal london stuff: bishop to d3.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1pp1pppp/p1n2n2/3p4/3P1Bb1/3BPN2: Even more regular london stuff: B-knight to d2.
Well done! That was.... just a very normal london setup game.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/1B1p4/3P1B2/4Pb1P: That's fine - we'll just take back with our queen. Queen to f3.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/1B1p4/3P1B2/4PQ1P: Well done! We'll keep developing and look for a c4 pawn break in the future.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p1b2/2PP1B2/8/PP2P: We'll almost always follow up pawn to c4 with knight to c3.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p1b2/2PP1B2/2N5/P: We'll continue with a normal london move: pawn to e3.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p1b2/2PP1B2/2N1P3: Well done! Nothing too exciting here, but we'll look for queen to b3 in the future to target that undefended b7 pawn.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Let's learn the Petrov Defense! Petrov? Petroff? However you say it, this opening will take white completely by surprise. They'll be on your turf, and there's barely any moves to memorize. We start by playing pawn to e5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1PPP: Instead of defending our pawn, we'll attack white's with knight to f6. This is the Petrov defense.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/4N3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP: Most chess courses will tell you NOT to copy white and take their e4 pawn because it's dangerous. Well, most chess courses are BORING. Chess is a game. Games are fun.  Knight takes pawn on e4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4N3/4n3/8/PPPPQPPP/R: What I love about this opening is we can just... copy our opponent! Queen to e7, SACRIFICING our knight.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppppqppp/8/4N3/4Q3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: OK we can't copy our opponent anymore, but we CAN win our knight back: pawn to d6. If white tries to move their knight, we win their queen.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1qppp/3p4/1B2N3/4Q3/8/PPPP1P: Pawn to c6 blocks the check and makes white have to retreat their bishop
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/pp2qppp/2Bp4/4N3/4Q3/8/PPPP1PPP: White's most common move is LITERALLY just a blunder of a piece. I can't even explain it. Just knight takes bishop on c6 and we have a free piece.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp2qppp/2np4/4N3/4Q3/8/PPPP1PPP: We really can't go wrong here - but the easiest move is just pawn takes knight.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/pp2qppp/2n5/4p3/4Q3/8/PPPP1PPP/: I can't believe white blundered a piece like that. What were they thinking??
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1qppp/3p4/4N3/3PQ3/8/PPP2PPP: Let's take our knight back with the pawn.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1qppp/8/4P3/4Q3/8/PPP2PPP/RN: OK, it looks like we're just a pawn down â right? But in practice, that extra pawn is incredibly hard for White to hang onto. Most players over-focus on defending it and end up in a worse position because of it. Knight to c6 adding an attacker.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1qppp/2n5/1B2P3/4Q3/8/PPP2PP: White has two attackers on our knight. We need two defenders. Bishop to d7.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pppbqppp/2n5/1B2P3/4Q3/8/PPP2PPP/: We should probably copy white and castle too.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/pppbqppp/2n5/1B2P3/4QB2/8/PPP2PP: Let's try and trap that bishop in the corner - pawn to g5.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/pppbqp1p/2n5/1B2P1p1/4Q3/6B1/PPP: White plays that move 85% of the time and it literally just loses them their bishop. Now we have Pawn to f5, hitting the queen. Once she moves, the bishop is trapped on the next move.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/pppbq2p/2n5/1B2Ppp1/Q7/6B1/PPP2P: Pawn to f4 to finally lock that bishop in jail :)
descriptions.2kr1b1r/pppbq2p/2n5/1B2P1p1/Q4p2/6B1/PPP: That bishop is as good as ours!
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1qppp/2n5/4P3/4QB2/8/PPP2PPP: White defended their pawn. Harmless, right? WRONG! They just LOST the game because of this very tricky line: first, pawn to g5 hitting the bishop.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1qp1p/2n5/4P1p1/4Q3/6B1/PPP2: That bishop looks like it can get trapped. Let's trap it! Pawn to f5 hitting the queen, and once the queen moves, we can trap the bishop with one more pawn push. Oh yeah - and white can't take en-passant because then we win their queen!
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1q2p/2n5/4Ppp1/8/6B1/PPP1QPP: The queen moved and now we can trap that bishop! Pawn to f4.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1q2p/2n5/4P1pQ/5p2/6B1/PPP2P: Meh - this doesn't really scare me: queen to f7 blocking the check.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2q1p/2n5/4P1Q1/5p2/6B1/PPP2P: White wins a pawn? We win a bishop. Pawn takes bishop on g3.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2q1p/2n5/4P1Q1/8/6p1/PPP2PPP: Being a piece up never hurt anyone!
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1qppp/8/4Q3/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/RN: White took back with the queen this time - which means we want to send this game to an endgame where we can create a lot of problems for white. Queen takes queen on e5.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/8/8/PPP2PPP/RNB1K: First things first, let's get our pawn back: knight to c6.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/5B2/8/PPP2PPP/R: White really wants to keep their e5 pawn - fine! Let's switch our focus to their c2 pawn with bishop to f5.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4Pb2/5B2/3B4/PPP2PPP/: Looks like white defended their c2 pawn right? WRONG! We have a winning sequence now: first, bishop takes bishop on d3.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/5B2/3P4/PP3PPP/RN: Now knight to b4, and we're threatening two things: capturing the d3 pawn, and forking the king and rook on c2.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1n3B2/3P4/PP1K1PPP/: White was so desperate to protect both squares they moved their king into the middle of the board - big mistake. Now we simply castle queenside, and in one easy move our king has become safe and their king is under fire from our rook!
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1n3B2/2NP4/PP1K1PP: Let's take the d3 pawn with our knight. Now we're attacking the undefended bishop on f4 and the undefended pawn on b2. Oh yeah - and we're threatening a discovered check too!
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/5B2/2NnK3/PP3PPP/R: Let's throw in bishop to c5 check - just bringing another piece to the party.
descriptions.2kr3r/ppp2ppp/8/2b1P3/5B2/2Nn1K2/PP3PPP/: We're spoiled for options here. Let's take f2 with our bishop.
descriptions.2kr3r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/5B2/2Nn1K2/PP3bPP/R6: The eval bar gives us +3 points here. We're crushing.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4N3/2B1n3/8/PPPP1PPP: White has a serious threat on f7 - let's block out the bishop with pawn to d5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pN3/4n3/1B6/PPPP1PPP: With white's light-squared bishop gone, we have this incredible fork: queen to g5. We're attacking the g2 pawn and white's e5 knight, and white can't save them both.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pN1q1/4n3/1B6/PPPP1P: White's most common move here just... wins us a knight. Queen takes knight on e5.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pq3/4n3/1B1P4/PPP2PP: Here's the only tricky part: if we just move our knight away, white's rook will come to e1 and pin our queen to our king. That's why here, we play knight to f2 and threaten THEIR queen.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pq3/8/1B1P4/PPP2RPP/: Last move to ensure us the win: bishop to c5, pinning the rook to the king.
descriptions.rnb1k2r/ppp2ppp/8/2bpq3/8/1B1P4/PPP2RPP/: Well done! We navigated through some tricky traps white had for us, and now we're completely crushing.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3p2q1/4n3/1B3N2/PPPP1: Two moves and white will resign: first, queen to g2, threatening checkmate.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/4n1b1/1B3N2/PPPP1P: I don't even have to tell you - you already KNOW that white has no hope here.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4Pb2/5B2/2P5/PP3PPP/R: Now's a good time to castle our king to safety.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B2Pb2/5B2/2P5/PP3PP: We have an awesome move now: knight SACRIFICE onto e5
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/8/1B2Bb2/8/2P5/PP3PPP/RN: BLUNDER from white!! Can you find the move to win us our piece back? Hint: rook to d5, forking the two bishops
descriptions.2k2b1r/ppp2pBp/8/1B1r1b2/8/2P5/PP3PPP/RN: And ANOTHER blunder from white: they were so desperate for a pawn but that move really just helped us develop even faster: bishop to g7.
descriptions.2k4r/ppp2pbp/8/1B1r1b2/8/2P5/PP3PPP/RN2K: Look how active our pieces are - and on the next move, we'll bring our last rook into the center and start checkmating white.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1qppp/2n5/4P3/4QP2/8/PPP3PP/: Let's play bishop to g4, with the idea to castle queenside as fast as possible.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1qppp/2n5/1B2P3/4QPb1/8/PPP3PP: White is threating a pretty nasty attack here: they can take our knight, and once we take back with our pawn, their queen can come in and fork our king and rook. We'll turn the tables on them by castling queenside. Now WE have a strong threat: rook to d1.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp1qppp/2n5/1B2P3/4QPb1/8/PPP3P: White walked RIGHT into a fork. Queen to c5 check.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1Bq1P3/4QPb1/4B3/PPP: Queen takes bishop on b5. Yum.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/5P2/8/PPP3PP/RN: Dang, white defended their e5 pawn. Now we switch our focus to the c2 pawn by playing bishop to f5.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4Pb2/5P2/2P5/PP4PP/RN: While white's been focused on defending their pawns, they totally forgot to develop! Now we're way ahead in development and can castle queenside.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4Pb2/5P2/2P1B3/PP4PP: White is extremely strong on the dark-squares. We need to undermine their position: pawn to g5.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2p1p/2n5/4Pbp1/5P2/2P1B1P1/PP: We can expose white's kingside and create an open file for our rook by playing pawn takes pawn on f4.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2p1p/2n5/4Pb2/5P2/2P1B3/PP5P/: We have a nice trap here - bishop to h6, pinning the f4 pawn to the e3 bishop. If white doesn't do anything, we can capture the pawn on e5 and if white takes back with the f4 pawn, we win their bishop.
descriptions.2kr3r/ppp2p1p/2n4b/4Pb2/5P2/2P1B3/PP1N3P: Yes! White finally blundered and fell into our trap. Knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.2kr3r/ppp2p1p/7b/4nb2/5P2/2P1B3/PP1N3P/R: That was a clever pin we found, and our bishops are so strong that we have a +2 point advantage
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1q2p/2n5/4Ppp1/Q7/6B1/PPP2PP: Now we just trap the bishop of course! Pawn push to f4.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1q2p/2n5/1B2P1p1/Q4p2/6B1/PP: We can't just take the bishop yet because white has a strong attack on our knight and we need to add a defender. Good news: before we do that, we can throw in queen takes pawn on e5 with check.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp4p/2n5/1B2q1p1/Q4p2/6B1/PPP2: Now we need to defend our knight: let's develop our bishop to d7.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pppb3p/2n5/1B2q1p1/Q4p2/6B1/PPP2P: Oh no!!! We forgot that white has that nasty pin!!!! Did we lose? Nope! King CASTLES, SACRIFICING his own QUEEN.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/pppb3p/2n5/1B2R1p1/Q4p2/6B1/PPP2: Oh wow, this is going to be beautiful. We're down a full queen.... can you find the checkmate in 2? Hint: bishop to g4, double-checking the king.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp4p/2n5/1B2R1p1/Q4pb1/6B1/PPP2: Can you find checkmate in one? Hint: Rook to d1
descriptions.2k2b1r/ppp4p/2n5/1B2R1p1/Q4pb1/6B1/PPP2P: One of the most gorgeous lines I've seen on this website. Well done.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1q2p/2n5/3QPpp1/8/6B1/PPP2PP: Let's trap that bishop! Pawn to f4.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1q2p/2n5/1B1QP1p1/5p2/6B1/PP: White has that annoying double-attack on our knight. Let's defend it with bishop to d7. This also gets us ready to long-castle
descriptions.r3kb1r/pppbq2p/2n5/1B1QP1p1/5p2/6B1/PPP2: Taking the bishop now is a totally fine move - but honestly, it's not going anywhere. We can just long-castle now and take it on the next move.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/pppbq2p/2n5/1B1QP1p1/5p2/6B1/PPP: Veryyy nice. Our future moves include winning the bishop and discovering an attack on the queen!
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp1qppp/2n5/1B2P3/4QPb1/2N5/PPP: White defended rook to d1, but our attack isn't nearly over! Knight to d4 does two things: attacks white's bishop, and threatens bishop to f5 on the next move.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp1qppp/8/4P3/3nQPb1/2NB4/PPP3P: White defended our threat of bishop to f5, but we still have so much attacking to do! Queen to h4 check
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/3nQPbq/2NB2P1/PPP4: White completely weakened their king, queen, and rook all in one move. First, we need to get our queen out of danger by moving her to h3. After that, our threat is bishop to f3 forking the queen and rook.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/3nQPb1/2NBB1Pq/PPP: Bishop to f3 - a nice and easy fork.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/3nQP2/2NBBbPq/PPP4: Who doesn't love a good fork?
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp1qppp/2B5/4P3/4QPb1/8/PPP3PP/: White completely missed the bigger picture: we don't care about our knight - we care about WHITE'S KING! Rook to d1 check!!
descriptions.2k2b1r/ppp1qppp/2B5/4P3/4QPb1/8/PPP2KPP/: Now we win white's rook. Rook to h1, nice and easy.
descriptions.2k2b1r/pBp1qppp/8/4P3/4QPb1/8/PPP2KPP/RN: This looks scary but its really not - king to b8.
descriptions.1k3b1r/pBp1qppp/8/4P3/4QPb1/4B3/PPP2KPP/: Remember - we care about white's KING! Queen to h4 check.
descriptions.1k3b1r/pBp2ppp/8/4P3/4QPbq/4B1P1/PPP2K1P: Don't let off the gas! Rook to h2 check.
descriptions.1k3b1r/pBp2ppp/8/4P3/4QPbq/4B1P1/PPP4r/R: KEEP GOING!! BISHOP TO H3 CHECK.
descriptions.1k3b1r/pBp2ppp/8/4P3/4QP1q/4B1Pb/PPP4r/R: DONT STOP!!! QUEEN TO G3 CHECK.
descriptions.1k3b1r/pBp2ppp/8/4P3/4QP2/4B1qb/PPP4r/RN: That was relentless. All our pieces are swarming white's defenseless king. Forced checkmate in 4 from here.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1qppp/3p4/4N3/Q7/8/PPPP1PPP/: White's trying to save their knight AND their queen by throwing in a check, but it's just not possible. We can block the check with bishop to d7 here, and white can't capture with their knight because their knight is pinned to their king.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pppbqppp/3p4/4N3/4Q3/8/PPPP1PPP/: Wow... white really moved the queen to the side, let us develop a piece for free, and then moved it right back to where it was. Now we just have a much better position than them. We don't even HAVE to take the knight yet, because it's still extremely pinned. Let's play knight to c6, adding even more pressure.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pppbqppp/2np4/4N3/3PQ3/8/PPP2PPP/: Ok, NOW we win the knight: pawn takes knight on e5.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pppbqppp/2n5/4P3/4Q3/8/PPP2PPP/RN: We could grab that pawn right now, but thereâs a really good chance weâll win it on the next move anyway. Thatâs why I actually like castling queenside here instead.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/pppbqppp/2n5/4P3/4Q3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Nice nice nice! We are so much more developed than white - and while we're a pawn down, but that e5 pawn will be impossible for white to hold on to.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1qppp/2n5/4P3/4Q3/2N5/PPP2PP: White didn't defend their e5 pawn - let's take it with our queen!
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4n3/5B2/2N5/PPP2PPP/R: There's only one way to save our knight and c7 pawn at the same time: bishop to d6.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/3b4/1N2n3/5B2/8/PPP2PPP/: Fun one here! Knight to f3, CHECKING the king and discovering an attack on the undefended f4 bishop.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/3b4/1N6/5B2/5P2/PPP2P1P/: Bishop takes bishop on f4, of course
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/8/1N6/5b2/5P2/PPP2P1P/R3: Nice! White is NEVER castling now - and we have a +1 point advantage.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4Pb2/5P2/3B4/PPP3PP/R: Let's take the bishop on d3, and once they take back, we can hop our knight in to b4.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/5P2/3P4/PP4PP/RNB: Knight hop to b4, attacking both the d3 pawn AND threatening a fork on c2.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1n3P2/3P4/PP1K2PP/R: After castling, our rook will stare down white's king.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/1n3P2/2NP4/PP1K2PP: OK from here it's SUPER tempting to take that d3 pawn, but the truth is the d3 pawn is so weak it's not even WORTH taking right now. Actually - according to the computer, taking the pawn LOSES us our advantage because it let's white activate their rook on the d-file. The best move is to play pawn to f6, surprisingly.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp3pp/5p2/4P3/1n3P2/2NP4/PP1K2P: Nicely done! We'll develop our bishop next and bring our other rook to the center.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4N3/4n3/5Q2/PPPP1PPP: Knight to g5 saves our knight, defends checkmate, and attacks white's queen all at the same time.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4N1n1/5Q2/8/PPPP1PPP: Pawn to d6. We need to kick that knight away - its just too dangerous in the center of the board
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p4/4N1n1/5Q2/8/PPPP1PP: Nice! We have the advantage over white now
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B2P3/8/8/PPP2PPP/R: Bishop to d7, defending our knight and preparing to castle.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pppb1ppp/2B5/4P3/8/8/PPP2PPP/RNB1: Bishop takes bishop back on c6.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2b5/4P3/8/2N5/PPP2PPP/R1: Let's develop our bishop to b4, threatening to capture white's knight and double their pawns.
descriptions.2kr3r/ppp2ppp/2b5/4P3/1b6/2N5/PPP2PPP/R1: Well done! We have a slight advantage coming out of the opening.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4N1n1/8/4Q3/PPPP1PPP: The threat of a discovered check is very scary - let's protect our king with bishop to e7.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppppbppp/8/4N1n1/8/4Q3/PPPP1PPP/: We defended all of white's threats, and after castling on the next move, our position is completely safe.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B2Pb2/5P2/2P5/PP4PP: Bishop to c5 and white is literally never castling.
descriptions.2kr3r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1Bb1Pb2/5P2/2P5/PP4PP/: Next we'll move our other rook to the center and start attacking white's exposed king.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4N3/4n3/3P4/PPP2PPP/: Let's run our knight back to f6
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/4N3/8/3P4/PPP2PPP/: That was easy! We'll develop and castle from here.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/pppbqppp/2n5/1B2P3/4Q3/2N5/PPP2P: White decided to give the pawn back - smart choice by them. Before we take it back though, we can throw in pawn to a6 and force white to make a decision for what to do with their bishop.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/1ppbqppp/p1n5/4P3/B3Q3/2N5/PPP2P: Remember that pawn we gave away a few moves ago? We can FINALLY win it back: knight takes on e5.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/1ppbqppp/p7/4n3/B3Q3/2N5/PPP2PPP: Nice! Both sides played that perfectly.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/1ppbqppp/p1B5/4P3/4Q3/2N5/PPP2PP: This trade is great for us! Now we get a super active bishop after bishop takes back on c6.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/1pp1qppp/p1b5/4P3/4Q3/2N5/PPP2PP: White has a pawn, we have an active bishop. The computer says it's and equal game from here.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4Pb2/5B2/2P5/PP1N1PP: We have a cool forcing sequence here, starting with knight SACRIFICE on e5.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/8/4Bb2/8/2P5/PP1N1PPP/R3: We have to win our piece back now. We'll do that by pinning the bishop to white's king. Rook to e8.
descriptions.2k1rb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4Bb2/5P2/2P5/PP1N2PP/R: It doesn't matter how white tries to defend their bishop, because it's still pinned to the king! Pawn to f6
descriptions.2k1rb1r/ppp3pp/8/4pb2/5P2/2P2N2/PP4PP/R3: The position is completely equal - from here you'll have to play chess.

shortDescriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1PPP: Let's continue with the Petrov defense.
