descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn a tricky and dangerous opening weapon: the Ponziani. Start by pushing the king's pawn forward two squares to e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Now let's develop the king's knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1P: After Black responds with knight c6, we can begin the Ponziani. Let's push our pawn to c3. The idea is to sacrifice the natural developing square for our knight in order to build a big pawn center.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b1p3/4P3/2P2N2/PP: Black used their bishop to defend the center, but they've walked right into our trap and they are now losing. Let's play pawn to d4 to attack the bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b5/3pP3/2P2N2/PP3: Let's capture back with our c pawn to keep the pressure on Black's bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/1b1PP3/5N2/PP3PP: Let's block Black's check while developing a piece with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/1b1PP3/2N2N2/PP3: Black moved their pawn to open up their light squared bishop, but this move slightly opens up their king and allows us to set a nasty trap. First, let's kick the knight out of the way with pawn to d5.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/3p4/3Pn3/1b2P3/2N2N2/PP: Black fell for our trap! Now White to move and win a piece. Can you find it? Hint: Queen to a4 check, winning the bishop on the next move.
descriptions.r2qk1nr/pppb1ppp/3p4/3Pn3/Qb2P3/2N2N2/PP: Now let's take the free bishop with queen b4!
descriptions.r2qk1nr/pppb1ppp/3p4/3Pn3/1Q2P3/2N2N2/PP: Well done! We are a full piece ahead and have a dominant position.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3pp3/4P3/2P2N2/PP1P: Black played d5, the best move, but we can still set some traps with queen a4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4p3/Q3p3/2P2N2/PP1P: Black made a mistake by taking on e4. Now we can move our knight out of danger, win back our pawn, and add pressure to Black's pinned piece with knight to e5.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/2n5/4N3/Q3p3/2P5/PP1P1P: Finally, Black has made a mistake and blundered a pawn! Let's first take the bishop with knight to d7.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pppq1ppp/2n5/8/Q3p3/2P5/PP1P1PPP/: Now we can take the free pawn. Queen takes e4 with check.
descriptions.r3k1nr/pppqbppp/2n5/8/4Q3/2P5/PP1P1PPP/R: Finally, let's build our strong center with pawn to d4. If you remember, that was the original goal of the Ponziani Opening!
descriptions.r3k1nr/pppqbppp/2n5/8/3PQ3/2P5/PP3PPP/RN: Well done! We are up a pawn and have much better position than our opponent. We'll move our queen to safety, develop our bishop, and castle kingside.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/4P3/2P2N2/PP: Let's continue our plan to take the center with pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/3Pn3/2P2N2/PP3: Black took our pawn with their knight which is a bit dangerous. We can now kick the other knight out with pawn to d5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppppnppp/8/3Pp3/4n3/2P2N2/PP3PP: Let's recapture the e5 pawn with our knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp1nppp/3p4/3PN3/4n3/2P5/PP3PP: Black opening up their king in this position is a huge blunder and loses them the game! We begin a vicious attack with bishop to b5 with check.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2nppp/2pp4/1B1PN3/4n3/2P5/PP3: Let's take back with pawn to c6, threatening discovered check on the next move.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p3nppp/2pp4/1B2N3/4n3/2P5/PP3PP: Let's take back with knight to c6, once again threatening discovered check on the next move
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/p3nppp/1qNp4/1B6/4n3/2P5/PP3PPP: Clever! Black forked our knight and bishop, but we can retreat the knight back to d4, guarding the bishop and discovering a check to the king.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/p3nppp/1q1p4/1B6/3Nn3/2P5/PP3PP: Well done! Black will have to move their king out of the way, losing their ability to castle. We are a pawn up and our position is so good that the computer puts our position at a +4 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p4ppp/2np4/1B6/4n3/2P5/PP3PPP/R: Let's take back with the bishop on c6, creating a beautiful triple fork on Black's king, rook, and knight.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/p2b1ppp/2Bp4/8/4n3/2P5/PP3PPP/RN: The bishop can take either trade for the rook, or capture the knight for free. Let's take the knight for free with bishop to e4.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/p2b1ppp/3p4/8/4B3/2P5/PP3PPP/RNB: Beautifully executed! We are way ahead in material.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/1b1PP3/2N2N2/PP: Black has developed their other knight, which allows us to shove our opponent's pieces backwards and finish our development. Pawn to d5 this time.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppppnppp/5n2/3P4/1b2P3/2N2N2/PP3: Let's finish our development and protect the pawn on e4 with bishop to d3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppppnppp/5n2/3P4/1b2P3/2NB1N2/PP: Well done! Look at how cramped Black's position is here - all thanks to our vicious Ponziani pawns. Our pieces are developed, we own the center, and we are ready to castle kingside. Even though the material is equal, chess engines give our position more than 1 point of advantage!
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp1nppp/3p1n2/3P4/1b2P3/2NB1N2/: Black blundered by opening up their king while their bishop is still undefended on b4! Now White to move and win a piece. Can you find it? Hint: Queen to a4 check, winning the bishop on the next move.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pppbnppp/3p1n2/3P4/Qb2P3/2NB1N2/P: Now let's take the free bishop with queen b4!
descriptions.r2qk2r/pppbnppp/3p1n2/3P4/1Q2P3/2NB1N2/P: Well done! We are a full piece ahead and have a dominant position. The computer puts our position at a +4 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/1bn5/8/3PP3/5N2/PP3PPP: Retreating the bishop completely loses for Black. They give up too much space in the center. Let's	 develop our other knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/1bn2n2/8/3PP3/2N2N2/PP3: With pieces in the center but no pawns to protect them, Black allows us to bully their pieces with our pawns. Pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/1bn5/4P3/3P2n1/2N2N2/PP: That knight has strayed too far from home. Lets kick it out one more time with our h pawn to h3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/1bn4n/4P3/3P4/2N2N1P/PP: We put one knight in the corner, now let's attack the other knight with pawn to d5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/1b5n/3PP3/1n6/2N2N1P/PP: It's tempting to continue attacking the knight here - and while it is a good move, we can now obliterate the opponent by switching the focus to their queen. Bishop to g5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp2pp/1b3p1n/3PP1B1/1n6/2N2N1P: Let's take back on f6 with our pawn, threatening to discover an attack on the queen on our next move.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp3p/1b3p1n/3P2B1/1n6/2N2N1P/P: Black removed the defender from the knight - which means we win a free piece! Bishop takes knight on h6.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp3p/1b3p1B/3P4/1n6/2N2N1P/PP3: Well done! We are up an entire piece and have humiliated Black's position. The computer puts this at a +5 point advantage for White.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/3pP3/2P2N2/PP3: Black has taken our pawn, but instead of immediately capturing back, let's push our pawn to e5 to attack the knight and improve our pawn structure.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/3p2n1/2P2N2/PP: Now we can take our pawn back with c pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/3P2n1/5N2/PP3P: Well done! We own the center and have a better position than our opponent.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/4p3/4P3/2P2N2/PP1P: Let's continue our plan to take the center with pawn to d4.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/4p3/3PP1b1/2P2N2/PP: By moving the bishop, Black left the b7 pawn unprotected. Let's attack it with queen to b3.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/4p3/3PP3/1QP2b2/PP3: Before taking the b pawn, let's take back our piece with g pawn takes f3.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/3pP3/1QP2P2/PP3P1: Black missed that we can take the b7 pawn. Let's take it with the Queen.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pQp2ppp/3p4/4n3/3pP3/2P2P2/PP3P1: We have a few options here, but the best move is continuing to kick the knight around with f pawn to f4.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pQp2ppp/3p4/8/3pPP2/2P2n2/PP3P1P: This check isn't scary. King to e2.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pQp2ppp/3p4/8/3pPP1n/2P5/PP2KP1P: Let's return the favor with queen c6 check.
descriptions.r2q1bnr/p1p1kppp/2Qp4/8/3pPP1n/2P5/PP2KP: Let's play pawn to f5 which completely traps Black's knight on the side of the board, and threatens bishop g5 forking the king and knight.
descriptions.r2q1bnr/p1p1kppp/2Qp4/5P2/3pP2n/2P5/PP2K: Well done! Although we are tied in material, we are completely dominating the board and the computer puts our position at +2.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pQp1nppp/2np4/8/3pP3/2P2P2/PP3P1: Let's add more pressure to the knight with bishop to b5.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pQp1nppp/2np4/1B6/3pP3/2P2P2/PP3: Well done! Black's position is crumbled and we will win this game.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppppnppp/1b5n/3PP3/8/2N2N1P/PP3P: Black retreated - let's attack! Pawn to d6.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1pnppp/1b1p3n/4P3/8/2N2N1P/PP3: Let's take back to keep the pressure on the knight. If we get the knight to move, our attack on the Black queen with our bishop becomes possible. Pawn takes d6.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1p1ppp/1b1P3n/5n2/8/2N2N1P/PP3: Let's once again switch focus to attack to the queen. Bishop to g5. We won't win a free piece this time but we will still paralyze the opponent.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1p2pp/1b1P1p1n/5nB1/8/2N2N1P/P: Let's take Black's knight on h6 with our bishop to weaken their kingside.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1p2pp/1b1P1p1n/8/8/2N2N1P/PP3P: We can develop our last piece and prevent black from castling kingside by playing bishop to c4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1p2pp/1b1P1p1n/8/2B5/2N2N1P/PP: Wow. Even though the material is equal, the computer puts our position at +5 point advantage. Look at how none of blacks pieces can move! They literally have no moves. The rest of the game is converting your dominant position into a win.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/3pP3/2P2N2/PP3PP: Black has taken our pawn, let's recapture with c pawn takes d4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/3PP3/5N2/PP3PPP/: Well done! We own the center and are ready to continue playing!
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/3PP1b1/5N2/PP3PPP: Black made a mistake moving their bishop to g3. We can now pin their knight with our queen. Queen to a4.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/Q2PP3/5b2/PP3PPP/: Let's take back with g pawn takes f3.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/Q2PP3/5P2/PP3P1P/: Well done! We have a winning position and are ready to continue developing.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2np4/3P4/4P3/2b2N2/PP3P: Black did not fall for our trap this time, so let's just capture back. Pawn takes c3.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2np4/3P4/4P3/2P2N2/P4PP: Well done! We completly own the center. Even though material is equal, the computer puts our position at a +1 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/1bnP3n/4P3/8/2N2N1P/PP3: Let's once again switch focus to attack to the queen. Bishop to g5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp2pp/1bnP1p1n/4P1B1/8/2N2N1P/: Let's take back on f6 with our pawn, threatening to discover an attack on the queen on our next move.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp3p/1bnP1p1n/6B1/8/2N2N1P/PP3: Black removed the defender from the knight - which means we win a free piece! Bishop takes knight on h6.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp3p/1bnP1p1B/8/8/2N2N1P/PP3PP: Well done! We are up an entire piece and have humiliated Black's position. The computer puts this at a +6 point advantage for White.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3qN3/Q3p3/2P5/PP1P1: We are up a pawn and our knight is under attack. Let's trade our knight with Black's and simplify the position. Knight takes c6.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/2N5/3q4/Q3p3/2P5/PP1P1P: Well done! According to the computer, we have a +1 point advantage against our opponent. We'll be looking to develop our bishop and castle kingside in the future.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppppqppp/2n2n2/4P3/3p4/2P2N2/PP: Clever! Black pinned our pawn to our king, stopping us from taking the f6 knight and threatening to take our e pawn. Let's defend the e pawn with c pawn takes d4.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1qppp/2np1n2/4P3/3P4/5N2/PP3: Black added an attacker to our e5 pawn. Let's remove an attacker by pinning their knight to their king with bishop b5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1qppp/2np1n2/1B2P3/3P4/5N2/P: It's a tense position, but we are better and ready to castle at any point to move our king to safety.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/3nP3/3p4/2P2N2/PP3: Now we can take our pawn back with c pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/3nP3/3P4/5N2/PP3PP: Black has played the opening by the book, and we are in an equal position.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/2n5/3pp3/Q3P3/2P2N2/PP1: Black gave us a free pawn. We'll take it but we need to be careful afterwards. E pawn takes d5
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/8/3Pp3/Q2n4/2P2N2/PP1P1: Our queen is under attack! let's move it back home where it is safe and can defend our knight. Queen to d1.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/8/3Pp3/8/2P2n2/PP1P1PPP: Let's take back with the queen. Queen to f3.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pppb1ppp/5n2/3Pp3/8/2P2Q2/PP1P1P: Let's develop our bishop and add a defender to our pawn with bishop to c4.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pppb1ppp/5n2/3Pp3/2B5/2P2Q2/PP1P: Well done! We are up a pawn and are ready to castle kingside.

shortDescriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1P: After Black responds with knight c6, we can begin the Ponziani.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: OK Beth, let's learn the Queen's Gambit (accepted). We start with, of course, the queen's pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3p4/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/R: Here we can initiate the Queen's Gambit with pawn to c4. Black has to make a tough choice here - either take our free pawn (which isn't actually free!), or try to hold onto the center.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/8/2pP4/8/PP2PPPP/RNB: Black has taken our pawn, which means we are now in the Queen's Gambit Accepted line. This is actually good for us, because we have a very nice move: pawn to e4. We get the entire center, and open up our bishop to take Black's pawn back on the next move.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/p1p1pppp/8/1p6/2pPP3/8/PP3PPP/R: That's... cute. Black is trying to save their pawn but we are about to crush any hope they have. We attack the defender with pawn to a4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/p3pppp/2p5/1p6/P1pPP3/8/1P3PPP/: Our best bet is to capture here with pawn takes b5, opening up our rook.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/p3pppp/8/1p6/2pPP3/8/1P3PPP/RNB: Now we have a very nice and provocative move: knight to c3. This attacks Black's pawn on b5 and it is nothing but trouble for them.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/p2bpppp/8/1p6/2pPP3/2N5/1P3PPP/: Now for a murderous and paralyzing move: pawn to d5. This stops Black's knight from developing and ever coming into the game, and the bishop is stuck too.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/p2b1ppp/4p3/1p1P4/2p1P3/2N5/1P3: Black is fighting back in the center. The best move here is to be proactive and take their pawn first with pawn takes e6.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/p2b2pp/4p3/1p6/2p1P3/2N5/1P3PPP: Black took with their pawn, which means we have a beautiful sacrifice: knight takes b5.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/p5pp/4p3/1b6/2p1P3/8/1P3PPP/R1B: OK you may be wondering why we just lost our knight for no reason? Well now we have the gorgeous move queen to h5 check. This forks the king and the bishop on b5.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/p6p/4p1p1/1b5Q/2p1P3/8/1P3PPP/R: And now we complete our journey around the board with queen to b5, which is yet another check!
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/p6p/4p1p1/1Q6/2p1P3/8/1P3PPP/R1: This is just complete brutality. No hope at all for them in this position.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4p3/2pPP3/8/PP3PPP/RN: This is a dangerous move from black. We need to play our cards right or we'll lose the game. Step 1: Do not capture. Instead, the simple knight to f3 defending our center.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/8/2ppP3/5N2/PP3PPP/RN: Let's leave the middle pawn, it's more important we take the one on the left with bishop takes c4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/8/2p5/2BpP3/5N2/PP3PPP/R: We have a very nice way to get a good position here: knight in to e5. Very fun move attacking the weak f7 pawn.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/pp3ppp/4b3/2p1N3/2BpP3/8/PP3PPP: They defended our attack. Let's capture with bishop e6.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/pp4pp/4p3/2p1N3/3pP3/8/PP3PPP/R: Now we have the killer queen to h5, checking the king
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/pp5p/4p1p1/2p1N2Q/3pP3/8/PP3PPP: That won't stop us. Let's play knight to g6.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/pp6/4p1p1/2p4Q/3pP3/8/PP3PPP/RN: Thanks for the free rook! Queen takes h8.
descriptions.rn1qkbnQ/pp6/4p1p1/2p5/3pP3/8/PP3PPP/RNB: Well done! Believe it or not, thousands of games end up exactly like this.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/2p1pppp/p7/1p6/P1pPP3/8/1P3PPP/: They tried to defend the defender, but this does not work! After we capture with pawn to b5, Black cannot capture back or they lose their rook!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/2p1pppp/8/1p6/2pPP3/8/1P3PPP/RN: Aaaaand game over. Rook takes rook on a8.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/8/2pPP3/8/PP3PPP/RN: Black has given up their pawn, which means we can take it back with bishop to c4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/2BPP3/8/PP3PPP/R: Let's play knight to c3 here, continuing our development and defending our e4 pawn from attack.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bppp/4pn2/8/2BPP3/2N5/PP3PPP: Black is trying to be safe and develop. We are not going to let them. Pawn to e5.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bppp/4p3/3nP3/2BP4/2N5/PP3PP: Now that Black's king side is vulnerable, we have the fun Queen move to g4 attacking their pawn.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/4p3/3nP3/2BP2Q1/2N5/PP: Black castled and now we win with bishop to h6.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1bp1p/4p1pB/3nP3/2BP2Q1/2N5/: This one is simple - bishop takes rook on f8.
descriptions.rnbq1Bk1/ppp1bp1p/4p1p1/3nP3/2BP2Q1/2N5/: Well done! We are up an exchange here and are crushing it. Once we finish developing and castle, the game will be ours.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4p3/2pPP1b1/5N2/PP3PP: Black forgot they have a hanging pawn. Now we have bishop to c4.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/8/2BpP1b1/5N2/PP3PPP/: A blunder from black! Now we have the very nice bishop takes on f7.
descriptions.rn1q1bnr/ppp2kpp/8/8/3pP1b1/5N2/PP3PPP/R: Now the follow up knight e5 check, forking the king and bishop
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp3pp/8/4N3/3pP1b1/8/PP3PPP/RN: Let's take the bishop with our queen to get her in the game. Queen to g4.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp3pp/8/4N3/3pP1Q1/8/PP3PPP/RN: Beautiful! Black is behind in development and can't castle.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/8/2BpP1b1/5N2/PP3PPP: This is a big mistake from black! Now we can set up a crushing attack with queen to b3, setting our sights on that f7 pawn.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pppq1ppp/2n5/8/2BpP1b1/1Q3N2/PP3P: Black is defending their f7 pawn but we are STILL going to play bishop takes f7 check.
descriptions.r3kbnr/ppp2qpp/2n5/8/3pP1b1/1Q3N2/PP3PPP: Now do NOT trade queens. We can instead play queen to b7 forking the rook and knight.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/8/2BpP3/1Q3b2/PP3PPP: Mate in 2! Can you find it? Hint: bishop takes f7.
descriptions.r2q1bnr/ppp1kBpp/2n5/8/3pP3/1Q3b2/PP3PPP: Now it's just mate in 1. Can you find it? Hint: Queen to e6.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/p1p1pppp/8/8/p1pPP3/8/1P3PPP/RN: OMG what an awful move. Now we have queen takes a4 with check...
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/p1pbpppp/8/8/2QPP3/8/1P3PPP/RNB: We won BOTH pawns, own the center, and Black's pawn structure is atrocious. This is just a trainwreck for Black.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4p3/2BPP3/5b2/PP3PPP/: This was a mistake from black. We simply capture with queen to f3 and now we have a ton of pressure on the f7 pawn.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4p3/2BPP3/5Q2/PP3PPP/: Well done! We are threatening checkmate on the next move with queen to f7. The computer loves our position.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/p3pppp/8/8/1ppPP3/2N5/1P3PPP/R1: That's a blunder! Black's queenside is weak, and now we can hop our knight into b5. Maybe one day we'll hop our knight into c7 and fork the king and rook...
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/4pppp/p7/1N6/1ppPP3/8/1P3PPP/R1: There's actually no threat here. Black can't take our knight because then we'll take black's rook. Let's go for bishop to f4, preparing the deadly knight to c7.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/1b2pppp/p7/1N6/1ppPPB2/8/1P3PPP: 8 moves into the game, and black just developed their first piece hahaha... Well, now knight to c7 forks the king and rook and the game is OVER.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/1bN1pppp/p7/8/1ppPPB2/8/1P3PPP/: Before you say "my opponent would never play this badly" - this is an EXACT game that happened between 2400 ELOs....
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/3bpppp/p7/1p1P4/2p1P3/2N5/1P3PP: Black is consolidating well. Let's continue our development. Knight to f3.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/3b1ppp/p3p3/1p1P4/2p1P3/2N2N2/1: Our pawn is a brave soldier, and in this position, our pawn should march one more square up. Pawn to d6, entering enemy territory.
descriptions.rn2kbnr/3b1ppp/pq1Pp3/1p6/2p1P3/2N2N2/1P: Now we defend our brave pawn with pawn to e5.
descriptions.rn2kbnr/3b1ppp/pq1Pp3/1p2P3/2p5/2N2N2/1P: Look how trapped every single one of Black's pieces is. Their king's bishop is not getting out. Their king's knight is not getting out. It's honestly depressing.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/8/2BpP3/5N2/PP3PPP: Let's defend our bishop while developing a piece with queen's knight to d2.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1bn2/8/2BpP3/5N2/PP1N1: Now we have the very nice queen to b3, once again applying a ton of pressure on Black's f7 pawn and threatening to take on b7.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/8/2bpP3/1Q3N2/PP1N: Remember how we moved the knight out to protect the bishop? Now we'll use the knight to take back with knight to c4. This maintains pressure on the b7 pawn.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/8/2NpP3/1Q3N2/PP3P: Well done! We have a great position and the computer puts us at a 1 or 2 point advantage.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp5p/4pnN1/2p4Q/3pP3/8/PP3PPP/R: Black was smart enough not to take our knight. Let's back up our queen to h3.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp5p/4pnN1/2p5/3pP3/7Q/PP3PPP/R: Well done! We are putting pressure on Black's pinned rook and attacking the e6 pawn. Things are looking great for us.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/4pppp/p7/1p6/2pPP3/2N5/1P3PPP/R: This simply doesn't work! We can play knight takes b5 and black cannot capture back or they lose their rook. Knight takes b5.
descriptions.Rn1qkbnr/1b2pppp/8/1p6/2pPP3/8/1P3PPP/2B: Now we simply retreat our rook back to a2.
descriptions.1n1qkbnr/1b2pppp/8/1p6/2pPP3/8/RP3PPP/2B: Well done! This is a great position for us as we have the center and traded a knight for a rook.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/1bBPP3/2N5/PP3PPP: Now that our knight is pinned, our e-pawn is back in danger again. Let's push our pawn to e5 so its safe again.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4p3/3nP3/1bBP4/2N5/PP3PP: Now our knight is getting attacked twice. Let's develop our other knight to e2.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/4p3/3nP3/1bBP4/2N5/PP2N: Well done! We have a better position and white wins more than 60% of the time from here.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/8/2bpP3/5N2/PP1N1PPP: Simply recapture with the knight on c4.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/8/2NpP3/5N2/PP3PPP/R: Well done! We are ready to continue playing chess.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: OK Mrs. Harmon, let's learn the Queen's Gambit (Declined). We start with, of course, the queen's pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3p4/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/R: Here we can initiate the Queen's Gambit with pawn to c4. Black has to make a tough choice here - either take our free pawn (which isn't actually free!), or try to hold onto the center.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/2PP4/8/PP2PPPP/: In this course we'll cover what happens when Black DOESN'T take our pawn. This is actually the most common way Black will play against us. When they decline our gambit, we move our knight to c3, adding more pressure on the center..
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/1bPP4/2N5/PP2PP: The best move is to open our light-square bishop with pawn to e3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/1bPP4/2N1P3/PP3: We have now transposed into another opening called the nimzo-indian. That opening deserves its own full course (which i will be making) but for now I won't leave you hungry and I'll throw you 1 line for it. Let's play pawn to a3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/2PP4/P1b1P3/1P3: Let's take back with pawn to c3.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/2PP4/P1P1P3/5P: Let's play pawn takes d5 here.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/4p3/3n4/3P4/P1P1P3/5PPP: Let's develop our bishop to d3.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/4p3/8/3P4/P1nBP3/5PPP/R: This is a huge mistake from black. It looked like a free pawn but now we have queen to c2, forking the knight and the h7 pawn.
descriptions.rnbq1r1k/ppp2ppB/4p3/3n4/3P4/P3P3/2Q2PPP: Now our bishop can come home to d3.
descriptions.rnbq1r1k/ppp2pp1/4p3/3n4/3P4/P2BP3/2Q2PP: Great. We are simply winning here.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2pp4/2PP4/2N5/PP2PPP: Black has played the Tarrasch Defense. From here, we should take the pawn on d5 first. c4 pawn takes d5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/8/2pp4/3P4/2N5/PP2PPPP/R: Let's continue our development with knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n5/2pp4/3P4/2N2N2/PP2PP: Now is a good time to take with pawn to c5.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pp3ppp/2n5/2bp4/8/2N2N2/PP2PPPP: Black forgot we have two attackers on the d5 pawn. Queen takes on d5.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pp3ppp/2n5/2bq4/8/2N2N2/PP2PPPP: And knight takes queen on d5.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pp3ppp/2n5/2bN4/8/5N2/PP2PPPP/R: Well done! We are up a pawn and life is good.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/3p4/2PP4/2N5/PP2PP: Let's have some fun: pawn to e4. This is called the Marshall Gambit
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/2p1pn2/3p4/2PPP3/2N5/PP3: This is a mistake from black! Let's play c-pawn captures on d5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/4pn2/3p4/3PP3/2N5/PP3PPP: Now we see why it was a mistake from black. We can push pawn to e5 here, booting the knight.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/4p3/3pP3/3P4/2N5/PP3PP: Let's wrap up with queen to g4, stopping the enemy dark-square bishop from being able to develop.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/4p3/3pP3/3P2Q1/2N5/PP3: Well done! The computer is absolutely in love with our position here. We'll develop our knight, bishop, and castle kingside soon.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/2PP4/2N5/PP2PP: And now let's relieve some of the pressure in the center with pawn takes on d5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/3P4/2N5/PP2PPPP: Let's pin Black's knight with bishop to g5.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bppp/5n2/3p2B1/3P4/2N5/PP2PP: We need to stabilize our center and prepare for more development. Pawn to e3.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/5n2/3p2B1/3P4/2N1P3/PP: Let's develop our bishop to d3.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p1p1bppp/1p3n2/3p2B1/3P4/2NBP3/: Blunder! Black didn't defend their d5 pawn or reinforce their f6 knight, which means we are going to get a winning position. First, bishop takes knight on f6.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p1p2ppp/1p3b2/3p4/3P4/2NBP3/PP3: Now the killer queen to h5, threatening mate on h1 and to take the pawn on d5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p1p2p1p/1p3bp1/3p3Q/3P4/2NBP3/P: Now we get our pawn! Queen to d5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/p1p2p1p/1p3bp1/3Q4/3P4/2NBP3/PP: Well done! We are up a pawn and have a better position. Life is good.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bppp/2p2n2/3p2B1/3P4/2NBP3/P: This is Black's most common response. Let's build a battery with queen to c2.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bpp1/2p2n1p/3p2B1/3P4/2NBP3/: Let's back our bishop up to h4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp1nbpp1/2p2n1p/3p4/3P3B/2NBP3/: Let's continue with our development plan: knight to e2.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp1nbpp1/2p4p/3p4/3Pn2B/2NBP3/P: Our bishop is now hanging! Before we mess with Black's knight, let's capture with bishop to e7.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp1nqpp1/2p4p/3p4/3Pn3/2NBP3/PP: One last thing before we mess with Black's knight - let's bring our a-rook over to e1.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp2qpp1/2p2n1p/3p4/3Pn3/2NBP3/P: Finally, we have done all the preparation and we can play pawn to f3, kicking the knight.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp2qpp1/2pn1n1p/3p4/3P4/2NBPP2/: Retreating was a mistake from black! Now we finally get our e-pawn push. Pawn to e4.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp2qpp1/2pn1n1p/8/3Pp3/2NB1P2/P: Let's capture back with pawn to e4.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp2qpp1/2pn1n1p/8/3PP3/2NB4/PPQ: Well done! We are threatening a fork on the next move with pawn to e5, and even though the material is equal, the computer thinks we are 2 point ahead.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/2p2n2/3p4/3PP3/2N5/PP3PP: Black's knight is vulnerable to attack. Pawn to e5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/2p2n2/3pP3/3P4/2N5/PP3PP: Well done! Our position is great and chess engines think we are 1 point ahead here.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1bpp1/5n1p/3p2B1/3P4/2NBP3/P: Black is attacking our bishop, let's back up with bishop to h4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bpp1/2p2n1p/3p4/3P3B/2NBP3/P: Let's continue developing with knight to e2.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/pp2bpp1/2p2n1p/3p4/3P2bB/2NBP3/: Bishop to g4 is what I like to call a bad move. We can kick it away with pawn to f3.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/pp2bpp1/2p2n1p/3p3b/3P3B/2NBPP2: Let's chase the bishop. Knight to f4.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/pp2bpp1/2p2n1p/3p3b/3P1N1B/2NBP: Well done! The computer loves our position and white wins like 70% of the time here.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/2PP4/2b1P3/PP3P: Take back with pawn to c3 of course.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/2PP4/2P1P3/P4PP: Now we have the evil bishop to a3, stopping Black from ever castling kingside.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/2PP4/B1P1P3/P4P: Well done! I'd be so annoyed if I were Black right now.
descriptions.r1bqrnk1/pp2bpp1/2p2n1p/3p4/3P3B/2NBP3/P: Let's go pawn to f3 here, beginning our attack. You'll see this a lot in Queen's Gambit declined: bishop to d3, knight to e2, castle, and we push our f-pawn and e-pawn. Once again, pawn to f3 here.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp2bpp1/2p1nn1p/3p4/3P3B/2NBPP2: Our plan is to one day play pawn to e4, but we need a little more preparation before we do it. Let's bring our a-rook to d1 to so we can defend our d pawn before we push the e pawn.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp2bpp1/4nn1p/2pp4/3P3B/2NBPP2/: When Black plays pawn to c5, we take. Pawn takes on c5.
descriptions.r1bqr1k1/pp2bpp1/4nn1p/2Pp4/7B/2NBPP2/PP: Well done! Our pieces are coordinated beautifully and the computer loves our position - even giving us a 1 or 2 point advantage.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/8/2pP4/2N5/PP2PPPP/: Let's play pawn to e4, opening up our bishop to attack the c4 pawn.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/8/2pPP3/2N5/PP3PPP/: Well done - we have transposed into the Queen's Gambit Accepted variation. To learn about how to play from here - go check out that course. I know the author and he's a really good guy.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp1nq1p1/2p4p/3p1p2/3Pn3/2NBP3/: Black just made a huge weakness we can target. First, let's get the knight out of the way with pawn to f3.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp1nq1p1/2p4p/3p1p2/3P4/2nBPP2/: And capture back with our knight to c3.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp1nq1p1/2p4p/3p1p2/3P4/2NBPP2/: Well done! We have 2 pieces aimed right at Black's undefended f-pawn, and black really has no good way to defend it.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bppp/5n2/2pp2B1/3P4/2NBP3/PP: Black is fighting our center. We should take their pawn with pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/5n2/2bp2B1/8/2NBP3/PP3PP: Let's continue with our development plan. Knight from g1 to e2
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/5n2/2bp2B1/8/2NBP3/PP2NP: Well done! The computer likes our position here.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4p3/3n4/3P4/2N5/PP2PPPP: Black took with the knight! Which means we can play pawn to e4, winning the center and booting the knight.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/2n5/PP3PPP/R: Take back with pawn to c3, of course.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bppp/4p3/8/3PP3/2P5/P4PPP/R1: Black is playing quite weak here - giving us the entire center. With absolutely no challenges from black, let's continue with simple chess and play knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/4p3/8/3PP3/2P2N2/P4PPP: Let's continue developing and stabilize our weak e4 pawn with bishop to d3.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bppp/4p3/2p5/3PP3/2PB1N2/P4P: That pawn push isn't scary. Let's castle.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bppp/4p3/8/3pP3/2PB1N2/P4PPP: Take back, of course. Pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2bppp/2n1p3/8/3PP3/3B1N2/P4PP: Let's develop our bishop and defend our d4 pawn with bishop to b2.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2bppp/2n1p3/8/3PP3/3B1N2/PB3P: Well done! We simply outplayed black in the opening and now have a better position for the middlegame.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/8/2PPp3/2N5/PP3PPP: Let's capture back with our knight. Knight to e4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/2p1pn2/8/2PPN3/8/PP3PPP/: Here it's best to trade knights. Knight takes on f6.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/pp3ppp/2p1pq2/8/2PP4/8/PP3PPP/R: Let's develop our other knight to f3.
descriptions.rnb1k2r/pp3ppp/2p1pq2/8/1bPP4/5N2/PP3PPP: And block with bishop to d2.
descriptions.rnb1k2r/pp3ppp/2p1pq2/8/2PP4/5N2/PP1Q1PP: Well done! The computer gives us the edge in this position
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/8/1bPPN3/8/PP3PPP/: Let's block with bishop to d2, baiting black into something nasty.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/8/1bPqN3/8/PP1B1PP: Black accepted the marshal gambit which means we have a very fun game ahead of us. Let's take blacks bishop with bishop to b4
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/8/1BP1q3/8/PP3PPP/: Now we block with bishop to e2. Yes - we are giving away the g2 pawn!
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/8/1BP5/8/PP2BPqP/R: We have to defend our rook here. Bishop to f3.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/6q1/1BP5/5B2/PP3P1: Let's develop our knight. Knight to e2.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/6q1/1BP5/5B2/PP2NP: Well done! Even though we are down two pawns, our rook will be coming into the open file, our dark-square bishop is piercing the position, and our queen is staring down the d-file. The computer is giving us a 1 point advantage here.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/3P4/3p4/2N5/PP2PPPP/: This is a mistake from black because we have queen to a4 check which is just a bit annoying for them. Queen to a4.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/pp1b1ppp/4p3/3P4/Q2p4/2N5/PP2PP: And once black defends, we scoop up a pawn. Queen takes on d4.
descriptions.rn1qkbnr/pp1b1ppp/8/3p4/3Q4/2N5/PP2PPPP/: Now let's take with the queen. Queen to d5.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp1b1ppp/5n2/3Q4/8/2N5/PP2PPPP/: Let's back our queen up to b3.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/pp1b1ppp/5n2/8/8/1QN5/PP2PPPP/R: Well done! We are simply up a pawn. We need to develop and castle but not a bad start! And the computer likes our position.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n5/2P5/3p4/2N2N2/PP2PPP: Our knight is under attack and so is our c-pawn. Let's put our knight on a4 to defend our c-pawn
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pp3ppp/2n5/2b5/N2p4/5N2/PP2PPPP: Let's trade with the bishop. Knight takes on c5. It may look like it's undefended but white has a trick up their sleeve.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pp3ppp/2n5/2q5/3p4/5N2/PP1BPPPP: Let's attack the queen with rook to c1.
Well done! We have a rook on the open c-file, more development, and a safer king.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/4p3/2p5/3PP3/2P5/P4PPP/R: Let's defend our pawn with knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/4p3/8/3pP3/2P2N2/P4PPP/R: Let's take back with the pawn, trying to keep our center intact. Pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3ppp/4p3/8/1b1PP3/5N2/P4PPP/R1: We have to block with bishop to d2.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/5N2/P2b1PPP/R2: Take back with queen to d2.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/5N2/P2Q1PPP/R: Black has castled and our king is still in the middle of the board. Priority number 1: get him to safety. Bishop to c4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp1n1ppp/4p3/8/2BPP3/5N2/P2Q1PP: Phew - we can shelter our king. Let's castle.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p2n1ppp/1p2p3/8/2BPP3/5N2/P2Q1P: Our next priority - bring our rooks to support our pawns. Let's bring the f-rook to e1.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pb1n1ppp/1p2p3/8/2BPP3/5N2/P2Q1P: And now the a-rook to d1.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pb1n1ppp/1p2p3/8/2BPP3/5N2/P2Q1P: If Black attacks our bishop, simply back up our bishop to b3.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pb1n1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/1B3N2/P2Q1: Well done! Our position is solid and we are ready to play chess!
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/3P4/P1P1P3/5PPP: Let's develop our bishop to d3 here.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/5n2/2pp4/3P4/P1PBP3/5PPP: Let's continue our development plan, knight to e2.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp2qpp1/2p2n1p/3p4/3P4/2nBPP2/P: Let's take back with the knight to c3.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/pp2qpp1/2p2n1p/3p4/3P4/2NBPP2/P: Well done! We are ready to continue our game.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Let's learn the Rousseau Gambit! I don't even know where to begin with this opening... it is SO aggressive. It is SO trappy. Best of all, it is SO fun. We begin with pawn to e5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1PPP: We'll defend our pawn with knight to c6 next. So far this is all standard stuff. The fun begins on the next move.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/2B1P3/5N2/PPPP: The next move is just disgusting. I guarantee your opponent has never seen it before and I guarantee you'll win a LOT of games with it: pawn to f5. Yup, we're giving away a pawn AND exposing our king. Trust me and do it :)
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/4pp2/2B1P3/2N2N2/PP: White defended their pawn with the knight. Pretty normal move, right? Looks harmless enough. But actuallyâ¦ nope. That little knight just lost white the whole game. I'm serious. Pawn takes pawn on e4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/4p3/2B1N3/5N2/PPPP1: Now we just play pawn to d5, forking the knight and bishop, and white can resign.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/3pp3/2B1N3/5N2/PPPP1: We're winning a piece. We're winning the game.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/4pP2/2B5/5N2/PPPP1P: OK so we gambited our pawn, now what? Well, now we can push our pawn to e4 and attack that helpless knight on f3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/5P2/2B1p3/8/PPPP1PP: We scared the knight away, now let's scare the bishop. Pawn to d5 wins us the whole center.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/1B1p1P2/4p3/8/PPPP1P: Boring people would just capture the f5 pawn here. But we're not boring, are we? Queen to g5, attacking the undefended g2 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp3pp/2B5/3p1Pq1/4p3/8/PPPP1PP: That's totally fine - pawn takes bishop on c6.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/p1p3pp/2p5/3p1Pq1/4p3/6P1/PPPP1: Time to grab the f5 pawn. We could take it with the bishop, but the queenâs sitting a little uncomfortably where she is. Queen takes f5 cleans things up and puts her on a better square.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/p1p3pp/2p5/3p1q2/4p3/6P1/PPPP1P: We have absolutely smoked white here - just look at their development! Or should I say, their lack-of-development.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/1B1p1Pq1/4p3/6P1/PPP: Weâve already messed up Blackâs pawn structure, so now we can go after the f5 pawn. Our queenâs not looking too comfy on g5âsheâs just wide open to attacks. So letâs solve both problems at once with queen takes pawn on f5.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/1B1p1q2/4p3/6P1/PPPP: Well done! We're just crushing white here because of our strong central control. The computer gives us a +1.5 point advantage
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/5P2/2B1p3/5N2/PPPPQ: Woahhhh. White is trying to be SNEAKY. Now that their queen is pinning our pawn to our king, we can no longer take the knight. Well not so fast, white! We can just play queen to e7 and all of a sudden, the threat on the knight is renewed.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppppq1pp/2n5/5P2/2B1p3/8/PPPPQP: White ran away like the cowards they are. Let's play knight to f6 here, to stop white's queen from ever coming to h5, and also to set up a pawn-to-d5 in the future.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppppq1pp/2n2n2/5P2/2B1p3/3P4/PP: Aaaaaaaand game over. We have a deadly move on white that will probably make them quit chess. Knight to d4 attacking the queen AND the c2 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppppq1pp/5n2/5P2/2Bnp3/3P4/PPPQ: Dang... white moved their queen AND defended knight to c2. The funny part? We can STILL play knight to c2, completely sacrificing our knight.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppppq1pp/5n2/5P2/2B1p3/3P4/PPQ2: Do you see the best move? The move that will make white quit the game? Hint: it's pawn takes pawn on d3, opening up a CHECK to the king and ATTACKING the queen. That means no-matter what white does, that queen is ours.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppppq1pp/5n2/5P2/2B5/8/PP2pPPP/: I think you got it from here :D
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/3p1P2/4p3/1B6/PPPP1P: Now we COULD play bishop takes pawn on f4, to even out the material. But I have a better idea: let's play queen to g5 and attack white's undefended g2 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/3p1Pq1/4p3/1B4P1/PPP: Itâs time to capture the f5 pawn. Both the bishop and queen could take it, but the queen is exposed on g5 and needs to move soon. Queen takes f5 is best, solving both problems at once.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/3p1q2/4p3/1B4P1/PPPP: Two pawns in the center? Check. More pieces developed? Check. Going to win this game? Check.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/4pp2/2B1P3/3P1N2/PP: OK white played a good move here, but hope is not lost! We still have tons of chances here. Bishop to c5.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1ppN1/2B1P3/3P4/P: White is trying to put their knight on f7, forking our queen and rook. We need to stop it! How do we stop it? Shoot... there's no way to stop it. The best move here is actually pawn to f4, completely ignoring white's threat.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1Npp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1Pp2/3P4/P: Our rook and our queen are forked. I guess we should just resign.... JUST KIDDING! We still have a trick to try and even out the game.  Queen to h4 threatening checkmate on f2.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1Npp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1Pp1q/3P4/: White defended checkmate, so I guess we should just resign? JUST KIDDING! We have another trick to even out the game. Knight to f6, LOSING our rook.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/pppp2pp/2n2n2/2b1p3/2B1Pp1q/3P4/: White took our rook. So I guess we should just resign the game? JUST KIDDING! We've actually won the game with one move: knight to g4. All of a sudden, white isn't looking so comfortable. There's just too much pressure on the h2 and f2 squares.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1Ppnq/3P3P/P: White had to defend checkmate on h2, but we still have knight takes pawn on f2.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1Pp1q/3P3P/P: We COULD take the rook with the bishop, but taking with the queen is actually better and will win us the game in just a few moves. Queen takes rook on f2.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1Pp2/3P3P/PP: OK so is our attack over? The white king looks pretty safe and we have no more checks to give. Well, here we have the deadly pawn to f3. A simple pawn push will win us the game. We are threatening mate with queen to g2.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1P3/3P1Q1P/P: White got rid of our dangerous pawn, but it's actually still checkmate in 1. Can you find it? Hint: queen to g1.
We just checkmated our opponent in 12 moves - chess is so easy.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1Bpp/2n5/2b1p1N1/4Pp2/3P4/P: That was an awful awful move hahahaha. We just move our king to f8 and all of a sudden both white's knight AND white's bishop are under attack, and white can't save them both.
descriptions.r1bq1knr/pppp1Bpp/2n5/2b1p1N1/4Pp2/3P4/P: It might not look like it, but we are actually way ahead here. Either white moves their bishop and loses their knight, or they move their knight and lose their bishop.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/3p1P1Q/2B1p3/8/PPPP1: OK white definitely just played the best move, checking our king. Only one move here keeps our advantage, and it's NOT blocking the check with pawn to g6. It's actually sliding our king up to e7. It's a little annoying we can't castle anymore, but it's worth it for the huge center we grabbed.
descriptions.r1bq1bnr/ppp1k1pp/2n5/3p1P1Q/4p3/1B6/PPP: Let's get white's annoying queen out of the way. Knight to f6 developing our knight and attacking her.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp1k1pp/2n2n2/3p1PQ1/4p3/1B6/P: The queen is really insisting on staying. Let's insist she doesn't. Pawn to h6.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp1k1p1/2n2n1p/3p1PQ1/4p3/1B6/: Well done! We simply have the center and more development, and we'll probably find a way to win that f5 pawn soon. The computer has us at a +1.5 point advantage.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1P3/3P1P1P/P: With white's king on a light square, we can't do much with just our queen and dark-squared bishop right now. We need to get our light-squared bishop in the game. Pawn to d5 to open him up!
descriptions.r1b1k2N/ppp3pp/2n5/2bBp3/4P3/3P1P1P/PPP2: Now bishop to h3, and white is toast.
descriptions.r3k2N/ppp3pp/2n5/2bBp3/4P3/3P1P1b/PPP2q2: It's a forced checkmate in 4, but I guarantee you white resigns at this point
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1Npp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1Pp1q/3P2P: Let's tuck our queen into into h3. Yes, we're losing the rook on h8 but our queen on h3 will be able to do a LOT more damage to white.
descriptions.r1b1k1nN/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1Pp2/3P2Pq/: White captured our rook - no surprise there. Before we start attacking with our queen, we want to get our light-squared bishop into the game. We can do that with pawn to d5. We sacrifice a pawn but now our bishop is free. You'll see why this is important in a second.
descriptions.r1b1k1nN/ppp3pp/2n5/2bBp3/4Pp2/3P2Pq/PPP: Now we begin our attack (which will win us the game). First: bishop to g4 hitting the queen.
descriptions.r3k1nN/ppp3pp/2n5/2bBp3/4Ppb1/3P2Pq/PPPQ: Let's add one MORE piece to the mix: knight to d4. On the next move we'll be able to play knight to f3 forking the king and queen.
descriptions.r3k1nN/ppp3pp/8/2bBp3/3nPpb1/3P2Pq/PPPQ1: Our attack on white is unstoppable. White's king is completely trapped with no squares to go to, and we're about to play knight to f3, forking the king and queen. The computer gives us a +6 point advantage.
descriptions.r3k1nN/ppp3pp/2n5/2bBp3/4Ppb1/3P1PPq/PPP: Our bishop is one of our only attacking pieces, and we're already 6 points down in material. We should probably save it right? WRONG! We SACRIFICE our bishop by playing pawn takes pawn on g3.
descriptions.r3k1nN/ppp3pp/2n5/2bBp3/4P1P1/3P2pq/PPP4: OK so what's the plan now? Well, see that pawn on g3? We're going to make it a queen. First; march the pawn to g2.
descriptions.r3k1nN/ppp3pp/2n5/2bBp3/4P1P1/3P3q/PPP3p: Iâm ending the line here because White can try a few moves to delay the inevitable, but in the end Whiteâs rook is completely trapped and our pawn will turn into a queen.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppppq1pp/2n2n2/5P2/2B1p3/2N5/PP: Let's charge headfirst: knight to d4 hitting the queen and threatening a fork on c2
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppppq1pp/5n2/5P2/2Bnp3/2N5/PPPP: Let's sacrifice another pawn for the sake of quick development. Pawn to d5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1q1pp/5n2/3N1P2/2Bnp3/8/PPPP: We have to take the knight here or else our attack is over. Knight takes knight on d5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1q1pp/8/3B1P2/3np3/8/PPPP1PP: We're 2 pawns down, but our future attack is so strong the computer gives us a +1.5 point advantage. The queen on e7 and pawn on e4 make it impossible for white to develop. Bishop takes pawn on f5.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1q1pp/8/3B1b2/3np3/2P5/PP1P1PP: Should we retreat our knight? Nope! Knight sacrifices himself on f3.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1q1pp/8/3B1b2/4p3/2P2P2/PP1P1P: Now we begin one of the most disgusting sequences I've ever written about: pawn takes pawn on f3 discovered check.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1q1pp/8/3B4/8/2Pb1p2/PP1PNP1P/: Now the DISGUSTING pawn takes knight on e2, forking the king and queen. Yes, a PAWN is forking the king and queen on the first rank. It's technically more accurate to take with the bishop here but I don't care. A pawn forking the king and queen is just way too cool to pass up.
descriptions.r1bqkbBr/pppp2pp/2n5/4pp2/4P3/5N2/PPPP1P: Woahhhh. I did NOT expect that move... I guess white thinks they're surprising us by taking our knight? We'll it's a good thing you took this course: rook recaptures bishop on g8
descriptions.r1bqkbr1/pppp2pp/2n5/4pP2/8/5N2/PPPP1PPP: Even without our knight, we can still crush white with the rousseau gambit. As usual, when white takes our f5 pawn, we play pawn to e4, hitting their knight.
descriptions.r1bqkbr1/pppp2pp/2n5/5P2/4p3/8/PPPP1PPP/: ...and as usual, once white moves their knight away, we can take the whole center with pawn to d5
descriptions.r1bqkbr1/ppp3pp/2n5/3p1P1Q/4p3/8/PPPP1PP: That check looks scary, but we can actually block it with the incredible pawn to g6.
descriptions.r1bqkbr1/ppp4p/2n3P1/3p3Q/4p3/8/PPPP1PPP: We can capture with the rook or the pawn here. I like capturing with the rook because it gives us full control of the g-file.
descriptions.r1bqkb2/ppp4Q/2n3r1/3p4/4p3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Queen to g5 defends our rook and also sets up a deadly battery along the g-file
descriptions.r1b1kb2/ppp4Q/2n3r1/3p2q1/4p3/6P1/PPPP1P: White defended the attack down the g-file but they missed the big picture. In 2 steps we can TRAP THE QUEEN. Step 1: Rook to h6
descriptions.r1b1kb2/ppQ5/2n4r/3p2q1/4p3/6P1/PPPP1P1P: White's queen can run but she can't hide! Bishop to d6 and white's queen is TRAPPED
descriptions.r1b1k3/ppQ5/2nb3r/3p2q1/4p3/6P1/PPPP1P1P: We trapped a queen! We trapped a queen!!!
descriptions.r3kb1r/pBp1q1pp/8/5b2/3np3/8/PPPP1PPP/R1: No crazy rook sacrifice this time... Rook to b8.
descriptions.1r2kb1r/p1p1q1pp/8/3B1b2/3np3/8/PPPP1PPP: Let's take advantage of the fact white's light squared bishop is away from home and play queen to g5, targeting the g2 pawn.
descriptions.1r2kb1r/p1p3pp/8/3B1bq1/3np3/6P1/PPPP1P1: The game is over at this point. Bishop to g4 and white's queen is lost
descriptions.1r2kb1r/p1p3pp/8/3B2q1/3np1b1/6P1/PPPP1P: We're going to win whites queen, and then the game :)
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1pP2/2B5/3P1N2/PP: Yay! White gave in and took our pawn. That means we can take the center - pawn to d5 takes the center and hits the bishop!
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp3pp/2n5/1BbppP2/8/3P1N2/PPP2: With white now pinning our knight on c6, nobody is defending our e5 pawn. The trick here is to IGNORE the threat on the e5 pawn and try to castle asap. You'll see in a second that we can create a nasty attack on white's kingside if they decide to take our pawn. Knight to e7
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp1n1pp/2n5/1BbpNP2/8/3P4/PPP2P: They took our pawn, and now our kingside attack begins: first step, castle.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1n1pp/2N5/1Bbp1P2/8/3P4/PPP2: Let's take back with our b7 pawn, winning a tempo against white's bishop
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p1p1n1pp/2p5/2bp1P2/B7/3P4/PPP2: Our nasty kingside attack is ready! All our pieces are active and pointing to the f-file, while white has absolutely no active pieces. So, even though we're down 2 pawns right now, we will absolutely crush white. First step: bishop takes pawn on f2.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p1p1n1pp/2p5/3p1P2/B7/3P4/PPP2K: Next step: knight takes pawn on f5, setting up a discovered check on the king.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p1p3pp/2p5/3p1n2/B7/3P4/PPP3PP/: The king is running - but is he safe? I don't think so. Lets activate our queen to f6, setting up a battery AND a check with queen-to-d4 if we ever need it.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1p3pp/2p2q2/3p1n2/B7/3P1Q2/PPP3: And now we win white's queen! Can you see the tactic? Hint: queen to d4 check.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1p3pp/2p5/3p1n2/B2q4/3P1Q2/PPP3: Now the beautiful knight to g3, checking the king AND discovering a skewer on the f-file right through the king and queen
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1p3pp/2p5/3p4/B2q4/3P1Qn1/PPP3P: It's times like these that make me remember why I love chess so much.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/4pp2/2BPP3/5N2/PPP2: White played the best move here. Maybe they've taken this course before? If so, let's hope they weren't paying close attention. Pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/5p2/2BNP3/8/PPP2PPP: One move here keeps us in the game, and its knight to f6. The idea is we'll sacrifice our f5 pawn but set up some traps if white decides to take it.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp2pp/2n2n2/5N2/2B1P3/8/PPP2P: White took our pawn, which means we can deploy our trap. Pawn to d5 hits the c4 bishop and discovers an attack on the f5 knight. All of a sudden, white isn't looking so great.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp3pp/2n2n2/3P1N2/2B5/8/PPP2PP: Let's take white's undefended knight with bishop to f5.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp3pp/2P2n2/5b2/2B5/8/PPP2PPP/R: It looks like we're just two pawns down, but we can save our position with this forcing sequence. First: queen takes queen check.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp3pp/2P2n2/5b2/2B5/8/PPPB1PPP/: We keep the pressure on white with knight to g4, threatening a fork on f2.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/pPp3pp/8/5b2/2B3n1/8/PPPB1PPP/RN: White threw in this in-between move, which doesn't really hurt us. With queens off the board, it's fine for our king to be a little exposed. King takes pawn on b7.
descriptions.3r1b1r/pkp3pp/8/5b2/2B3n1/8/PPPBKPPP/RN5: White defended the pawn on f2 - a very natural move, but it's a mistake! Let's add our bishop to the party with bishop c5, adding another attacker on that f2 pawn.
descriptions.3r3r/pkp3pp/8/2b2b2/2B3n1/5P2/PPPBK1PP/R: We don't even have to move our knight here. Instead let's bring our last piece to the party with rook to e8 check.
descriptions.3rr3/pkp3pp/8/2b2b2/2B3n1/5P2/PPPBK1PP/R: Our attack is just crushing here. Despite being down two points of material, the computer gives us a +5 point advantage!
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1q1pp/8/3B1b2/3np3/8/PPPPNPPP/: White wants to castle so bad. We can stop them with bishop to g4. Now if white tries to castle, they'll lose the knight to our 2 attackers.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1q1pp/8/8/2Bnp1b1/8/PPPPNPPP/R: That bishop is annoying - queen to c5 to scare him off!
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp3pp/8/2q5/2Bnp1b1/2P5/PP1PNPPP: The only good move here is taking the bishop and giving up our knight, because it doubles up white's pawns on the d-file. Queen takes bishop on c4.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp3pp/8/8/2qPp1b1/8/PP1PNPPP/R1B: Let's castle our king to safety and target that d4 pawn.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp3pp/8/8/2qPp1b1/8/PP1PNPPP/R1: Look how depressing white's position is here. They can't move their bishop (it's blocked in), they can't castle (or they'll lose their knight), they can't move their queen (or they'll get checkmated), and they can't move their knight (they'll lose their queen).
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/5P2/2Bp4/5N2/PPP2PP: That was the wrong move for white. Now we go on the attack with pawn to d5, hitting white's light-squared bishop and opening up our OWN light-squared bishop
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/1B1p1P2/3p4/5N2/PPP2: One last thing before we take the unguarded f5 pawn: let's play queen to e7 check. This will disrupt white's position, as they either have to block with their own queen or pull their bishop back.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp1q1pp/2n5/1B1p1P2/3p4/5N2/PP: If white blocks with the queen, we can simply trade queens. Queen takes queen on e2.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp3pp/2n5/1B1p1P2/3p4/5N2/PPP1: Now white's position will get completely messed up! If they try and recapture with their bishop, it's an ugly retreating move, and if they recapture with their king, they can no longer castle.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1pp2/2B1P3/3P1N2/: White is playing this really well. Let's just keep going with regular development: knight to f6.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp2pp/2n2n2/2b1pp2/2B1P3/2NP1N: Stockfish isn't that happy with our position, but we can still put white into an uncomfortable spot. First: pawn to f4 to block in white's dark-squared bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp2pp/2n2n2/2b1p3/2B1Pp2/P1NP1: The kingside is completely closed for white, so they're trying to start an attack on the queenside. We can ignore this and just play pawn to d6, opening up our light-squared bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp3pp/2np1n2/2b1p3/1PB1Pp2/P1NP: We'll drop our bishop down to b6 - no problem.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp3pp/1bnp1n2/3Np3/1PB1Pp2/P2P1: Let's trade off white's knight before he takes our good bishop on b6. Knight takes knight on d5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp3pp/1bnp4/3Bp3/1P2Pp2/P2P1N2/: Let's get rid of white's only defender on the kingside: the f3 knight. We can do this by playing knight to d4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp3pp/1b1p4/3Bp3/1P1NPp2/P2P4/2: We take the knight back, of course. Bishop to d4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp3pp/3p4/3Bp3/1P1bPp2/P2P4/2P2: With white's pieces no longer defending the king, we can start our attack: Queen to g5.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp3pp/3p4/3Bp1q1/1P1bPp2/P2P4/2: With our bishop staring at f2, our queen pinning g2, and our bishop on it's way to g4 or h3, white is in a LOT of trouble here.
descriptions.r1bq1b1r/ppp1k1pp/2n2n2/3p1P2/4p2Q/1B6/P: And now we just get to take that delicious f5 pawn with our bishop.
descriptions.r2q1b1r/ppp1k1pp/2n2n2/3p1b2/4p2Q/1B6/PP: Nicely done. Besides our king not being able to castle, life is great.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1pp2/2B1P3/2NP1N2: White doesn't want our f-pawn? Fine. They lost their chance. Pawn to f4, blocking in white's last dark-squared bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1Pp2/2NP1N2: We really want to activate our light-squared bishop: pawn to d6.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp3pp/2np4/2b1p3/2B1Pp2/P1NP1N: White's going for a queenside attack but that does't concern us one bit. We're interested in white's kingside. Bishop to g4.
descriptions.r2qk1nr/ppp3pp/2np4/2b1p3/2B1Ppb1/P1NP1N: Well done! On our next move we'll play knight to d4 and apply maximum pressure on that poor f3 knight.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/5P2/2BNp3/8/PPPP1PP: Woah woah woah. White's trying to trick us! If we take that "free" knight, they'll play queen to h5 check and we'll practically be checkmated. In the rousseau gambit, we're supposed to trick white, not the other way around! We'll ignore that "free" knight and instead play knight to f6 to defend against any queen-h5 business.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp2pp/2N2n2/5P2/2B1p3/8/PPPP1: Let's take back towards the center: b-pawn takes knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p1pp2pp/2p2n2/5P2/2B1p3/8/PPPP1: Well done! We resisted white's trap, equalized the position, and white really has nothing.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp2pp/2n5/2b1ppB1/2B1P3/3P1N2: OK we'll need to block that check with our bishop. Bishop to e7. Ideally white trades with us
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppppB1pp/2n5/4pp2/2B1P3/3P1N2/P: We'll capture back with the queen here, because we want to long-castle asap. Short-castling won't work anymore because of white's bishop on c4.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppppq1pp/2n5/4pp2/2B1P3/3P1N2/P: Well done! The position is almost equal, and once we develop our light-squared bishop we'll be able to castle our king queenside for safety.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp2pp/2n5/4Pp2/2Bp4/5N2/PPP2P: White is playing very well hereâour pieces feel cramped and short on space. To fight back, we need to break out our light-squared bishop. Let's play pawn to d5 to hit white's bishop and open up our own.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp3pp/2nP4/5p2/2Bp4/5N2/PPP2PP: Ok, we have some more breathing room now. Queen takes pawn on d6.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp3pp/2nq4/5p2/2Bp4/5N2/PPP2PP: Let's continue developing; knight to f6.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp3pp/2nq1n2/5p2/2Bp4/5N2/PPP2: Let's block the check with bishop to e7.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp1b1pp/2nq1n2/5p2/2Bp4/5N2/PPP: Well done! We can't castle kingside because of white's annoying c4 bishop, so our #1 priority going forward will be to develop our ligh-squared bishop and castle queenside. Once you do that, you should be in fine shape.

shortDescriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1PPP: Let's continue with the Rousseau Gambit
