descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the Ruy Lopez! This opening is unstoppable. It's irrefutable. It's so good that not a single line in this ENTIRE course will leave you in a bad position. Master this course, and I guarantee you'll have a significant advantage in every game you play. First things first: pawn to e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Second things second: knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1P:
To kick off the Ruy Lopez, we play bishop to b5. This does two things:
1. It lets us castle (nice).
2. It puts pressure on their knight, which is the only defender of their e5 pawn.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/1B2p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP: That was a very passive move, and it lets us play pawn to d4 immediately.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1pp2ppp/p1np4/1B2p3/3PP3/5N2/PP: Now we have a more-or-less forcing line that will win us a pawn. First: bishop takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/2p2ppp/p1pp4/4p3/3PP3/5N2/PPP2P: Now pawn takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/2p2ppp/p1p5/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPP2PPP: Now queen takes queen on d8.
descriptions.r1bk1bnr/2p2ppp/p1p5/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPP2PPP: Finally, we win a pawn with knight takes e5.
descriptions.r1bk1bnr/2p2ppp/p1p5/4N3/4P3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Well done! We are up a pawn and also threatening a nasty fork on f7. The computer loves our position and graces it with a +2.5 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/1Bb1p3/4P3/5N2/PPP: Black put their bishop in a bad square. Our plan is to boot it out with pawn to d4, but first we have to prepare that move with pawn to c3.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2np4/1Bb1p3/4P3/2P2N2/P: This falls right into our d4 plan: pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2np4/1Bb5/3pP3/2P2N2/PP: We take back with pawn to d4 to hit the bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2np4/1B6/1b1PP3/5N2/PP3: Now for a move you've probably NEVER done before. We aren't going to block check with the knight. We aren't going to block check with the bishop. We're going to MOVE OUR KING over to f1. No, seriously. The idea is we don't want to give a way for black to trade their dark squared bishop. This king slide to f1 will mean we'll likely win one of black's pieces.
descriptions.r2qk1nr/pppb1ppp/2np4/1B6/1b1PP3/5N2/PP3: Queen to a4, attacking the bishop and adding a bit more pressure to the c6 knight
descriptions.r2qk1nr/1ppb1ppp/2np4/pB6/Qb1PP3/5N2/PP3: Black's most common move here literally just loses them a bishop. No, seriously, the bishop is trapped right now. Pawn to a3 wins it on the spot.
descriptions.r2qk1nr/1ppb1ppp/2np4/pB6/Qb1PP3/P4N2/1P: Nice!! I won't complain about a free bishop.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/2p2ppp/p1p5/4p3/4P1b1/5N2/PPP2PP: OK, back to winning a free pawn. First: Queen takes queen on d8.
descriptions.3rkbnr/2p2ppp/p1p5/4p3/4P1b1/5N2/PPP2PPP: Now we finally get the pawn: Knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/1B6/3pP3/5N2/PPP2P: Knight captures back on d4, adding more pressure to the c6 knight.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/2np4/1B6/3NP3/8/PPP2PPP: Let's just play simple chess: knight to c3.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/3p4/1B6/3nP3/2N5/PPP2PP: Black is trying to break out of the position. Before we capture back on d4, let's play bishop takes bishop on d7.
descriptions.r3kbnr/pppq1ppp/3p4/8/3nP3/2N5/PPP2PPP/R: NOW we can play queen captures back on d4.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pppq1ppp/3p1n2/8/3QP3/2N5/PPP2PPP: Instead of castling kingside, let's actually play bishop to f4 and try to castle queenside.
descriptions.r4rk1/pppqbppp/3p1n2/8/3QPB2/2N5/PPP2PPP: Now we can unleash our master plan: Pawn to e5, hitting the f6 knight and adding a ton of pressure down the d-file.
descriptions.r4rk1/pppqbppp/3p1n2/4P3/3Q1B2/2N5/PPP2P: Well done!! There's a few ways black can try to untangle themselves out of this, but honestly none of them will work. We have a crushing position.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/1pp2ppp/p1np4/1B6/1b1PP3/5N2/PP: OK, we have the ability to trap black's bishop. First, we play bishop takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/2p2ppp/p1pp4/8/1b1PP3/5N2/PP3PP: Now queen to a4 and the bishop is TRAPPED.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/2p2ppp/2pp4/p7/Qb1PP3/5N2/PP3PP: Nice try black, but that does nothing to save the trapped bishop. Pawn to a3 now.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/1Bb1p3/4P3/2P2N2/: OK now we continue with our plan: pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/1Bb5/3pP3/2P2N2/P: Now before we take back, let's actually hit the knight with pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/1Bb1P3/3p2n1/2P2N2/: Black is double-attacking our e5 pawn now, so its a good time to play pawn takes pawn on d4 to reinforce that e5 pawn.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/1B2P3/1b1P2n1/5N2/P: We should block this check with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/1B2P3/1b1P2n1/2N2N: Finally, we can castle our king to safety.
Well done! Our dominant center gives us a +2.5 point advantage over our poor opponent.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/1ppp1ppp/p1n5/1B2p3/4P3/5N2/PPP: Black played the morphy defense, which asks us the question: do we want to take the knight or retreat the bishop? Retreating is actually a LOT more fun, so let's retreat to a4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/1ppp1ppp/p1n2n2/4p3/B3P3/5N2/PP: Sometimes I like to teach you how to play the most fun and aggressive moves possible. This is one of those times. Pawn to d4 CRASHING open the center.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/1ppp1ppp/p1n2n2/8/B2pP3/5N2/PPP: Here, do we retake the pawn? NO! We castle. Having our king out of the center is crucial for our plan.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1ppp1ppp/p1n2n2/2b5/B2pP3/5N2/PP: Black is trying to hold onto their pawn, but this won't work out well for them. We can play pawn to e5 and start causing problems for their knight.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1ppp1ppp/p1n5/2bnP3/B2p4/5N2/PPP: Black moved their knight, but we can attack it again with bishop to b3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1ppp1ppp/pnn5/2b1P3/3p4/1B3N2/PP: OK, black's knight is safe - but look at how all their pieces are stuck on the queen side! Now we make a sharp attack to the weak f7 pawn on the king's side with knight to g5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1ppp1ppp/pnn5/2b1P1N1/3p4/1B6/P: Ugh, it gets even WORSE for black. Queen to h5 and we're threatening all kinds of nasty stuff now.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1ppp1ppp/pnn5/2b1P1NQ/3p4/1B6/P: Nice!! Black is likely going to be checkmated here, or if not, they're going to be in a world of trouble.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/1bnp4/1B6/3PP3/5N2/PP3P: Running away was a huge mistake for black. Now we can just play pawn to d5 and their knight is in some real trouble.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/1pp2ppp/pbnp4/1B1P4/4P3/5N2/PP3: We retreat our bishop to a4, keeping the tension of the pin.
descriptions.r2qk1nr/1ppb1ppp/pbnp4/3P4/B3P3/5N2/PP3P: Aaaaand that move just lost them a knight. Pawn takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r2qk1nr/1ppb1ppp/pbPp4/8/B3P3/5N2/PP3PPP: Nice! We're up a whole knight.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppnppp/p1n5/2b1P3/3p4/1B3N2/PP: Let's play knight to g5 and attack the weak f7 pawn.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppnppp/p1n5/2b1P1N1/3p4/1B6/P: Black didn't think this one through... Now we can play queen to h5 and threaten all kinds of nasty stuff - including checkmate on h7.
descriptions.r1bq2k1/1pppnrp1/p1n4p/2b1P2Q/3p4/1B6/PP: Now bishop takes rook on f7.
descriptions.r1bq2k1/1pppnBp1/p1n4p/2b1P2Q/3p4/8/PPP2: Well done! Our attack is going to destroy black.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/1B2p3/4P3/5N2/PP: Black played the Berlin defense. The idea is we are putting pressure on black's e5 pawn, so in response, black puts pressure on our e4 pawn. The best move here is to castle. Our king will be out of the center (black's king is still stuck there) and our rook will be able to defend that pawn on the next move.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/1ppp1ppp/p1n2n2/1B2p3/4P3/5N2/P: This is one of the rare cases where it's best to actually trade off our bishop for the knight on c6 instead of running our bishop to a4. You'll see in a second it actually wins us a pawn. Bishop to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/1pp2ppp/p1p2n2/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP: Now we win our free pawn! Knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pp2ppp/p1pb1n2/4N3/4P3/8/PPPP1P: Let's drop our knight back to f3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pp2ppp/p1pb1n2/8/4P3/5N2/PPPP1P: Well done! We literally just have a pawn. I can't complain.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/1pp2ppp/p1p2n2/4N3/3qP3/8/PPPP1: So this is a common trap that black plays on us - and for the most part in this course I have made sure we've avoided this trap. Black is forking our knight and pawn, so they think they'll win atleast a pawn back. But, in this case, because we have castled, black actually CANNOT win the pawn back. I'll show you in a second - for now: knight to f3.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/1pp2ppp/p1p2n2/8/4q3/5N2/PPPP1P: YES!!! Black thought they won the pawn back but actually they lost their queen hahahahaa. Rook to e1 pins the queen against her own king.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/1pp2ppp/p1p2n2/8/8/5N2/PPPP1PPP: Queen takes queen on e1 of course.
LMAO, you're a queen up! This win isn't so much because we played perfectly, but more because Black tried to be sneaky and completely misunderstood the position. Well, a win is a win!
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/1B2p3/4n3/5N2/PPPP: Oh shoot. Black just won a free pawn... Or did they? In a second, we'll completely win it back, and maybe even get a better position afterwards. How do we do that? Well, Black's king is in the center and ours isn't, so lets open up the center with pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/1B6/3pn3/5N2/PPP2P: Now THAT was a mistake. If we see a king and a knight on the same empty file, we pin it, plain and simple. Rook to e1.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B1p4/3pn3/5N2/PPP2: Black tried to "anchor" their knight so we can't capture with the rook. But we don't need to capture with the rook! Because the knight is pinned, its stuck there and we can attack it with a pawn. Knight to d4 wins us back a pawn, puts pressure on the c6 knight, but most importantly it FREES up the f2 pawn to attack the e4 knight.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pppb1ppp/2n5/1B1p4/3Nn3/8/PPP2PP: We want to play pawn to f3 here to win the knight, but before we do that, let's quickly simplify. Bishop takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/p1pb1ppp/2p5/3p4/3Nn3/8/PPP2PPP/: ok NOW we can play f3. Pawn to f3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/p1pb1ppp/2p5/2bp4/3Nn3/5P2/PPP3PP: Black is prepping to castle. Doesn't matter to us, we can win a knight. Pawn takes knight on e4.
descriptions.r2qk2r/p1pb1ppp/2p5/2bp4/3NP3/8/PPP3PP/R: We are simply a knight up. Nice job!!
descriptions.r2qk2r/pppbnppp/2np4/1B6/Qb1PP3/5N2/PP3P: Black's bishop is only defended by the c6 knight. Let's give him the boot with pawn to d5.
descriptions.r2qk2r/1ppbnppp/p1np4/1B1P4/Qb2P3/5N2/PP: There's a few good ways to win from here, but the most fun is actually playing pawn takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r2qk2r/1ppbnppp/2Pp4/1p6/Qb2P3/5N2/PP3PP: Both of black's bishops are free for the taking. Let's take the d7 bishop first with check, then we can take the c4 bishop on the next move.
descriptions.r3k2r/1ppqnppp/3p4/1p6/Qb2P3/5N2/PP3PPP/: Nevermind, instead of taking the free bishop on b4, lets take the free ROOK on a8.
descriptions.Q3k2r/1ppqnppp/3p4/1p6/1b2P3/5N2/PP3PPP/: Up 7 points of material. Not bad.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/1Bb1p3/4P3/5N2/PP: Yes!! We get to do a very fun trick now. Knight takes pawn on e5 SACRIFICING the knight (don't worry, we'll win it back).
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/1Bb1n3/4P3/8/PPPP1P: Now for the trick: pawn to d4 forking the bishop and knight.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/3b1n2/1B2n3/3PP3/8/PPP2: That was black's WORST response because it walks them directly into ANOTHER fork. First: pawn takes knight on e5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/1B2b3/4P3/8/PPP2PPP: OK, now we set up the second fork: Pawn to f4 pushing the bishop back.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/3b1n2/1B6/4PP2/8/PPP3PP: Yes! Now we have pawn to e5 forking black AGAIN.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/1Bb1P3/5P2/8/PPP3PP: Ah dang it... We ALMOST won a piece with that fork but black had that annoying check to get out of it... King to h1.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/1Bb1P3/4nP2/8/PPP3PP/: That might seem like a wierd move but black actually had very few squares to put the knight. And actually - now the knight is trapped! Queen to e2.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/1Bb1P3/5P2/8/PPP1QnPP: Ah, black went for a sacrifice. Black gets a rook and we get a knight and bishop. That is a very winning trade for us. Rook takes knight on f2.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/8/1B2P3/5P2/8/PPP2QPP/R: I mean seriously, the rest of blacks pieces haven't even MOVED yet. We are dominating here.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/1B2n3/3bP3/8/PPP2PP: OK, queen captures the bishop on d4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/1B6/3QP3/8/PPP2PP: Black dropped their knight and is hitting our queen. We COULD move the queen but why complicate anything? Simply Bishop takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1pp1ppp/2p2n2/8/3QP3/8/PPP2PPP/: Black has two ways to capture back - and that one was both the most common way AND the wrong way. Seriously - now we have a +1.5 point advantage because of how strong our queen is and how trapped we'll make black's queen. Bishop to g5 pinning the knight to her.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p1pp1ppp/2p2n2/6B1/3QP3/8/PPP2P: That was - no joke - black's most common move, and now we win the game. Pawn to e5 hitting black's pinned knight.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p1pp1pp1/2p2n1p/4P1B1/3Q4/8/PPP: Bishop to h4, maintaining that deadly pin on the knight.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p1pp1p2/2p2n1p/4P1p1/3Q3B/8/PPP: Now that the pin is broken, its time to finally play pawn takes knight on f6.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p1pp1p2/2p2P1p/8/3Q3p/8/PPP2PPP: Mate in 2. Can you find it? Hint: It's queen to g4.
descriptions.r1bq1r2/p1pp1p1k/2p2P1p/8/6Qp/8/PPP2PPP/: Mate in 2. Can you find it? I hope so... Hint: It's queen to g7.
descriptions.r1bq1r2/p1pp1pQk/2p2P1p/8/7p/8/PPP2PPP/R: If you do this in a game, screenshot it and send it to me at ethan@chessreps.com
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1p1ppp/2p5/1Bb1P3/4nP2/8/PPP1Q: This delays the inevitable. Bishop back to safety to d3, adding another attacker to the knight.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1p1ppp/2p5/2b1P3/4nP2/3B4/PPP1: Well done! Black's knight is essentially trapped in the middle of the board. The computer puts us at a +4 point advantage and we win from here 80% of the time, even though the material is completely equal!
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pppb1ppp/2np4/1B2p3/3PP3/5N2/PPP: Let's develop with a simple knight to c3 here.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pppb1ppp/2np1n2/1B2p3/3PP3/2N2N2: Let's get rid of our light-square bishop. Bishop takes knight on c6. If you're curious why sometimes we trade off our bishop and sometimes we don't... so am I. But I promise this is the best way to play lol.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2bp1n2/4p3/3PP3/2N2N2/PP: Now we need to defend our e4 pawn, so queen to d3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp1bppp/2bp1n2/4p3/3PP3/2NQ1N2/P: Now's a good time to open up the center. Pawn takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp1bppp/2b2n2/4p3/4P3/2NQ1N2/PPP: Now we just get a free pawn lol. Knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r3k2r/ppp1bppp/2b2n2/4N3/4P3/2Nq4/PPP2PP: We want to take back with our pawn to keep our strong center. Pawn takes queen on d3.
descriptions.r3k2r/ppp1bppp/2b2n2/4N3/4P3/2NP4/PP3PPP: Nice!! We are up a pawn & own the center. We have like an 80% winrate from here.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/2pp1ppp/p1n5/1p2p3/B3P3/5N2/PPP: A LOT of people play this line as black, but it's actually not good for them. First things first, we need to back our bishop up to b3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2pp1ppp/p1n2n2/1p2p3/4P3/1B3N2/: Black is attacking our e4 pawn. Instead of passively defending, let's strike back in the center with pawn to d4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2pp1ppp/p4n2/1p2p3/3nP3/1B3N2/P: Let's play knight takes knight on d4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2pp1ppp/p4n2/1p6/3pP3/1B6/PPP2P: Black plays that move 97% of the time, but its actually a blunder. Now we have pawn to e5 to knock around their knight. The only square it can really go to is back home. Poor knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2pp1ppp/p7/1p2P3/3pn3/1B6/PPP2P: Awww poor knight. It went to the wrong square. Now simply queen to f3 and we have three DEADLY threats. First, we attack the undefended knight. Second, if the knight moves we attack the undefended rook on a8. Oh yeah - and third - we have checkmate threat on f7.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2ppp/p7/1p1pP3/3pn3/1B3Q2/PPP: It looks like pawn to d5 stopped all of our threats but simply e5 pawn en passants to d6 and our threats are renewed.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2ppp/p2n4/1p6/3p4/1B3Q2/PPP2P: Black protected checkmate but remember! Now we get the free rook. Queen to a8.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/2pp1ppp/p7/1p2P3/3p4/1B6/PPP2PP: Now simply queen to f3, forking the rook on a8 and checkmate on f7.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/2ppqppp/p7/1p2P3/3p4/1B3Q2/PPP2: Queen takes rook on a8. Easy peasy.
descriptions.Q1b1kbnr/2ppqppp/p7/1p2P3/3p4/1B6/PPP2PP: Aaaaaand now we have a rook. Game over. Black should resign. Chess is easy huh?
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppbppp/p1n2n2/8/B2pP3/5N2/PPP2: Black wants to castle. We aren't going to let that happen. Pawn e5 attacks the black knight.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppbppp/p1n5/4P3/B2pn3/5N2/PPP2: Let's take our pawn back: knight takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppbppp/p1n5/2n1P3/B2N4/8/PPP2P: Here's a fun one: Black is attacking our bishop so we should defend it right? NOPE! We SACRIFICE the bishop by playing knight to f5, threatening to capture on g7.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppbppp/p1n5/4PN2/n7/8/PPP2PPP/: That capture just lost white the game. Knight takes g7 check.
descriptions.r1bq1k1r/1pppbpNp/p1n5/4P3/n7/8/PPP2PPP/: Now bishop to h6, threatening some nasty discovered checks in the future.
descriptions.r1bq2kr/1pppbpNp/p1n4B/4P3/n7/8/PPP2PPP/: Black had to move out of the way, they really had no other option. Now we simply play f4 to stabilize our e5 pawn and stop black's knight from ever coming in.
descriptions.r1bq2kr/1pp1bpNp/p1np3B/4P3/n4P2/8/PPP3P: The last thing to remember here? When black tries to fight back and reclaim the e5 square, we actually PUSH our e5 pawn to e6. The idea here is to put our queen on g4 but we can't YET because the black's light-squared bishop is defending it. Once we push the pawn, the bishop no longer defends that square.
descriptions.r1bq2kr/1pp1bpNp/p1npP2B/8/n4P2/8/PPP3PP: Well done! From here, do whatever you can to put your queen on g4 and win the game.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2pp1ppp/p1n2n2/1p6/B2pP3/5N2/PP: We need to back our bishop up to b3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/2pp1ppp/p1n2n2/1pb5/3pP3/1B3N2/P: Black really wants to castle, but before they do, we can play pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/2pp1ppp/p1n5/1pb1P3/3p2n1/1B3N2/: Both of black's knights are attacking our e5 pawn. Instead of adding a defender to the e5 pawn, we can play bishop to d5 which pins the c6 knight to the a8 rook, removing an attacker of the pawn.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/2pp1ppp/p1n5/1pbBP3/3p2n1/5N2/P: Pawn to h3 boots the knight away.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/2pp1ppp/p1n4n/1pbBP3/3p4/5N1P/P: Bishop takes knight on h6, opening up the king for us, muahahahahaha
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/2pp1p1p/p1n4p/1pbBP3/3p4/5N1P/P: Now? The cool, calm, and collected b-knight to d2. The plan is to route him into the attack.
Now that's how you play chess! Black's position is completely devastated.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1ppp1ppp/pn6/2b1n1N1/3p4/1B6/PPP: Black moved the knight to e5 to defend the weak f7 pawn, but now simply rook to e1 pinning the knight to the king. Not much else to say.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pp2ppp/pn1p4/2b1n1N1/3p4/1B6/PP: Remember how we were attacking the f7 pawn? And then black defended with the knight? And then we pinned the knight to the king? Well that means the f7 pawn is undefended now. Knight takes pawn on f7 forking the queen and rook.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2ppp/p1np1n2/1p2p3/3PP3/1B3N2: Pawn takes pawn on e5 is the way.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2ppp/p1n2n2/1p2p3/4P3/1B3N2/P: Now queen takes queen on d8.
descriptions.r1bk1b1r/2p2ppp/p1n2n2/1p2p3/4P3/1B3N2/P: Black should have taken back with the knight, but about half the time they take back with the king and lose the game! Now we can play knight to g5 and threaten a nasty fork on f7.
descriptions.r2k1b1r/2p2ppp/p1n1bn2/1p2p1N1/4P3/1B6/P: That actually does nothing to stop our fork on f7. All we have to do first is get rid of the bishop with bishop to e6.
descriptions.r2k1b1r/2p3pp/p1n1pn2/1p2p1N1/4P3/8/PPP2: With the bishop gone, NOW we can fork. Knight to f7 check, forking the king and rook.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/2ppqppp/p4n2/1p2P3/3p4/1B6/PPP2: Black is attacking our pawn. Let's castle and INVITE black to take our pawn. If they do, we can pin the queen against her own king with our rook.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/2ppqppp/p7/1p2P3/3p4/1B6/PPP2PP: Queen to f3 attacks the a8 rook and puts more pressure on the f7 pawn.
descriptions.1rb1kbnr/2ppqppp/p7/1p2P3/3p4/1B3Q2/PPP2: Black saved their rook, but we have bigger plans. We want to get our queen to the f7 square, but black's queen is defending it. What if we try to lure the queen away? Bishop to g5 is a full bishop sacrifice but it LURES the queen away from the f7 square.
descriptions.1rb1kbnr/2ppq1pp/p4p2/1p2P1B1/3p4/1B3Q2/: While black's king and queen are still exposed in the middle of the board, let's rip open the center. Pawn takes pawn on f6.
descriptions.1rb1kbnr/2ppq1pp/p4P2/1p4B1/3p4/1B3Q2/PP: Well done! There's a few continuations from here but they're all completely winning for us. Especially when we connect our rooks and try and pin the queen against the king - it's game over.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2ppp/p1np1n2/1p6/3pP3/1B3N2/P: Now we can play knight to g5 attacking the weak f7 pawn.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2ppp/p2p1n2/1p2n1N1/3pP3/1B6/: Black's knight is the only thing stopping us from getting to the f7 square. Let's boot the knight with pawn to f4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2ppp/p2p1n2/1p4N1/2npPP2/1B6/: Now notice how our king is safe and black's king is still in the center. Let's open up the center with pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2ppp/p4n2/1p2p1N1/2np1P2/1B6/: OK we obviously would LIKE to take back with pawn to e5, but if we do that, black's knight just gets to go back to e5. Let's get rid of black's knight first with bishop takes knight on c4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2ppp/p4n2/4p1N1/2pp1P2/8/PPP3: NOW we can play pawn takes pawn on e5. Black is in a tough spot because if they move their knight, our knight can get to f7 (our rook is also pointing at f7).
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2pp1/p4n1p/4P1N1/2pp4/8/PPP3P: Black's queenside is already destroyed. We destroy the kingside now with pawn takes knight on f6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2pp1/p4P2/6p1/2pp4/8/PPP3PP/R: Now the killing blow: queen to f3 hitting the rook on a1 and adding a ton more pressure down the f-file.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/2p2pp1/p3bP2/6p1/2pp4/5Q2/PPP3PP: Now for one of the most fun forcing sequences I've ever seen. By the way - no other chess website in the world will show you this (I checked). Queen to c6 check.
descriptions.Q2qk2r/2pb1pp1/p4P2/6p1/2pp4/8/PPP3PP/RN: Now we sacrifice the queen with pawn takes pawn on g7. If black takes our queen, we just capture the rook and make a new one (which results in a check and lets us win black's queen as well).
descriptions.2k3r1/2pb1pP1/p7/6B1/2pp4/8/PPP3PP/RN4K1: Finally, let's protect our passed pawn with bishop to f6.
descriptions.r2qk2r/2pbnppp/p1pp4/1B6/Qb2P3/5N2/PP3PP: OK, we won our piece. Now is a good time to get out of here. Bishop back to d3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/2pbnppp/p1pp4/8/Qb2P3/3B1N2/PP3PP: Nice job! Just watch out for any discovered attacks on our queen but otherwise we should be good!
descriptions.r2q3r/1ppknppp/3p4/1p6/Qb2P3/5N2/PP3PPP/: OK let's take our free bishop now: queen takes bishop on b4.
descriptions.r2q3r/1ppknppp/3p4/1p6/1Q2P3/5N2/PP3PPP/: Up 5 points of material. Not bad.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/2p2ppp/p7/1p1pP3/3p4/1B3Q2/PPP2: Bishop to d5! Bishop to d5!!! We threaten the rook on a8 and CHECKMATE on f7. White can't save both.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/2p2ppp/p3b3/1p1BP3/3p4/5Q2/PPP2P: Black protected checkmate but now we just steal that free rook :) Bishop to a8
descriptions.B2qkbnr/2p2ppp/p3b3/1p2P3/3p4/5Q2/PPP2PP: We have a free rook! It should be very easy to convert this to a win
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/1pp2ppp/p1np4/b2P4/B3P3/5N2/PP3: The best way to block this check is with knight to d2, because we'll want him to be routed to c4 later in the game anyways.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/2p2ppp/p1np4/bp1P4/B3P3/5N2/PP1: Now a trade that will leave us a pawn up: pawn takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/2p2ppp/p1Pp4/b7/p3P3/5N2/PP1N1P: Now we get our pawn! Queen takes pawn on a4.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/2p2ppp/pbPp4/8/Q3P3/5N2/PP1N1PP: Finally - remember how I said we want our knight to end up on c4? Well now we can do it! Knight to c4 hitting the bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/2p2ppp/pbPp4/8/Q1N1P3/5N2/PP3PP: Nice!! Would you be surprised if I told you that white has a 90% winrate from here?
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp2pp/2n5/1B3p2/3pn3/5N2/PPP2: Black tried to "anchor" their knight so we can't capture with the rook. But we don't need to capture with the rook! Because the knight is pinned, its stuck there and we can attack it with a pawn. Knight to d4 wins us back a pawn, and FREES up the f2 pawn to attack the e4 knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp2pp/8/1B3p2/3nn3/8/PPP2PPP/: Black took our knight. I'm not sure why. Let's just recapture with our queen to d4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1p2pp/2p5/1B3p2/3Qn3/8/PPP2PP: OK it sucks but we ACTUALLY can't save our bishop and capture the knight at the same time. Trust me, I tried. The best thing to do is LET black capture our bishop and just play pawn to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1p2pp/8/1p3p2/3Qn3/5P2/PPP3PP: Pawn takes the pinned knight. Pawn to e4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1p2pp/8/1p6/3Qp3/8/PPP3PP/RNB: Aaaaaaaaaaand game over. Black is actually done. Rook takes pawn on e4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1pb1pp/8/1p6/3QR3/8/PPP3PP/RNB: That was black's only real move. Now queen takes pawn on g7.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1pb1Qp/8/1p6/4R3/8/PPP3PP/RNB3: OK winning from here will be easy. We have a +5 point advantage and a literal 95% win rate lol.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2pp1ppp/p1p2n2/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP: We see a free pawn? We take a free pawn. Knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2pp1ppp/p1p5/4N3/4n3/8/PPPP1PPP: This is a HUGE mistake from black. We simply play rook to e1 here and black really has no way to save the knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2p2ppp/p1p5/3pN3/4n3/8/PPPP1PPP: Black is in serious trouble with that knight. All we have to do is play pawn to d3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/2p2ppp/p1pb4/3pN3/4n3/3P4/PPP2PP: You might be thinking that we should move our knight now, and then capture black's knight next. NOPE. We'll actually capture black's knight with pawn takes e4 and LET black capture our knight. Trust me, this is the way.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/2p2ppp/p1p5/3pb3/4P3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Why did we let black capture a piece and tie up the material when we had a killer pin on black's knight? Well, now we play pawn takes pawn on d5, and now we have a killer pin on black's bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/2p3pp/p1p2p2/3Pb3/8/8/PPP2PPP/RN: Should be no surprise what we want to do now: Pawn to f4 hitting the pinned bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/1Bb1P3/3pn3/2P2N2/P: Here, I actually recommend castling and LETTING black take our c3 pawn. We have a trap for them if they do.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/1Bb1P3/4n3/2p2N2/PP: OK they took the bait, which means its time for our trap: Queen to d5 FORKING the bishop and knight.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/1BbQP3/4n3/2p2N2/PP: Well done! We have a 75% winrate from here :)
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/1B2p3/4P3/5N2/PP: We need to defense our e4 pawn - so let's play rook e1.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/1B2p3/4P3/5N2/PP: Ideally we play pawn to d4, but we aren't quite ready to play it yet. Let's play pawn to c3 first to prepare pawn to d4 in the future.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/1B2p3/4P3/2P2N2: Now we complete our plan: pawn to d4, crashing open the center.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/1B6/3pP3/2P2N2/: Let's take back with pawn to d4.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/1B6/3PP1b1/5N2/P: We'll continue with normal development with knight to c3.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/1B6/3PP3/2N2b2/P: We're going to take this bishop back with our PAWN. I know - crazy right? The truth is, if we take back with our queen, black's c6 knight can take our d4 pawn. We need to keep the queen where she is and just play pawn takes f3. Even though it looks like our king is exposed, this is the ONLY way to keep our +1 point advantage.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/1pp1bppp/p1np1n2/1B6/3PP3/2N2P2/: Now that our king is exposed, he can use all the help he can get. Instead of dropping our bishop back to a4, let's bring it all the way back to f1. That's right, the bishop is coming home.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/1pp1bppp/p1np1n2/8/3PP3/2N2P2/PP: Well done! Not only are we completely fine here, we're actually WINNING. Our center is too strong and black will actually have a tough time getting to our king.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pppb1ppp/2np1n2/1B2p3/4P3/5N2/PP: Our king is safe and black's king is still in the center, which means we want to open up the center ASAP. We could do this by playing pawn to d4 immediately, but even better is playing pawn to c3 to PREPARE pawn to d4. Also, this will give us a nice square (c2) for our light square bishop to run away to in the future.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pppbbppp/2np1n2/1B2p3/4P3/2P2N2/P: Black is about to castle! Let's crash open the center with pawn to d4.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pppbbppp/2np1n2/1B2p3/3PP3/2P2N2: Our biggest problem right now is our bishop is undefended. This let's black do some nasty tricks like sacrificing their knight on d4. Let's avoid all that mess by dropping our bishop back to a4. Now the bishop is defended by our queen.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pppbbppp/2np1n2/8/B2pP3/2P2N2/PP: We should take back with the pawn here to keep our strong center - pawn takes d4.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/8/B2PP1b1/5N2/PP: Black pinned our knight but we aren't that worried about it. Let's continue with normal development with knight to c3.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/8/B2PP3/2N2b2/PP: We're going to take this bishop back with our PAWN. I know - crazy right? The truth is, if we take back with our queen, black's c6 knight can take our d4 pawn. We need to keep the queen where she is and just play pawn takes f3. Even though it looks like our king is exposed, this is the ONLY way to keep our +1 point advantage.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np4/7n/B2PP3/2N2P2/PP3: Pawn to f4 does 2 crucial things: First, it lets our queen attack the undefended h5 knight. Second, it defends the g5 square so the queen can never come. This is CRUCIAL because our king is a bit exposed right now, and if we let the black queen infiltrate our position, its game over.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np4/7n/B2PPP2/2N5/PP3P: Well done! It looks weird having our king so exposed, but we are actually completely safe. Not only are we safe, but we are actually WINNING! We have a +1.5 point advantage and an 85% winrate from here.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2nn4/1B2p3/3P4/5N2/PPP: Ugh. Black moved back and now they're attacking our undefended bishop. So, we should defend it right? WRONG. We'll actually ENCOURAGE black to take our bishop with pawn takes pawn on e5. Don't worry, we'll win our piece back.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/1n2P3/8/5N2/PPP2PP: Alright I have bad news and I have good news. The bad news is we are down 3 points of material. The good news is the black horsey on b5 is TRAPPED. No, seriously, if we played pawn to a4, we would win the horse. Before we do that though, let's win a tempo by playing bishop to g5, attacking the queen.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppppbppp/2n5/1n2P1B1/8/5N2/PPP2P: That was blacks only good move. Let's win one more tempo by trading bishops, bishop takes bishop on e7. Black must recapture with the queen.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppppqppp/2n5/1n2P3/8/5N2/PPP2PPP: Did you forget about that trapped knight? I sure didn't. Pawn to a4 to hit the poor horse.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppppqppp/2n5/4P3/P2n4/5N2/1PP2PP: Take the horse! Knight takes knight on d4.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppppqppp/2n5/4P3/P2N4/8/1PP2PPP/: Let's charge in. Knight to b5 hitting the undefended c7 pawn.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/1N2q3/P7/8/1PP2PPP/: Black thinks they're clever by taking a free pawn and defending the c7 pawn at the same time. But actually, black is bad at chess. Rook slides to e1, hitting the queen. She must leave the defense of the c7 pawn.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/1N6/P7/8/1qP2PPP/RN: Black chose to play offense instead of defense. Now, we will win the game. First things first, we need to save our rook. We can play b-knight to c3 and now the black queen is actually 1 move away from being trapped!
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/1N6/Pq6/2N5/2P2PPP/: Black's queen escaped being trapped, but she's not safe yet. Knight to d5, hitting the queen and the c7 pawn.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/qN1N4/P7/8/2P2PPP/R: B5 knight takes c7, planting our knight deep into enemy territory.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppNp1ppp/2n5/q2N4/P7/8/2P2PPP/R2: Look how sad black's position is here. Every piece is literally doing nothing. You win this easily.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/1N6/P4q2/8/1PP2PPP/: Wow, black is determined to defend that c7 pawn. Let's hop our knight from b1 to c3, threatening to go knight to d5 on the next move which would fork the queen and c7 pawn.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp2ppp/2np4/1N6/P4q2/2N5/1PP2PP: And now knight to d5. We hit the queen, and we hit the c7 pawn.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp2ppp/2np4/1N1N4/P4q2/8/1PP2PP: Well done! We are completely crushing here. Our two knights are unstoppable, and our queen and rook stare down the center. Black's queen is out of place. The computer loooooves our position.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/1ppp1ppp/p1n5/8/B2pn3/5N2/PPP2P: Whenever we see moves like this in the ruy lopez, alarm bells should be going off in our head. The alarm bells are saying "play rook e1"
Well done! We have (nearly) transposed to another line we've already learned so just know that we are completely winning from here and it'll be tough for black to keep ownership of that knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2pp1ppp/p1n5/1p2p3/3Pn3/1B3N2/P: Thats a mistake! Pawn takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/2pp1ppp/p1n5/1pn1P3/8/1B3N2/PPP: The best thing to do now is to plant our bishop on d5. Black really has no way of getting rid of it.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/2ppbppp/p1n5/1pnBP3/8/5N2/PPP2PP: Knight to c3, continuing our standard development.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/2ppbppp/p1n5/1pnBP3/8/2N2N2/PPP: Let's continue even more development with bishop to e3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/2ppbppp/p1n5/1pnBP3/8/2N1BN2/PP: Well done! We'll castle, finish development, and be left with a +1 point positional advantage.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/3QP3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Queen takes queen on d8, making our opponent lose the right to castle.
descriptions.r1bk3r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/4P3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB: Now knight to c3: simple development.
descriptions.r1bk3r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/4P3/2N5/PPP2PPP/R: Well done! We have a +1 point advantage simply because we own more of the center and our king is safer.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppppqppp/8/4P3/P2n4/8/1PP2PPP/RN: Take back with our queen, of course. Queen to d5.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppppqppp/8/4P3/P2Q4/8/1PP2PPP/RN: Black castled to get their king to safety. Let's just develop ourselves, with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppppqppp/8/4P3/P2Q4/2N5/1PP2PPP/: Well done! We evened up the material and have way more space than our opponent. From here, we win over 2/3rds of the time.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/1BbnP3/3p4/2P2N2/PP: OK so ordinarily I'd say we should take the pawn on d4 because otherwise, the d4 pawn will take our pawn on c3. BUT, black's knight is undefended on d5, which means black CAN'T take our pawn on c3. So, while we have some time, let's just castle our king.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/1BbnP3/3p4/2P2N2/P: Ok, NOW let's play pawn takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/1BbnP3/3P4/5N2/PP3: Well done! We have a better position than our opponent.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbppp/p1n5/4P3/B2Nn3/8/PPP2P: Let's play rook to e1, hitting the e4 knight.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbppp/p1n5/2n1P3/B2N4/8/PPP2: Black is attacking our bishop, so we should defend it right? NO! We SACRIFICE the bishop by playing knight to f5. This might look completely ludicrous but I promise you it'll make sense.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbppp/p1n5/4PN2/n7/8/PPP2PPP: We are a bishop down, but on our next move we threaten checkmate! Queen to g4. Now do you see the point? We are threatening checkmate on g7 but also hitting the undefended knight on a4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbp1p/p1n3p1/4PN2/n5Q1/8/PPP: OK black stopped our checkmate, but the real point of the plan is to win back our piece. Before we do that, we need to trade off our under-attack knight. Knight takes bishop on e7.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pppqp1p/p1n3p1/4P3/n5Q1/8/PPP2P: Finally, we win our piece back with queen to a4.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pppqp1p/p5p1/4n3/Q7/8/PPP2PPP/R: OK it might be tempting to immediately play pawn to f4 and threaten to capture the pinned knight, but we'll actually lose the game if we do that. Instead, let's defend our e1 rook with bishop to d2.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1ppp1p1p/p4qp1/4n3/Q7/8/PPPB1PPP: Really no matter what black does, we want to hop our knight to c3 in hopes of getting him to d5.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pp2p1p/p2p1qp1/4n3/Q7/2N5/PPPB1: The point of knight to c3 was to get him to d5. So, knight to d5.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pp2p1p/p2p1qp1/3Nn3/Q7/8/PPPB1P: Well done! Black's dark squares are completely weak. Despite being down a pawn we are actually UP a point of advantage. Our dark square control is just too good.
descriptions.r2qk2r/pppbbppp/2np1n2/1B6/3pP3/2P2N2/PP: Black really shouldn't take when their king is still in the center! Pawn takes back on d4.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pppbbppp/2np1n2/1B6/3PP3/5N2/PP3: Let's keep development with knight to c3.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/1ppbbppp/p1np1n2/1B6/3PP3/2N2N2/: We should drop our bishop back to a4.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/2pbbppp/p1np1n2/1p6/B2PP3/2N2N2/: Black really wants our bishop... let's drop him back to c2.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/2pbbppp/p1np1n2/1p6/3PP3/2N2N2/P: Well done! We secured a +1 point advantage and are ready to continue playing chess.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pp1qp1p/p1np2p1/4P3/Q7/8/PPP2PP: Black threatens our pawn - let's threaten their rook! Bishop to h6.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/1pp1qp1p/p1np2pB/4P3/Q7/8/PPP2P: Black has 1, 2, 3, FOUR pieces attacking our e5 pawn. There's no reason to hang on anymore. We can let black have the pawn and just play knight to c3.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/1pp1qp1p/p1n3pB/4p3/Q7/2N5/PPP2: Now we can jump in with our knight and hit the queen :) Knight to d5. Black's dark squares are WEAK.
descriptions.r1b1r1k1/1pp1qp1p/p1n3pB/3Np3/Q7/8/PPP2P: Well done! Our dark square control is just too overpowering for black.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1bpp1ppp/p1n5/1pnBP3/8/5N2/PPP2P: Let's continue development with knight to c3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/1bppbppp/p1n5/1pnBP3/8/2N2N2/PPP2: Let's continue development with bishop to e3
descriptions.r2qk2r/1bppbppp/p1n5/1pnBP3/8/2N1BN2/PPP: Well done! We get to choose whether we want to castle kingside or queenside in the future.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2bp1n2/8/3NP3/2NQ4/PPP2P: Well done! We have a better position than black here.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppbppp/p1n5/3nP3/B2p4/5N2/PPP2: Now let's recapture our pawn: knight takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbppp/p1n5/3nP3/B2N4/8/PPP2P: The best move here is knight to f5. We discover an attack on the knight and also threaten to trade off black's dark squared bishop.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbppp/pnn5/4PN2/B7/8/PPP2PPP: Queen to g4 threatens checkmate. Not much else to say about that one...
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbp1p/pnn3p1/4PN2/B5Q1/8/PPP: Lastly, we need to do a series of trades that will result in us in a better position. First, bishop takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp1bp1p/pnp3p1/4PN2/6Q1/8/PPP2: Now knight takes bishop on e7.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pp1qp1p/pnp3p1/4P3/6Q1/8/PPP2PP: Our queen and e5 pawn are both under attack. Queen to g3 moves the queen to safety and defends the pawn.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pp1qp1p/pnp3p1/4P3/8/6Q1/PPP2PP: Well done! You played the opening perfectly and now we have a +1 point advantage over our opponent.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/1ppb1ppp/p1np1n2/1B2p3/4P3/2P2N2: We can take the knight and be boring, or we can run away and have an interesting game. Let's have an interesting game. Bishop back to a4.
descriptions.r2qk2r/1ppbbppp/p1np1n2/4p3/B3P3/2P2N2/P: Black is about to castle - let's crash open the center before they do! Pawn to d4.
descriptions.r2qk2r/1ppbbppp/p1np1n2/8/B2pP3/2P2N2/PP: Let's take back with our pawn to keep our strong center. Pawn takes d4.
descriptions.r2qk2r/1ppbbppp/p1np1n2/8/B2PP3/5N2/PP3P: Well done! Our strong center gives us a +1 point advantage over our opponent.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/2pb1ppp/p1np1n2/1p2p3/B3P3/2P2N2: Keep running away! This time bishop to c2. Told you that square we made a few moves ago would come in handy!
descriptions.r2qk2r/2pbbppp/p1np1n2/1p2p3/4P3/2P2N2/P: Black is prepping to castle - this is our last chance to crash open the center! Pawn to d4.
descriptions.r2qk2r/2pbbppp/p1np1n2/1p6/3pP3/2P2N2/PP: Take back with the pawn! We want to keep our pawns strong in the center. Pawn takes d4.
descriptions.r2qk2r/2pbbppp/p1np1n2/1p6/3PP3/5N2/PPB2: Well done! Our strong center is giving us a +1 point advantage over our opponent. Meanwhile, black's position is incredibly cramped.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/1ppp1ppp/p1n5/1Bb1p3/4P3/2P2N2/: This is another one of the rare times where I'll recommend you take the knight instead of dropping back. The reason being, if we take the knight, we can win the pawn on e5. Bishop takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/1pp2ppp/p1p5/2b1p3/4P3/2P2N2/PP: Great, now knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/1pp2ppp/p1p2q2/2b1N3/4P3/2P5/PP: Whenever black attacks our knight here with their queen, we can actually LET them take the knight because if they do, we have a nasty fork. So, instead of moving or defending, let's castle.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/1pp2ppp/p1p5/2b1q3/4P3/2P5/PP1P: We lost a piece but now pawn to d4 FORKING the queen and bishop.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/1pp2ppp/p1p5/4q3/3bP3/2P5/PP3PP: Let's keep our strong center by retaking with the pawn. Pawn takes bishop on d4.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/1pp2ppp/p1p5/4q3/3PP3/8/PP3PPP/: Well done! Our safe king and strong center gives us a +1 point advantage over our opponent.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppbppp/p7/3nP3/B2n4/8/PPP2PPP/: Queen recaptures on d4, of course. And now we hit the d5 knight.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppbppp/pn6/4P3/B2Q4/8/PPP2PPP/: We can simply drop our bishop down to b3 here.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbppp/pn6/4P3/3Q4/1B6/PPP2PP: Finally, let's bring our bishop to f4 to reinforce the e5 pawn.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbppp/pn6/4P3/3Q1B2/1B6/PPP2: Well done! We completely own the center and have a better position than black.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1p1ppp/2p2n2/1Bb1n3/3PP3/8/PPP: That was black's best move. Our best move? Pawn takes knight on e5
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1p1ppp/2p5/1Bb1P3/4n3/8/PPP2PP: Best move now? Bishop retreats to d3, hitting the knight
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp1p1ppp/2p5/2b1P3/4n3/3B4/PPP2P: Well done! Black's knight is actually trapped by the way. They have a couple ways to get out of it but its straightforward to play on our end. We have a 70% winrate from here!
descriptions.r1bnkb1r/2p2ppp/p4n2/1p2p3/4P3/1B3N2/PPP: The move from here is knight takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1bnkb1r/2p2ppp/p7/1p2N3/4n3/1B6/PPP2PPP: We WANT to put our bishop on d5 and fork the knight and rook. But, if we do that now, black just plays bishop to b7 (defended by the d8 knight) and our plan is ruined. So let's bait the d8 knight AWAY from d8 with knight sacrifice onto f7. Knight to f7.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/2p2npp/p7/1p6/4n3/1B6/PPP2PPP/R: NOW we can play bishop to d5, forking the knight and rook.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/2p2npp/p7/1p1B4/4n3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Nice!! We're winning back our piece and we have a 70% winrate from here.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppbppp/p7/4P3/B2nn3/8/PPP2PPP/: Take back with queen to d4, of course.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppbppp/p7/2n1P3/B2Q4/8/PPP2PPP: Black is threatening to take our bishop. Let's just use this as an opportunity to develop our knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/1pppbppp/p7/4P3/n2Q4/2N5/PPP2PPP: Let's take back with queen takes a4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbppp/p7/4P3/Q7/2N5/PPP2PPP/: Let's develop our last piece with bishop to f4, reinforcing our strong central pawn.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbppp/p7/4P3/Q4B2/2N5/PPP2PP: Well done! We played perfectly and earned a slight advantage from the opening.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbppp/p1n5/2n1PN2/B7/8/PPP2P: Queen to g4 does two things for us: it threatens checkmate on g7 and it defends our bishop on a4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pppbp1p/p1n3p1/2n1PN2/B5Q1/8/P: OK, now we really should do something about our bishop before we get into trouble. Bishop takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp1bp1p/p1p3p1/2n1PN2/6Q1/8/PP: Now knight takes bishop on e7 with check.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pp1qp1p/p1p3p1/2n1P3/6Q1/8/PPP2: Our queen is under attack, and so is our pawn on e5. We can simply drop our queen down to g3 to save our queen and defend our e5 pawn.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pp1qp1p/p1p3p1/2n1P3/8/6Q1/PPP2: Well done! Honestly both us and our opponent played pretty perfectly, so the position is equal and we have a game ahead of us.

shortDescriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Let's continue with the Ruy Lopez
shortDescriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1P: Let's kick off the Ruy Lopez

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Let's learn the Scandinavian Defense! There's no dilly-dallying on this one. After White plays e4 we force the issue immediately with pawn to d5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3P4/8/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: And now for the fun part! We recapture with the queen, placing her in the middle of the board. Queen to d5.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3q4/8/2N5/PPPP1PPP/R: Remember, with great power comes great responsibility. With our queen in the middle board, she is an easy target. Let's bring her to safety with queen to a5.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp1pppp/8/q7/8/2N2N2/PPPP1PPP/: Let's develop our knight to f6.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/2B5/2N2N2/PPPP1: This is a common way to play for White. In this position I recommend knight to c6.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/q7/2B5/2NP1N2/PP: Now that White's light-square bishop is trapped in, we can set up a nasty pin on White's queen with bishop to g4.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/q7/2B3b1/2NP1N2/PP: Now we can swing our queen around to h5, adding more pressure on White's knight.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/7q/2B3b1/2NP1N1P/P: Remember! White's pawn is not actually attacking our bishop because its pinned against their rook. We can actually add even more pressure to White's knight with knight to d4.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/7q/2Bn2b1/2NP1N1P/PP: Well done! We are absolutely crushing White's position and its not clear how they'll get out of this. The computer puts us at a +3 point advantage simply because of how dominant our position is.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp1pppp/8/q7/3P4/2N5/PPP2PPP/R: While White prepares to attack our queen again, let's take a moment and develop some pieces. Knight to f6.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/3P4/2N2N2/PPP2P: We did the knight, now we do the bishop! Bishop to f5.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q4b2/3P4/2N2N2/PPPB: White is setting up a discovered attack but we honestly do not need to be worried about it. Let's continue with our plan to develop. We want to develop the dark-square bishop but it is currently blocked in. Let's open it up with pawn to e6.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/q4b2/3PN3/5N2/PPPB1: This looks scary but its not. We just move the queen to b6. We're actually setting up an attack on White's pawns on b2.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/1q2pN2/5b2/3P4/5N2/PPPB1: Nothing else to do here but capture back with pawn to f6.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2p1p/1q2pp2/5b2/3P4/2P2N2/PP1: White forgot their pawn was hanging on b2. Now we gobble up! Queen to b2.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2p1p/4pp2/5b2/3P4/2P2N2/Pq1B1: Beautiful, White's position is collapsing. In the future we want to continue developing and castle.
Aaaaand thats a blunder. Let's take on b1 with our queen.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2p1p/4pp2/5b2/3P4/2P2N2/P2B1P: And capture back on b1 with out bishop.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2p1p/4pp2/8/3P4/2P2N2/P2B1PPP: Great! We are up a full rook and the game is ours.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/3P4/2N5/PPPB1PP: Since White has not developed their other knight yet, we can actually set up a direct attack on White's queen with bishop g4.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/3P2b1/2N2P2/PPPB: Now that white has damaged their pawn structure and stunted their own development, we can move our bishop back to d7.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pppbpppp/5n2/q7/2BP4/2N2P2/PPPB2: Now we have a fork! Let's play queen to b6, forking the d4 and b2 pawns.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pppbpppp/1q3n2/8/2BP4/2N2P2/PPPB: Now our queen gets to eat! Queen takes d4.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pppbpppp/5n2/8/2Bq4/2N2P2/PPPB2P: Well done! We are up a pawn and the computer loves our position.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/q4b2/2BP4/2N2N2/PPP: Now that our queen is being targeted, it's a great time to develop our black bishop and defend her with bishop to b4.
descriptions.rn2k2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/q4b2/1bBP4/P1N2N2/1P: White doesn't like our bishop here. Fine. Bishop takes knight on c3.
descriptions.rn2k2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/q4b2/2BP4/P1B2N2/1PP: Now we can slide our queen back to b6.
descriptions.rn2k2r/ppp2ppp/1q2pn2/5b2/2BP4/P1B2N2/1P: Now let's lay a trap. Instead of castling kingside, we will develop our knight to c6 and prepare to castle queenside.
descriptions.r3k2r/ppp2ppp/1qn1pn2/3P1b2/2B5/P1B2N2/1: They fell for our trap! Now we can castle queenside, pinning the pawn to it's queen. Muahahaha.
descriptions.2kr3r/ppp2ppp/1qn1pn2/3P1b2/2B5/P1B2N2/1: We are winning that pawn, and more often than not, winning the game. The computer loves our position here.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/3P4/2NB4/PPP2PP: White moved their light-square bishop out too early. Let's develop our other knight with plans to hop it down to the board and attack that bishop. Knight to c6.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/q7/3P4/2NB1N2/PP: No hesitation, we should pin the knight here with bishop to g4.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/q7/3P2b1/2NB1N2/PP: Well done! We are threatening to win the pawn on d4 and are ready to castle queenside. The computer puts us at a slight advantage.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/3P2b1/2N5/PPPBBP: If White wants to trade light square bishops in the Scandinavian, we are always happy to capture. Bishop takes e2.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/3P4/2N5/PPPBbPPP: Great job! We are ready to develop our other knight and castle queenside!
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/q7/3P4/2NB4/PPP1: Let's pin White's knight with bishop to g4.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/q7/3P2b1/2NB1P2/PP: White has weakened their dark squares with that pawn move. Now we retreat our bishop one square to f5 and offer a bishop trade.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/q4b2/3P4/2NB1P2/PP: Great job! We are ready to castle and continue our game.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/3P2b1/2N2N2/PPPB: Now we can play queen F5, adding some pressure on the pinned knight.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/5q2/3P2b1/2N2N2/PPP: Now we can play knight c6, preparing to castle queenside.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/5q2/3P2b1/2N2N2/PP: Well done! After castling next move, we will have strong pressure on White's d4 pawn. The computer thinks we are ahead in this position.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp1pppp/8/q7/2B5/2N5/PPPP1PPP/: This one's not rocket science. Let's play knight to f6.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/2B5/2NP4/PPP2PP: As usual, we play bishop to g4, attacking their queen.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/2B3b1/2NP1N2/PPP: White is placing themselves in a pin, which is really bad for them. Lets open up our dark-square bishop with pawn to e6.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/q7/2B3b1/2NP1N2/PPP: Now for our main idea: we can swing our queen over to h5 applying even more pressure against White's knight. The best part about this variation? The white bishop cannot come back to help.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/7q/2B3b1/2NP1N2/PPP: Well done! We have a very strong attack against White's knight. The computer thinks we are ahead in this position.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/2BP4/2N5/PPP2PP: White has moved their light-square bishop out too early, which gives us the opportunity to attack their queen with bishop to g4. The reason this is nice is if white retreats their bishop to defend their queen, they essentially lost a move.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/2BP2b1/2N2N2/PPP: Let's continue development with knight to c6.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/q7/2BP2b1/2N2N1P/P: Very important! You must remember that here, we can actually play queen to h5. By pinning the pawn to White's rook, it is actually saving our bishop.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/7q/3P2b1/2N2N1P/PP: Let's castle. Remember, our bishop is NOT under threat from white because if they took, we can take their rook.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/7q/3P2b1/2N1BN1P/: Now a beautiful idea: pawn to e5 threatening the d4 pawn which already has so much pressure on it because of our rook.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/3Pp2q/6b1/2N1BN1P/: Remember! Our bishop is still not hanging because our queen pins the h3 pawn to the rook, and our knight is not hanging because our rook pins the d5 pawn to the queen. Now we can add even more tension to this crazy position with bishop to b4.
descriptions.2kr3r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/3Pp2q/1b4b1/2N1BN1P/: White's position is completely destroyed. There is just so much pressure coming from every angle. Black wins almost every time in this position just because it is nearly impossible to play white here.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2p1p/1q2pp2/5b2/3P4/2B2N2/PPP: Our main goal now is to castle queenside. To do that, let's bring our knight out to c6.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2p1p/1qn1pp2/5b2/3P4/2BB1N2/PP: OK one last thing before we castle: it's better we take White's bishop rather than the other way around. If they take us, our pawns become an ugly 3-stack. Bishop takes d3.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2p1p/1qn1pp2/8/3P4/2BQ1N2/PPP: Way to stick with it! We are developed and have a safe king.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/5q2/3P2b1/2NB1N2/PP: White is attacking our queen! Let's return the favor with bishop takes f3.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/5q2/3P4/2NB1Q2/PPPB: This one is self explanatory. We trade queens on f3 to damage our opponent's pawn structure.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/8/3P4/2NB1P2/PPPB1P: Now let's develop our knight with knight to c6 and prepare to castle queenside.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/8/3P4/2NB1P2/PPPB1: Well done! We'll castle on the next move and continue our chess game.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/2B3b1/2NP1P2/PPP: And as usual, we retreat our bishop back to d7.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pppbpppp/5n2/q7/2B5/2NP1P2/PPP3P: Well done! We are ready to continue our game.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q4b2/3P4/2NB1N2/PPP: If White wants to trade bishops, they get no argument from us! Bishop takes on d3.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/3P4/2NQ1N2/PPP2P: Now we want to develop our dark square bishop, but first we need to open it up. Pawn to e6.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/q7/3P4/2NQ1N2/PPP2P: Now our bishop goes to e7, preparing us to castle. In the Scandinavian, when we lose our light-square bishop, our dark-square should stay close to home. Don't ask me why, I don't make the rules.
descriptions.rn2k2r/ppp1bppp/4pn2/q7/3P4/2NQ1N2/PPPB1: White is setting up a discovered attack on our queen but to be honest with you, we aren't really scared by it. Let's call their bluff and castle.
descriptions.rn3rk1/ppp1bppp/4pn2/q7/3PN3/3Q1N2/PPPB1: OK the discovered attack happened. Let's move our queen down to a6 and offer a queen trade. Everything is defended so life is totally fine.
descriptions.rn3rk1/ppp1bppp/q3pn2/8/3PN3/3Q1N2/PPPB1: Congrats on navigating through the scandinavian. Nobody made any mistakes. Time to play chess.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/2BP2b1/2N2P2/PPP: Now that we've damaged our opponent's pawn structure, we can retreat our bishop back to d7.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pppbpppp/5n2/q7/2BP4/2N2P2/PPP3P: Well done! We will continue developing and castle.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/q7/2B5/2N2N2/PPP: Because the white light-square bishop has already wasted a move, we can set up a nasty pin on the knight with bishop to g4.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/q7/2B3b1/2N2N2/PPP: Well done! We are ready to castle queenside and cause more issues.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q7/3P1B2/2N5/PPP2P: White is ignoring our queen for whatever reason, which is great for us. Let's develop our bishop to f5.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q4b2/3P1B2/2N5/PPP2: Well done! We'll develop our other knight and castle queenside in the future.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/5B2/3P4/2N2b2/PPPB1: White TOOK our queen. We return the favor once again with bishop takes d1.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/5B2/3P4/2N5/PPPB1PP: Finally, let's kick out White's bishop and open up our own with pawn to e6.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/5B2/3P4/2N5/PPPB1PP: Great! We're ready to continue developing and castle our king.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q4b2/2BP4/2N2N2/PPP: The next moves for Black are very easy to play. The goal is to develop our dark-square bishop but it's blocked in, so first we play pawn to e6.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/q4b2/2BP4/2N2N2/PPP: Because White's king is out of the way, there is no need to add more pressure to White's knight. Let's instead create an escape path for our queen with pawn to c6.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp3ppp/2p1pn2/q4b2/2BP4/2N2N2/PP: Well done! You're getting good at understanding the subtle differences between these positions.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pppbpppp/1q3n2/8/2BP4/2N2P2/PPPB: OK we should NOT take the b2 pawn because the rook will just attack us right after. Instead, let's open up our dark-square bishop with pawn to e6.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pppb1ppp/1q2pn2/8/2BP4/2N2P2/PPP: Well done! We are ready to finish development and castle very soon.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/q4b2/3P4/2N2N2/PPP1: We want to develop our dark square bishop but it's blocked in right now. Let's open it up with pawn to e6.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/q4b2/3P4/2N2N2/PPP1: It's hard to go wrong here with Black. You can develop your bishop, you can castle, etc. The computer recommends playing pawn to c6 so that's what we'll do in this course. Pawn to c6 stops the white knight from advancing forward, and gives our queen a getaway path back home.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pp3ppp/2p1pn2/q4b2/3P4/2N2N2/PPP: We are in a good position to play the bishop out, castle our king, and continue the rest of our game!
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/5q2/3P4/2NB1P2/PPPB: OK white was not interested in trading queens. Let's run ours away with queen to d7.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/pppqpppp/5n2/8/3P4/2NB1P2/PPPB1P: Well done! We'll continue developing and castle very soon.
descriptions.r3k2r/ppp2ppp/1qn1pn2/5b2/2BP4/P1B2N2/1P: White did not fall into our trap, so now we should just castle kingside.
descriptions.r4rk1/ppp2ppp/1qn1pn2/5b2/2BP4/P1B2N2/1P: Well done! We are developed and ready to continue the game.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/q3Nb2/3P4/2N5/PPPB1: We need to play this very delicately. If we don't move our queen, we risk it getting trapped on the next move. The good news: if we move our queen to b6, she remains safe and in fact she is forking the d4 pawn and the b2 pawn.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/1q2pn2/4Nb2/3P4/2N5/PPPB: Well done! We have set up a fork against our opponent and will likely win material.  Good job avoiding that attack on our queen.
