descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the scotch game! This opening literally just feels like a cheat code - it's so easy to get a winning position in just a few moves, and ALL of black's most common responses, especially at <2000 ELO, will make them lose on the spot. We begin with pawn to e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Let's develop our knight to f3. I'm sure you've played this a million times before.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1P: Now in other openings you might develop your other knight or your bishop, but in the scotch game, we force the issue NOW. Pawn to d4. Black must decide if they will take our pawn or defend their own.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/3pP3/5N2/PPP2PPP: Let's recapture our pawn: knight to d4. We are baiting black to take our knight next.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b5/3NP3/8/PPP2PPP: Now we're entering the scotch game mainline. First move is pretty simple: Black added an attacker on our knight, we'll add a defender. Bishop to e3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b5/3NP3/4B3/PPP2: GAME OVER. Black fell right into a trap. Things may look normal right now, but we simply play knight takes knight on c6. Now the queen is under attack, and the c5 bishop is hanging. Black can't save both.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1pp1ppp/2p2n2/2b5/4P3/4B3/PPP2P: Beautiful, now we get a free bishop. Bishop takes bishop on c5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/3nP3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB: This is the most common move from black, and its also the WORST move for black. They've just let us bring our queen out to the middle of the board. Bringing our queen out this early is usally bad, but in this case Black doesn't have the b8 knight to attack her. Queen captures knight on d4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp1p1ppp/8/2p5/3QP3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Another awful move from black. We really can't go wrong here - any queen move works. I recommend keep the queen active by sliding her to e3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1p1ppp/5n2/2p5/4P3/4Q3/PPP2PP: A HUGE point of the scotch is the fact that our e-pawn can march forward and hit the knight when the knight develops to f6. Well, the knight developed to f6, so lets hit it with pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp1p1ppp/5n2/2p1P3/8/4Q3/PPP2PP: Well done! We have transposed into another line we've already learned :)
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/3PP3/5N2/PPP: This is the third most common move for black. From here, we just play pawn takes pawn on e5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/4n3/5N2/PPP2PP: Now we develop our bishop to c4
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b1P3/2B1n3/5N2/PPP: Blunder! Black thinks they're doing some smart attack on our f2 pawn, but we simply have queen to d5, forking checkmate on f7 and the knight on e4
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n5/3QP3/2B1n3/5N2/PPP2: This delays the inevitable. King slides over to f1.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/3QP3/2B1n3/5N2/PPP: Black castled to handle the checkmate threat, but now we get our free knight! Queen takes knight on e4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/2B1Q3/5N2/PPP2: Nice! We have an extra knight.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/4p3/3PP3/5N2/PPP2P: Black is playing too defensively here - they've given us the whole center. Pawn to d5 forces the knight back.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/3Pp3/3nP3/5N2/PPP2P: I have no idea why this is black's second most common move... It simply loses a central pawn. Knight takes knight on d4.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/3P4/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/: Now we get our free pawn! Queen takes pawn on d4.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/2n2q2/8/3NP3/8/PPP2PPP: Black took their queen out to attack our knight, but now we turn the tables. Knight to b5 and all of a sudden, we are threatening a fork on the now unguarded c7 square. We win 60% of the time JUST from making this move.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n2q2/1Nb5/4P3/8/PPP2P: Black is threatening checkmate on f2, so we should probably deal with that. Simply queen to e2.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/1bn2q2/1N6/4P3/8/PPP1Q: Black thinks they've stabilized, but we have a nasty threat coming. Knight from b1 to c3 and we're threatening knight to d5 forking the queen, the bishop, and the c7 pawn. If we can get our knight to d5 successfully, it's all over.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/1ppp1ppp/pbn2q2/1N6/4P3/2N5/PPP: Beautiful, black let us do it. Now knight to d5 and we fork the bishop, queen, and c7 pawn.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/1ppp1ppp/pbn5/1N1N4/4P3/8/PPP1Q: Knight takes bishop on b6, removing a key defender...
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/1p1p1ppp/ppn5/1N6/4P3/8/PPP1QPP: And now you see the master plan: knight to d6 CHECK.
descriptions.r1bq1knr/1p1p1ppp/ppnN4/8/4P3/8/PPP1QPPP: Finally, develop our bishop to f4.
descriptions.r1bq1knr/1p1p1ppp/ppnN4/8/4PB2/8/PPP1QPP: Wow. The material is equal but we will win from here 100% of the time. Our knight is just too good. We'll castle now, develop our last pieces, and then launch a huge attack on black's weak position.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/8/3QP3/8/PPP2PPP/RN: Black is playing very passively. The plan from here is simply: develop our knight, our bishop, and castle long. Let's begin with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/8/3QP3/2N5/PPP2PP: We continue with our plan, bishop to g5. This also pins the knight, which is cool.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp1bppp/3p1n2/6B1/3QP3/2N5/PPP2: Finally, we complete our plan by castling queenside.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/3p1n2/6B1/3QP3/2N5/PPP: Now notice: our rook is on the same file as the black queen. If we can open up that file, black's queen is in trouble. Let's crack open that file, then, with pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/5n2/4p1B1/3Q4/2N5/PPP2: Perfect! All according to our plan. Now queen takes pawn on e5 and black's queen is hit by our rook.
descriptions.r1b1qrk1/ppp1bppp/5n2/4Q1B1/8/2N5/PPP2PP: And thanks to our hard work, we can scoop up a pawn. Queen takes pawn on c7.
descriptions.r3qrk1/ppQ1bppp/4bn2/6B1/8/2N5/PPP2PPP/2: The key to winning the whole game now? Bishop to b5 hitting the black queen.
descriptions.r1q2rk1/ppQ1bppp/4bn2/1B4B1/8/2N5/PPP2PP: Black ran their queen, but hung their bishop! Queen takes bishop on e7.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/3QP3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Black simply did not think ahead here, and now pawn to e5 is a knockout punch.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4P3/3Q4/8/PPP2PPP/RN: That is humiliating. Black developed a knight just to put him back in his stable. We simply continue developing with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/4P3/3Q4/2N5/PPP2PPP: Continue developing: bishop f4. We want to castle queenside.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4p3/3Q1B2/2N5/PPP2PPP: Let's take back with the queen so we can throw a check in. Queen to e5.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp1qppp/8/4Q3/5B2/2N5/PPP2PPP/: We have a million options here. You seriously cannot go wrong. But the BEST thing to do is throw our knight onto b5 and add yet ANOTHER attacker to the c7 square. In a move or two, after the queens are traded, our knight will go to c7 and fork the king and rook.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/1N2q3/5B2/8/PPP2PPP/R: Bishop takes back on e5, of course. And now we threaten the knight to c7 fork and black has no good way to defend.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/1N2B3/8/8/PPP2PPP/R3K: Knight will be coming to c7. Knight will win a rook. GG.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/3NP3/8/PPP2PPP: Black is playing the Schmidt variation. From here, we take the knight with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p1pp1ppp/2p2n2/8/4P3/8/PPP2PPP/: From here, we want to develop and castle as soon as possible. So, bishop to d3, which saved our e4 pawn and lets us castle.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1pp1ppp/2p2n2/2b5/4P3/3B4/PPP2P: Before we castle, let's play pawn to e5 to hit the f6 knight.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/p1ppqppp/2p2n2/2b1P3/8/3B4/PPP2P: Our pawn is under attack. Our move? Castle! If black takes our pawn, then we can move our rook to e1 and pin the queen to her own king.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/p1ppqppp/2p5/2bnP3/8/3B4/PPP2PPP: We are after the c5 bishop. First step? Knight to d2. By the way, black still cannot take our central pawn because if they do, we pin the queen to her king.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1ppqppp/2p5/2bnP3/8/3B4/PPPN1PP: Knight to e4 hits the dark-squared bishop.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1ppqppp/1bp5/3nP3/4N3/3B4/PPP2P: Pawn to c4, hitting the knight now. The knight only has 1 safe square.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1ppqppp/1bp5/4P3/1nP1N3/3B4/PP3: Now, we simply win the game. Knight to f6 check.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1ppqp1p/1bp2p2/4P3/1nP5/3B4/PP3: Black's king is weak, but where's our attack? Well, here we can SACRIFICE THE BISHOP. Bishop takes pawn on h7.
descriptions.r1b2r2/p1ppqp1k/1bp2p2/4P3/1nP5/8/PP3PPP: Now the king is even WEAKER. Queen to h5 check.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1ppqp2/1bp2p2/4P2Q/1nP5/8/PP3PP: You need to remember this sequence to convert this position to a win: Queen to g4, checking the king again.
descriptions.r1b2r2/p1ppqp1k/1bp2p2/4P3/1nP3Q1/8/PP3P: Now we check on the h4 square. Queen to h4.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1ppqp2/1bp2p2/4P3/1nP4Q/8/PP3PP: Now we play bishop to h6, adding another piece to the party.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1pp1p2/1bp2p1B/4q3/1nP4Q/8/PP3P: Queen to g4 check. The queen must defend or it's checkmate.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p1pp1p2/1bp2p1B/6q1/1nP3Q1/8/PP3: Aaaaaand we win the queen. Bishop to g5.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp1bppp/8/4Q3/5B2/2N5/PPP2PPP/: It's tempting to play queen to g7 here and try and win a rook - but we actually won't be able to take the rook as black can play bishop to f6 defending it. Instead, lets add even MORE pressure to the c7 pawn with knight to b5.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp1bppp/8/1N2Q3/5B2/8/PPP2PPP/: It's over. We just have too much pressure on the c7 square. There's a bunch of ways black COULD respond here, but none of them are good.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppppqppp/5n2/4P3/3Q4/8/PPP2PPP/: Black thinks they're being clever by pinning our pawn to our king, so the knight can't be captured. But we have a simple response: bishop to e3. Now we just got easy development and the pawn is no longer pinned to the king.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppppqppp/8/4P3/3Q4/4B3/PPP2PPP/: Let's keep developing with the goal to castle ASAP. Knight to c3.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp1qppp/3p4/4P3/3Q4/2N1B3/PPP2: Now black is just lost. Completely and utterly lost. Knight to d5 attacks the queen and threatens a fork on c7.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppq1ppp/3p4/3NP3/3Q4/4B3/PPP2P: Black is in danger. Let's continue to open up the position with pawn takes pawn on d6.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppq1ppp/3b4/3N4/3Q4/4B3/PPP2PP: I can't even hate on black. They had no good moves. But that move in particular was REALLY bad. Queen takes pawn on g7.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppq1pQp/3b4/3N4/8/4B3/PPP2PPP/: It's over. We're winning a rook and probably a few other pieces too.
descriptions.2r1qrk1/ppQ1bppp/4bn2/1B4B1/8/2N5/PPP2PP: Why not take another free pawn? Queen to b7.
descriptions.1r2qrk1/pQ2bppp/4bn2/1B4B1/8/2N5/PPP2PPP: Ok, NOW it's a good time to finally take that queen we attacked a couple moves ago. Bishop takes queen on e8.
descriptions.4Brk1/pr2bppp/4bn2/6B1/8/2N5/PPP2PPP/2KR: Now that we've won two pawns, lets run our bishop back. Bishop to a4.
descriptions.5rk1/pr2bppp/4bn2/6B1/B7/2N5/PPP2PPP/2KR: Nice! We made out like bandits and are now up two pawns!
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/2b5/3nP3/4B3/PPP2PPP: Black decided it's time to trade all the pieces in the center. OK. Bishop takes knight back on d4.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/8/3bP3/8/PPP2PPP/RN1: And queen takes bishop on d4
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/5q2/8/3QP3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Black wants to trade queens. We say NO. We like our queen in the scotch game. Pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/1q6/4P3/3Q4/8/PPP2PPP/: Black has insisted on a queen trade. At this point we have to do it. Queen takes queen on b6.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/1ppp1ppp/1p6/4P3/8/8/PPP2PPP/RN: Let's develop our knight to c3
descriptions.r1b1k2r/1pppnppp/1p6/4P3/8/2N5/PPP2PPP/R: Simple chess from here on: let's castle queenside.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pppnppp/1p6/4P3/8/2N5/PPP2PPP/2: And we simply develop our bishop to c4.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/1pppnppp/1p6/4P3/2B5/2N5/PPP2PPP: Nice! We have a very comfortable position. It'll be up to you to convert our 1.5 point advantage into a win.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/5q2/8/3QP3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Black wants to trade queens, but our queen is our best asset right now. Let's say no by playing pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/4q3/4P3/3Q4/8/PPP2PPP/: BLUNDER! Bishop to c4, developing a piece and hitting the queen.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/6q1/4P3/2BQ4/8/PPP2PPP: Black is threatening the pawn on c2 AND the pawn on g2. Honestly, its a huge bluff. As we'll see, capturing either of those two pawns is losing for black. Lets continue developing with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4P3/2BQ4/2N5/PPP2PqP: Like I said, this is a complete bluff. Bishop to d5 hit's the queen and saves the rook
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/6q1/3BP3/3Q4/2N5/PPP2P: Bishop to d2, preparing to castle queenside.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/6q1/3BP3/3Q4/2N5/PPPB1: Even though material is equal, this game is not even close. Our development is so much better, and our king is about to be so much safer.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/3q4/3N4/3Q4/4B3/PPP2PPP: Black is insisting on defending the c7 pawn. Let's add another attacker with bishop to f4, skewering the queen to that c7 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/4q3/3N4/3Q1B2/8/PPP2PPP: Simply block with bishop to e2.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/4q3/3N4/3Q1B2/8/PPP1BPP: Well done! The material is equal but we will literally win this game 100% of the time. Our pieces are just so good, and the computer gives us a +5 point advantage.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/1q6/4P3/2BQ4/8/PPP2PPP: Black is insisting on a queen trade, but we have something better in mind: queen to f4 threatens checkmate on f7.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/1q6/4P3/2B2Q2/8/PPP2PP: Well done! Black will scramble to stop our attack, and in the meantime we'll castle and keep developing our pieces. The computer has at a +2 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp1nppp/3p4/3Pp3/4P3/5N2/PPP2P: Let's continue taking the center. Pawn to c4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp1nppp/3p1n2/3Pp3/2P1P3/5N2/P: Let's keep developing with knight to c3.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp1nppp/3p1n2/3Pp3/2P1P3/2N2N2: Well done! We have so much space - giving us a +1 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1pp1ppp/2p5/2bnP3/8/3B4/PPP2PPP: Let's play queen to g4, hitting the undefended g7 pawn.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1pp1p1p/2p3p1/2bnP3/6Q1/3B4/PPP: Great. Black defended the g7 pawn but now we can just play bishop to h6 and black will never castle.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1p2p1p/2pp2pB/2bnP3/6Q1/3B4/PPP: Careful! That pawn push exposed an attack on our queen. Let's move our queen to a4 and threaten the c6 pawn.
descriptions.r2qk2r/p1pb1p1p/2pp2pB/2bnP3/Q7/3B4/PPP2: Now we just castle - rubbing it in to black's face that we can castle and they can't.
Well done! Our position is just terrifying for black.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/4P3/8/PPP2PPP/R: I mean this is just a silly move from black, but it does get played, so I'm including it in the course. Queen to d8, ruining black's right to castle.
descriptions.r1bk1b1r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/4P3/8/PPP2PPP/R: Now simply pawn to f3 to stabilize our central pawn.
descriptions.r1bk1b1r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/4P3/5P2/PPP3PP/: Well done! We will develop and castle - something our opponent no longer has the ability to do.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n2q2/2b5/3NP3/4B3/PPP: Ok, black added ANOTHER attacker. We add ANOTHER defender. Pawn to c3.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppppnppp/2n2q2/2b5/3NP3/2P1B3/PP: Let's continue developing: bishop to c4.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppppnppp/5q2/2b1n3/2BNP3/2P1B3/P: Black is hitting our bishop, so we need to move it. The best square is actually dropping it back to e2 where it will never be bothered again.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp1nppp/5q2/2bpn3/3NP3/2P1B3/PP: Black is attacking our pawn. What's better than a pawn? A knight. Pawn to f4 attacking black's knight.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp1nppp/5q2/2bp4/2nNPP2/2P1B3/P: Now bishop takes knight on c4. This will divert black's d5 pawn AWAY from the center, leaving the entire center to us.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp1nppp/5q2/2b5/2pNPP2/2P1B3/PP: Finally, let's develop and hit that weak c4 pawn with knight to d2.
Well done! We own the center and have more development and a better pawn structure. The computer gives us a +1 point advantage.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/1q6/4P3/3Q4/8/PPP2PPP/: OK black is insisting on trading queens. Fine. Let's play bishop to e3 so we can atleast get some development.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4P3/3q4/4B3/PPP2PPP/: Bishop takes back on d4, of course.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4P3/3B4/8/PPP2PPP/RN: Well done! We simply own the center now.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp1nppp/3p1q2/2b1n3/3NP3/2P1B3/: Remember when black brought their knight to e5 to hit our bishop, so we moved our bishop to e2? Well, now we get our revenge. Pawn to f4 hits that very knight.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp1nppp/3p1q2/2b1n3/3NPP2/2P1B3: Well done! That pawn push is giving us an edge of the opponent.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppppnppp/5q2/2b1n3/2BNP3/2P1B3/P: Let's drop our bishop back to e2 where it will never be bothered again.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp1nppp/5q2/2bpn3/3NP3/2P1B3/PP: Black is opening up the center. Our first priority is to get our king OUT of the center so he's no longer a target. King castles kingside. Technically, this move gambits our e4 pawn but trust me its worth it.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp1nppp/5q2/2b1n3/3Np3/2P1B3/PP: Now a lethal trap: knight to b5. Now our knight hits the c7 pawn threatening a fork, and our bishop hits the undefended c5 bishop.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp1nppp/3b1q2/1N2n3/4p3/2P1B3/P: Black thought they saved their bishop and c7 pawn - but they didn't. We can distract the bishop AWAY from the c7 pawn with bishop to c5.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp1nppp/3b1q2/1NB1n3/4p3/2P5/PP: Black had to castle - there was really no other option. Now we can clean up the board with knight takes bishop on d6.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pp2nppp/3p1q2/2B1n3/4p3/2P5/PP2B: Now this is very important. DONT take the pawn with the bishop. Take it with the queen. Queen takes pawn on d6.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pp2nppp/3B4/4n3/4p3/2P5/PP2BPPP/: Well done! We win over 70% of the time from here.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp1nppp/2np1q2/2b5/2BNP3/2P1B3/: Let's castle our king to safety.
Well done! We are ready to play some chess.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppppnppp/1bn2q2/1N6/4P3/2N5/PPP1: Dang... black stopped our knight-to-d5 idea. Let's try and get rid of that key bishop another way: bishop to e3.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppppnppp/1bn2q2/1N6/4P3/2N1B3/PP: Well done! We'll try and take that bishop if we can, and castle if we can't.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp1nppp/2np1q2/2b5/2BNP3/2P1B3/: Let's clear up the center: knight takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp2ppp/2np1q2/2b5/2B1P3/2P1B3/P: Keep clearing up the center: bishop takes bishop on c5.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/ppp2ppp/2n2q2/2p5/2B1P3/2P5/PP3P: Now we begin the kingside attack. The point here is black's queen is kind of uncomfortable right now. Let's make her more uncomfortable with pawn to f4.
descriptions.r4rk1/ppp2ppp/2n1bq2/2p5/2B1PP2/2P5/PP4P: And now e5, attacking the queen.
descriptions.r4rk1/ppp1qppp/2n1b3/2p1P3/2B2P2/2P5/PP4: Let's trade bishops next. Bishop takes bishop on e6.
descriptions.r4rk1/ppp2ppp/2n1q3/2p1P3/5P2/2P5/PP4PP/: Now let's develop our other knight. Knight to d2.
descriptions.r4rk1/ppp2ppp/2n1q3/2p1P3/5P2/2P5/PP1N2P: Well done! Let's play some chess now.
descriptions.r4rk1/ppp2ppp/2n1b1q1/2p1P3/2B2P2/2P5/PP: The queen can't get away that easily. Bishop to d3.
descriptions.r4rk1/ppp2ppp/2n5/2p1Pq2/5P2/2P5/PP1N2PP: Well done! We have a slightly better position.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p1p2ppp/2p2n2/3p4/4P3/3B4/PPP2P: Black is putting pressure on our central e-pawn. Surprisingly, the best move here is pawn takes pawn on d5, un-doubling our opponent's pawn structure. I don't know why. Chess is weird sometimes.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p1p2ppp/5n2/3p4/8/3B4/PPP2PPP/R: Now let's castle our king to safety.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1p1bppp/5n2/3p4/8/3B4/PPP2PPP/R: We shouldn't let black have the center for long. Pawn to c4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p1p1bppp/5n2/3p4/2P5/3B4/PP3PPP/: Well done! Both you and black played absolutely perfectly.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Let's learn the Sicilian Defense! Legends like Kasparov, Fischer, and Carlsen mastered this opening â and who knows, maybe after this course, your name will be on that list too. Or hey, maybe youâre just trying to claw your way out of 600 ELO. Either way, youâre in the right place. Pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/8/2p5/4P3/5N2/PPPP1PPP: White plays knight to f3, which means we're doing the OPEN sicilian. There are other moves white could've played, but this course is already 50 lines long so I'll save them for a future course. Next we play pawn to d6 to open up our light-squared bishop and stop white's e-pawn from marching down into our territory.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/3p4/2p5/3PP3/5N2/PPP2PP: Ok, well that was quite aggressive from white. We need to take the pawn here or we risk white pushing the d-pawn forward and taking all the central space. Pawn takes on d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/3p4/8/3NP3/8/PPP2PPP/RN: Great, we got rid of one of white's center pawns while keeping ours. Let's naturally develop and hit the e4 pawn next with knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p1n2/8/3NP3/2N5/PPP2PP: OK now we're going to enter the DRAGON sicilian with pawn to g6. It's called the dragon because supposedly our pawns are in the shape of a dragon. I think whoever named it has never seen a dragon - it should be called the squiggly line sicilian. In any case, pawn to g6 so we can put our bishop on g7 and castle.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pp1p/3p1np1/8/3NP3/2N1B3/PPP: Our plan: bishop to g7 and castle. Then we launch an attack on the queenside.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/8/3NP3/2N1BP2/PPP: That move defended the e4 pawn. That doesn't really affect us or our plans. Let's just castle.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/8/3NP3/2N1BP2/PP: Let's develop the knight to c6. Simple chess, simple life.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2np1np1/8/2BNP3/2N1BP2/: Let's keep developing before we do anything crazy. Bishop to d7. This is a waiting move - we want to see which way white castles before we launch an attack.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp1bppbp/2np1np1/8/2BNP3/2N1BP2/: Aaaand we bring our rook over to c8, aiming straight down for the king.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/2np1np1/8/3NP3/1BN1BP2/: Now that white's bishop is on b3, our idea is to use our queenside pawns to race down and attack him. Before we do that though, let's play knight to d4 to trade off white's strong centralized knight and open up our rook.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1np1/8/3BP3/1BN2P2/PP: OK! Time to use our pawns. Pawn to b5. We are TELLING our opponent that an attack is coming.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/p2bppbp/3p1np1/1p6/3BP3/1BN2P2/P: White moved his king to b1 - a common move, just to solidify everything. But now we continue our attack: Pawn to a5.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bppbp/3p1np1/pp6/P2BP3/1BN2P2/1: That move just LOST white the game after this forcing sequence: pawn takes a4...
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bppbp/3p1np1/p7/N2BP3/1B3P2/1PP: ... then bishop takes knight on a4 ...
descriptions.2rq1rk1/4ppbp/3p1np1/p7/B2BP3/5P2/1PPQ2P: .... and finally, rook to c4, FORKING the two bishops.
descriptions.3q1rk1/4ppbp/3p1np1/p7/2rBP3/1B3P2/1PPQ2: Our rook is under attack, but one brilliant move here wins us the game. And no, it's not moving the rook. Knight to e4 - hitting the QUEEN!
descriptions.3q1rk1/4ppbp/3p2p1/p7/2rBP3/1B6/1PPQ2PP/: Now that our knight moved out of the way for our bishop, we have a second attacker on the bishop on d4. So, let's play rook takes on d4.
descriptions.3q1rk1/4ppbp/3p2p1/p7/3rP3/1B6/1PPQ2PP/1: Yes!! We are a pawn up, but more than that: our position is so strong here the computer gives us a +4 point advantage and we win over NINETY PERCENT OF THE TIME FROM HERE
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2np1np1/8/3NP3/2N1BP2/P: Now that white castled, we want to launch an attack. A serious one. To prep, let's move our bishop to d7. This let's our rook slide to c8 in the future and stare down at the white king
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp1bppbp/2np1np1/8/3NP1P1/2N1BP2: Now rook to c8. Our rook is looking down the board directly at the white king.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/2np1np1/8/3NP1PP/2N1BP2: White is RACING down our king side but... if I'm being honest... I don't really care. I'm way more interested in causing some chaos with our knight and queen. First up: knight to e5.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1np1/4n2P/3NP1P1/2N1B: Again. I simply do. not. care. about white's attack. Queen to a5 and all of a sudden, we win MOST of our games from here. You'll see why. Spoiler alert: we're going to sacrifice our knight on f3 and our rook on c3 a LOT.
descriptions.2r2rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1nP1/q3n3/3NP1P1/2N1BP: If anything, white's attack on our king side is HELPING us. Now we can play f-pawn takes g6 and open up our other rook. All our pieces are becoming active.
descriptions.2r2rk1/pp1bp1bp/3p1npB/q3n3/3NP1P1/2N2P2: Here, we actually take the bishop to LURE the queen AWAY from the guard of the c3 knight. Bishop takes bishop on h6.
descriptions.2r2rk1/pp1bp2p/3p1npQ/q3n3/3NP1P1/2N2P2/: Now? We sacrifice... THE ROOOOOOK. Rook takes knight on c3.
descriptions.5rk1/pp1bp2p/3p1npQ/q3n3/3NP1P1/2P2P2/P1: And the follow up: Queen takes pawn on c3.
descriptions.5rk1/pp1bp2p/3p1npQ/4n3/4P1P1/1Nq2P2/P1P: Why not bring our other rook to the party? rook to c8, adding tons of pressure on that scrawny c2 pawn.
descriptions.2r3k1/pp1bp2p/3p1npQ/4n3/4P1P1/1Nq2P2/P1: Well done! White will defend their c2 pawn and our knight will gobble on f3 to win a pawn.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1np1/4n3/3NP1PP/2N1BP: White moved their king to b1 a bit earlier than we're used to. It doesn't change much - we still go queen to a5.
descriptions.2r2rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1np1/q2Nn3/3NP1PP/4BP2: White is threatening to fork us on e7 with check. We'll see in a second that this idea is actually completely losing for white. Queen takes queen on d2.
descriptions.2r2rk1/pp1bNpbp/3p1np1/4n3/3NP1PP/4BP2/P: King to h8, only move. It looks like we're losing a rook here but remember, white has to take our queen first which means we'll get a chance to move our rook out of the way.
descriptions.2r2r1k/pp1bNpbp/3p1np1/4n3/3NP1PP/4BP2/P: Now we move our rook to e8, hitting the knight, and white is completely lost.
descriptions.4rr1k/pp1b1pbp/3p1np1/3Nn3/3NP1PP/4BP2/P: To win from here we have a forcing sequence. First, knight takes knight on d5.
descriptions.4rr1k/pp1b1pbp/3p2p1/3Pn3/3N2PP/4BP2/PPP: Now we sacrifice our knight on f3. Don't worry, we'll get the material back on the next move.
descriptions.4rr1k/pp1b1pbp/3p2p1/3P4/6PP/4BN2/PPPR4/: Time to get the material back. Rook takes bishop on e3.
descriptions.5r1k/pp1b1pbp/3p2p1/3P4/6PP/4rN2/PPPR4/1: White is dead. We are simply threating too many things. The knight on f3 is hanging, and we also have backrank checkmate in one.
descriptions.2r2rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1np1/q3n2P/3NP1P1/2N1B: I told you there'd be sacrifices. And I didn't lie. The line here goes 20 moves deep, and it starts with sacrificing our knight on f3.
descriptions.2r2rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1np1/q6P/4P1P1/2N1BN2/: One sacrifice wasn't cool enough? Well how about sacrificing our rook on c3?
descriptions.5rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1np1/q6P/4P1P1/2Q1BN2/PP: We're down in material, so we want to keep queens on the board right? WRONG. Queen takes queen on c3.
descriptions.5rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1np1/7P/4P1P1/2P1BN2/P1P: We're 4 points of material down. White is just simply up a rook. But our position is so deadly that it might not even matter. Bishop takes pawn on g4.
descriptions.5rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/7P/4P1b1/2P1BN2/P1P1: White had to defend their knight. Now we get knight takes pawn on e4, which wins a pawn (obviously) and also creates a DOUBLE attack on the c3 pawn. We have nasty intentions to put our knight on c3 and fork the king and rook.
descriptions.5rk1/pp2ppbp/3p2p1/7P/3Bn1b1/2P2N2/P1P1B: Oof. White defended the pawn, but they did so the wrong way. Now we just have pawn to e5, hitting the bishop and forcing it away.
descriptions.5rk1/Bp3pbp/3p2p1/4p2P/4n1b1/2P2N2/P1P1B: We don't even care about that pawn. We have bigger plans. Knight to c3 forking the rook and king. Splash.
descriptions.5rk1/Bp3pbp/3p2p1/4p2P/6b1/2n2N2/PKP1B3/: Now we win our rook back. Knight takes rook on d1.
descriptions.5rk1/Bp3pbp/3p2p1/4p2P/6b1/5N2/PKP1B3/3n: We won our rook back, and we'll win even more material soon because we have pawn to e4 discover-checking the king and hitting the f3 knight.
descriptions.5rk1/pp1bp2p/3p1npQ/4n1P1/3NP3/2q2P2/P1P: Aaaaaaand game over. Queen to a1 check, forcing the king to d2.
descriptions.5rk1/pp1bp2p/3p1npQ/4n1P1/3NP3/5P2/P1PK4: Now with the king on d2, we can take the knight on d4 with our queen with check.
descriptions.5rk1/pp1bp2p/3p1npQ/4n1P1/3qP3/5P2/P1PK4: Obliterated. All our pieces are coming to hunt down this king. By the way - don't forget about our hanging knight on f6.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/p2bppbp/3p1np1/1p6/3BP2P/1BN2P2/: White counter attacks us, but our own attack is even faster. Pawn to a5.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bppbp/3p1np1/pp6/P2BP2P/1BN2P2/: We can either push our pawn to b4 and lock the position, or take on a4 and open up the position. Given the white king is back there, we want to open up the position. Pawn takes pawn on a4.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bppbp/3p1np1/p7/N2BP2P/1B3P2/1P: Let's continue opening up the position: bishop takes knight on a4.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/4ppbp/3p1np1/p7/B2BP2P/5P2/1PPQ2: Now we have a beautiful tactic, starting with rook to c4. It looks like a weird move, but it'll win us a game. White has to move or defend the a4 bishop.
descriptions.3q1rk1/4ppbp/3p1np1/p7/2rBP2P/1B3P2/1PPQ: Our rook is under attack, but what's better than a rook? A queen! Knight takes e4, threatening to take the queen on the next move. White has to address the threat.
descriptions.3q1rk1/4ppbp/3p2p1/p7/2rBP2P/1B6/1PPQ2P1: Now that the knight moved out of the way, our rook can take the bishop on d4. Now we're hitting the queen AGAIN, and we're a pawn up.
descriptions.3q1rk1/4ppbp/3p2p1/p7/3rP2P/1B6/1PPQ2P1/: We literally win 90% of the time from here. It's over for white.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bppbp/3p1np1/1p1B3P/p2BP3/2N2P2: KEEP. PUSHING. Pawn to e5 boots the dark squared bishop out of the position.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3b1pbp/3p1np1/1p1Bp2P/p3P3/2N1BP: Keeeeep. Pushiiiiing. Pawn to b4 forces the knight out of the position.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3b1pbp/3p1np1/3Bp2P/pp2P3/4BP2/P: For the first time in a long time, we don't play a pawn move. We take the bishop on d5 with our knight. That bishop is the only active piece in white's army.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3b1pbp/3p2p1/3Pp2P/pp6/4BP2/PPPQ: By taking back with the pawn, white just gave us a deadly attack. Bishop to f5 and now we have two attackers on the c2 pawn. White only has a king and queen to defend.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/5pbp/3p2p1/3Ppb1P/pp6/2P1BP2/PP1: We are smash open white's king. Pawn to a3.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/5pbp/3p2p1/3Ppb1P/1p6/p1P1BP2/PP: Even though material is equal, our attack is so strong and white's pieces are so weak that the computer gives us a +3 point advantage.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3b1pbp/3p2p1/3Qp2P/pp2P3/4BP2/PP: Now that white's pieces are all pushed back, let's bring our own pieces in. Queen to c7 creates a checkmate threat on c2.
descriptions.2r2rk1/2qb1pbp/3p2p1/3Qp2P/pp2P3/4BP2/PP: Let's add our bishop to the party! Bishop to e6 to hit the queen and create a powerful diagonal for us.
descriptions.2r2rk1/2q2pbp/3Qb1p1/4p2P/pp2P3/4BP2/PPP: Queen to c4 and it is OVER for white. We are threatening our queen to infiltrate through the a2 pawn.
descriptions.2r2rk1/5pbp/3Qb1p1/4p2P/ppq1P3/4BP2/PPPR: Well done! The computer gives us a huge advantage because, at the end of the day, our queen is taking the a2 pawn and getting into the white position.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pp1p/3p1np1/8/3NP3/2N5/PPP1B: This is so passive from white. But, like always, we just continue with our plan. Bishop to g7.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/8/3NP3/2N1B3/PPP: Let's continue developing: knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2np1np1/8/3NPP2/2N1B3/P: OK this move is a bit high level: ideally we want our queen on b6, but we've never been able to play it because the e3 bishop can discover attack us on b6 by just moving the knight. But, now that white moved that f-pawn, that e3 bishop is no longer defended! Which means we CAN play queen to b6.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pp2ppbp/1qnp1np1/5N2/4PP2/2N1B3/: There's a hanging pawn on b2. Let's take it with queen to b2. Oh - and now we're attacking a hanging knight on c3! White can't defend both knights at the same time
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pp2ppNp/2np1np1/8/4PP2/2N1B3/PqP: Two knights are hanging - which should we take? Well. the g7 knight is TRAPPED. It can't go anywhere. So let's take the c3 knight with our queen on this turn, and we'll get the g7 knight on the next one
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pp2ppNp/2np1np1/8/4PP2/2q5/P1PBB: White is delaying the inevitable. Queen to d4 check.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pp2ppNp/2np1np1/8/3qPP2/8/P1PBB1: NOW we can take the g7 knight.
descriptions.r1b2r2/pp2ppkp/2np1np1/8/3qPP2/8/P1PBB1P: We literally just have an extra piece and pawn. Not bad!
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/2np1np1/8/2BNP3/2N1BP2/: HUGE blunder from white. They CANNOT leave the bishop on c4 because it is simply undefended. All we need to do is play knight takes d4, and the c4 bishop is under attack from our rook.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1np1/8/2BQP3/2N1BP2/P: White took back with the queen so that they could defend the bishop. It won't work. Knight to g4 DISCOVERS an attack on the QUEEN from our bishop on g7. Did you forget about him? Well, don't. He's our best friend in the dragon sicilian.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/3p2p1/8/2B1P1n1/2NQBP2/: White's queen is overloaded. She can't defend both bishops at the same time. Knight takes bishop on e3.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/3p2p1/8/2B1P3/2N1QP2/PP: And rook takes bishop on c4. Boom.
descriptions.3q1rk1/pp1bppbp/3p2p1/8/2r1P3/2N1QP2/PPP: That, right there, is how it's done.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bppbp/3p1np1/pp6/3BP2P/PBN2P2/1: That move runs directly into pawn to b4. We really want white's queenside pawns to fall so we can expose the king. Pawn to b4.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bppbp/3p1np1/p7/1P1BP2P/1BN2P2/: We take back with pawn to b4.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bppbp/3p1np1/3N4/1p1BP2P/1B3P2/: We simply must trade off the knights if we want our attack to continue. Knight to d5.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bppBp/3p2p1/3n4/1p2P2P/1B3P2/1P: King takes back on g7 of course.
descriptions.2rq1r2/3bppkp/3p2p1/3P4/1p5P/1B3P2/1PPQ2: See that open a-file. It is CALLING our queen's name. Queen to a5.
descriptions.2r2r2/3bppkp/3p2p1/q2P4/1p1Q3P/1B3P2/1PP: King has to drop back to g8.
descriptions.2r2rk1/3bpp1p/3p2p1/q2P3P/1p1Q4/1B3P2/1P: White's attacking us, but I'll say it again: our attack is faster. And better. Bishop to f5 putting the c2 pawn under pressure.
descriptions.2r2rk1/4pp1p/3p2p1/q2P1b1P/1p1Q2P1/1B3P2: White hits our bishop? We SACRIFICE OUR BISHOP. Bishop to c2. Kaboom.
descriptions.2r2rk1/4pp1p/3p2p1/q2P3P/1p1Q2P1/5P2/1PB: It's game over. Pawn to b3 hitting the pinned c2 bishop.
descriptions.2r2rk1/4pp1p/3p2p1/q2P3P/3Q2P1/1p3P2/1PB: The king is basically trapped in his castle right now. Let's build our attack by doubling our rooks on the c-file. First step: rook to c7.
descriptions.5rk1/2r1pp1p/3p2p1/q2P3P/3Q2P1/1p3P2/1PB: Well done! White has no defense from the upcoming rook battery we'll build on the c-file
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2Np1np1/8/4P3/2N1BP2/PP: White took our knight - which is actually a pretty big mistake from them. Now when we take back with pawn to c6, we have an open b-file for our rook.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p3ppbp/2pp1npB/8/4P3/2N2P2/PPPQ: The best way to play this is with bishop takes h6, luring the queen away from the defense of her king.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p3pp1p/2pp1npQ/8/4P3/2N2P2/PPP3: With white's queen out of the way, we can begin taking apart white's queenside. Queen to a5, putting a bit of pressure on the a2 pawn and the c3 knight.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/p3pp1p/2pp1npQ/q7/4P3/2N2P2/PPP3: White just castled into danger. Let's add another attacker to the a2 pawn with bishop to e6.
descriptions.r4rk1/p3pp1p/2ppbnpQ/q7/4P3/P1N2P2/1PP3P: Remember that open b-file? We can finally take advantage of it. Lets bring our a-rook to b8
descriptions.1r3rk1/p3pp1p/2ppbnpQ/q7/4P3/P1N2P2/1PP3: White is completely losing here ALREADY. We're putting way too much pressure on the queenside.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pp1p/3p1np1/6B1/3NP3/2N5/PPP: White played bishop to g5 instead of pawn to f3 which is important, but it will only become important later. For now we continue with our setup: bishop to g7.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/6B1/3NP3/2N5/PPPQ: Let's target that dark-squared bishop. Pawn to h6.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppb1/3p1npp/8/3NP2B/2N5/PPPQ1: Let's continue developing with knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp2ppb1/2np1npp/8/3NP2B/2N5/PPPQ: Here, we have a beautiful sacrifice: knight takes pawn on e4. Don't worry - we'll win the knight back on the next move!
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp2ppb1/2np2pp/8/3NN2B/8/PPPQ1PP: White captured our knight, but we win him back with knight takes knight on d4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp2ppb1/3p2pp/8/3nN2B/8/PPPQ1PPP: Yay! We're up a pawn and we'll win the game.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/8/3NP3/2N1B3/PPPQ: This is actually a... big mistake from white. Because white trapped the bishop in, we can try and take it with knight to g4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/3p2p1/8/3NP1n1/2N1B3/PPP: Aaaand we take the bishop. Bishops are better than knights so why not.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/3p2p1/8/3NP3/2N1n3/PPPQ1: Nice. Now our dark-squared bishop is even more powerful, and we are likely winning this game.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppb1/3p1npp/8/3NP3/2N1B3/PPPQ: Black ran away, but we can still hunt the bishop down with knight to g4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppb1/3p2pp/8/3NP1n1/2N1B3/PPP: And now we take the bishop. Knight takes on e3.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppb1/3p2pp/8/3NP3/2N1n3/PPPQ1: Now that the white dark-squared bishop is gone, our dark-squared bishop has become even stronger than it already was
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp2ppb1/2Np2pp/8/4n2B/2N5/PPPQ1P: DONT capture the knight back. If we do, we'll end up down a knight. To keep our advantage, we actually play knight takes queen on d2.
descriptions.r1bNk2r/pp2ppb1/3p2pp/8/7B/2N5/PPPn1PPP/: We still don't capture the knight, and instead we play knight takes bishop on f1
descriptions.r1bNk2r/pp2ppb1/3p2pp/8/7B/2N5/PPP2PPP/2: We STILL don't capture the knight, and we instead play pawn to g5, attacking the bishop. The knight is trapped, so there's no rush to capture
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pp2pNb1/3p3p/6p1/7B/2N5/PPP2PPP/: Believe it or not, white taking that pawn actually helped us. We're moving to an endgame, and our king is better on f7 than e8. So, king to f7.
descriptions.r1b4r/pp2pkb1/3p3p/6p1/8/2N3B1/PPP2PPP/2: Finally, we want to ruin white's pawn structure with bishop to c3.
descriptions.r1b4r/pp2pk2/3p3p/6p1/8/2b3B1/PPP2PPP/2K: Nice! We'll bring our bishop to f5 to attack the c2 and our rooks to center to start attacking white's weak pawns.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/3p4/2p5/2B1P3/5N2/PPPP1: Let's continue creating our dragon: knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p1n2/2p5/2B1P3/2N2N2/P: So it's kind of interesting - white is not playing the correct way against our sicilian. They should've played pawn to d3 to open up their bishop. The best reponse here is to FORGET about the dragon sicilian and play pawn to e6. Honestly, I have no idea why, but that's what the computer says... Our idea is to develop our bishop to e7, instead of the regular g7.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp3ppp/3ppn2/2p5/2B1P3/2NP1N2/P: Let's continue with our new plan: bishop develops to e7.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2bppp/3ppn2/2p3B1/2B1P3/2NP1N: Nice! We actually have a solid edge against our opponent here.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/8/3NP3/2N1B3/PPP: We keep going with the setup: knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2np1np1/8/3NP3/2N1BP2/P: White has taken way too long to castle, and given we're already castled and most of our pieces are developed, we should try and crash open the center. Pawn to d5 is winning.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2n2np1/3P4/3N4/2N1BP2/P: Great! The center is opening up and now we're winning the game. Knight takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2n3p1/3N4/3N4/4BP2/PPPQ: Queen takes knight on d5 of course
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pp2ppbp/2N3p1/3q4/8/4BP2/PPPQB1P: We take back with the queen. Queen to c6.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pp2ppbp/2q3p1/8/8/4BP2/PPPQB1PP/: Nice work! Our pieces are just better coordinated than whiteâs, and our king is completely safe. Our g7 bishop is dominating the board, and the position is looking greatâthe engine agrees, weâre in control.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pp1p/3p1np1/8/3NPP2/2N5/PPP3: White is trying to play a sneaky attack. If we just play our regular move - bishop to g7 - then white plays pawn to e5 and forces our knight back leaving us with no space and no chance to win the game. So, instead, let's develop our other knight with knight to c6 to defend that e5 square.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pp1p/2Np1np1/8/4PP2/2N5/PPP3: White took our defender of the e5 square, which sucks. We have to capture back with pawn to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p3pp1p/2pp1np1/4P3/5P2/2N5/PPP3: White went ahead with their plan to push to e5. The best move here is NOT to take the pawn but instead drop the knight down to d7. Taking the pawn would just trade away a central pawn and after white takes back, we'd be in the same spot. So, knight to d7.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p2npp1p/2pP2p1/8/5P2/2N5/PPP3PP: We need to capture back with pawn to d6
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/p2n1p1p/2pp2p1/8/5P2/2N1B3/PPP3: Very important! We DON'T play bishop to g7 here, because it hangs our d6 pawn. So, to develop the bishop, we actually play bishop to e7.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p2nbp1p/2pp2p1/8/5P2/2N1B3/PPPQ2: One more move before we castle: let's play pawn to d5. This frees up our bishop so it no longer has to guard the pawn.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p2nbp1p/2p3p1/3p4/5P2/2N1B3/PPP: Nice! White tried to rush-attack us but we ended up in a better position with a higher winrate.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp2ppb1/2Np1npp/8/4P2B/2N5/PPPQ1: We need to take back with our pawn. Pawn to c6.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/p3ppb1/2pp1npp/8/2B1P2B/2N5/PPPQ: Let's play queen to b6 and hit white's undefended b2 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/p3ppb1/1qpp1npp/8/2B1P2B/2N5/PPP: Nice! We'll march our a-pawn up the board and cause serious problems for white.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/3p4/8/3QP3/5N2/PPP2PPP/: This move is called the Chekhover Sicilian, and it tells you White knows what they're doing. We should develop here with knight to c6, hitting the queen to get a tempo.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pp2pppp/2np4/1B6/3QP3/5N2/PPP2P: We need to respect this threat by playing bishop to d7. If we don't, white has all sorts of nasty tricks for us.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp1bpppp/2Bp4/8/3QP3/5N2/PPP2PPP: Let's take back with the bishop to put it on the diagonal. Bishop takes on c6.
descriptions.r2qkbnr/pp2pppp/2bp4/8/3QP3/5N2/PPP2PPP/: And now its time to play chess!
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/6B1/2BNP3/2N5/PPP: Let's castle here, continuing with our dragon plan.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/6B1/2BNP3/2N5/PP: Well done! Now it's time to play chess.
descriptions.4rr1k/pp1bNpbp/3p1np1/4n1P1/3NP2P/4BP2/P: This was white's only good move. Here, let's sacrifice our knight on e4 given we can win it back on the next move.
descriptions.4rr1k/pp1bNpbp/3p2p1/4n1P1/3NP2P/4B3/PPP: Let's win our knight back! Rook takes knight on e7.
descriptions.5r1k/pp1brpbp/3p2p1/4n1P1/3NP2P/4B3/PPPR: Nice! The material is equal but we win like 70% of the time from here.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/3p4/2p5/4P3/2P2N2/PP1P1: White is trying to play the Alapin Sicilian. If these words mean nothing to you, thats OK. All that matters is that we play knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p1n2/2p5/4P3/2P2N2/PP1: It might be tempting to take that harmless e4 pawn, but if you do, you'll lose the game. White has this deadly queen a4 check in their back pocket, and they'd win our knight. Instead, keep going as planned: pawn to g6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pp1p/3p1np1/2p5/4P3/2P2N2/PP: You got this! Bishop to g7.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/2p5/4P3/2P2N2/PP: White is trying to play pawn to d4 here. You can tell because they spent a move playing pawn to c3 to build up into the d4 square. Let's stop them by simply playing pawn to e5.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3pbp/3p1np1/2p1p3/4P3/2P2N2/P: Well done! We stopped the Aalapin Sicilian in its tracks.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pp2pp1p/2np1np1/8/3NPP2/2N1B3/P: With our c6 knight adding a defender to the e5 square, NOW it's safe to put our bishop on g7. Bishop to g7.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp2ppbp/2np1np1/8/3NPP2/2N1B3/PP: Well done! We'll castle and continue on with our game.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pp1p/3p1np1/8/2BNP3/2N5/PPP2: Let's continue with our plan, bishop to g7.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/6B1/2BNP3/2N5/PP: Knight to c6. We've seen these moves a million times.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2Np1np1/6B1/2B1P3/2N5/P: Take back with the pawn, of course. Pawn takes on c6.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p3ppbp/2pp1np1/6B1/2B1P3/2N5/PP: White led us into a pretty boring and passive game. Whatever, now its time to play chess.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/3p1n2/2p5/2B1P3/3P1N2/P: Pawn to g6 so we can put our bishop on g7...
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pp2pp1p/3p1np1/2p5/2B1P3/3P1N2/: And let's play bishop to g7 - this is all textbook.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/2p3B1/2B1P3/3P1N2: It seems tempting to castle here - I mean we did all that work just so we could castle - but the bishop coming to g5 means we should chase it away first. Pawn to h6.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppb1/3p1npp/2p5/2B1P2B/3P1N2/: And we keep chasing it away. Pawn to g5.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppb1/3p1n1p/2p3p1/2B1P3/3P1NB: Why not set up a nasty pin on white's f3 knight? White's light-squared bishop is locked away on the other side of the board so it can't unpin his friend. Bishop to g4.
descriptions.rn1qk2r/pp2ppb1/3p1n1p/2p3p1/2B1P1b1/3P1: Well done! We have a solid position and in the future we'll hop our knight from b8, to c6, to d4 and apply even more pressure on that f3 knight.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp2ppbp/3p1np1/8/2BNP3/2N1BP2/P: White is playing the Yugoslav attack. Personally, I'm not worried. Let's continue with natural development: knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2np1np1/8/3NP3/1BN1BP2/: Let's continue with developing our bishop to d7...
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp1bppbp/2np1np1/8/3NP3/1BN1BP2/: We want to push our pawn to b5 to attack white's bishop, BUT there's two white knights defending that square. We can fix that by playing knight takes knight on d4.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp1bppbp/3p1np1/8/3BP3/1BN2P2/PP: Now we have a defender on the b5 square (our bishop) and white only has one attacker (the knight). So, let's play pawn to b5.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/p2bppbp/3p1np1/1p6/3BP3/1BN2P2/P: Well done! The pawn storm is coming.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2N2np1/3p4/4P3/2N1BP2/P: Take back with pawn to c6, of course.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p3ppbp/2p2np1/3pP3/8/2N1BP2/PPP: White is attacking our knight - but we can move it to d7 and now our knight and bishop have a DOUBLE attack on the pawn.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p2nppbp/2p3p1/3pP3/5P2/2N1B3/PP: Let's play pawn to e6 to further stabilize our center
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/p2n1pbp/2p1p1p1/3pP3/5P2/2N1B3/: Nice! Look how our pawns are strong and control the center! In the future we'll creep our c6 pawn up to take even more space away from white and even threaten a fork with pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/3p2p1/6B1/3NP1n1/2N5/PPP: You can run but you cant hide! Pawn to h6.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp2ppb1/3p2pp/8/3NP1nB/2N5/PPPQ1: OK turns out you CAN hide. We're no longer interested in taking that bishop. Lets just keep developing: knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pp2ppb1/2np2pp/8/3NP1nB/2N5/PPPQ: Well done! We win most of the games from here.
descriptions.2r2rk1/4pp1p/3p2P1/q2P1b2/1p1Q4/1B3P2/1P: We should take back with the f-pawn to open up our rook. F7 takes g6.
descriptions.2r2rk1/4p2p/3p2p1/q2P1b2/1p1Q4/1B3P2/1PP: Nice job handling that pawn attack from white!
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2np1np1/8/3NP3/2N1B3/PP: Because white never played pawn to f3, we can unleash knight to g4, hitting the dark-squared bishop.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2np2p1/8/3NP1B1/2N1B3/P: Take back with the bishop, of course. Bishop to g4.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2ppbp/2np2p1/8/3NP1b1/2N1BP2/P: Let's be active here. Instead of bringing our bishop all the way back to d7, we can bring our bishop to e6, and start pointing our pieces towards the white king.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2ppbp/2npb1p1/8/3NP2P/2N1BP2/P: White is starting a kingside attack but our attack is faster. Queen to a5.
descriptions.r4rk1/pp2ppbp/2npb1p1/q7/3NP2P/2N1BP2/PP: Well done! We have serious pressure on the a2 pawn and the c3 knight.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2ppbp/2npN1p1/8/4P3/2N1BP2/PPP: That is totally fine! We take back with pawn to e6 and now our rook is active on the f-file.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2p1bp/2npp1pB/8/4P3/2N2P2/PPPQ: Let's bring our queen to a5, adding more pressure on the c3 knight and a2 pawn.
descriptions.r4rk1/pp2p1Bp/2npp1p1/q7/4P3/2N2P2/PPPQ2: King takes back on g7, of course.
descriptions.r4r2/pp2p1kp/2npp1p1/q7/4P3/2N2P2/PPPQ2P: Well done! We'll bring our rook to c8 and begin our queenside attack.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2np1np1/8/3NP1P1/2N1BP2: White is playing the Panov Variation - which is just them telling us "I am going to attack you right now". Let's punish them for it. Usually we develop our bishop to d7, but here, we'll actually develop it to e6 and LET white trade with our bishop.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2ppbp/2npNnp1/8/4P1P1/2N1BP2/P: Pawn takes back on e6, of course.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2p1bp/2nppnp1/8/4P1P1/2N1BP2/P: Finally, let's plant our knight on e5.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp2p1bp/3ppnp1/4n3/4P1P1/2N1BP2/: Well done! Even though it looks like our pawn structure is damaged, it's actually quite strong against white's position.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/2np1np1/6P1/3NP3/2N1BP2: Blunder! We can move our knight to h5 and now our dark-square bishop stares down the whole board.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppbp/2np2p1/6Pn/3NP3/2N1BP2/: Well done! White did all that work just to blunder and give us a winning position.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bppbp/3p1Bp1/1p5P/p3P3/1BN2P2/P: Weirdly enough, we should take back with the pawn here, not the bishop. We need the bishop to stay where he is and guard the h6 square so the queen can never come. Pawn takes on f6.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3b1pbp/3p1pp1/1p5P/p3P3/1BN2P2/P: Nice job! We win more often than not from here.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp1bppbp/2np1np1/8/3NP2P/2N1BP2/: Let's nip this attack in the bud. Pawn to h5.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/pp1bppb1/2np1np1/7p/3NP2P/2N1BP2: We're transposing into similar situations we've seen before. Rook to c8.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/pp1bppb1/2np1np1/7p/3NP2P/2N1BP2: Well done! We'll continue playing from here with the same sacrifice ideas we've been learning.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/p2bppbp/3p1np1/1p1N4/3BP3/1B3P2/: Now there's two attackers on our knight. It's best to just play knight to d5 and trade off that annoying white knight.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/p2bppBp/3p2p1/1p1n4/4P3/1B3P2/PP: Take back on g7 with the king, of course.
descriptions.2rq1r2/p2bppkp/3p2p1/1p1P4/8/1B3P2/PPPQ2: The more trades white does, the less of an attack they have. Meanwhile, we have our pawns who are just WAITING to get to the other wide of the board and hit that bishop. Pawn to a5.
descriptions.2rq1r2/3bppkp/3p2p1/pp1P4/8/PB3P2/1PPQ2P: Here, we'd LOVE to play pawn to b4 but white has queen to d4 check, ruining some of our plans. So, let's anticipate that move and play king back to g8 first.
descriptions.2rq1rk1/3bpp1p/3p2p1/pp1P4/8/PB3P2/1PPQ2: Nice, it'll be a fun game from here.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Let's learn the most venomous, tricky, and trappy opening I know: the Stafford Gambit! First, let's respond to pawn e4 with pawn e5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1PPP: Now, let's move the knight from g8 to f6. Copying our opponent... easy peasy.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/4N3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP: To play the Stafford Gambit, we need White to take this pawn. Rather than winning back the pawn, let's play knight c6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2N2n2/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP: They took our knight and the computer says we are completely lost. However, we are about to unleash some nasty tricks on our opponent. Let's take the knight back with our d pawn, opening the file for our queen and the diagonal for our bishop. The point of this opening is accelerating our development at the cost of giving away a pawn.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/4P3/3P4/PPP2PPP: Let's develop our bishop to c5.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/2b3B1/4P3/3P4/PPP2: Now we play a crazy, absurd, brilliant move: knight e4, losing our queen. Trust me and do it.
descriptions.r1bBk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/4n3/3P4/PPP2PPP/: One move here wins us the game. Can you find it? Hint: bishop to f2 check, forcing the king up to e2.
descriptions.r1bBk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/4n3/3P4/PPP1KbPP/R: Now bishop g4 check - and not just any check... it's checkmate. GG.
descriptions.r2Bk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/4n1b1/3P4/PPP1KbPP/: You've won, but at what cost? Beyond this screen is someone whose hopes you shattered with ruthless precision, their plans crushed under the weight of your cruelty. This wasnât just victory - it was destruction, cold and calculated, and you reveled in it. Remember, no matter how brilliantly you played, the stain of your inhumanity lingers. (cool checkmate though)
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/4P3/8/8/PPPP1PPP/: White is attacking our knight, not even giving us a chance to develop our bishop. It's best here to put our knight in the center to e4, threatening bishop to c5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/4n3/3P4/PPP2PPP: White is continuing to attack our knight, but this is a blunder. Let's play bishop to c5 anyway, sacrificing our knight.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b1P3/4P3/8/PPP2PPP/: White took the bait and lost the game. Black to move and win the queen. Can you find it? Hint: it's bishop f2.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/4P3/8/PPP1KbPP/R: White didn't take the bait? Fine. Bishop g4, checking with the other bishop.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/4P1b1/8/PPP2KPP/R: With the king out of the way, let's take the queen with queen d1.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/4P3/2N5/PPPP1PP: Let's naturally develop our bishop to c5, attacking the f2 pawn.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/2b5/2B1P3/2N5/PPPP: White is developing naturally and trying to castle - let's punish them with the same idea: knight to g4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/2B1P1n1/2N5/PPPP: Castling added a defender to the f2 square. Let's add an attacker with queen h4. This also threatens checkmate on h2! White is in trouble.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/2B1P1nq/2N4P/PPP: Let's take the f2 pawn with the knight, hitting the queen and threatening discovered check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/2B1P2q/2N2Q1P/PP: White is threatening our f7 square, but we are the first to strike. Now we can play the most violent moves in chess: a double check. Knight to h3 means both the knight and bishop are checking the king at the same time.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/2B1P2q/2N2Q1n/PP: Now we can move the knight back to f2, with yet another discovered check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/2B1P2q/2N2Q2/PPP: Mate in 1, can you find it? Hint: Queen to h1.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/2B1P3/2N2Q2/PPPP: It was so natural for White to play all the moves we just saw. Then they suffered the consequences.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/3Pn3/8/PPP2PPP/: Let's play Queen h4 here, threatening mate.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/3Pn2q/6P1/PPP2P: Once again, this is a mistake from white and we will win material. Let's play knight to g3.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/3P3q/6P1/PPP4P/: White to play and win material. Can you find it? Hint: Queen to e4, forking the king and rook.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/3Pq3/6P1/PPP1Q2: And now we win the rook. Queen takes h1.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/3P4/6P1/PPP1Q2P: Well done! We are up in material and will likely go on to win the game.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/4P3/8/PPP2KPP/RN: With the king out of the way, let's take the queen with queen d1.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/4P3/8/PPP2KPP/RN: I think you got it from here.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b3B1/4P3/8/PPP2PPP/: White saw our checkmate coming, and chose to take our knight instead of our queen. Unfortunately for them, now we will win their queen. First, we need to move the king away as a defender of the queen with bishop to f2.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/6B1/4P3/8/PPP1KbPP/R: Now let's check once again with the other bishop. Bishop to g4.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/6B1/4P1b1/8/PPP2KPP/R: Their queen is undefended, let's take it with ours! Queen to d1.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b1P3/4n3/3PB3/PPP2P: White didn't take the bait, but they're still losing. Let's play bishop takes e3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/4n3/3PP3/PPP3PP/: With the king exposed, now we play Queen h4 check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/4n2q/3PP1P1/PPP4: We've seen this idea before. Knight takes g3.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/7q/3PP1P1/PPP5/R: Now we win the rook! Queen takes h1.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/8/3PP1P1/PPP5/RN: It's so easy for White to stumble into these tricks and lose the game.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4P3/4n2q/3PP3/PPP1K1: Checkmate in 1. Can you find it? Hint: Queen to f2.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/2b5/4P3/2NP4/PPP2P: Knight c3 was not a good move from white. Let's attack their weak f pawn with knight g4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/4P1n1/2NP1P2/PPP: White moved the pawn so it couldn't be captured, but we don't even care. We can still dive in with the knight to f2 to fork the queen and rook.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/4P3/2NP1P2/PPP1Q: And now we take the rook with knight to h1.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/2b5/4P3/3P4/PPP1BP: White is playing the main-line, which means they know what they're doing. The question is: who out-prepped who? We have a couple more tricks up our sleeve that they probably haven't seen yet. First, pawn to h5 to let us plant our knight on g4 on the next move.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2pp1/2p2n2/2b4p/4P3/3P4/PPP1B: OMG. White castled their king DIRECTLY into our attack. We continue with our plan: knight to g4, PRAYING they take our knight and open up our rook.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2pp1/2p5/2b4p/4P1n1/3P3P/PPP1: What's a stafford gambit without a knight sacrifice? Queen to d6, disregarding the attack on our knight entirely. If they do take, we'll open up our rook and have checkmate on the h-file with our queen and rook in no-time.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2pq4/2b4p/4P1B1/3P3P/PPP: YES. They fell for the bait. Pawn takes bishop on g4, opening up our rook.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2pq4/2b1P3/6p1/3P3P/PPP2: DONT take that pawn. If we do, our queen will get pinned. Instead, slide the queen over to g6. The threat? Playing pawn takes h3 on the next move, and white can't capture back because their g2 pawn is pinned.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p3q1/2b1P3/3P2p1/7P/PPP: Ignore all distractions. Pawn takes h3 threatening checkmate on the next move.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p3q1/2b1P3/3P4/6Pp/PPP2: We're 2 squares away from queening. Let's make it 1. Pawn to h2, check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p3q1/2b1P3/3P4/6P1/PPP2: I see a diagonal; I take the diagonal. Queen to e4 check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p5/2b1P3/3Pq3/5PP1/PPP4: OK, both our queen and bishop are under attack by pawns. Let's solve both problems in 1 move with queen to d4.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p5/2b1P3/3Q4/5PP1/PPP4p: Bishop takes back on d4 of course.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p5/4P3/3b4/5PP1/PPP4p/R: If I were white's king, I would be so depressed.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/4n3/3PB3/PPP2PPP: White really thought they were smart defending their f2 square. Let's capture their e3 bishop with ours.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/4n3/3PP3/PPP3PP/RN: White's king is exposed, now we can play a Queen h4 check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/4n2q/3PP1P1/PPP4P/: Our knight is hungry. Let's eat the pawn on g3.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/7q/3PP1P1/PPP5/RN1: White can't catch a break. They took our knight and now will lose their rook. Queen to h1.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/4P3/5P2/PPPP2PP: White pushed their f-pawn, weakening their kingside. Let's continue our attack with knight to h5. Attacking the exposed king is a key theme of the Stafford Gambit.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2p5/7n/4P3/2N2P2/PPPP2P: White did not defend Queen h4 check, losing them all their advantage. Queen to h4 check.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2p5/7n/4P2q/2N2PP1/PPPP: That won't stop us. Knight takes g3.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/4P2q/2N2PP1/PPPP4: And we win the rook! Queen takes h1.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/4P1n1/2NP1Q2/PPP: We can still take the pawn with knight to f2, threatening the rook.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/4P3/2NP1Q2/PPP2n: Now we have a beautiful move: knight to d3 check, checking the king with our knight and discovering an attack on the rook with our bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/4P3/2NB1Q2/PPP3P: Now we take the rook. Bishop to g1.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/4n2q/3PP3/PPP1K1PP: Checkmate in 1. Can you find it? Hint: Queen to f2.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/4n3/3PP3/PPP1KqPP/: I actually feel bad for White here. They gave it their best shot.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2Bpp/2p5/2b5/4P2q/2N4P/PPPP1n: White is trying to be sneaky and sacrifice their bishop. If we take, we open our king up to Queen f3 check, losing us all our advantage. Instead, let's slide our king to safety to the f8 square.
descriptions.r1b2k1r/ppp2Bpp/2p5/2b4Q/4P2q/2N4P/PPPP1: Now we can play a vicious move - knight to e4, discovering a check on the white king and defending the checking bishop with the knight we just moved!
descriptions.r1b2k1r/ppp2Bpp/2p5/2b4Q/4n2q/2N4P/PPPP2: There's a royal fork - can you find it? Hint: Knight to g3.
descriptions.r1b2k1r/ppp2Bpp/2p5/2b4Q/7q/2N3nP/PPPP2P: Well done! We're winning their queen and checkmate is on the way.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/4P1n1/2NPB3/PPP2: You're getting the hang of it. Let's capture their bishop with knight e3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/2b5/4P3/2NPP3/PPP3PP: Now we can take our pawn back and create a powerful bishop with bishop to e3.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/4P3/2NPbQ2/PPP3PP/: We can defend our bishop here with queen g5.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/6q1/4P3/2NPbQ2/PPP3P: Well done! We earned back our pawn and have a dominant position. The computer puts us at a +1 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/2b5/4P3/3P3P/PPP2P: Black stopped us from hopping our knight in, so it looks like our attack is dead. But, we have one trick up our sleeve: a bishop sacrifice! Bishop takes pawn on f2.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/4P3/3P3P/PPP2KP1: What was the point of the bishop sacrifice? Well now we can do a KNIGHT SACRIFICE! Knight takes pawn on e4. White can't capture our knight because then we'll win the queen.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/4n3/3P3P/PPP3P1/RN: Looks like the king is safe, but we still have a check: queen to d4
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/3qn3/3P3P/PPP3PK/R: We might be able to force a draw by perpetual check, which is pretty good considering we're down a full piece. Queen checks king on e5.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/4q3/4n3/3P3P/PPP3P1/: Yup, looks like it's going to be a draw: queen checks king on d4
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2ppp/2p5/8/3qn3/3P3P/PPP3P1/R: We'll just keep checking white over and over and take the draw
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/2b5/3PP3/2N5/PPP2P: White forgot we have two attackers on the d4 square. Now we win our pawn back with bishop d4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2p2n2/8/3bP3/2N5/PPP2PPP: White gave a pawn back, making the position equal. We are now ready to continue the rest of the game.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/4P3/5N2/PPPP1P: White refused our gambit. The best move here is to take our pawn back with knight to e4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/4n3/5N2/PPPPQPPP: Let's defend our knight with queen to e7.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppppQppp/2n5/8/8/2n2N2/PPPP1PPP: Let's take back with bishop to e7.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppppbppp/2n5/8/8/2P2N2/PPP2PPP/R: The best move here is pawn to d6, preparing to develop our bishop.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp1bppp/2np4/8/8/2P2N2/PPP2PPP/: Well done! We are in an equal position and ready to play a middlegame.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2pp1/2p2n2/2b4p/4P3/2PP4/PP2B: Ugh, white is playing pretty well against us here. Whatever. We continue with our plan: knight to g4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2pp1/2p5/2b4p/3PP1n1/2P5/PP2B: We have one last trick here. Queen to h4, sacrificing our bishop but threatening to take that sweet, sweet, f2 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p5/2b4p/3PP1nq/2P3P1/PP: We continue annoying White. Queen to f6, one again looking right at f2.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p2q2/2b4p/3PP1n1/2P2PP1: White is playing really well, if I'm being honest. Almost as if they've taken a course on this... Whatever. One last trick. Pawn to h4, sacrificing our KNIGHT. Yes, both our knight and bishop are now hanging.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p2q2/2b5/3PP1Pp/2P3P1/P: We lost one piece, why not lose the other? Ignore our hanging bishop and march on. Pawn takes pawn on g3.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p2q2/2b5/3PP1P1/2P3p1/P: FINALLY, a mistake from white. After sacrificing a pawn at the start, then a knight, and then leaving a hanging bishop, now we sacrifice our QUEEN. Completely disregarding the attack on our queen, we play pawn takes h2.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2pp1/2p2R2/2b5/3PP1P1/2P5/PP2: You know the craziest part of this whole thing? We could play pawn to h1 and promote to a new queen for free - BUT THAT'S NOT EVEN THE WINNING MOVE. We first need to take the rook. Pawn takes rook on f6.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2p2/2p2p2/2b5/3PP1P1/2P5/PP2B: That was so much fun!! White cracked under the pressure and we're promoting our pawn to a new queen on the next move.
