descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Let's learn the Traxler Counterattack! It's a cold, evil, vicious response to the Fried Liver Attack. It's so poisonous, that I... well I don't even know what to say. I really just want to jump right in and show you. First up, pawn to e5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/5N2/PPPP1PPP: White attacked our pawn, knight to c6 defending it. Standard stuff.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/2B1P3/5N2/PPPP: We now invite the Fried Liver Attack with knight to f6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p1N1/2B1P3/8/PP: And yep, White's going for the Fried Liver Attackâa sneaky opening where they dive straight for our weak f7 pawn. White might even think they already have a winning position, with the knight coming to f7 on the next move forking our queen and rook. Here, we COMPLETELY IGNORE that threat and play bishop to c5, pretending that we've blundered.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1Npp/2n2n2/2b1p3/2B1P3/8/PPP: White fell for the bait. They think they've successfully forked our rook and queen, and believe they're winning the game. But here, we redirect lighting. Bishop takes f2 check.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1Npp/2n2n2/4p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1: We have sacrificed our bishop, and our queen/rook are forked. The good news: we have a necessary check on the exposed White king. Knight to e4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n3/4K3/PPPP2: White's king is brave, coming into the center. Queen to h4 to defend our knight.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/pppp2pp/2n5/4p3/2B1n2q/4K3/PPPP2: OMG what a BLUNDER. Mate in 4. Move 1: Queen to f4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1Npp/2n2n2/4p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1: White didn't take the bait, bringing us to the declined variation. Don't worry, we still have winning chances. Now, our queen is ACTUALLY under attack so we have to move it to the only safe square: queen to e7.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/ppppq1pp/2n2n2/4p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1: We need to open up our bishop: pawn to d5. This is a very common traxler idea.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/ppp1q1pp/2n2n2/3Bp3/4P3/8/PPPP1b: Blunder! We have the amazing bishop to g4, actually just trapping their queen. No, seriously, their queen has nowhere to go.
descriptions.r3k2N/ppp1q1pp/2n2n2/3Bp3/4P1b1/8/PPPP1K: Bishop takes queen on d1 of course.
descriptions.r3k2N/ppp1q1pp/2n2n2/3Bp3/4P3/8/PPPP1KPP: Game is as good as over.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n3/8/PPPP2PP: This is completely losing for White. Queen to h4 check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n2q/6P1/PPPP: A very common Traxler idea: Knight takes on g3.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B4q/6P1/PPPP4/: Now we get the rook with check. Yum. Queen to h1.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B5/6P1/PPPPK3/: Let's add a knight to this party! Knight to d4 check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2Bn4/3K2P1/PPPP4/: Can you find the best move? There's a free queen on d1 for our queen to take!
Look at white's queenside! It's the exact starting position, except the White queen has turned black.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/ppp1q1pp/2n2n2/3Pp3/2B5/8/PPPP1b: Our knight is under attack. Now we want to hop it into the center. Knight to d4.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/ppp1q1pp/5n2/3Pp3/2Bn4/2P5/PP1P1: This is white's most common move, and its actually VERY bad. All their advantage is lost. However, only one move wins for us: Bishop to g4 attacking the queen.
descriptions.r3k2N/ppp1q1pp/5n2/3Pp3/Q1Bn2b1/2P5/PP1P: One more time, we only have one move that wins: Knight back to d7 to block check.
descriptions.r3k2N/pppnq1pp/8/3Pp3/Q1BP2b1/8/PP1P1bPP: We're literally down 9 points of material, but let's keep going. Queen to f6, threatening a discovered check against white's king.
descriptions.r3k2N/pppn2pp/5q2/3PP3/Q1B3b1/8/PP1P1bPP: Do NOT capture back, as we lose the threat of discovered check. Instead, keep our queen on the f-file with Queen to f4.
descriptions.r3k2N/pppn2pp/8/3PP3/Q1B2qb1/8/PP1P1bPP/: Well done! We're down TEN points of material but our attack is so strong that Black wins 90% of the time here. I have never seen anything like it.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n3/8/PPPP2PP: Let's get more pieces to the party. Queen to h4, threatening checkmate on the next move. Just like that, we are escaping from the fork White has us in.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n2q/5Q2/PPPP: White put their queen out and now she's a big target. Rook to f8, pinning the knight to the queen.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n2q/5QP1/PPP: We have the beautiful (and common) Traxler idea of knight to g3. You see this move in a lot of lines
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B4q/5QP1/PPPP4: It looks like we don't have anything here but.. did you forget about White's bishop? Queen takes on c4. Even better, now the knight is not defended and its still pinned to the queen.
descriptions.r3k2N/pppn2pp/5q2/3Pp3/Q2P2b1/8/PP1PBbPP: White didn't address our discovered check, and now the game is over. Bishop takes on d4 discovering a check.
descriptions.r3k2N/pppn2pp/8/3Ppb2/Q2b4/8/PPKPq1PP/RN: It's hard to go wrong with this attack. The computer gives us a +10 advantage.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n2q/8/PPPPK1: Aaaaand checkmate is on the board. Queen to f2.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n3/3K4/PPPP1: Now knight drops back to c5 with check.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n2q/3P1Q2/PP: That move doesn't work. We infiltrate with queen to e1 check.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n3/3P4/PPP3P: Now we trade queens. This is uncommon for the traxler but it's important as it means the knight becomes pinned to the KING. We'll use that on the next move.
See our hanging knight? Let's drop him to d6. Now we have an attack on White's bishop and a DOUBLE attack on white's pinned knight. Woah.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pppp1Npp/2nn4/4p3/2B5/3P4/PPP1K1: Taking the knight or the bishop is winning here, but taking the bishop is better because it damages White's pawns and bishops are usually a bit better than knights. Knight takes  on c4.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2n5/3P4/PPP1K1P: Well done! We are completely winning here.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n2q/4KQ2/PPP: White's most common response loses on the spot. We actually retreat our knight here back to f6. We are disconnecting white's queen from looking at our vulnerable f7 square.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/pppp2pp/2n2n2/4p3/2B4q/4KQ2/PPPP: Forget about our rook, we have bigger fish to fry. Knight to d4, attacking the queen.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/pppp2pp/5n2/4p3/2Bn3q/4K1Q1/PPPP: I cannot believe that awful move was White's most common response. Knight to f5 forking the king and queen.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/8/6P1/PPPP4/RNB: Now the very slick kingside-castle. This protects our king and attacks the knight with our rook.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/8/6P1/PPPP4/RNB: Well done! We'll win the knight on the next move. The knight can't really move because of our checkmate threat on f1.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n2q/4K1P1/PP: This was White's only good response. Now a very common Traxler tactic: Knight takes on g3.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B4q/4K1P1/PPPP: Now whatever you do, DONT capture the bishop. Atleast not yet. First, we do an in-between move. Queen to d4 check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2Bq4/6P1/PPPPK3: This doesn't work for white, because now we have queen takes on c4 forking the king and the f7 knight.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1qpp/2n5/4p3/8/3P2P1/PPP1K3/: After all these shenanigans, we're actually up material and have a safer king. Well done.
descriptions.r3k2N/pppnq1pp/8/3Pp3/Q1Bn2b1/2P5/PP1P1K: The ONLY move here that wins for us is queen h4 check.
descriptions.r3k2N/pppn2pp/8/3Pp3/Q1Bn2bq/2P3P1/PP1P1: We don't have any knight to sacrifice on g3 this time, so let's drop back with Queen to f6 check.
descriptions.r3k2N/pppn2pp/5q2/3Pp3/Q1Bn2b1/2P3P1/PP1: White's king is completely trapped on the e1 square. He has no squares to move to. If we somehow give a check to him, its game over. So our plan? Put our knight on c2 with check. But FIRST, we need to defend the c2 square. So, here, you should play queen to f5 to allow knight to c2 in the future.
descriptions.r3k2N/pppn2pp/8/3Ppq2/Q1Bn2b1/2P3P1/PP1P: Great, now we have knight to c2 with check. White MUST sacrifice their queen, its their only move.
descriptions.r3k2N/pppn2pp/8/3Pp3/2B3b1/2P3P1/PPqP3P/: Well done! White's knight is stuck in the corner, most of the other pieces aren't developed, and the king is unsafe. the computer gives us a HUGE advantage here, and black almost always wins from this position.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n3/8/PPPP2PP: This is a bad response from white, and we will likely win this game. Queen to h4, threatening checkmate.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n2q/5Q2/PPPP: White brought their queen out, and she is vulnerable. Knight to d4 attacking her and the pawn on c2.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2Bnn2q/4Q3/PPPP2P: We play the very nice knight to c2 here, forking the rook and queen.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2B1n2q/5Q2/PPnP2P: So... that was white's most common move... and it just gave us checkmate in 1. WHAT??? Queen to e1 checkmate.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2B1n3/5Q2/PPnP2PP: I don't even know what else to say except White played awful.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2Bnn2q/5QP1/PPPP3: White counter-attacks our queen. But it doesn't matter. Queen slides in to h3 with check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2Bnn3/6Pq/PPPP2QP: Here we DON'T trade queens. Instead, we should drop our queen back to f5 with check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4pq2/2Bnn3/6P1/PPPP2Q: Now we win White's queen with a dance of our knight. Knight to f3 check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4pq2/2B1n3/5nP1/PPPP2: Now the discovered check Knight to h4.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4pq2/2B1n2n/6P1/PPPP2: Finally, Knight to g2, winning the queen.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n2q/6P1/PPPP: White is playing well here. The only pay to progress is to sacrifice another piece. Knight takes on g3, opening up the king even more
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B5/6q1/PPPP4/R: Let's get our rook out of the fork too now, and even pin the knight to the king with it. Rook to f8.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B5/3P2q1/PPP5/: We need our light square bishop to join the party. Unfortunately, he's currently blocked in. Pawn to d5 to gain a tempo and open our bishop up
descriptions.r3kr2/ppp2Npp/2n5/3Bp3/8/3P2qR/PPP5/RNBQ: White sacrificed some material to stay in the game. Queen takes h3 of course. With check.
descriptions.r3kr2/ppp2Npp/2n5/3Bp3/8/3P3q/PPP5/RNBQK: We need to get our last pieces into the party. Knight to d4, patrolling the c2 square. If White's queen ever leaves, we get a nasty fork with knight to c2.
descriptions.r3kr2/ppp2Npp/8/3Bp3/3n4/3P3q/PPP5/RNBQK: Look at White's home row - half their pieces haven't even moved! We're down a bit of material but we have a suffocating position. Black wins from here 85% of the time.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2B1n2q/8/PPnPQ1PP: White really thinks there's a chance they might come back from this. There's not. Knight to g3 check. This forks the king and queen, and when they capture our knight with the pawn, we win the rook with check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2B4q/6P1/PPnPQ1P1: Queen to h1, winning the rook with check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2B5/6P1/PPnPQKP1/: And now the very cool: kingside castle. Our king is safe and the White knight is pinned.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2B5/6P1/PPnPQKP1/: We have a deadly pin on white's knight and - I hope you didn't forget - White's rook is still trapped in the corner, ready to be taken by our knight whenever we want.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p2Q/2B5/6q1/PPPP4/: White added a defender on the f7 knight - let's block a defender with pawn to d5. Now the bishop is no longer protecting the knight. Also keep in mind that the knight cannot escape because it is pinned.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/ppp2Npp/2n5/3Bp2Q/8/6q1/PPPP4/RN: Oh shoot... looks like white could just take the pawn and defend the knight again... NOT. We are winning here, and you'll see why in a second. Knight to b4, attacking the bishop and threatening knight to c2 to take the rook.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/ppp2Npp/8/4p2Q/1n6/1B4q1/PPPP4/R: Shoot... White defended that c2 square. It seems all our plans get shut down... NOT. The bishop is overloaded right now, defending both the c2 square and the f7 knight. Sacrifice our knight to c2 now.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/ppp2Npp/8/4p2Q/8/6q1/PPBP4/RNB2K: Now we have a ton of winning moves here. The easiest one is simply rook takes f7 with check.
descriptions.r1b1k3/ppp2rpp/8/4p2Q/8/6q1/PPBPK3/RNB4R: It is so, so, over. Bishop to g4 check & fork the queen.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B1n3/8/PPPPK1P: Now we swarm our pieces around White's vulnerable king. Knight to d4 with check.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2Bnn3/4K3/PPPP2PP: Next up to the party is our queen: Queen to h4.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2Bnn2q/4K1P1/PPPP: Very common Traxler idea: Knight takes on g3.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2Bn3q/4K1P1/PPPP4: OK in positions like these we usually want to take the rook or the bishop. However, the rook is defended and the bishop is not in our queen's line of sight. So, this time, lets take the pawn on g3 with check.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/8/4p3/2BnK3/6q1/PPPP4/R: It's actually forced checkmate in 13. Can you see it? If so - hi Magnus Carlsen! For the rest of us, the next move is Pawn to d5 to open our bishop.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2Npp/8/3Bp3/3nK3/6q1/PPPP4/RN: Mate in 1! Can you find it? Bishop to F5.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/pppp1Bpp/5n2/4p3/3n3q/4KQ2/PPPP2: That's a meaningless check. King to e7.
descriptions.r1b4N/ppppkBpp/5n2/4p3/3n3q/4KQP1/PPPP3P: White is trying to counter-attack our queen, but we have a resource: queen to g5 check. Once white moves, we get to take their queen.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppp2Npp/8/3Kp3/2Bn4/6q1/PPPP4/RN: Next up, we check with bishop to e6.
descriptions.r3k2r/ppp2Npp/4b3/2K1p3/2Bn4/6q1/PPPP4/R: Now pawn to b6 - another check.
descriptions.r3k2r/p1p2Npp/1p2b3/2K1p3/2Bn4/6q1/PPPP4: Well done!  I won't bore you with the details on this checkmate. All you need to know is you're completely winning from here!
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2B5/6q1/PPPPQ3/: We need to open up our bishop. Pawn to d5.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/ppp2Npp/2n5/3Bp3/8/6q1/PPPPQ3/RN: Actually, new plan. We can fork the d5 bishop and the c2 pawn with knight to b4.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/ppp2Npp/8/1Q1Bp3/1n6/6q1/PPPP4/R: This was White's most common move, and it completely loses them the game. Pawn to c6, forking the bishop and queen.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pp3Npp/2p5/3Bp3/1Q6/6q1/PPPP4/RN: We take the bishop with pawn to d5. Now the pinned knight has no defenders.
descriptions.r1b1kr2/pp3Npp/8/3pp3/7Q/6q1/PPPP4/RNB2K: Finally, we win the knight. Rook to f7 with check....
descriptions.r1b1k3/pp3rpp/8/3pp3/7Q/6q1/PPPP4/RNB2K1: Oh, and there's checkmate in 6 on the board. GG.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2Bq4/5KP1/PPPP4: STILL don't take the bishop. Now that white's king is on the f-file,  we have a very nice move: castling kingside.  This pins the knight to the king on that f-file.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1Npp/2n5/4p3/2Bq3R/5KP1/PPPP: Ugh, that rook is annoying. It's attacking our queen and our queen can no longer take the bishop we've been eyeing. The ONLY move that we do not lose on the spot is pawn to e4.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1Npp/2n5/8/2BqR3/5KP1/PPPP4/: Once again, the ONLY winning move is knight to e5, forking the king, bishop and knight.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1Npp/8/4R3/2Bq4/5KP1/PPPP4/R: You may be tempted to take the rook here, but actually it's better to take the bishop on c4 as its the only defender of the pinned f7 knight. That bishop has been the bane of our existence, I'll be glad to see it go. Queen to c4.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1Npp/8/4R3/2q5/5KP1/PPPP4/RN: I love how White's queenside just... hasn't moved. Anyways, we will be winning the knight and likely the game here.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1Npp/2n5/8/2Bqp2R/6P1/PPPP2K: OK White ran their king. NOW we can take the bishop. Queen takes on c4.
descriptions.r1b2rk1/pppp1Npp/2n5/8/2q1p2R/6P1/PPPP2K: Well done! Honestly, White played that perfectly and the position is about equal.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1Bpp/2n2n2/2b1p1N1/4P3/8/PPP: This is the best line against the Traxler. We don't have much here except king to e7.
descriptions.r1b1k2N/ppp1q1pp/3P1n2/4p3/2Bn4/8/PPPP1b: White attacks our queen. Let's take with our queen with queen to d6.
descriptions.r1b1k3/ppp2Npp/3q1n2/4p3/2Bn4/8/PPPP1bPP: White thinks attacking our queen with their knight was a good move, but it's actually a mistake. Now we have queen to c5, attacking the White bishop.
descriptions.r1b1k3/ppp2Npp/5n2/2q1p3/2Bn4/3P4/PPP2bP: We need to bring more pieces to the party. Because we're down so much material, we can't afford to let our attack die out. Bishop to g4.
descriptions.r3k3/ppp2Npp/5n2/2q1p3/2Bn2b1/3P4/PPPQ1b: With White's queen attacking our bishop, we need to retreat. Bishop to h4.
descriptions.r3k3/ppp2Npp/5n2/2q1p3/2Bn2bb/3P4/PPPQ2P: Honestly this was just really good play by White. We're down material but the engine thinks we have some winning chances here. because white is so underdeveloped and all our pieces are surrounding the king. Good luck with the game!

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn one of the most crushing openings for White: The Vienna. Start by pushing the king's pawn forward two squares to e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Now develop the queen's knight to c3, which begins the Vienna Game.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/4p3/4P3/2N5/PPPP1P: The Vienna Gambit is played after Black plays knight f6. Let's gambit our f pawn by pushing it 2 squares forward.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/4Pp2/2N5/PPPP2PP: Black has taken our pawn - a huge mistake we will now exploit. Pushing our e pawn forward forces their knight back to its home square. If it goes anywhere else, it can be taken.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4P2n/5p2/2N5/PPPP2PP: Black made a huge blunder! What's the best move here? Hint: We can take the knight with the queen.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/4P2Q/5p2/2N5/PPPP2PP: Well done capitalizing on Black's blunder! You'll be surprised how often Black's reluctance to retreat the knight ends up losing them the piece altogether.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppppqppp/5n2/4P3/5p2/2N5/PPPP2P: Black tried to be clever by pinning our e5 pawn against our king so we can't use it to take the knight. But this is losing for Black! Let's block the pin by moving our queen to e2.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppppqppp/8/4P3/5p2/2N5/PPPPQ1PP: Before we do anything else, we need to housekeep and take care of Black's threat of queen h4 check. Let's develop our knight to protect that square.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp1qppp/3p4/4P3/5p2/2N2N2/PPPP: By trying to fight back in the center, Black has allowed us to commit a vicious attack. I almost feel bad playing it, but it must be done. Let's attack their queen with knight to d5.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/3pq3/3NP3/5p2/5N2/PPPPQ: Can you spot the royal fork? Hint: it's knight to c7.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppN2ppp/3pq3/4P3/5p2/5N2/PPPPQ1: Well that was fun! Enjoy the free ELO.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/pppq1ppp/3p4/3NP3/5p2/5N2/PPPPQ: There's two great options here. We could play pawn takes d6 which opens a discovered check to the black king. But even more fun is sacrificing our knight onto c7. Let's try it out!
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/ppq2ppp/3p4/4P3/5p2/5N2/PPPPQ1P: Black has accepted our sacrifice and lost the game. We can play pawn takes d6 now which discovers a check and wins the queen.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/pp2qppp/3P4/8/5p2/5N2/PPPPQ1PP/: Finally, we take the queen with our pawn.
descriptions.rnb1kbnr/pp2Pppp/8/8/5p2/5N2/PPPPQ1PP/R1: Wow. You actually need to be evil to play like this... well done.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/4PP2/2N5/PPP: If Black plays knight c6, Black is essentially losing already! Let's take their pawn with fxe5.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/4n3/4P3/2N5/PPPP2P: Now we storm with our pawns to take the center and force their knights back! First, let's push the d pawn forward to d4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5nn1/8/3PP3/2N5/PPP3PP: Now we attack their other knight with our e pawn, once again forcing it back to its home square! Pawn to e5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/6n1/4P3/3P4/2N5/PPP3PP: Now is a good time to develop our king's knight to f3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/6n1/4P3/3P4/2N2N2/PPP3: Well done! We have a huge lead in development and have crippled the Black position. Even though the material is equal, chess engines think this position is so good for White that it's equivalent to being up 1 or 2 pawns!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4P3/5p2/2N5/PPPP2PP/: Black is threatening to move their queen to h4 with check. This would be devastating, so let's develop our king's knight to f3 so it can guard the h4 square.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/5p2/2N2N2/PPPP: Let's push our pawn to d4 to take the center and prepare our bishop to recapture Black's f4 pawn.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/4P3/3P1p2/2N2N2/PP: Now we can recapture our gambited pawn with our bishop, developing it to f4. We regain material while improving our position.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4p3/3P1B2/2N2N2/PPP: We have 3 ways to recapture the e5 pawn, but capturing with our knight is the best. If we capture with our d4 pawn, it opens up a queen trade which helps black. If we take with the bishop, Black can take it for a knight, which also helps black.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4n3/3P1B2/2N5/PPP3PP/: The best way to capture the e5 knight is with our bishop. If we capture with our d4 pawn, it opens up a queen trade which helps black.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4B3/3P4/2N5/PPP3PP/R2: Well done! You have a huge lead in development and have recaptured all your material.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/4P3/5p2/2N2N2/PPPP2: Black has fought back against our center. Let's reinforce it by pushing our pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/4p3/3P1p2/2N2N2/PPP3P: Instead of just capturing back on e5, we can be even more devious by moving our queen to e2, pinning Black's pawn against its own king.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4p3/3P1p2/2N2N2/PPP: Black defended the e5 pawn but did not address the pin on it, which means the f4 pawn is undefended. Let's take the f4 pawn with our bishop.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/4p3/3P1B2/2N2N2/PPP: Well done! Our pin is so strong against Black's king that despite being down a pawn, the computer puts our position at a +1 point advantage.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppppqppp/2n5/4P3/5p2/2N2N2/PPPP: Let's push our pawn to d4 to take the center and prepare our bishop to recapture Black's f4 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppp1qppp/2np4/4P3/3P1p2/2N2N2/P: Black playing d6 in positions like this is a huge blunder. It gives us the ability to discover check once the queen moves. So, let's attack the black queen with our knight. Knight to d5.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/3NP3/3P1p2/5N2/PPP: Now that we have discovered check up our sleeve, we can sacrifice our knight on c7.
descriptions.r1b1kbnr/ppq2ppp/2np4/4P3/3P1p2/5N2/PPP1: Black has accepted our sacrifice and lost the game. We can play pawn takes d6 now which discovers a check and wins the queen.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppq1bppp/2nP4/8/3P1p2/5N2/PPP1Q: Let's take the queen with the pawn.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppP1bppp/2n5/8/3P1p2/5N2/PPP1Q1: What a deadly, deadly trick. Well done!
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1p1p/8/4P1p1/5p2/2N2N2/PPPP: If Black lets us take the center, let's take the center! Pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1p1p/8/4P3/3P1pp1/2N2N2/PPP: Black is trying to move our knight - but remember the knight is doing an important job of keeping the Black queen away! So we can't move him. Instead let's sacrifice our knight by playing bishop to f4. The idea here is to develop a ton of pieces while Black hasn't developed any. We'll use those pieces to launch a very strong attack.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1p1p/8/4P3/3P1B2/2N2p2/PPP3: We lost our knight but remember - the goal is development! Queen to f3.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/ppp2p1p/3p4/4P3/3P1B2/2N2Q2/PPP: Black has not developed a single piece yet. It's honestly kind of sad. Now we will win the game. The goal is to castle and get our queen and rook on the same file to target the weak f7 pawn. Step 1: Bishop to b5 check.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3p1p/2pp4/1B2P3/3P1B2/2N2Q2/P: Now we castle king-side, getting our rook and queen on the same file to target that weak f7 pawn.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3p1p/3p4/1p2P3/3P1B2/2N2Q2/PP: Black is so crazy for STILL not developing. Yes, we lost 2 pieces, but the game is ours. Bishop to g5, threatening the queen and checkmate.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pp3p1p/3p4/1p2P1B1/3P4/2N2Q2/PP: Well done! We lost 2 pieces but our development is just too much for black to handle. We'll bring our rook and knight to the party next and the game is ours.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp2ppp/8/4p3/1b1P1p2/2N2N2/PPP: Let's take the pawn with check with queen e5.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp1qppp/8/4Q3/1b1P1p2/2N2N2/PP: Remember the pawn we gambited at the start? Let's finally win back our gambited pawn while developing a piece with bishop f4.
descriptions.rnb1k1nr/ppp1qppp/8/4Q3/1b1P1B2/2N2N2/PP: Well done! We have a huge lead in development, we have recaptured our pawns, and we are ready to castle queenside.
descriptions.rnbqk1nr/ppp1bppp/8/4p3/3P1p2/2N2N2/PPP1: Black developed a piece and undid the pin. Here we should play queen takes on e5, so that we can repin the bishop to the king.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/ppp1bppp/2n5/4Q3/3P1p2/2N2N2/PP: Black is trying to make us move our queen, but let's not let them. We can pin their knight to their king with bishop to b5.
descriptions.r2qk1nr/pppbbppp/2n5/1B2Q3/3P1p2/2N2N2/P: Black undid the pin, so our queen is in danger again. Let's just take the knight so our queen is once again safe. Bishop takes c6.
descriptions.r2qk1nr/ppp1bppp/2b5/4Q3/3P1p2/2N2N2/PPP: Now we have the very powerful response pawn to d5, hitting the bishop and forcing it to drop back.
descriptions.r2qk1nr/pppbbppp/8/3PQ3/5p2/2N2N2/PPP3PP: Now we can develop a piece, win a pawn back, and set up an attack on the c7 pawn with bishop to f4.
descriptions.r2qk1nr/pppbbppp/8/3PQ3/5B2/2N2N2/PPP3PP: Well done! Our queen is forking the c7 and g7 pawns. Black is in trouble here and the game is likely ours.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/4p3/4PP2/2N5/PPPP: If Black wants to deny the gambit, they must do it with the d-pawn. In this case, it's quite straightforward. Let's develop our king's knight to f3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/8/4Pp2/2N2N2/PPPP: Taking our pawn is a mistake for Black! If we push our pawn to d4, we can take the center and open up our bishop to recapture the pawn.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/8/3PPp2/2N2N2/PPP: Well done! We own the center and are about to win back our material!
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/4p3/4PP2/2N2N2/P: The best move here is to develop our bishop to b5, pinning the knight to the king.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/1B2p3/4PP2/2N2N2: Well done! We are ready to castle and continue our game.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3pp3/4PP2/2N5/PPPP2: By pushing the pawn up, the opponent has brought us to the Vienna main line. This means they know what they're doing. Here, we should win a pawn and attack their knight at the same time with fxe5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pP3/4n3/2N5/PPPP2PP/: We have many options here, like developing our knight or attacking their knight with a pawn. The most forcing and dangerous line is attacking their knight with our queen. Queen to f3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pP3/8/2n2Q2/PPPP2PP/: The best way to recapture the knight is with our b2 pawn. This will allow us to push our d pawn to d4 soon, giving us a very strong center.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bppp/8/3pP3/8/2P2Q2/P1PP2PP/: By playing slow, Black has allowed us to take the center with our d pawn. Pawn to d4.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/8/3pP3/3P4/2P2Q2/P1P3P: The best way to continue our development is to move bishop to d3. If we develop our knight first, it will block in our bishop.
descriptions.rn1q1rk1/ppp1bppp/4b3/3pP3/3P4/2PB1Q2/P1: Let's continue developing with the goal to castle kingside. Knight to e2.
Well done! We have a lead in development, are ready to castle, and have prepared a strong attack on our opponent's king!
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bppp/5n2/4Q3/3P1p2/2N2N2/PPP: Let's develop another piece, capture a pawn, and put pressure on the c7 square with bishop to f4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp1bppp/5n2/4Q3/3P1B2/2N2N2/PPP: Well done! We have a nice position here because our pieces are developed and active, and Black's pieces are kind of just... not doing anything.

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Well, well, well. So you took the Vienna Gambit course, and now you want to find out how to BEAT the Vienna Gambit? You came to the right place. Let's begin: pawn to e5.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/2N5/PPPP1PPP: White goes for the Vienna. I hope you're not shocked when I say we'll play into it with knight to f6.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/4p3/4PP2/2N5/PPPP2: Aaaaand there's the gambit. Here, a lot of people take the pawn on f4 - and those people have no idea what they're doing. Taking the pawn just invites a huge attack from white, so instead we'll play pawn to d5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3Pp3/5P2/2N5/PPPP2P: Huh, this is NOT the mainline of the vienna gambit. Something tells me our opponent doesn't know what they're doing... Knight takes pawn on d5.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3nP3/8/2N5/PPPP2PP/R1: Another trap here: Knight takes knight on c3.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/8/2P5/P1PP2PP/R1B: With the knight gone, now we can play our favorite move: Queen to h4 check.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/7q/2P3P1/P1PP3P/R: Thanks for the free rook, kiddo. Queen to e4 check, forking the king and rook.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/4q3/2P3P1/P1PPQ2P: Give. Me. That. Rook. Queen to h1.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/8/2P3P1/P1PPQ2P/R: Something tells me we're winning this game.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3pP3/4P3/2N5/PPPP2P: We continue down the Vienna gambit mainline. We lost a pawn and our knight is under attack, so knight takes e4.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pP3/4n3/2N2Q2/PPPP2P: White has 2 attackers on our knight. We only have 1 defender. So we should either trade knights or defend the knight right? WRONG. Here, let's play a counter-trick by developing our other knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/3pP3/4N3/5Q2/PPPP2P: Aaaaand white fell for our trap. Now whatever you do, DON'T take back. Instead, let's fork the queen and the c2 pawn with knight to d4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pP3/3nN3/3Q4/PPPP2PP: White just lost the game. How? You'll see why in a second. First, let's take the knight with pawn to e4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/3nQ3/8/PPPP2PP/R1: Now we have the killer move bishop to f5, skewering the queen against that weak c2 pawn. The queen has to move, and she can no longer defend that c2 pawn, which means our knight will be able to hop in and fork the king and rook.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pQp2ppp/8/4Pb2/3n4/8/PPPP2PP/R1B: Before we fork c2, let's toss in 1 last move so our rook can be active: rook to b8. This also guards the b5 square so White doesn't get any bishop-to-b5-check ideas once we move our knight.
descriptions.1r1qkb1r/Q1p2ppp/8/4Pb2/3n4/8/PPPP2PP/R1: OK, now we strike. Knight to c2, forking the king and rook.
descriptions.1r1qkb1r/Q1p2ppp/8/4Pb2/8/8/PPnP2PP/R1BK: And now we claim our reward. Knight takes rook on a1, yummmm
descriptions.1r1qkb1r/Q1p2ppp/8/4Pb2/8/8/PP1P2PP/n1BK: That'll teach white a lesson to never play the Vienna gambit against us.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B1pP3/4n3/2N2Q2/PP: We baited white into taking our knight, but they didn't fall for it this time. So, should we now add a defender to the e4 knight? Or what about the c6 knight? The answer is NO and NO. We once again ignore all of that and lay another trap: bishop to e6.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/1B1pP3/4N3/5Q2/PPP: Let's take back, pawn to e4.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/1B2P3/4Q3/8/PPPP2P: Oh no! It looks like we're a pawn down!! And there's a ton of pressure on our knight!!! One move here can give us the edge: bishop to d5, skewering the queen against the g2 square. All of a sudden, white is on their back foot.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B1bP3/8/8/PPPPQ1PP/: Onwards! Queen h4 check. White is NOT happy about being a pawn up anymore.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B1bP3/7q/6P1/PPPPQ2P: Aaaaand the game is over. Queen to e4, and our battery against white's rook is unstoppable.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B1bP3/4q3/5NP1/PPPPQ: Oh! A free knight! Let's take. Queen to f3.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B1bP3/8/5QP1/PPPP3P/: Bishop takes queen back on f3, of course.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B2P3/8/5bP1/PPPP3P/R: I don't really know what to say here
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/2B1p3/8/PPPP2PP/R: I'm not really sure what white's trying to do here, but Knight to c6 to attack the e5 square.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P2Q/2B1p3/8/PPPP2P: Oh... That was white's plan? Well, they just lost the game. Pawn to g6 first, to stop checkmate.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2p1p/2n3p1/4P3/2B1p3/8/PPPPQ: Now knight to d4, forking both the queen and the c2 pawn. This baits white into taking our e4 pawn - which is all part of the plan.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2p1p/6p1/4P3/2BnQ3/8/PPPP2PP: This move should be familiar: bishop to f5, skewering the queen to the c2 pawn.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/pQp2p1p/6p1/4Pb2/2Bn4/8/PPPP2PP/: Before taking on c2 with our knight, let's gain a tempo with rook to b8.
descriptions.1r1qkb1r/Q1p2p1p/6p1/4Pb2/2Bn4/8/PPPP2PP: Now we strike. Knight to c2 forking the king and rook.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/4p3/8/PPPPQ1PP/R1: We need to defend our pawn, and the best way to do it is with bishop to f5.
descriptions.rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4Pb2/4p1P1/8/PPPPQ2P/: HUGE mistake for white to move their g-pawn. Now we get our FAVORITE move: Queen to h4 check.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4Pb2/4p1Pq/8/PPPPQ2P/R: OMG ð­ð­ White just hung their queen for no reason! They literally had two movesâone loses the queen, one doesn'tâand somehow they pick wrong like HALF THE TIME. I can't even... Bishop takes pawn on g4, skewering the queen against her own king.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/4p1bq/5N2/PPPPQ2P/: NOW THEY LOST THEIR KNIGHT AS WELL. THIS WAS THEIR MOST COMMON MOVE. I'm actually so done with this game. Bishop takes knight on f3.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/7q/5p2/PPPP3P/R1BK: IDK why I got so emotional there...
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pP3/3nN3/8/PPPP2PP/R: Now this is a mistake from black. By retreating, they gave us the entire center. Pawn takes e4.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/3np3/2P5/PP1P2PP/: OK time to leave. Knight back to c6, attacking white's weak e5 pawn.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B2P3/4p3/2P5/PP1P2: White pinned our knight so now we technically aren't attacking the e5 pawn anymore. The best move here? Queen to d5, forking that annoying bishop and that tasty pawn.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B1qP3/4p3/2P5/PP1P: Well done! We have a lead in development, own the center, the computer gives us a +2 point advantage, and we win over 70% of these games. Happy?
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pP3/4n3/2N2N2/PPPP2P: White is playing solid. Let's continue developing with bishop to c5, threatening to put our knight on the f2 square.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/8/2bpP3/3Pn3/2N2N2/PPP3P: This was pretty much White's only move. Now our bishop is under attack. Let's move it to b4, pinning the knight.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/8/3pP3/1b1Pn3/2N2N2/PPPB: White's central pawns are too strong; we need to strike back in the center. Pawn to c5.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3ppp/8/2ppP3/1b1PN3/5N2/PPPB2P: Pawn takes knight on e4. We can't take the bishop because then the e4 knight drops back to recapture, making us a full piece down.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3ppp/8/2p1P3/1B1Pp3/5N2/PPP3PP: NOW we can take the bishop. Pawn takes bishop on b4.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3ppp/8/4P3/1p1Pp3/8/PPP3PP/R2Q: Crazy. 9 moves in and every piece on the board is still on their home square. Let's castle.
descriptions.rnbq1rk1/pp3ppp/8/4P3/1p1Pp3/8/PPP3PP/R2: Well done! Our king is safe while White's king is still in the middle of the board. Even though material is equal, the computer gives us a +1 advantage and black wins over 60% of the games from here.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/1B1bP3/6Q1/8/PPPP2PP: We really need the queen on e2 - not g4 - for our plan. So, let's boot the queen. Pawn to h5.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2pp1/2n5/1B1bP2p/8/6Q1/PPPP2P: White is stubborn. Whatever. We'll have to try and set up the bishop/queen battery the slow way. First step: queen to d7.
descriptions.r3kb1r/pppq1pp1/2n5/1B1bP2p/8/5NQ1/PPPP2: Step 2: kick out the bishop. Pawn to a6.
descriptions.r3kb1r/1pp2pp1/p1q5/3bP2p/8/5NQ1/PPPP2PP: Beautiful! We have a battery looking straight at White's kingside, and our queen is also looking directly at the undefended c2 pawn. Our position is awesome.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/3Pp3/8/PPP3PP/R1B: Here, we can play a move called "En Passant" - which translates to english as "Pawn Cheats". Our e4 pawn can en passant to e3, capturing the d4 pawn. Just click the pawn and then the circle on the right, you'll see what I mean.
descriptions.rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/8/3B4/PPP3PP/R1BQ: Now for everyone's favorite move: Queen to h4 check.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/7q/3B2P1/PPP4P/R1: Now that we weakened white's pawn structure, let's drop our queen back to e7, attacking the e5 pawn.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp1qppp/8/4P3/8/3B1NP1/PPP4P/R: White adds a defender? We add an attacker. Knight to c6.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp1qppp/2n5/4P3/8/3B1NP1/PPP4P: Well done! White will have a tough time defending the e5 pawn, and their king who is very-much vulnerable right now. Because of this, we win like 60+% of the games from here.
descriptions.r2qkb1r/ppp2pp1/2n5/1B1bP2p/8/8/PPPPQ1PP: Great, we know the plan from here. Queen to h4 check.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2pp1/2n5/1B1bP2p/7q/8/PPPPQ1PP: Well done! This transposes to the other line we've already seen.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3pP3/3nN3/2Q5/PPPP2PP: Our knight is under attack, lets win back a knight and defend our own with pawn takes e4. Now our queen defends our knight.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/3np3/2Q5/PPPPN1PP: Look, I hate retreating as much as you do, but in this position its best to go back and regroup. Knight to c6.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/4p3/2Q3N1/PPPP2: White is attacking our pawn. The best way to defend is is with our queen, surprisingly. Queen to d5. This also attack's white's e5 pawn.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/3qP3/2B1p3/2Q3N1/PP: That's totally fine, it was always our plan to take White's e5 pawn. Queen to e5.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4q3/2B1p3/2Q3N1/PPP: Well done! We're up a pawn and Black wins like 70% of their games from here.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/7q/2P5/P1PPK1PP/R: Wow, white did NOT want us to get that rook. But now their king looks silly being the only developed piece. Bishop to g4 check.
descriptions.rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4P3/6bq/2P2N2/P1PPK1PP: It's kind of weird, but the only move that keeps our advantage is developing our knight to c6, hitting the e5 pawn.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/3P2bq/2P2N2/P1P1K: That was NOT a good response from white. Sure, the d4 pawn defends the e5 pawn, but now we have the beautiful king castles queenside. This pins the d4 pawn to the queen, meaning e5 is once again undefended.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P3/3P2bq/2P2N2/P1P1: We should 100% NOT trade queens here. Our queen is just so powerful in the center of the board. Let's drop her back to h5, adding even more pressure to the pinned knight.
descriptions.2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4P2q/3P2b1/2P2N2/P1P: I love how white's king is in front of his queen. And they say chivalry is dead.
descriptions.rnbqk2r/pp3ppp/8/1BppP3/1b1Pn3/2N2N2/PPP: We're in check. Knight to c6 to block.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp3ppp/2n5/1BppP3/1b1Pn3/2N2N2/: Well done! It's a tense position, but we win over 60% of our games from here.
descriptions.rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3qP3/8/8/PPPP2PP/R1BQ: Patience. Instead of capturing back immediately, let's spend our time developing a piece. Knight to c6.
descriptions.r1b1kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/3qP3/8/5N2/PPPP2PP/: Again, we technically could capture that pawn whenever we wanted, but there's no rush quite yet. We should keep developing. Bishop to g4.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/3qP3/6b1/5N2/PPPPB1PP: OK, NOW we can take. Knight takes pawn on e4.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3qN3/6b1/8/PPPPB1PP/R1B: The only winning move here is queen takes knight on e5. It looks like it hangs a bishop, but we are actually pinning the e2 bishop to the white king. In fact, with our queen and bishop both hitting white's e2 bishop, we're stopping white from castling. If white castled, we'd have 2 attackers on the b2 bishop and only the White queen defending.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/8/4q3/3P2b1/8/PPP1B1PP/R1: It's crucial we keep the pin on the bishop, completely paralyzing white's whole position. Queen drops down to e7.
descriptions.r3kb1r/ppp1qppp/8/8/3P2b1/8/PPP1B1PP/R1B: Well done! I'm not kidding you when I say black has won 90% of games from here, just because white literally can't move any pieces. They are completely stuck. In the future we'll long castle and life is good.

shortDescriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB: Let's play into the vienna game.
shortDescriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/2N5/PPPP1PPP: Let's play into the vienna gambit

descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK: Let's learn the Vienna Game! If you loved the Vienna Gambit, and want to know what happens if the opponent doesn't play that knight move - this is the course for you. Let's start the same way: pawn to e4.
descriptions.rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R: Then to play the Vienna Game, we bring our knight out to c3.
descriptions.r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/4P3/2N5/PPPP1P: And here is where the game differs from the Vienna Gambit! Going pawn f4 here is no longer a good move because there is no knight to kick away, so what do we do in this situation? Let's play bishop to c4 here.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b1p3/2B1P3/2N5/PP: This is called the Copycat Variation, because so far our opponent has just copied all our moves. Let's put an end to the copying with queen to g4. This is a deadly move and you will win a LOT of games here.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n2q2/2b1p3/2B1P1Q1/2N: Black has a double attack on our weak f2 pawn. If we don't defend it, we lose on the spot. That's why we play... knight to d5. Yes that's right we completely ignore the attack and just play knight to d5. Trust me and do it.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2bNp3/2B1P1Q1/8/PP: Black thought it was checkmate, but they missed that our bishop is protecting that square. Bishop to f1 only move.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2bNp3/4P1Q1/8/PPPP: Black won't often hang their queen, but I included this because, as White, it's crucial to remember that other lines from this position only work because we have a bishop defending that square. That said, over 10,000 games have reached this position, sooo...
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2ppp/2np4/2bNp3/2B1P1Q1/8/PP: We are completely completely winning here. Black is attacking our queen but now we have queen to g7.
descriptions.r3k1nr/ppp2pQp/2npb3/2bNp3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1: Now instead of taking the rook, we should actually play knight takes c7, forking the king and the OTHER rook.
descriptions.r5nr/ppNk1pQp/2npb3/2b1p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1q: Now instead of taking the other rook, we instead take the bishop! Knight takes bishop on e6. Black cannot capture back because their pawn is pinned.
descriptions.r6r/pp1knpQp/2npN3/2b1p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1qP: Now is a good time to attack the black queen and give her the boot. Knight to h3.
descriptions.r6r/pp1knpQp/2npN3/2b1p3/2B1P3/7N/PPPP1q: It's so so over for Black here. Well done.
descriptions.r1bqk1nr/pppp1p1p/2n3p1/2b1p3/2B1P1Q1/2N: Black is only thinking one move ahead. Yes, they saved their g pawn, but now we put our queen on f3 and put a ton of pressure on their f pawn.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1p1p/2n2qp1/2b1p3/2B1P3/2N2: If Black offers a queen trade, we should play knight to d5, threatening the queen and a fork on c7.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1p1p/2n3p1/2bNp3/2B1P3/5q2/: Let's recapture with knight to f3.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/pppp1p1p/1bn3p1/3Np3/2B1P3/5N2/: Black defended the fork we were threatening. Here, the best move is pawn to d3, surprisingly.
descriptions.r1b1k2r/ppppnp1p/1bn3p1/3Np3/2B1P3/3P1N2: A blunder! Now we have knight to f6 checking the king.
descriptions.r1b2k1r/ppppnp1p/1bn2Np1/4p3/2B1P3/3P1N2: Mate in 1. Can you find it? Hint: bishop to h6.
descriptions.r1b2k1r/ppppnp1p/1bn2NpB/4p3/2B1P3/3P1N2: Oh my GOD that was nasty. Would you believe me if I said this exact sequence has been played thousands and thousands of times?
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2pQp/3p4/2bNp3/2BnP3/8/PPPP1: This is a good try from black, and it's a bit tricky. If we just take the rook we will lose on the spot because black will bring their light-square bishop out and check us. Let's instead play knight to e2 to give our king some shelter.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2pQp/3p4/2bNp3/2B1P3/8/PPPPn: Let's recapture with the bishop on e2.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2pQp/3p4/2bNp3/4P3/8/PPPPBqP: Well done! We are completely safe now and we can capture the rook on the next move. The game is pretty much over.
descriptions.r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/2B1P3/2N5/PP: Let's play pawn to d3 here. This opens up our dark square bishop.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b1p3/2B1P3/2NP4/: Let's crack open the position with pawn to f4.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/2b1p3/2B1PP2/2NP4: Let's continue development with knight to f3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/2b1p3/2B1PPb1/2NP1: Here, the best move is knight to a4 attacking Black's bishop since the bishop is preventing us from castling.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/2b1p3/N1BnPPb1/3P1N: Black is adding more pressure to our pinned knight, but this is actually a mistake. First, we capture the bishop on c5 with our knight.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/5n2/2p1p3/2BnPPb1/3P1N2/P: Now we play the killer pawn to c3. Yes - we are actually INVOKING a capture on our knight.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/5n2/2p1p3/2B1PPb1/2PP1n2/: Let's take back with pawn to f3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/5n2/2p1p3/2B1PP2/2PP1P1b/: This doesn't look great for us, but actually after rook to g1, we are completely winning.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/8/2p1p2n/2B1PP2/2PP1P1b/P: Now we have the fantastic rook to g5, forking the knight and pawn. It also stops any queen to h4 check.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/8/2p1p1R1/2B1Pn2/2PP1P1b/: Now we win the game. Rook captures on e5 with check
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/8/2p1R3/2B1Pn2/2PP1P1b/PP: Well done! We are crushing our opponent here. Between our strong pieces, our ownership of the center, and Black's weak king, I don't see how we can lose this.
descriptions.r1b2knr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2bNp3/2B1P1Q1/8/PPP: This was Black's ONLY move that does not lose on the spot, and this only happens 10% of the time. From here, we develop our knight to h3 to attack the queen.
descriptions.r1b2knr/pppp1ppp/2n5/2bNp3/2BqP1Q1/7N/PP: Now we need to defend our bishop with pawn to d3.
descriptions.r1b2knr/ppp2ppp/2np4/2bNp3/2BqP1Q1/3P3N/: Black is trying a nice idea, opening up their bishop to hit both our queen and knight. Lets drop our queen one square to g3.
descriptions.r4knr/ppp2ppp/2np4/2bNp3/2BqP3/3P2Qb/PPP: Here we actually DON'T recapture and instead play rook to f1.
descriptions.r4knr/ppp2ppp/2npb3/2bNp3/2BqP3/3P2Q1/PP: Now you get to play the coolest move in your chess career. Pawn to c3, TRAPPING THE QUEEN. I mean she is literally just trapped. That is so gangster.
descriptions.r4knr/ppp2ppp/2npb3/2bNp3/2BqP3/2PP2Q1/P: Well done! This is one of the coolest chess lines I have ever seen.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2p1p/1bnp2p1/3Np3/2B1P3/3P1N: Now we have the finishing blow bishop to e3 attacking their bishop.
descriptions.r3k1nr/ppp2p1p/1bnpb1p1/3Np3/2B1P3/3PBN2: Here comes a lot of trades, and at the end, we will be up a piece. First we have bishop takes bishop on b6.
descriptions.r3k1nr/ppp2p1p/1Bnp2p1/3bp3/2B1P3/3P1N2/: Then pawn takes bishop on d5.
descriptions.r3k1nr/1pp2p1p/1pnp2p1/3Pp3/2B5/3P1N2/PP: Then finally, pawn takes knight on c6.
descriptions.r3k1nr/1pp2p1p/1pPp2p1/4p3/2B5/3P1N2/PPP: Well done! We are simply up a piece and will win this game
descriptions.r2k2nr/ppN2pQp/2npb3/2b1p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1: If we are greedy and take either rook, we actually lose the game because our bishop will be taken and the bishop is the only thing stopping their queen from checkmating us right now. Here we play knight takes bishop on e6.
descriptions.r2k2nr/pp4Qp/2npp3/2b1p3/2B1P3/8/PPPP1qP: One last thing: we shouldn't capture the rook immediately. Lets first develop our knight to f3.
descriptions.r2k2nr/pp4Qp/2npp3/2b1p3/2B1P3/5N2/PPPP1: Well done! We are capturing the rook on the next move. The computer gives this position a 5 or 6 point advantage.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1p1p/2n2np1/2b1p3/2B1P3/2N2Q: Let's develop our king's knight to e2. This protects the enemy knight from jumping to d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1p1p/2n2np1/2b1p3/2B1P3/2N2: Let's open up our bishop with pawn to d3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2p1p/2np1np1/2b1p3/2B1P3/2NP: That was a huge mistake from black! Now we have the killer bishop to g5, pinning their knight to their queen.
descriptions.r1bq1r2/ppp2pkp/2np1np1/2b1p1B1/2B1P3/2N: Believe it or not, that pathetic king move happens 60% of the time in that position. Gross. Let's add one more piece to the attack with knight to d5.
descriptions.r2q1r2/ppp2pkp/2np1np1/2bNp1B1/2B1P1b1/3: Cute move, Black, but it doesn't work. Bishop takes f6 with check.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/ppp2p1p/2np1Bp1/2bNp3/2B1P1Q1/3P: GG. It is so, so over for Black.
descriptions.r1b1k1nr/ppp2p1p/2np2p1/3Np3/2B1P3/3PbN2: Now we are completely winning with knight to c7, forking the king and rook
descriptions.r1b3nr/ppNk1p1p/2np2p1/4p3/2B1P3/3PbN2/P: Now we take the rook in the corner with knight to a8.
descriptions.N1b3nr/pp1k1p1p/2np2p1/2b1p3/2B1P3/3P1N2: The last thing to do here is play pawn to c3 to stop the knight from ever coming into our position.
descriptions.N1b3nr/pp1k1p1p/2np2p1/2b1p3/2B1P3/2PP1N: Well done! The computer puts us at a +3 point advantage here.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2p1p/5np1/2p1p3/2B1PP2/2PP1P1b: Huge blunder from black! Now we have f-pawn takes on e5.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2p1p/6p1/2p1P2n/2B1P3/2PP1P1b/: Finally, bishop to g5 hitting the queen.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2p1p/6p1/2p1P1Bn/2B1P3/2PP1P1b: Wow, that was a lot to remember. The good news is our position is crushing here.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/2b1p3/2B1PP2/2NP: Now that black castled, we can unleash one of my favorite attacking ideas in the vienna: pawn to f5. This completely suffocates Black's position.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp2ppp/p1np1n2/2b1pP2/2B1P3/2N: Let's develop our bishop to g5, pinning Black's knight against their queen.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp2pp1/p1np1n1p/2b1pPB1/2B1P3/: Let's take a step back with bishop to h4
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp2pp1/p2p1n1p/2b1pP2/2BnP2B/2: Simple knight takes knight on d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp2pp1/p2p1n1p/4pP2/2BbP2B/2NP: Now for the main idea: knight hops into d5, adding an attacker on the pinned f6 knight.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/1pp2pp1/p2p1n1p/3NpP2/2BbP2B/3P: Well done! Black really has no options here and they will lose the game.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/2p2pp1/p1np1n1p/1pb1pP2/2B1P2B/: Let's take another step back with bishop to b3
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/2p2pp1/p2p1n1p/1pb1pP2/3nP2B/1B: Now our position is really, really good. Knight captures on d4 to save our bishop.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/2p2pp1/p2p1n1p/1p2pP2/3bP2B/1BN: Now for our final idea: knight d5, adding another attacker on the pinned f6 knight.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/2p2pp1/p2p1n1p/1p1NpP2/3bP2B/1B: Our pin is too strong. This line has gone on long enough so I'll end it here, but just know from this position white wins like 90% of their games.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/5n2/2p1p3/2BnPP2/2PP1b2/P: If Black captures us with the bishop, we simply capture back with our pawn to f3.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/2p1p3/2B1PP2/2PP1P2: Now we pin the knight to the king with bishop to b5.
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/1Bp1p3/4PP2/2PP1P2/: Well done! This is a very comfortable position for us. We're even threatening to capture the knight on c6 which would triple Black's pawns on the c file
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/1bB1P3/2NP4/P: We can handle this pin with knight to e2, preparing to castle.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p3/1bB1P3/2NP4/: If Black castles, we castle! Unpinning ourselves from the bishop.
Well done! We have an edge on our opponent and are ready to play some chess!
descriptions.r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/1bnp1n2/4p3/N1B1PPb1/3P1N: Now we trade with knight to b6.
descriptions.r2qk2r/1pp2ppp/1pnp1n2/4p3/2B1PPb1/3P1N2: One last thing before we castle, let's play pawn to c3 to stop the enemy knight from hopping in.
descriptions.r2q1rk1/1pp2ppp/1pnp1n2/4p3/2B1PPb1/2PP1: Well done! Our king is safe and we are ready to continue our game.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/3pp3/1bB1P3/2NP4/P: Black is playing well here. Let's capture on d5 with our pawn.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2n5/3np3/1bB5/2NP4/PPP1N: Now we can simply castle, undoing the pin.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2n5/4p3/1bB5/2nP4/PPP1NP: Now here we should actually capture back with b2 pawn to c3. This wins a tempo for us.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2nb4/4p3/2B5/2PP4/P1P1NP: Now we can rotate our knight to g3 to open up our queen.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2nb4/4p3/2B5/2PP2N1/P1P2: Well done! Both sides played well and we are ready to have ourselves a good game.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1p1p/5np1/2b1p3/2BnP3/2NP1Q: That was Black's best move, and it leads to a bunch of trades. First, knight takes knight on d4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1p1p/5np1/2b5/2BpP3/2NP1Q2/: Now we should go knight to d5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1p1p/6p1/2bn4/2BpP3/3P1Q2/P: Finally, bishop takes knight on d5.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp1p1p1p/2p3p1/2bB4/3pP3/3P1Q2/: Now we have to retreat our bishop to b3.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pp1p1p1p/2p3p1/2b5/3pP3/1B1P1Q2: Well done! The computer gives us a slight edge, but honestly I think white is doing a lot better here. We have a ton of pressure on the f pawn and in the future we may play bishop to h6 to remove the rook as a defender. I like our chances.
descriptions.r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b5/2B1Pp2/2NP4/P: Black captured and this is actually a mistake! Now we get free development by capturing back with the bishop to f4.
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b5/2B1PB2/2NP4/: The fun way to play is after Black castles, we go queen to d2...
descriptions.r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/2b5/2B1PB2/2NP4/: ... and then we long castle to the queenside. For those who don't know, when White & Black castle on opposite sides, a war is about to break out.
Oh boy! From here, it'll be a bloodbath. Good job and good luck.
